entry.title: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says - WPBF
entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: The Martin County Sheriff’s Office is actively investigating after a shooting Friday afternoon at Gary's Towing and Recovery near Stuart. At 1 p.m., deputies responded to Southeast Cove Road at 4405 SE Cove Road. A woman from Miami arrived at the tow yard to claim a vehicle that had been towed there earlier in the day. Then, people in another vehicle arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, according to the sheriff's office. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl The Miami woman then retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a vehicle and fleeing the area, the agency said. Because the tow yard is about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road Patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units began searching for the suspect vehicle. Deputies located the vehicle traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. The driver fled, and deputies subsequently performed a PIT maneuver, bringing the vehicle to a stop, MCSO said. Additional units moved in and successfully immobilized the vehicle before the driver could flee again. The individuals targeted by the gunfire had left the area before deputies arrived. At this time, it is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire, the agency said. The woman was taken into custody and taken to the Sheriff’s Office, where detectives are currently questioning her. entry.title: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County
entry.summary: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff's Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff's office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman's car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff's office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff's office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

entry.article_text: A woman is in custody after deputies say an altercation at a Martin County towing facility escalated into gunfire, triggering a law enforcement response, a school lockout and a pursuit Friday afternoon. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the shooting happened shortly after 1 p.m. at a towing facility on Southeast Cove Road. Investigators said a woman from Miami arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a vehicle that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly afterward, people in another vehicle arrived at the facility and became involved in an altercation with the woman, according to MCSO. The sheriff's office said the woman retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a vehicle and fleeing the area. Because the tow yard is about a half-mile from Murray Middle School , the sheriff's office activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while deputies responded. Deputies located the vehicle traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop, according to MCSO. The sheriff's office said the driver fled, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver to stop the vehicle. entry.title: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting - cw34.com
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man convicted in connection with a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop has been sentenced to decades in prison, police said Friday. Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys & Girls Clubs of America
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys Girls Clubs of America. Enrique Rosario Liz has been named the organizations 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, a recognition that celebrates outstanding leadership, academic achievement and service to others. The honor marks the latest milestone in a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, advancing to the national level of competition. In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the exciting news during a special presentation. Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: Overflow crowd, heated debate mark Palm Beach County Ag Reserve development meeting
entry.summary: Hundreds of residents packed the South County Civic Center on Friday, while many more were turned away, as concerns over development in Palm Beach County's Agricultural Reserve sparked a heated public meeting that at times became contentious. The meeting, hosted by Palm Beach County Commissioner Maria Sachs, focused on approved projects planned for the area, including a DMV office, a nursing home and an Islamic center. Residents raised concerns about traffic, development impacts and whether enough public notice was given before the projects moved forward. entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents packed the South County Civic Center on Friday, while many more were turned away, as concerns over development in Palm Beach County's Agricultural Reserve sparked a heated public meeting that at times became contentious.The meeting, hosted by Palm Beach County Commissioner Maria Sachs, focused on approved projects planned for the area, including a DMV office, a nursing home and an Islamic center. Residents raised concerns about traffic, development impacts and whether enough public notice was given before the projects moved forward.WATCH BELOW: Overflow crowd, heated debate mark Ag Reserve development meetingBefore the meeting even began, tensions were already running high.More than 1,000 people RSVP'd for the event, despite the venue having space for only about 300 attendees. As crowds gathered outside, many said they were frustrated they could not get inside.Faith Kohn, who traveled from Parkland, said she RSVP'd but never received a response."We all want to be part of this meeting, and they won't let us in," said Kohn. Others outside voiced frustration as they waited outside."We have all these elderly people sweltering in the heat; we're not getting any information, we the people have no respect, they won't let us in to talk or even see the proceedings," said a man standing near the locked front doors as security guarded the entrance.When WPTV reporter Joel Lopez made it inside, there were still chairs available. We learned county officials shut the doors promptly at 9:30 a.m. so the meeting could begin, with Sachs noting she only had until 11 a.m. to get through the discussion.Earlier in the week, WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache reported the meeting had already reached its capacity for RSVPs on Wednesday, and encouraged residents who couldn't secure a seat to watch the meeting online via livestream.Inside the meeting, Sachs found herself fielding concerns from residents who say they want the Agricultural Reserve to remain focused on farming and preservation rather than additional development.When Sachs asked how many people wanted more farming and less housing and school development in the Ag Reserve, the crowd responded overwhelmingly.The discussion quickly turned to concerns over traffic, growth and public notification requirements.Pamela Higer-Polani, an attorney who lives in the Ag Reserve and helped organize residents to attend the meeting.She told WPTV residents have always been vocal about defending the ag reserve, and the fact that many weren't present during the approval process should have been a red flag. "If they did not receive notice, how would they have known that there was supposed to be a commissioner vote or anything of that?" said Pamela Higer-Polani.Higer-Polani said she believes residents living within 1,000 feet of the proposed projects should have been notified, rather than only those within 500 feet."I'm not here how to tell people how to have their religion, how to practice it, that is not my purpose. My purpose is I am extremely concerned that we have had our due process rights violated," said Higer-Polani.At one point during the meeting, Higer-Polani was asked to sit down and was escorted back to her seat by PBSO security after repeatedly attempting to continue her remarks while Sachs worked to restore order.It was one of several moments during the meeting where audience members shouted, stood up and chanted, nearly causing the event to end early as Sachs struggled to regain control.Following the meeting, Sachs told WPTV that residents have every right to express concerns and hold elected officials accountable."People need to be able to voice their opinion on who their neighbors are or aren't, and whether their elected representative listens to them; they can vote them out of office," said Sachs.She also noted she has consistently voted against every development project in the Agricultural Reserve but is only one of seven commissioners.Sachs encouraged residents to contact all county commissioners about their concerns. She explained that the projects residents were protesting were approved through an administrative review process that has existed for years and allows certain government entities and houses of worship to move forward without direct approval from county commissioners."I think for the most part people had their voices heard, but what they said is they want to have a voice in what comes to development in this county. I respect that I hear them," Sachs said.She is now working on a proposal that would require future development applications to come before elected county commissioners for approval."Do you think there's anything that can be done for the developments that have already been approved in the area?" asked Lopez."That's up to the lawyers," said Sachs, adding that she supports looking into it, and that legal action would likely be required to revisit previous approvals.Another major point of contention centered on an Islamic center planned for the Agricultural Reserve.The project was approved in 2022 and was repeatedly discussed during Friday's meeting, calling for stricter background checks and more information about applicants seeking approval for places of worship.Outside the venue, some attendees held signs agaisnt the site and during the meeting, Sachs directed questions regarding the applicant and project funding to attorney Brian Seymour of the Gunster law firm.In response to growing concerns and rhetoric surrounding the project, the Boca Raton Interfaith Clergy Association released the following statement urging respect and tolerance:"As faith leaders in Boca Raton, we believe we live our best lives in a pluralistic, respectful democracy where faith communities live side by side in peace. For decades we have worked together in partnership and mutual respect to build a vibrant, diverse religious community. We write today to urge everyone to seek the peace and welfare of our city and to protect what we have built together.We know some in our community are concerned about plans for expansion, including a new house of worship, in the Agricultural Reserve. Questions about how that area will be developed are before the Palm Beach County Commission and we trust our commissioners to act in the community's best interests.Over the past week we have seen painful and at times hateful remarks about various faith traditions in online conversations about this issue. We condemn unreservedly any expressions of hatred, bigotry, and the vitriol we have seen. We cannot tolerate this level of intolerance.We always encourage residents to bring their concerns to elected officials. We ask that they do so with respect and gratitude for the blessing of a diverse religious community.We stand together in defending every faith community's right to gather and to build houses of worship and community centers. This is a fundamental freedom of our American democracy, and it is essential to living out our commitments to our faiths."-Boca Raton Interfaith Clergy AssociationSachs told WPTV she plans to hold a second public meeting to further discuss the issues raised Friday.A date and location have not been finalized, but Sachs indicated a much larger venue will likely be needed given the turnout.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.title: 21-year-old Okeechobee woman killed in car crash involving tractor-trailer on State Road 710
entry.summary: The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating a car crash involving a tractor-trailer that killed a 21-year-old Okeechobee woman Thursday afternoon. The deadly accident happened at around 1 p.m. at the T-intersection of State Road 710 and Southeast 86th Boulevard. FHP said the woman was at a stop sign at Southeast 86th Boulevard turning left onto State Road 710, when her car was struck by a man driving a tractor-trailer. The woman failed to yield the right of way, traveling into the tractor-trailers lane of travel, causing the tractor-trailer to collide with the drivers side of the womans car. The woman was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital where she died from her injuries. The man was not injured. FHP said the investigation is ongoing.

entry.title: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Jensen Beach residents frustrated by recurring septic backups after storms
entry.summary: WPTV is looking into drainage and septic issues on the Treasure Coast. Neighbor Daniel Fletchall reached out to our news team about septic issues in his community on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach. WATCH BELOW: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Neighbors demand septic solution Neighbors deal with septic back-ups following heavy rainfall Fletchall said after a heavy rain, he and his neighbors' septic backs up and comes up into their yards 'The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard,' said Fletchall. 'It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out.' Fletchall said they can't even flush their toilets for days. 'I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom,' said Fletchall. Fletchall added he can't shower or wash his clothes. 'Thankfully, my parents live nearby, so I can go take a shower,' said Fletchall. 'But it's just not happening here. Fletchall isn't the only one affected by this issue. Neighbors like Christie Berger are also having septic issues every time there's heavy rain. 'I go to McDonald's to use the bathroom if I have to,' Berger said. Neighbor Rachelle Kukan said it's becoming unacceptable. 'I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could,' said Kukan. Fletchall said he had septic companies come out to fix the drainage in his yard. Elevating the septic tank, Fletchall said, would be costly, and even then he's been told it might not solve the problem. Fletchall said he'd like the Martin County staff to extend the sewer lines into his neighborhood. 'I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but Im not getting any help here,' said Fletchall. WPTV reached out to Martin County about any solutions. Staff said the neighborhood on Northwest Sunset Boulevard is on the list to get septic-to-sewer conversions, but no date has been set yet. Staff said they're looking at ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems to convert.

entry.title: Rising dating costs push Gen Z, millennials toward cheaper date nights
entry.summary: The price of dating is going up, and younger adults are looking for less expensive ways to enjoy a date night, according to new data. Payment app Zelle did some research and found 84% of Gen Z and Millennial daters say rising costs have led them to date less, choose less expensive activities or just stop dating. WATCH BELOW: Gen Z, Millennials seek cheaper date nights, study says Higher Prices Impacts Date Night for Gen Z and Millennials Over half also say they value being thoughtful, honest and transparent with money and prefer planning a budget-friendly date. A few adults in their 20s told me a night with a TV movie and ordering food is usually preferred. Not anything extravagant,' said Nia Pierre. 'I like something that's casual or activity-filled, but it usually starts off like a coffee date or something.' And when it comes to paying for the date, 52% say they don't want to make the situation awkward. 'I would say usually the guy pays, but yeah, it's like a 50-50 thing when deciding if its the guy or girl,' Pierre said.

entry.summary: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage    WPEC
entry.article_text: Flooding continues to be a problem across Indiantown, leaving some residents questioning why the issue persists despite years of efforts to improve drainage. Large areas of the village saw flooding this week including Booker Park despite spending more than $2 million on drainage improvements in the area in recent years. Residents have seen some improvements over the years but believe more need to be done. I’ve been here almost 60 years and it hasn’t gotten right, Brown said. It is better than it was at some point, but in 60 years you would think it would be far greater than what it is now. The latest round of flooding has affected other parts of Indiantown as well. Oak River saw significant flooding this week, while floodwater also surrounded Indian River Middle School. For residents whose homes take on water, the problem can quickly become a financial burden. Flood insurance can help cover some flood-related damage, but it can also come with a significant cost. For homeowners without a flood policy, recovery can become more difficult. Brian Christensen, president of Coast to Coast Adjuster, said homeowners facing a flood claim without coverage may have to look for other ways to pay for repairs. See also: GALLERY: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach If you don’t have a flood policy and it is a flood claim and your homeowners policy won’t cut it, I start looking for a loan, Christensen said. Start looking for something a second mortgage, friends, family, churches anything that can assist you. Indiantown Councilman Anthony Dowling said the village is working with Martin County on the flooding problem. The village is also considering a municipal bond that could help address broken pipes and other infrastructure issues. Dowling said the village is repairing pipes that are already damaged and clearing debris from drainage systems. He acknowledged that addressing the flooding problem will not happen overnight and urged residents to take precautions when floodwater is present. I would encourage no kids to play in the water, Dowling said. Village officials say they are continuing to look for ways to address flooding throughout Indiantown. But after years of flooding and millions of dollars spent on drainage improvements residents say they want to know when they will finally see a significant difference.

entry.title: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County - WFLX
entry.summary: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County    WFLX
entry.article_text: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff’s Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman’s car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff’s office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff’s office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

entry.title: Woman in custody after Martin County tow yard shooting leads to pursuit, PIT maneuver - WPEC
entry.summary: Woman in custody after Martin County tow yard shooting leads to pursuit, PIT maneuver    WPEC
entry.article_text: A second woman has been arrested following a chaotic chain of events that began with a shooting at a Martin County tow yard, triggered a nearby school lockout and ended with multiple crashes and a police pursuit. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the incident unfolded shortly after 1 p.m. Friday at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road. Investigators said 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in and drove recklessly while attempting to leave the area. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. CBS12 News spoke with Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, who said he's grateful no one was hurt during the incident. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

entry.article_text: Lucie man was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison after a shooting in January 2025 at a vape shop. On Tuesday, Circuit Judge Elizabeth Metzger also sentenced Joshua Gibbs to 10 years of probation after his time in state prison, Stuart police said Friday. 2, he changed his plea to guilty of five charges: robbery while wearing a mask, attempted robbery while wearing a mask, aggravated assault with a firearm while wearing mask, shooting with a deadly missile and carrying a concealed weapon. Deputies responded to a shooting at 7:31 p.m. 25, 2025, at Miller’s Vapory at 1596 SE Federal Highway. Gibbs entered the business wearing a ski mask and armed with a handgun before opening fire on the store clerk. The clerk returned fire and no one was injured. After an extensive investigation by Stuart Police detectives, Gibbs was identified as the suspect. A person matching Gibbs' description was riding an electric bike near an apartment complex on Southeast St. Lucie Boulevard in Stuart, near where records confirmed he lived at one time. The arrest report also listed his address in Altamonte Springs, where family members live. A warrant was issued, and he was apprehended in Douglasville, Georgia, with the assistance of the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force on Feb. One month earlier, Gibbs was denied service for being underage. Gibbs also threatened the store clerk, asking if they "valued his life over his products," and then proceeded to steal $300 worth of merchandise and leave the area. entry.title: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain - WPBF
entry.summary: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie County mosquito control are working to stop mosquitoes from breeding after recent rain created standing water. In a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 and Fort Pierce, mosquito control teams treated swales and used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide. Officials said the rain has increased standing water, which allows mosquito eggs to hatch. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment’s notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," said Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control. DENGUE FEVER: Dengue fever case in Palm Beach County prompts mosquito control action Kenneth Fusco, a nearby resident, shared his experience with the mosquito problem. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He added, "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!" Crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. They are asking residents to empty or remove containers holding water to prevent mosquito breeding. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project designed to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. More rain is expected, which could lead to additional standing water and, Tuzzolino said, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" If you are dealing with a mosquito problem near your home, contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org. entry.title: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County - WFLX
entry.summary: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County    WFLX
entry.article_text: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff’s Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman’s car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff’s office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff’s office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard in Stuart led to a police chase and a violent crash. “I have more questions than I have answers,” said Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek. Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. The sheriff said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing over, but deputies located her shortly after. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, also from Miami. Budensiek said she was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. “Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we’re not sure. We didn’t even know for sure that that car was involved at that time,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said investigators are working to answer these questions and plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects’ cars and phones. He hopes to have more answers by next week. entry.summary: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A second woman has been arrested following a chaotic chain of events that began with a shooting at a Martin County tow yard, triggered a nearby school lockout and ended with multiple crashes and a police pursuit. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the incident unfolded shortly after 1 p.m. Friday at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road. 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in. "The other female was driving erratically, passing cars, and ended up losing control, going over into the oncoming lane down U.S. 1 and having a significant crash," sheriff John Budensiek said. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. CBS12 News spoke with Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, who said he's grateful no one at the business was injured. I love all the people around me. Even the people next door," Reed said. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

entry.title: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says - WPBF
entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard led to a police chase and a violent crash Friday afternoon. “I have more questions than I have answers,” Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at Gary’s Towing and Recovery, 4405 SE Cove Road, near Stuart, to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. The sheriff said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing, but deputies located her shortly later on Cove Road near U.S. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon, 23, from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, 22, also from Miami. Budensiek said she was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. “Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we’re not sure. We didn’t even know for sure that that car was involved at that time,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said investigators are working to answer these questions and plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects’ cars and phones. He hopes to have more answers by next week. Rondon already is facing two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, felony criminal mischief. Valdes has been cited for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Because the incident was a half-mile from Murray Middle School, MCSO activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. entry.title: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage - WPEC
entry.summary: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage    WPEC
entry.article_text: Flooding continues to be a problem across Indiantown, leaving some residents questioning why the issue persists despite years of efforts to improve drainage. Large areas of the village saw flooding this week including Booker Park despite spending more than $2 million on drainage improvements in the area in recent years. Residents have seen some improvements over the years but believe more need to be done. I’ve been here almost 60 years and it hasn’t gotten right, Brown said. It is better than it was at some point, but in 60 years you would think it would be far greater than what it is now. The latest round of flooding has affected other parts of Indiantown as well. Oak River saw significant flooding this week, while floodwater also surrounded Indian River Middle School. For residents whose homes take on water, the problem can quickly become a financial burden. Flood insurance can help cover some flood-related damage, but it can also come with a significant cost. For homeowners without a flood policy, recovery can become more difficult. Brian Christensen, president of Coast to Coast Adjuster, said homeowners facing a flood claim without coverage may have to look for other ways to pay for repairs. See also: GALLERY: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach If you don’t have a flood policy and it is a flood claim and your homeowners policy won’t cut it, I start looking for a loan, Christensen said. Start looking for something a second mortgage, friends, family, churches anything that can assist you. Indiantown Councilman Anthony Dowling said the village is working with Martin County on the flooding problem. The village is also considering a municipal bond that could help address broken pipes and other infrastructure issues. Dowling said the village is repairing pipes that are already damaged and clearing debris from drainage systems. He acknowledged that addressing the flooding problem will not happen overnight and urged residents to take precautions when floodwater is present. I would encourage no kids to play in the water, Dowling said. Village officials say they are continuing to look for ways to address flooding throughout Indiantown. But after years of flooding and millions of dollars spent on drainage improvements residents say they want to know when they will finally see a significant difference.

entry.title: Federal report says pilots weren't warned about wind before Amazon cargo plane crashed in Miami
entry.summary: Despite regulations requiring it, an air traffic controller failed to tell the pilots of an Amazon cargo plane about the potential for strong tail winds as they landed in Miami, careening off the runway and killing five people last month, according to a preliminary report Thursday from the National Transportation Safety Board. Just four minutes before clearing the plane for landing, an air traffic controller had provided a wind advisory to a different flight, noting gusts of up to 25 mph from the south. But the controller did not issue information about the wind to the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane, the report said. According to federal regulations, both wind direction and velocity were required to be stated when authorizing use of a runway when a tail wind component exists, the NTSB report said. The preliminary report did not list a cause of the crash. The ongoing investigation could take more than a year to complete. The airplane, carrying packages of contact lenses for Amazon, came in fast after a flight from Puerto Rico and barreled roughly 1,200 feet past the end of the runway at Miami International Airport on Sept. 6. It smashed into a van carrying workers for a company that cleans airplanes. Five people who were in the van died. Two others in the van sustained serious injuries, as did the driver of a car that was hit by the plane. The two pilots had minor injuries. entry.article_text: Despite regulations requiring it, an air traffic controller failed to tell the pilots of an Amazon cargo plane about the potential for strong tail winds as they landed in Miami, careening off the runway and killing five people last month, according to a preliminary report Thursday from the National Transportation Safety Board.Just four minutes before clearing the plane for landing, an air traffic controller had provided a wind advisory to a different flight, noting gusts of up to 25 mph from the south. But the controller “did not issue information about the wind” to the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane, the report said.According to federal regulations, “both wind direction and velocity were required to be stated when authorizing use of a runway when a tail wind component exists,” the NTSB report said.The preliminary report did not list a cause of the crash. The ongoing investigation could take more than a year to complete.The airplane, carrying packages of contact lenses for Amazon, came in fast after a flight from Puerto Rico and barreled roughly 1,200 feet past the end of the runway at Miami International Airport on Sept. It smashed into a van carrying workers for a company that cleans airplanes. Five people who were in the van died. Two others in the van sustained serious injuries, as did the driver of a car that was hit by the plane. The two pilots had minor injuries.RELATED STORY | 5 dead after Amazon cargo aircraft overruns runway in Miami, striking multiple vehiclesTail winds can make landing a plane harderExperts said it appears the weather played at least some role in the accident. Tail winds can make it harder to slow a plane and push it past an ideal landing spot on a runway.“When you’ve got winds like that, it is your responsibility as a controller to issue that to a pilot, especially on landing and especially when you have gusts,” said Tony Mello, a former Federal Aviation Administration official who oversaw air traffic control services in the central U.S.Landing with a gusting tail wind “requires more concentration on the part of the pilot” but is not impossible, said former NTSB member John Goglia.Failing to share the wind conditions “was a significant omission but, in and of itself, would not have caused a crash,” Goglia said. “Every crash is a chain of events. That’s just one event.”The plane had little runway left when it touched downA summary of cockpit voice recordings previously released by the NTSB said one of the pilots repeatedly warned his counterpart that they were going too fast as they approached for landing and after touchdown. But the fellow pilot never gave “a consistent verbal response” to the warnings, the NTSB said. The two pilots had flown together for the first time just earlier that day, according to the preliminary NTSB report.The cockpit audio recordings also captured a series of automated warnings from the plane about the speed of descent and the approaching terrain.When it touched down, the plane was traveling at 184 mph and was already about three-quarters of a mile past the start of the runway, the NTSB report said.The pilots may have tried too late to abort the landing. Data from the plane show its wheel brakes were applied, then released as the engines throttled to “go-around” thrust values before the brakes again were applied with about 415 feet of runway remaining.The plane ran off the pavement while still traveling at 130 mph, then struck some airport equipment and the cleaning crew’s van before crashing through a perimeter fence, hitting a car on a public road and coming to rest with its nose in a parking lot fence, the preliminary report said.RELATED STORY | Amazon suspends use of 21 Air, the cargo carrier whose plane careened off Miami runway and killed 5Plane's operator says it is focused on safetyAfter the crash, Amazon suspended its partnership with 21 Air, which operated the plane. The North Carolina carrier had flown packages for Amazon since 2024. The Boeing 767 that crashed was 32 years old and originally built to carry passengers. It was converted to a cargo plane in June 2016, the preliminary NTSB report said.The plane’s operator, 21 Air, said in a written statement Thursday that safety is “a core focus” of its organization.“We are reviewing the information in the NTSB preliminary report closely, alongside our own internal safety and operational protocols, and we will take all appropriate action to improve our safety based on the facts as they are established,” the company said.The Miami crash came less than a year after a UPS cargo plane crashed at Louisville’s Muhammad Ali International Airport after losing its engine while accelerating down the runway. That crash killed all three pilots and 12 people on the ground. Twenty-three more were injured.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in prison in Stuart vape shop shooting - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in prison in Stuart vape shop shooting    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie man was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison after a shooting in January 2025 at a vape shop. On Tuesday, Circuit Judge Elizabeth Metzger also sentenced Joshua Gibbs to 10 years of probation after his time in state prison, Stuart police said Friday. 2, he changed his plea to guilty of five charges: robbery while wearing a mask, attempted robbery while wearing a mask, aggravated assault with a firearm while wearing mask, shooting with a deadly missile and carrying a concealed weapon. Deputies responded to a shooting at 7:31 p.m. 25, 2025, at Miller’s Vapory at 1596 SE Federal Highway. Gibbs entered the business wearing a ski mask and armed with a handgun before opening fire on the store clerk. The clerk returned fire and no one was injured. After an extensive investigation by Stuart Police detectives, Gibbs was identified as the suspect. A person matching Gibbs' description was riding an electric bike near an apartment complex on Southeast St. Lucie Boulevard in Stuart, near where records confirmed he lived at one time. The arrest report also listed his address in Altamonte Springs, where family members live. A warrant was issued, and he was apprehended in Douglasville, Georgia, with the assistance of the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force on Feb. One month earlier, Gibbs was denied service for being underage. Gibbs also threatened the store clerk, asking if they "valued his life over his products," and then proceeded to steal $300 worth of merchandise and leave the area. A crown and a lab coat may seem like they belong in two very different worlds, but for Florida Atlantic University graduate student Paige Aldred, they serve the same purpose: getting people to care about the environment around them. She is also Miss Fort Lauderdale, a title she is using to take the science she studies in the lab out into the community. entry.article_text: — A crown and a lab coat may seem like they belong in two very different worlds, but for Florida Atlantic University graduate student Paige Aldred, they serve the same purpose: getting people to care about the environment around them.Aldred is a biological science master's student at FAU studying water quality, harmful algal blooms, and Sargassum in and around the Indian River Lagoon. She is also Miss Fort Lauderdale, a title she is using to take the science she studies in the lab out into the community.At FAU, Aldred's research examines water quality at locations stretching from Sebastian Inlet south to Jupiter Inlet, including Fort Pierce and the St. Lucie Inlet.“The work that I'm doing at FAU is I'm studying the Indian River Lagoon,” Aldred said. “I'm not only studying the water quality of the Indian River Lagoon, but as well as what the Sargassum is bringing into the Indian River.”For Aldred, much of the work begins with something Floridians know all too well: Sargassum.She collects samples in the field before drying and grinding the seaweed into a fine powder that can be sent for isotope testing. Water associated with the Sargassum is also preserved and analyzed to determine what microscopic organisms may be present.One organism she's investigating is a type of dinoflagellate that has also been detected during research into the unusual spinning behavior observed in fish in the Florida Keys.Aldred is examining whether the organism can travel on Sargassum and make its way into the Indian River Lagoon.“I'm looking to see if that dinoflagellate ... is traveling on Sargassum and finding its way into the Indian River Lagoon,” Aldred said. “And so far I have found traces of that dinoflagellate in my samples.”Researchers are continuing to investigate the cause of the abnormal fish behavior in the Florida Keys, and the presence of a dinoflagellate does not by itself establish that it caused the spinning behavior.Aldred's work doesn't stop when she leaves FAU.As Miss Fort Lauderdale, she uses public appearances and community events to advocate for clean drinking water, healthy ecosystems and more sustainable choices.Aldred said participating in the Miss America organization has also helped her develop another skill she considers important for scientists: communicating complicated research to people outside the scientific community.“Now I have opportunities where I can speak in front of people, but not just speak in front of scientists, speak in front of the community,” Aldred said. “And be able to communicate and translate my science into ways that the community can understand how it impacts them and what they can do to make that difference.”Her environmental message even extends to her pageant wardrobe.Aldred says the clothing she wears for appearances is thrifted, upcycled or purchased secondhand. Rather than continually buying new outfits, she reworks pieces she already owns with different accessories, jackets and styling.The choice is intended to call attention to fast fashion, textile waste and synthetic fibers that can shed from clothing.“We have to understand that we are wearing clothes each day that are shedding,” Aldred said.She encourages people to consider natural fibers, secondhand clothing, upcycled materials and simply asking whether they need to purchase another new item.Aldred also works with children, including through environmental education materials for students in kindergarten through 12th grade.During some classroom visits, she brings trash collected from beaches and places it around the classroom before students enter.When the children question why garbage is in their space, Aldred turns the reaction into a lesson: marine animals are experiencing the same thing when human trash enters their environment.But there's another message she hopes young girls take away when Miss Fort Lauderdale walks into their classroom wearing a crown.“I absolutely love when I go out in the community and, you know, the little girls see a princess,” Aldred said. “But I want them to not only see a princess but a girl who's in science, a girl who can get her hands dirty ... as well as a girl who wants to create that change.”For Aldred, the crown and the science aren't competing identities. One helps her study what's happening in Florida's waters. The other gives her a platform to make sure people understand why it matters.

While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. entry.summary: Martin County border collie hoarding case moves forward as 30 rescued dogs find new homes    WFLX
entry.article_text: A criminal case involving 36 rescued border collies in Martin County is moving forward. Paige O’Donnell faces 72 criminal charges — two for each dog rescued from her home. She was not present at her docket sounding Thursday afternoon in the Martin County courthouse, but I spoke with her attorney, Russell Ferraro. “At this point I can’t really say anything on her behalf for or against her,” Ferraro said. “We just got the discovery in the case yesterday. We’re organizing it, going through it, and we’ll take it from there.” It has been just under two months since Martin County deputies took 36 dogs out of O’Donnell’s feces-filled home on Aug. The county condemned it days after the Border Collies were rescued. Ferraro said O’Donnell is staying elsewhere while the house is under repair. O’Donnell faces an animal cruelty and improper confinement charge for each dog and has pleaded not guilty. “Everybody’s got a right to a fair trial and to due process,” Ferraro said. The next hearing in O’Donnell’s case is scheduled for Dec. While the outcome of the case remains uncertain, most of O’Donnell’s former dogs have found loving homes. According to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, 30 of the dogs have been adopted, five have gone or are about to go to animal rescues, and one remains up for adoption. Lucie and Colleen Tilley near Deltona each adopted one of the rescued border collies. Both say their new family members — now named Nadia and Leila — have had little trouble adjusting to their new lives. “She’s just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,” Cale said. Cale said Nadia, named after a character from the show “New Girl,” goes to work with him every day and usually warms up to new people after they offer her a treat. “She’s just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,” Cale said. “When I saw where they came from, I expected a lot more of a challenge,” he added. She wants to be out there and interacting with the world.” “There’s no off switch; it’s all go, go, go,” Tilley said, as Leila raced back and forth behind her in her backyard during a Zoom interview. “It’s really satisfying to see, actually. Just that she’s— she’s happy.” Tilley recalled how nervous Leila was when she first came home on Sept. “At first — like the first three days — it took her to be able to go out the doors— like when I opened the front door, she would run and hide under the bed,” Tilley said. “Now she just runs straight through the sliding glass door, or into it.” Cale and Tilley both said their new border collies have taken well to training as they work to shed old habits, like jumping onto countertops. “I think that’s how they got their food,” Tilley speculated. When Tilley thinks about the criminal case against Leila’s former owner, she wonders what went wrong. Tilley, who showed dogs with her family during her childhood, said she remembers O’Donnell and her outstanding reputation. Like she had very well-bred dogs, very well-trained dogs, beautiful dogs,” Tilley said. “And so all of us were just like, what happened?” Cale revealed that he’d been grieving the loss of his beloved Border Collie, Jessie, who’d died from cancer a year before he heard about what had happened in Palm City. “You just never know when the right dog is gonna come along, and this was the right dog,” Cale said. “(Jessie) was the ride-or-die that would have gone anywhere with me — roaming the woods and getting into mischief ... And that’s gonna be Nadia now.” “You just never know when the right dog is gonna come along, and this was the right dog,” Cale said. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says one Border Collie is still up for adoption. entry.title: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain - WPBF
entry.summary: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie County mosquito control are working to stop mosquitoes from breeding after recent rain created standing water. In a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 and Fort Pierce, mosquito control teams treated swales and used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide. Officials said the rain has increased standing water, which allows mosquito eggs to hatch. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment’s notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," said Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control. DENGUE FEVER: Dengue fever case in Palm Beach County prompts mosquito control action Kenneth Fusco, a nearby resident, shared his experience with the mosquito problem. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He added, "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!" Crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. They are asking residents to empty or remove containers holding water to prevent mosquito breeding. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project designed to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. More rain is expected, which could lead to additional standing water and, Tuzzolino said, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" If you are dealing with a mosquito problem near your home, contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org. entry.title: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County - cw34.com
entry.summary: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A second woman has been arrested following a chaotic chain of events that began with a shooting at a Martin County tow yard, triggered a nearby school lockout and ended with multiple crashes and a police pursuit. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the incident unfolded shortly after 1 p.m. Friday at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road. 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in. "The other female was driving erratically, passing cars, and ended up losing control, going over into the oncoming lane down U.S. 1 and having a significant crash," sheriff John Budensiek said. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. CBS12 News spoke with Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, who said he's grateful no one at the business was injured. I love all the people around me. Even the people next door," Reed said. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

entry.summary: Teen dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old boy died after a shooting late Friday close to a boat ramp near Fellsmere and Vero Beach, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Saturday. The Indian River School District said the unnamed teen had recently withdrawn from Sebastian River High School to homeschool and was not enrolled in the district at the time of the shooting. "We are deeply saddened by the loss of this young person, and our hearts are with his family, friends, and the Sebastian River High School community," district spokeswoman Kyra Schafte said in a statement to WPBF. In a follow-up email she wrote: "This remains an active investigation, and we are in constant communication with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. Please direct questions about the investigation to IRCSO. Our primary focus is supporting our students, staff, families, and community during this difficult time." A dance is scheduled for 7 p.m. Saturday at Sebastian River High. Read more at: https://www.miamiherald.com/news/article317482082.html#storylink=cpy At 11:24 p.m., deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the area of Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512 and near the Fort Drum Marsh Conservation Area. Deputies located the teen and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries, the sheriff's office said. "At this time, this appears to be an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public," Lt. Kevin Jaworski wrote in an alert to the media. "This is an active investigation." He told WPBF that investigators have interviewed all parties involved in the case. Anyone with information about this incident is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office (772-569-6700) or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers (1-800-273-TIPS). Detectives from the Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel were processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. The area remains open to the public. entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard led to a police chase and a violent crash Friday afternoon. “I have more questions than I have answers,” Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at Gary’s Towing and Recovery, 4405 SE Cove Road, near Stuart, to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. The sheriff said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing, but deputies located her shortly later on Cove Road near U.S. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon, 23, from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, 22, also from Miami. Budensiek said she was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. “Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we’re not sure. We didn’t even know for sure that that car was involved at that time,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said investigators are working to answer these questions and plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects’ cars and phones. He hopes to have more answers by next week. Rondon already is facing two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, felony criminal mischief. Valdes has been cited for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Because the incident was a half-mile from Murray Middle School, MCSO activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. entry.title: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain - wpbf.com
entry.summary: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: Lucie County mosquito control are working to stop mosquitoes from breeding after recent rain created standing water. In a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 and Fort Pierce, mosquito control teams treated swales and used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide. Officials said the rain has increased standing water, which allows mosquito eggs to hatch. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment’s notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," said Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control. DENGUE FEVER: Dengue fever case in Palm Beach County prompts mosquito control action Kenneth Fusco, a nearby resident, shared his experience with the mosquito problem. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He added, "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!" Crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. They are asking residents to empty or remove containers holding water to prevent mosquito breeding. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project designed to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. More rain is expected, which could lead to additional standing water and, Tuzzolino said, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" If you are dealing with a mosquito problem near your home, contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org. entry.title: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: A second woman has been arrested following a chaotic chain of events that began with a shooting at a Martin County tow yard, triggered a nearby school lockout and ended with multiple crashes and a police pursuit. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the incident unfolded shortly after 1 p.m. Friday at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road. 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in. "The other female was driving erratically, passing cars, and ended up losing control, going over into the oncoming lane down U.S. 1 and having a significant crash," sheriff John Budensiek said. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. CBS12 News spoke with Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, who said he's grateful no one at the business was injured. I love all the people around me. Even the people next door," Reed said. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

entry.title: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says - WPBF
entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard led to a police chase and a violent crash Friday afternoon. “I have more questions than I have answers,” Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at Gary’s Towing and Recovery, 4405 SE Cove Road, near Stuart, to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. The sheriff said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing, but deputies located her shortly later on Cove Road near U.S. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon, 23, from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, 22, also from Miami. Budensiek said she was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. “Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we’re not sure. We didn’t even know for sure that that car was involved at that time,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said investigators are working to answer these questions and plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects’ cars and phones. He hopes to have more answers by next week. Rondon already is facing two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, felony criminal mischief. Valdes has been cited for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Because the incident was a half-mile from Murray Middle School, MCSO activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout.
