entry.title: 2 women arrested after shooting at Martin County tow yard sparked a chase and crash, more charges possible - WPTV
entry.summary: 2 women arrested after shooting at Martin County tow yard sparked a chase and crash, more charges possible    WPTV
entry.article_text: Two women are under arrest after a shooting at Garry's Towing and Recovery in Martin County triggered a school lockout, a police chase and a separate crash. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says more charges could be coming.Jade Rondon, a Miami resident, opened fire in the tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m.WATCH BELOW: Tow yard shooting leads to arrests; more charges possibleThe sheriff's office says the car she came to retrieve had been involved in criminal activity Thursday evening, then reported stolen. Detectives recovered it Friday morning.Around 1 p.m., Rondon arrived at the tow yard accompanied by another woman, Valerie Valdes. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said."They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car which by the way the only thing really in the car was a couple guns," Sheriff John Budensiek said.Rondon got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into the car and leaving the area. The individuals who were shot at also left the scene before deputies arrived.Garry Reed, the owner of Garry's Towing and Recovery, said his employee was left shaken by the ordeal."Young lady who works in my office — she was terrorized," Reed said.Reed told me they had helped the Martin County Sheriff's Office recover the car Friday morning, but when the owner came to pick it up this afternoon, things turned dangerous."The young lady went to see what was going on and all of a sudden she heard gunfire," Reed said."[It’s] scary. I'm racing — my heart is racing," Reed said.Because the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff's office immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout.Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for Rondon's car and located it traveling on Cove Road near US-1. Deputies attempted a traffic stop, but she fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver to bring the car to a stop.Later, Valdes was reportedly driving recklessly, lost control and caused a significant crash near Osprey Street and US-1. No one was seriously hurt.The Sheriff's Office is still conducting search warrants and reviewing data and video evidence to figure out what happened at the tow yard."We're honestly not sure what we have," Budensiek said. "We're sure that shots are fired. We're sure that she fled from our deputies. Something happened with that vehicle the night before. There was a reason why everyone had interest in that car."Rondon faces two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving with a suspended license and felony criminal mischief. Valdes faces charges for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The sheriff says more charges are likely as investigators piece together what happened.Despite the chaos, Reed said he is counting his blessings."Thank God that everybody was okay," Reed said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.title: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Tow yard shooting leads to two arrests, multiple crashes in Martin County    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: A second woman has been arrested following a chaotic chain of events that began with a shooting at a Martin County tow yard, triggered a nearby school lockout and ended with multiple crashes and a police pursuit. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the incident unfolded shortly after 1 p.m. Friday at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road. 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in. "The other female was driving erratically, passing cars, and ended up losing control, going over into the oncoming lane down U.S. 1 and having a significant crash," sheriff John Budensiek said. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. CBS12 News spoke with Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, who said he's grateful no one at the business was injured. I love all the people around me. Even the people next door," Reed said. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

entry.article_text: Lucie man was sentenced to 37.5 years in prison after a shooting in January 2025 at a vape shop. On Tuesday, Circuit Judge Elizabeth Metzger also sentenced Joshua Gibbs to 10 years of probation after his time in state prison, Stuart police said Friday. 2, he changed his plea to guilty of five charges: robbery while wearing a mask, attempted robbery while wearing a mask, aggravated assault with a firearm while wearing mask, shooting with a deadly missile and carrying a concealed weapon. Deputies responded to a shooting at 7:31 p.m. 25, 2025, at Miller’s Vapory at 1596 SE Federal Highway. Gibbs entered the business wearing a ski mask and armed with a handgun before opening fire on the store clerk. The clerk returned fire and no one was injured. After an extensive investigation by Stuart Police detectives, Gibbs was identified as the suspect. A person matching Gibbs' description was riding an electric bike near an apartment complex on Southeast St. Lucie Boulevard in Stuart, near where records confirmed he lived at one time. The arrest report also listed his address in Altamonte Springs, where family members live. A warrant was issued, and he was apprehended in Douglasville, Georgia, with the assistance of the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force on Feb. One month earlier, Gibbs was denied service for being underage. Gibbs also threatened the store clerk, asking if they "valued his life over his products," and then proceeded to steal $300 worth of merchandise and leave the area. entry.summary: Teen dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old boy died after a shooting late Friday close to a boat ramp near Fellsmere and Vero Beach, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Saturday. The Indian River School District said the unnamed teen recently withdrew from Sebastian River High School to homeschool and was not enrolled in the district at the time of the shooting. "We are deeply saddened by the loss of this young person, and our hearts are with his family, friends, and the Sebastian River High School community," district spokeswoman Kyra Schafte said in a statement to WPBF. In a follow-up email she wrote: "This remains an active investigation, and we are in constant communication with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. Please direct questions about the investigation to IRCSO. Our primary focus is supporting our students, staff, families, and community during this difficult time." A dance is scheduled for 7 p.m. Saturday at Sebastian River High. Read more at: https://www.miamiherald.com/news/article317482082.html#storylink=cpy At 11:24 p.m., deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the area of Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512 and near the Fort Drum Marsh Conservation Area. Deputies located the teen and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries, the sheriff's office said. "At this time, this appears to be an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public," Lt. Kevin Jaworski wrote in an alert to the media. "This is an active investigation." He told WPBF that investigators have interviewed all parties involved in the case. Anyone with information about this incident is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office (772-569-6700) or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers (1-800-273-TIPS). Detectives from the Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel were processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. The area remains open to the public. entry.title: Trump holds Ohio midterm rally, urging voters to consider him on the ballot during 32-day campaign tour
entry.summary: President Donald Trump rallied supporters at Butler High School in Ohio on Saturday, urging them to consider him as a key factor as he continued his midterm campaign push. 'We win when I'm on the ballot,' Trump said. The rally is part of what Trump calls a 32-day tour ahead of the election to help boost Republicans amid a number of competitive races across the country. RELATED STORY | New midterm polling gives Democrats an edge in battleground states Ohio is home to several closely watched races. Former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown is seeking to unseat incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted in a race that could determine who controls the Senate. Republican Vivek Ramaswamy is also running against Democrat Amy Acton. 'On election night Ohio is going to prove America does not belong to those who hate it, America belongs to those who love it,' Trump said. Trump touted both Republican candidates and his administration to the crowd. His message included promoting investments, tariffs and action against Iran, defending data centers which have divided some Republicans and promising they would ensure the centers benefit communities, while warning against Democratic leadership. A short distance from the rally, 1,400 people at a Navistar truck factory were laid off, according to the Associated Press. The campaign push comes as polls show persistent voter concerns about the economy. A recent AP/NORC poll found only 17% of adults approved of his handling of the cost of living. More broadly, a number of polls show the president's approval rating generally under 40%. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Trump claims Iran is waiting until after midterm elections to strike deal Trump dismissed the surveys to the crowd, contending they do not account for his campaigning. 'They don't account that Trump is out campaigning,' he said. He spoke to a high school stadium filled with supporters donning MAGA gear, many touting support for Trump some for all three campaigns. One protestor was drowned out by the crowd. 'I think we're gonna have a surprise,' Trump said. 'Just get out and vote and if you do that we're gonna win big,' Trump said. Trump has acknowledged concern over messaging and races in some states in recent days. His focus in the final weeks ahead of the election has centered on red states to thank supporters including Texas, Oklahoma and Alabama with a visit to Nebraska ahead.

Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Jensen Beach residents frustrated by recurring septic backups after storms
entry.summary: WPTV is looking into drainage and septic issues on the Treasure Coast. Neighbor Daniel Fletchall reached out to our news team about septic issues in his community on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach. WATCH BELOW: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Neighbors demand septic solution Neighbors deal with septic back-ups following heavy rainfall Fletchall said after a heavy rain, he and his neighbors' septic backs up and comes up into their yards 'The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard,' said Fletchall. 'It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out.' Fletchall said they can't even flush their toilets for days. 'I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom,' said Fletchall. Fletchall added he can't shower or wash his clothes. 'Thankfully, my parents live nearby, so I can go take a shower,' said Fletchall. 'But it's just not happening here. Fletchall isn't the only one affected by this issue. Neighbors like Christie Berger are also having septic issues every time there's heavy rain. 'I go to McDonald's to use the bathroom if I have to,' Berger said. Neighbor Rachelle Kukan said it's becoming unacceptable. 'I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could,' said Kukan. Fletchall said he had septic companies come out to fix the drainage in his yard. Elevating the septic tank, Fletchall said, would be costly, and even then he's been told it might not solve the problem. Fletchall said he'd like the Martin County staff to extend the sewer lines into his neighborhood. 'I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but Im not getting any help here,' said Fletchall. WPTV reached out to Martin County about any solutions. Staff said the neighborhood on Northwest Sunset Boulevard is on the list to get septic-to-sewer conversions, but no date has been set yet. Staff said they're looking at ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems to convert.

entry.article_text: Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys Girls Clubs of America. The honor marks the latest milestone in a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, advancing to the national level of competition. In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the exciting news during a special presentation. Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County - wflx.com
entry.summary: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County    wflx.com
entry.article_text: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff’s Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman’s car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff’s office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff’s office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.title: SLC seniors demand answers as Fort Pierce center prepares to close
entry.summary: A Fort Pierce senior center is expected to close, leaving some of the older adults who rely on it worried about losing a gathering place in their own community. The Council on Aging of St. Lucie confirmed the senior center at 1505 Orange Avenue in Fort Pierce is expected to close in the near future. The property is currently listed for sale for $2.2 million. The news came as a surprise to some seniors who use the center regularly, including 77-year-old Sandy Pietrewicz. She has relied on the center for nearly a decade. That's the community center that I go to for lunch and friendship and social activities with other elderly women, said Pietrewicz. After hearing the center could be closing, Pietrewicz said she and other seniors were left with questions about what would happen to the services they depend on. We were all talking about who we could contact, and I thought of WPTV immediately, she said. WPTV reporter Brooke Chau went to the center to get answers and hear directly from the seniors who use it. The Council on Aging said the closure will not mean an end to the services provided to seniors. You're going to get the same treatment. You're going to get the same love. You're going to get the same meals, said Trekina Smith with the Council on Aging. Once the property sells, seniors who currently use the Orange Avenue location are expected to transition to the Council on Aging's facility on Bayshore Boulevard in Port St. Lucie. The organization said transportation will be provided to help seniors get to the new location. But some seniors say the location itself is important. That makes us even angrier. We can't have something in our own community, Pietrewicz said. Geneira Lovett, who also uses the center, told WPTV that seniors in Fort Pierce want to be able to access services close to where they live. We live here, we want rights to do thing, besides trouble, Lovett said. The Council on Aging said it understands those concerns, but says change is necessary. For now, the Council on Aging says services at the Orange Avenue center are continuing. There is no finalized timeline for the closure because the transition is tied to the sale of the property. We understand the concerns, it's a change for us too. But hey, change comes, and you got to go with the change, Smith said. The organization said seniors will continue to have access to meals, activities, social opportunities and transportation once services move to the Port St. Lucie location.

entry.title: Wrong-way driver causes deadly 3-vehicle crash on I-95 in West Palm Beach
entry.summary: A wrong-way driver sparked a deadly three-vehicle crash early Sunday morning on I-95 in West Palm Beach, killing one person and seriously injuring two others, according to the Florida Highway Patrol (FHP). The crash happened around 5:30 a.m. Sunday on the northbound lanes of I-95 near Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard. Investigators say a GMC Sierra pickup truck was traveling south in the inside lane of northbound I-95, driving the wrong way as it approached Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard. A Dodge Grand Caravan was traveling north in the inside lane when its driver, a 68-year-old West Palm Beach man, attempted to swerve right to avoid the oncoming pickup, but was unable to avoid collision. Following the initial impact, the pickup rotated and came to rest in the inside northbound lane. The van spun across the roadway from west to east. A Cadillac El Dorado was traveling north behind the van and was unable to avoid the wreckage. The Cadillac then struck the rear of the van, according to FHP. The driver of the Dodge Grand Caravan was pronounced dead at the scene. FHP has not shared the identity of the driver. The wrong-way driver, a 26-year-old West Palm Beach man, and the Cadillac driver suffered serious injuries and were transported to St. Mary's Medical Center for treatment. All northbound lanes of I-95 at Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard remained closed while the crash was being investigated, but have since reopened.

The van spun across the roadway from west to east.A Cadillac El Dorado was traveling north behind the van and was unable to avoid the wreckage. The Cadillac then struck the rear of the van, according to FHP.The driver of the Dodge Grand Caravan was pronounced dead at the scene. FHP has not shared the identity of the driver. The wrong-way driver, a 26-year-old West Palm Beach man, and the Cadillac driver suffered serious injuries and were transported to St. Mary's Medical Center for treatment.All northbound lanes of I-95 at Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard remained closed while the crash was being investigated, but have since reopened.

entry.title: 3 Ag Reserve projects fuel growth concerns among western Delray Beach residents
entry.summary: Western Delray Beach residents are voicing concerns about growth and development in the Agricultural Reserve as three major projects move forward along Lyons Road, including a new driver's license office, a nursing home and an Islamic school and daycare. The debate intensified Friday after a public meeting hosted by Palm Beach County Commissioner Maria Sachs that drew hundreds of residents seeking answers about traffic, zoning and public notification. WATCH BELOW: 3 Ag Reserve projects spark debate in western Delray 3 Ag Reserve projects spark growth debate in Western Delray Beach The projects are already at various stages of approval and construction, but some neighbors say they were not adequately informed about developments that could significantly change the character of the area. As Palm Beach County continues to experience rapid population growth, development in the Ag Reserve has become a recurring issue for residents concerned about traffic congestion, infrastructure demands and preservation of open land. The latest projects have reignited that debate in western Delray Beach. Public meeting draws large crowd Hundreds of residents attended a public meeting Friday hosted by Commissioner Sachs to discuss development activity in the Agricultural Reserve. Residents raised concerns about traffic, density and transparency in the approval process. One resident, Michelle, said she believes nearby homeowners should have received more notice before projects advanced. 'We were not notified,' Michelle said. 'This is a natural reserve and if you're going to destroy the natural reserve you need to notify residents who live in the neighborhood.' Others questioned whether development should continue in the area at all, arguing the Agricultural Reserve should remain protected from additional growth. Three projects moving forward 1. According to county officials, Palm Beach County Tax Collector Anne Gannon purchased the property for approximately $4.3 million. The facility will replace the current office on Congress Avenue. Construction is already underway on the 4.2-acre site, with the new location expected to open in 2027. 2. entry.title: Arya Tea Bar makes GreenMarket debut as one of this season's new vendors
entry.summary: The West Palm Beach GreenMarket is known for bringing together local farmers, makers and small businesses, and this season, five new vendors are joining the lineup. On Saturday, WPTV reporter Christy Waite showcased one of them. WATCH Arya Tea Bar Makes GreenMarket Debut as One of This Season's New Vendors Small Business Saturday at the GreenMarket Arya Tea Bar, a downtown West Palm Beach tea shop, specializes in matcha drinks, loose-leaf teas and fruit refreshers made with clean, high-quality ingredients. Owner Sophie DeWaal says tea has always been a part of her life. 'I have drunk tea my whole life. I have only ever had coffee literally three times,' DeWaal said. At her Clematis Street storefront, customers can find classic teas, specialty matcha drinks and loose-leaf teas sourced from around the world. DeWaal said she carefully selected teas she believes are the best representation of their type, including hibiscus, black tea, Earl Grey and Japanese floral teas she discovered while visiting Japan. Arya Tea Bar also offers fruit refreshers that can be made with either tea or lemonade. The drinks feature house-made fruit purees and freshly diced fruit. 'When matcha became a thing, I was like, this is amazing. There is so much cool stuff you can do with it. If you use high-quality tea, you can use clean ingredients and not fill it with a bunch of sugar and still get a really nice drink.' Popular menu items include strawberry, mango and lavender matchas, along with the shop's bestselling salted date matcha. 'The salted date matcha is one of our most popular,' DeWaal said. Arya Tea Bar opened its Clematis Street storefront in January, but DeWaal's connection to the GreenMarket began long before she became a vendor. She said the GreenMarket was one of the reasons she decided to move to West Palm Beach and was thrilled when she learned Arya Tea Bar had been selected as a vendor this season. 'I feel like I got into the Harvard of farmers' markets,' DeWaal said. 'I moved to West Palm because of the GreenMarket.' Now, she's excited to introduce her products to a whole new audience. 'I am so excited to meet everyone and meet the people who are interested in what we have to offer. I think it's really unique,' she said. The business also carries a personal connection for DeWaal. Arya Tea Bar is named after her horse, Arya, a nod to the years she spent horseback riding and show jumping in Wellington. As one of five new vendors joining the West Palm Beach GreenMarket

entry.article_text: A 17-year-old died after being shot near a boat ramp in Indian River County late Friday night, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near Garcia's Boat Ramp, at approximately 11:24 p.m. WATCH: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp The sheriff's office said deputies found the 17-year-old and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he died from his injuries. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. Investigators said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public. No information about a possible suspect or what led up to the shooting has been released. Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys & Girls Clubs of America
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys Girls Clubs of America. Enrique Rosario Liz has been named the organizations 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, a recognition that celebrates outstanding leadership, academic achievement and service to others. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys Girls Clubs of America The honor marks the latest milestone in a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, advancing to the national level of competition. In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the exciting news during a special presentation. Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: Panthers place Aleksander Barkov on long-term injured reserve with injury to left leg
entry.summary: Florida center Aleksander Barkov has been placed on long-term injured reserve by the Panthers, meaning the injury to his left leg will keep him sidelined for at least the next 10 games and quite possibly beyond. The Panthers are still unclear on the extent of Barkov's injury , coach Paul Maurice said, adding that Barkov will see Florida team physicians on Monday. RELATED: More Panthers news 'We know its going to be 10 (games) anyway,' Maurice said after the Panthers practiced in Irvine, California. 'Well see what they say Monday. ... Im not the doctor here. So, well see. Whatever they say.' Florida made a pair of roster additions after placing Barkov on the injured list Saturday, bringing up center Sam Lafferty and defenseman Alexander Petrovic. Barkov was hurt midway through the second period of Florida's 4-3 overtime loss to the San Jose Sharks on Thursday night. He was jostling for the puck along the boards, got pushed by the Sharks' Darnell Nurse and awkwardly fell to the ice with his left leg at an unnatural angle. It appeared his knee buckled on the play. Barkov remained down for a few moments, then got up and headed toward the tunnel leading to the Florida dressing room. He walked with a bit of a limp and appeared to angrily try to throw off his gloves as he moved toward the room. Barkov Florida's captain and a huge part of the Panthers' runs to Stanley Cup championships in 2024 and 2025 missed the entire 2025-26 season with torn ligaments in his right knee. He went scoreless in his first two appearance of this season for Florida, which plays Sunday at Anaheim. There was some good injury news Saturday, with Maurice saying that forward Brad Marchand is getting closer to making his season debut 'real close,' Maurice said and that defenseman Gustav Forsling, who had the overtime goal in the opener at Carolina but was a last-minute scratch at San Jose with an upper body issue, is a game-time decision for Sunday.

entry.title: Vikings defeat Dolphins 15-10 as Miami still searches for first win of season
entry.summary: Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings' offense would've appreciated a touchdown for their progress down the stretch, but there was only one way to truly secure this victory. T.J. Hockenson fittingly took the winning slide. The Vikings stayed undefeated with more dominance by their defense and five field goals from Will Reichard, sidestepping their early passing game problems to beat the winless Miami Dolphins 15-10 on Sunday. Hockenson tied a career high with 13 receptions for 119 yards on 13 targets from Murray, including the game-sealing 8-yard catch on third-and-5 from the 10. The eighth-year tight end was wide open and could've coasted into the end zone, but he wisely slid in front of the goal line to drain the clock to the two-minute warning. 'Once you get the first down, you've got to get down,' said Hockenson, who had his highest yardage total since Week 10 of the 2023 season. 'It was tough. I saw that goal line and I wanted it, but it's for the betterment of the team that we ended on offense.' With the Dolphins out of timeouts, the Vikings had Murray take three straight kneel-downs to move to 4-0 for the second time in three years despite going without a touchdown in two games. 'If we want to score, we should do it earlier,' Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said. Murray finished 27 for 37 for 247 yards without a turnover, but he took four sacks for 34 yards against a Dolphins defense that had none in the first three games and was often tentative and unsteady in the pocket until Hockenson helped him open up the field with a handful of clutch and difficult catches. The Dolphins, who are 0-4 for the first time since starting 0-7 in 2019 in their first season under then-coach Brian Flores, were crushed by a combination of unforced mistakes including nine penalties for 55 yards. New Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis went just 9 for 17 for 85 yards, losing a fumble during one of the two sacks by Dallas Turner. The four teams the Dolphins have faced in coach Jeff Hafley's first year are 15-1. Gordon, who ended the game with 100 yards rushing, had a 12-yard touchdown run on the next drive to pull the Dolphins within 12-10.Reichard, who stretched the NFL's longest active streak to 31 consecutive made field goals, drew a loud roar when he was shown on the videoboard during the two-minute warning. entry.title: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Jensen Beach residents frustrated by recurring septic backups after storms - WFLX
entry.summary: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Jensen Beach residents frustrated by recurring septic backups after storms    WFLX
entry.article_text: WPTV is looking into drainage and septic issues on the Treasure Coast. Neighbor Daniel Fletchall reached out to our news team about septic issues in his community on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach. WATCH BELOW: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Neighbors demand septic solution Fletchall said after a heavy rain, he and his neighbors' septic backs up and comes up into their yards "The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard," said Fletchall. "It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out." Fletchall said they can't even flush their toilets for days. "I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom," said Fletchall. Fletchall added he can't shower or wash his clothes. "Thankfully, my parents live nearby, so I can go take a shower," said Fletchall. "But it's just not happening here.” Fletchall isn't the only one affected by this issue. Neighbors like Christie Berger are also having septic issues every time there's heavy rain. "I go to McDonald's to use the bathroom if I have to," Berger said. Neighbor Rachelle Kukan said it's becoming unacceptable. "I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could," said Kukan. Fletchall said he had septic companies come out to fix the drainage in his yard. Elevating the septic tank, Fletchall said, would be costly, and even then he's been told it might not solve the problem. Fletchall said he'd like the Martin County staff to extend the sewer lines into his neighborhood. "I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but I’m not getting any help here," said Fletchall. WPTV reached out to Martin County about any solutions. Staff said the neighborhood on Northwest Sunset Boulevard is on the list to get septic-to-sewer conversions, but no date has been set yet. Staff said they're looking at ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems to convert.

entry.title: I-TEAM: A widow maps brain cancer cases in St. Lucie County — some just doors apart - cbs12.com
entry.summary: I-TEAM: A widow maps brain cancer cases in St. Lucie County — some just doors apart    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Matt Elliott wants to know whether his brain cancer could be connected to other diagnoses on the Treasure Coast. He also knows he may not live long enough to get an answer. It might take them years to even figure out what the hell’s going on around here, Elliott said. I can’t expect myself to be around at the end of it. Lucie County have raised similar questions for years, pointing to diagnoses just houses apart and, in some cases, among unrelated residents of the same home decades apart. In June, I-Team reporter Katie Bente revisited families’ search for answers. In this second part of her investigation, Bente went street by street with a widow tracking the diagnoses and pressing health officials for updated findings. A few houses apart For Stephanie Ankiel , one stop on the drive through Fort Pierce brings the questions back to her own family. She pointed to her late husband’s childhood home, then another home a few houses away where she said a resident was diagnosed in 2025 with the same type of brain tumor. This is the house my late husband grew up in, Ankiel said. He was diagnosed with the same exact thing as that gentleman in 2025. Both men were initially diagnosed with oligodendroglioma, a different type of brain tumor from glioblastoma . Ankiel said her husband Mark Cunningham’s cancer later progressed to glioblastoma. A few streets away, she identified another home where she said two unrelated residents developed glioblastoma decades apart. This is the house where we’ve had two glioblastoma cases, 20 years apart, no family relation, she said. Elsewhere along the route, Ankiel pointed to neighboring homes where she said a woman and an 18-year-old had been diagnosed with brain cancer. The I-Team is withholding exact addresses to protect families’ privacy. PART 1: Brain cancer diagnoses leave St. Lucie County families searching for answers, again Ankiel helps patients through the Brain Cancer Foundation of the Treasure Coast , including a child who is just 3. She has spent years mapping where patients lived and looking for possible connections. Three additional brain cancer cases were confirmed in August alone in the areas families are tracking. Those diagnoses and the proximity of patients’ homes do not establish a cancer cluster or a common cause. But Ankiel wants officials to examine the range of brain cancers represented on her map, beyond glioblastoma alone. Regardless if it’s Glio at this point, we have too much brain cancer in this area. CDC guidance allows consideration of different cancer types when evidence suggests shared causes or exposures. No such connection has been established among the cases families are tracking. What the state studied and what is new The Florida Department of Health’s 2019 review examined glioblastoma diagnoses from 1998 through 2017 in ZIP codes 34952, 34982 and 34983. It found no statistically significant increase and did not designate a cancer cluster. That review did not include later diagnoses and focused on glioblastoma rather than the range of brain tumors represented on Ankiel’s map. Her husband’s initial diagnosis is one reason she wants officials to examine that broader picture. The I-Team asked whether the department had analyzed cases diagnosed since 2017 and what would trigger new environmental testing. Lucie County Health Officer Clint Sperber said officials have been reviewing cancer registry data and environmental influences. Our latest analysis, which includes data through 2023, shows no indication of higher rates in St. Lucie County or in the specific zip codes people have asked about, Sperber wrote. Lucie’s rates are in line with nearby counties and with the state as a whole. The updated report was not available when he responded. Sperber said officials were finishing a summary to release online. His response did not explain how the analysis handled tumors initially classified as another type and later diagnosed as glioblastoma, or whether other brain cancers were examined separately. It also did not specify what would trigger additional environmental testing. No environmental factor questioned by families has been established as a cause of these cancers. A call for another look Rep. Brian Mast said he has again asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to examine the concerns and provide the data behind its conclusions. You need to give us the receipts, Mast said. Give us the data of where these took place, how many of them took place. The CDC said state and local health departments lead examinations of unusual cancer patterns. It confirmed that it assisted Florida’s investigation in 2018, but did not specifically address whether it had received Mast’s latest request or would open a new review. In a statement to the I-Team, a CDC spokesperson said: CDC is prepared to provide additional assistance upon the Florida Department of Health’s request. Making the most of the time left Elliott was diagnosed this year with glioblastoma, an aggressive, fast-growing grade 4 brain cancer. The former bar manager described struggling to speak after surgery and initially believing his diagnosis was an isolated case. Meeting other local patients changed that. I thought I was the only one, he said. He has decided not to continue treatment, choosing to spend his remaining time with friends and family, going to the beach and swimming. While he wants investigators to find answers, he is focused on the life he still has. I’m not going to be that person that lives to be 65, 70, 80 years old, Elliott said. But I get to hang out with my friends. I get to go take a swim, have some fun.

entry.title: Fort Pierce man faces aggravated assault charge after incident involving U-Haul - WPBF
entry.summary: Fort Pierce man faces aggravated assault charge after incident involving U-Haul    WPBF
entry.article_text: A Fort Pierce man is facing an aggravated assault charge after two tow trucks were hit with a U-Haul truck. On Thursday, Fort Pierce Police officers responded to the 5400 block of Jamboree Drive, east of Interstate 95, regarding a report of a U-Haul box truck crashing into two vehicles. Officers learned that the U-Haul had been parked in violation of homeowner association restrictions, and the contracted tow company was attempting to remove it. During the tow attempt, the person intervened, police said. A second tow truck was positioned behind the U-Haul to prevent it from leaving. After the person refused to pay a drop fee, he entered the U-Haul, backed off the tow truck and struck the tow truck parked behind him, police said. He then continued to drive forward and reverse repeatedly until he freed the U-Haul from between the two vehicles, police said. The person drove down the street, where responding officers located him shortly afterward. No injuries were reported. The U-Haul was towed and the man was taken to the St. Police didn't identify him. entry.title: Is it legal? Trump promises Medicare and ACA checks without Congress ahead of midterm elections
entry.summary: President Trump announced that more than 20 million seniors on Medicare will soon receive a direct deposit of nearly $100, drawing Democratic criticism and questions about whether the payments made without congressional approval are legal. 'I am pleased to announce over 20 million seniors on Medicare will still be receiving a deposit of nearly $100 directly into their bank accounts,' Trump said. RELATED STORY | Trump announces $500 refunds for nearly 1 million 'Obamacare' enrollees Trump said the money will come from the Medicare Improvement Fund. A White House fact sheet says most eligible seniors will receive $90 via direct deposit in early October. Those without direct deposit will receive a check. The Medicare payment is not the only check the administration is cutting. Last month, Trump announced refunds to some people enrolled in Affordable Care Act health plans, saying they had been previously overcharged. 'Nearly 1 million hardworking Americans in 30 states will soon be getting refunds of $500 each,' Trump said. On the campaign trail, Trump has also promised more money if Republicans win in the November midterm elections. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | $5K reality check: Experts say Trump's promise of midterm checks would strain the economy So far, no legal challenge has resulted in a court blocking either the $500 ACA refunds or the $90 Medicare payments, though Democrats have been sharply critical of both. 'If you want to BUY midterm votes, maybe start by not gutting everyone's health care in the first place,' Oregon Sen. Ron Wyden said, referring to the $500 ACA checks. Also drawing scrutiny on Capitol Hill is Trump's use of taxpayer dollars to pay for commercials this campaign season. The White House says the spending is legal, but others disagree. Complaints have been filed with the FCC and broadcasters, though no judge has yet blocked the commercials from airing.

entry.title: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County
entry.summary: A 17-year-old died after being shot near a boat ramp in Indian River County late Friday night, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near Garcia's Boat Ramp, at approximately 11:24 p.m. WATCH: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County The sheriff's office said deputies found the 17-year-old and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he died from his injuries. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. Investigators said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public. No information about a possible suspect or what led up to the shooting has been released. Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: Back to Basics Angel Program seeks help to provide holiday gifts for 10,000 Palm Beach County children
entry.summary: While many people are just beginning to think about the holidays, volunteers with Back to Basics are already hard at work making sure thousands of Palm Beach County children have gifts to open this Christmas. The nonprofit's annual Angel Program provides new sneakers, socks, underwear, and a toy to children in need throughout the county. Each year, the organization serves more than 10,000 children through the effort. Sign Up For An Angel . 'We work directly with the schools to provide gifts for kids in need throughout Palm Beach County,' said Kelly Enriquez, executive director for Back to Basics. 'We provide new sneakers, socks, underwear, and a toy for all of them.' Because of the large number of children served, preparations begin months before the holiday season arrives. Some gifts are already being sorted and wrapped as volunteers work to get ahead of the demand. 'The biggest part of our program is we can depend on the community to adopt these children,' Kelly said. 'About 7,000 will go out to the community each year and the rest of them we do in-house.' The organization is encouraging local residents, businesses and civic groups to participate by adopting children, donating gifts or volunteering their time. Back to Basics is also celebrating another successful community initiative. The nonprofit recently completed its annual school uniform drive, which provided approximately 20,000 uniforms to students at more than 60 elementary and middle schools throughout Palm Beach County. 'We serve over 60 schools here in Palm Beach County,' said board member Mike O'Dell. 'Many of the children who go to school are required to have uniforms, and they just don't have the financial wherewithal to do that.' Volunteers say community support is essential to the success of both programs and helps ensure local children have the resources they need to thrive both in school and during the holiday season. 'You're helping those in need, and this is a great way to have your children learn the generosity and the joy of giving,' Santa Claus joked during WPTV's Shining A Light visit. As the holiday season approaches, Back to Basics hopes more people will step forward to help make Christmas brighter for thousands of Palm Beach County children.

entry.title: Flood safety tips shared as Indiantown residents prepare for more rain - WPEC
entry.summary: Flood safety tips shared as Indiantown residents prepare for more rain    WPEC
entry.article_text: Indiantown residents remain concerned about flooding after heavy rain left streets covered in water last week, with more rain and storms in the forecast for this week. CBS12 crews captured video of vehicles driving through standing water on roadways in parts of the village. Residents say flooding can quickly become expensive when water affects homes and property. The sad part is, if you don’t have insurance or anything like that you’re just stuck, your stuck with the bill, said Mary Brown, a Booker Park resident. The flooding has renewed questions about the more than $2 million drainage and roadway project in Booker Park. The project began in 2022 to help reduce flooding, but residents say heavy rain is still leaving some streets underwater. Village leaders have said they are working with Martin County on longer-term drainage solutions, including the possible repair or replacement of broken pipes. The next Indiantown Village Council meeting is Thursday night. With more rain possible this week, Martin County Fire Rescue and the Florida Department of Health in Martin County have tips available online for residents to plan ahead and avoid driving or walking through floodwater. You can CLICK HERE to view the entire list. Officials say water on a roadway may be deeper or more contaminated than it appears. Drivers who encounter a flooded road should turn around rather than attempt to drive through it. Martin County Fire Rescue responds to flooding-related emergencies, including when a vehicle becomes stuck in floodwater. Residents should call 911 during an emergency. For ongoing drainage problems or flooded roadways, residents can submit a report through Martin County’s online Request for Service system . The county asks residents to include the specific address or location and details about the issue, such as standing water, a blockage or a low spot near a drainage structure. CLICK HERE to submit a request. Health officials also advise residents whose wells flood to use bottled or boiled water until the well can be tested.

entry.title: I-TEAM: A widow maps brain cancer cases in St. Lucie County — some just doors apart - WPEC
entry.summary: I-TEAM: A widow maps brain cancer cases in St. Lucie County — some just doors apart    WPEC
entry.article_text: Matt Elliott wants to know whether his brain cancer could be connected to other diagnoses on the Treasure Coast. He also knows he may not live long enough to get an answer. It might take them years to even figure out what the hell’s going on around here, Elliott said. I can’t expect myself to be around at the end of it. Lucie County have raised similar questions for years, pointing to diagnoses just houses apart and, in some cases, among unrelated residents of the same home decades apart. In June, I-Team reporter Katie Bente revisited families’ search for answers. In this second part of her investigation, Bente went street by street with a widow tracking the diagnoses and pressing health officials for updated findings. A few houses apart For Stephanie Ankiel , one stop on the drive through Fort Pierce brings the questions back to her own family. She pointed to her late husband’s childhood home, then another home a few houses away where she said a resident was diagnosed in 2025 with the same type of brain tumor. This is the house my late husband grew up in, Ankiel said. He was diagnosed with the same exact thing as that gentleman in 2025. Both men were initially diagnosed with oligodendroglioma, a different type of brain tumor from glioblastoma . Ankiel said her husband Mark Cunningham’s cancer later progressed to glioblastoma. A few streets away, she identified another home where she said two unrelated residents developed glioblastoma decades apart. This is the house where we’ve had two glioblastoma cases, 20 years apart, no family relation, she said. Elsewhere along the route, Ankiel pointed to neighboring homes where she said a woman and an 18-year-old had been diagnosed with brain cancer. The I-Team is withholding exact addresses to protect families’ privacy. PART 1: Brain cancer diagnoses leave St. Lucie County families searching for answers, again Ankiel helps patients through the Brain Cancer Foundation of the Treasure Coast , including a child who is just 3. She has spent years mapping where patients lived and looking for possible connections. Three additional brain cancer cases were confirmed in August alone in the areas families are tracking. Those diagnoses and the proximity of patients’ homes do not establish a cancer cluster or a common cause. But Ankiel wants officials to examine the range of brain cancers represented on her map, beyond glioblastoma alone. Regardless if it’s Glio at this point, we have too much brain cancer in this area. CDC guidance allows consideration of different cancer types when evidence suggests shared causes or exposures. No such connection has been established among the cases families are tracking. What the state studied and what is new The Florida Department of Health’s 2019 review examined glioblastoma diagnoses from 1998 through 2017 in ZIP codes 34952, 34982 and 34983. It found no statistically significant increase and did not designate a cancer cluster. That review did not include later diagnoses and focused on glioblastoma rather than the range of brain tumors represented on Ankiel’s map. Her husband’s initial diagnosis is one reason she wants officials to examine that broader picture. The I-Team asked whether the department had analyzed cases diagnosed since 2017 and what would trigger new environmental testing. Lucie County Health Officer Clint Sperber said officials have been reviewing cancer registry data and environmental influences. Our latest analysis, which includes data through 2023, shows no indication of higher rates in St. Lucie County or in the specific zip codes people have asked about, Sperber wrote. Lucie’s rates are in line with nearby counties and with the state as a whole. The updated report was not available when he responded. Sperber said officials were finishing a summary to release online. His response did not explain how the analysis handled tumors initially classified as another type and later diagnosed as glioblastoma, or whether other brain cancers were examined separately. It also did not specify what would trigger additional environmental testing. No environmental factor questioned by families has been established as a cause of these cancers. A call for another look Rep. Brian Mast said he has again asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to examine the concerns and provide the data behind its conclusions. You need to give us the receipts, Mast said. Give us the data of where these took place, how many of them took place. The CDC said state and local health departments lead examinations of unusual cancer patterns. It confirmed that it assisted Florida’s investigation in 2018, but did not specifically address whether it had received Mast’s latest request or would open a new review. In a statement to the I-Team, a CDC spokesperson said: CDC is prepared to provide additional assistance upon the Florida Department of Health’s request. Making the most of the time left Elliott was diagnosed this year with glioblastoma, an aggressive, fast-growing grade 4 brain cancer. The former bar manager described struggling to speak after surgery and initially believing his diagnosis was an isolated case. Meeting other local patients changed that. I thought I was the only one, he said. He has decided not to continue treatment, choosing to spend his remaining time with friends and family, going to the beach and swimming. While he wants investigators to find answers, he is focused on the life he still has. I’m not going to be that person that lives to be 65, 70, 80 years old, Elliott said. But I get to hang out with my friends. I get to go take a swim, have some fun.

entry.title: Wrong-way driver arrested, faces DUI manslaughter charge after deadly I-95 crash
entry.summary: A wrong-way driver sparked a deadly three-vehicle crash early Sunday morning on I-95 in West Palm Beach, killing one person and seriously injuring two others, according to the Florida Highway Patrol (FHP). The crash happened around 5:30 a.m. Sunday on the northbound lanes of I-95 near Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard. Investigators say a GMC Sierra pickup truck was traveling south in the inside lane of northbound I-95, driving the wrong way as it approached Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard. A Palm Beach County Sheriff's deputy spotted the vehicle traveling the wrong way and paced it at about 60 to 65 mph before losing sight of it shortly before the crash. A Dodge Grand Caravan was traveling north in the inside lane when its driver, later identified as Angelo Genova, 68, of West Palm Beach, attempted to swerve right to avoid the oncoming pickup but was unable to avoid a collision. Following the initial impact, the pickup rotated and came to rest in the inside northbound lane. The van spun across the roadway from west to east. A Cadillac El Dorado was traveling north behind the van and was unable to avoid the wreckage. The Cadillac then struck the rear of the van, according to FHP. Genova was pronounced dead at the scene. The wrong-way driver, identified in an arrest report as Edwin Castro, 26, of West Palm Beach, and the Cadillac driver suffered serious injuries and were transported to St. Mary's Medical Center for treatment. FHP said the driver of the Cadallic suffered incapacitating injuries. According to the arrest report, deputies and troopers observed that Castro showed signs of impairment after the crash, including a strong odor of alcohol, bloodshot eyes and slurred speech. Hospital toxicology results showed Castro's blood alcohol level was 0.239, nearly three times Florida's legal limit of 0.08, investigators said. Castro was arrested and charged with DUI causing death, vehicular homicide, DUI causing serious bodily injury, reckless driving causing serious bodily injury, two counts of DUI causing property damage or injury and two counts of reckless driving causing property damage or injury. He was also cited for driving the wrong way on the interstate. The arrest report also states that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement told investigators that Castro had a final order of removal after a denied asylum claim from Guatemala. entry.title: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says - WPBF
entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two women are in custody in Martin County after a shooting at a tow yard led to a police chase and a violent crash Friday afternoon. “I have more questions than I have answers,” Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek said the incident began around 1 p.m. when two women arrived at Gary’s Towing and Recovery, 4405 SE Cove Road, near Stuart, to retrieve a car that had been towed earlier that morning. While they were there, two other individuals showed up to claim the same vehicle. “They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car, which, by the way, the only thing in the car really was a couple of guns,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said one of the original women then grabbed a gun and began shooting. No one was injured, but bullets struck trailers in the yard. “It’s just crazy how it went down,” said Gary Reed, the owner of Gary’s Towing and Recovery. Reed, who was not present during the shooting, said his employee called him, screaming for help. And I’m running as fast as I can,” Reed said. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl By the time deputies and Reed arrived at the scene, all four individuals involved had fled. The sheriff said the accused shooter had taken the car they were disputing, but deputies located her shortly later on Cove Road near U.S. She attempted to flee but was quickly arrested. Investigators identified her as Jade Rondon, 23, from Miami. The other woman she was with has been identified as Valerie Valdes, 22, also from Miami. Budensiek said she was taken into custody after causing a violent collision on U.S. “Why she was driving at a high rate of speed, why she was weaving out of traffic, we’re not sure. We didn’t even know for sure that that car was involved at that time,” Budensiek said. The sheriff said investigators are working to answer these questions and plan to obtain search warrants for the suspects’ cars and phones. He hopes to have more answers by next week. Rondon already is facing two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, felony criminal mischief. Valdes has been cited for operating an unregistered motor vehicle and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. Because the incident was a half-mile from Murray Middle School, MCSO activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout. entry.article_text: The man accused of crossing state lines and traveling to Indian River County to kill his ex-girlfriend was booked into the Indian River County Jail on Monday. According to Indian River County Jail records, Matthew Waggle, 33, was booked into the Indian River County Jail at around 5:20 a.m. He faces a charge of first-degree murder. CBS12 reported on the August shooting after authorities found the victim's body, identified as Dawn Kriskewic , in a roadway in the southern part of the county. Investigators say Waggle traveled to Vero Beach by bus and Uber before allegedly killing Kriskewic outside her home Sunday morning. See also: FHP: Wrong-way driver caused deadly I-95 crash Sunday near PB Lakes Boulevard Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said surveillance video captured Waggle walking through Kriskewic's neighborhood shortly after an Uber dropped him off. Investigators say Waggle then left the area, taking an Uber back to Orlando before boarding another Greyhound bus. He eventually made his way to West Virginia, where investigators say he hid at a motel. Flowers said at the time that Flock Safety cameras were instrumental in tracking down Waggle. Authorities had later tracked Waggle to a motel in West Virginia and taken him into custody. Authorities said Kriskewic had ended her relationship with Waggle before the shooting and had warned coworkers at the hair salon that she wanted no contact with him.

entry.title: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County - WFLX
entry.summary: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County    WFLX
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old died after being shot near a boat ramp in Indian River County late Friday night, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near Garcia's Boat Ramp, at approximately 11:24 p.m. WATCH: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp The sheriff's office said deputies found the 17-year-old and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he died from his injuries. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. Investigators said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public. No information about a possible suspect or what led up to the shooting has been released. Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys & Girls Clubs of America
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys Girls Clubs of America. Enrique Rosario Liz has been named the organizations 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, a recognition that celebrates outstanding leadership, academic achievement and service to others. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys Girls Clubs of America The honor marks the latest milestone in a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, advancing to the national level of competition. In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the exciting news during a special presentation. Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: 2 killed, including a high school student, in Florida school bus crash, sheriff says
entry.summary: A 10th-grade student and another person were killed after a multi-vehicle crash involving a school bus happened Monday morning in Central Florida. Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said during a morning news conference that the crash happened around 6 a.m., when a Chevrolet Malibu veered over the center line of a road and hit a Winter Haven High School bus traveling in the opposite direction. There were 37 students on board. The impact of the collision ripped the tire off the bus and caused it to crash head-on into an oncoming Jeep before rolling over off the side of Winter Haven Road. The sheriff said the driver of the Jeep had died. At least five other people involved in the crash were hospitalized, according to authorities. 'It was a horrible crash,' Judd said. 'It was a terrible, tragic morning. We had a beautiful 10th grade girl lose her life.' The city of Winter Haven is located about 51 miles east of Tampa and 47 miles southwest of Orlando. This story was originally published by Leilyn Torres and Anthony Romano with the Scripps News Group in Tampa.

entry.title: I-TEAM: A widow maps brain cancer cases in St. Lucie County - some just doors apart - WPEC
entry.summary: I-TEAM: A widow maps brain cancer cases in St. Lucie County - some just doors apart    WPEC
entry.article_text: Matt Elliott wants to know whether his brain cancer could be connected to other diagnoses on the Treasure Coast. He also knows he may not live long enough to get an answer. It might take them years to even figure out what the hell’s going on around here, Elliott said. I can’t expect myself to be around at the end of it. Lucie County have raised similar questions for years, pointing to diagnoses just houses apart and, in some cases, among unrelated residents of the same home decades apart. In June, I-Team reporter Katie Bente revisited families’ search for answers. In this second part of her investigation, Bente went street by street with a widow tracking the diagnoses and pressing health officials for updated findings. A few houses apart For Stephanie Ankiel , one stop on the drive through Fort Pierce brings the questions back to her own family. She pointed to her late husband’s childhood home, then another home a few houses away where she said a resident was diagnosed in 2025 with the same type of brain tumor. This is the house my late husband grew up in, Ankiel said. He was diagnosed with the same exact thing as that gentleman in 2025. Both men were initially diagnosed with oligodendroglioma, a different type of brain tumor from glioblastoma . Ankiel said her husband Mark Cunningham’s cancer later progressed to glioblastoma. A few streets away, she identified another home where she said two unrelated residents developed glioblastoma decades apart. This is the house where we’ve had two glioblastoma cases, 20 years apart, no family relation, she said. Elsewhere along the route, Ankiel pointed to neighboring homes where she said a woman and an 18-year-old had been diagnosed with brain cancer. The I-Team is withholding exact addresses to protect families’ privacy. PART 1: Brain cancer diagnoses leave St. Lucie County families searching for answers, again Ankiel helps patients through the Brain Cancer Foundation of the Treasure Coast , including a child who is just 3. She has spent years mapping where patients lived and looking for possible connections. Three additional brain cancer cases were confirmed in August alone in the areas families are tracking. Those diagnoses and the proximity of patients’ homes do not establish a cancer cluster or a common cause. But Ankiel wants officials to examine the range of brain cancers represented on her map, beyond glioblastoma alone. Regardless if it’s Glio at this point, we have too much brain cancer in this area. CDC guidance allows consideration of different cancer types when evidence suggests shared causes or exposures. No such connection has been established among the cases families are tracking. What the state studied and what is new The Florida Department of Health’s 2019 review examined glioblastoma diagnoses from 1998 through 2017 in ZIP codes 34952, 34982 and 34983. It found no statistically significant increase and did not designate a cancer cluster. That review did not include later diagnoses and focused on glioblastoma rather than the range of brain tumors represented on Ankiel’s map. Her husband’s initial diagnosis is one reason she wants officials to examine that broader picture. The I-Team asked whether the department had analyzed cases diagnosed since 2017 and what would trigger new environmental testing. Lucie County Health Officer Clint Sperber said officials have been reviewing cancer registry data and environmental influences. Our latest analysis, which includes data through 2023, shows no indication of higher rates in St. Lucie County or in the specific zip codes people have asked about, Sperber wrote. Lucie’s rates are in line with nearby counties and with the state as a whole. The updated report was not available when he responded. Sperber said officials were finishing a summary to release online. His response did not explain how the analysis handled tumors initially classified as another type and later diagnosed as glioblastoma, or whether other brain cancers were examined separately. It also did not specify what would trigger additional environmental testing. No environmental factor questioned by families has been established as a cause of these cancers. A call for another look Rep. Brian Mast said he has again asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to examine the concerns and provide the data behind its conclusions. You need to give us the receipts, Mast said. Give us the data of where these took place, how many of them took place. The CDC said state and local health departments lead examinations of unusual cancer patterns. It confirmed that it assisted Florida’s investigation in 2018, but did not specifically address whether it had received Mast’s latest request or would open a new review. In a statement to the I-Team, a CDC spokesperson said: CDC is prepared to provide additional assistance upon the Florida Department of Health’s request. Making the most of the time left Elliott was diagnosed this year with glioblastoma, an aggressive, fast-growing grade 4 brain cancer. The former bar manager described struggling to speak after surgery and initially believing his diagnosis was an isolated case. Meeting other local patients changed that. I thought I was the only one, he said. He has decided not to continue treatment, choosing to spend his remaining time with friends and family, going to the beach and swimming. While he wants investigators to find answers, he is focused on the life he still has. I’m not going to be that person that lives to be 65, 70, 80 years old, Elliott said. But I get to hang out with my friends. I get to go take a swim, have some fun.

entry.title: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain - WPBF
entry.summary: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie County mosquito control are working to stop mosquitoes from breeding after recent rain created standing water. In a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 and Fort Pierce, mosquito control teams treated swales and used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide. Officials said the rain has increased standing water, which allows mosquito eggs to hatch. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment’s notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," said Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control. DENGUE FEVER: Dengue fever case in Palm Beach County prompts mosquito control action Kenneth Fusco, a nearby resident, shared his experience with the mosquito problem. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He added, "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!" Crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. They are asking residents to empty or remove containers holding water to prevent mosquito breeding. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project designed to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. More rain is expected, which could lead to additional standing water and, Tuzzolino said, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" If you are dealing with a mosquito problem near your home, contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org.
