entry.title: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected - WFLX
entry.summary: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected    WFLX
entry.article_text: No arrests have been made in the shooting death of a 17-year-old at a teen meetup near Garcia’s Boat Ramp in Indian River County, with a self-defense claim expected in the case, Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Monday. “We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media,” Flowers said. The shooting occurred late Friday night when approximately 100 teens, ranging in age from 14 to 19, gathered at Garcia’s Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512, the sheriff said. Deputies had broken up a similar group earlier that evening before the crowd moved to the boat ramp. “The 17-year-old, and a group of his friends, are approaching a truck, and there are two people, both 18 years old, inside of that truck. The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch,” Flowers said. “He’s going to punch on the people that are inside of that truck. That shot is the shot that ultimately killed 17-year-old in this case.” The teen’s friends drove him away from the scene, east on County Road 512, while calling 911 and a dispatcher told them to stop at Fellsmere City Hall, where emergency crews performed CPR, the sheriff said. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries. The two individuals in the truck were identified using the sheriff’s office’s Flock technology, the sheriff said. Flowers said both have been cooperative with investigators, surrendering the weapon used in the shooting and the truck. Additional individuals involved in the incident have also been identified through Flock, though some remain unidentified. Investigators also recovered other weapons from the vehicle in which the 17-year-old was transported from the scene. Flowers said a warrant will be submitted in the case, but it will be up to the state to determine whether charges are filed. “There have been no arrests on this case at this time, because the preliminary investigation shows that the 17-year-old was opening the door to attempt to fight with the two that were inside of the vehicle. They had a history of fighting,” Flowers said. “Self defense plays a part in these, and when these kids go out and videotape these fights, and now guns are involved, there’s going to be more of this.” Names of those involved are not being released as the investigation continues, the sheriff said. Investigators believe at least four fights occurred at the boat ramp on the night of the shooting. Multiple shell casings and rounds were recovered from the scene. During Monday’s news conference, Flowers released video of the shooting, noting the footage had already circulated widely on social media and that the victim’s mother had seen it. One of the 18-year-olds involved in the shooting attends Vero Beach High School. The sheriff said teen meetups like the one at Garcia’s Boat Ramp are coordinated through Snapchat, making them difficult for law enforcement to track in advance. “When it’s Snapchat, it’s basically a private conversation,” Flowers said. “But it quickly can escalate to over 100, 150, 200 people there.” Flowers said the meetups, which have included alcohol, fighting, and firearms, have been taking place for years across Indian River County, Okeechobee, and surrounding areas, but that social media has intensified the danger. “Now we’re adding guns and alcohol into the mix, and we’re adding social media into the mix, and so what we’re seeing is an escalation of each one of these,” Flowers said. There’s guns, and those two just don’t mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead.” The sheriff said teens at these gatherings are motivated in part by a desire for online attention. “The kids like to fight, and they like to videotape it, and they like to get their likes and shares because of that,” Flowers said. Parents, you see these videos. You do not want your teens out at these meetups." With Vero Beach High School’s homecoming game scheduled for Friday and the dance on Saturday, Flowers said additional deputies will be on duty. Meanwhile, the sheriff urged parents to monitor their children’s whereabouts and report any information about planned meetups to the sheriff’s office. “Parents, if your kids are telling you that they’re headed out to one of these meetups, ask them where they’re going. Ask, find out the details. Share that with us,” Flowers said. He recommended parents use location-sharing apps such as Life360 to track their children and said a child appearing to be in a remote or unusual location can be an indicator that a meetup is taking place. The investigation remains active. Flowers said anyone who witnessed any of the events that night, including the shooting itself, and has not yet spoken to investigators is urged to come forward. “I can tell you, our investigation is not even remotely over, and if we are able to identify people that were involved in this, from underage drinking to fighting, hurting other people,” Flowers said. " If they did something wrong, they’re going to have to be accountable for that." Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

This order will allow the Florida Division of Emergency Management to stage critical preparedness resources and ensure Florida is ready to respond, DeSantis said. The governor urged Floridians to make disaster plans and check hurricane supplies. The current forecast indicates a tropical storm or hurricane could make landfall somewhere along the central Gulf Coast later this week, the governor said in a Tuesday statement. 'Impacts are expected to extend beyond the point of landfall, with heavy rainfall, strong winds, coastal flooding and isolated tornadoes possible across North Florida,' the statement said. 'Additional precipitation could further saturate soils and increase the potential for flash flooding following the states recent significant rainfall.'

entry.title: Port St. Lucie streets flood after downpour, stranding vehicles and disrupting commutes - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie streets flood after downpour, stranding vehicles and disrupting commutes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Heavy rain flooded roads across Port St. Lucie Tuesday afternoon, leaving some vehicles stranded, forcing children to walk through standing water after school and prompting a response from police officers and city crews. According to the City of Port St. Lucie , a large amount of rain fell in a short period of time, leading to temporary road closures and flooding in multiple areas. Public Works crews responded to flooding near Savona Boulevard and California Boulevard, closing the roadway until it was safe for travel. The city also reported high-water conditions near Thornhill Drive and Floresta Drive, where Phase 3 construction is underway. On Southwest Thornhill Drive, school buses continued dropping off students despite flooded streets. CBS12 News saw children step off buses carrying their shoes and walk barefoot through standing water to reach home. Along Southwest Broadview Avenue near Crosstown Parkway, residents watched as water spilled across the roadway, making it difficult for drivers to tell where the street ended and floodwater began. "If you didn't see the grass here, you wouldn't know where the road is," resident Kevin Burke told CBS12 News. "It was steady sheets of rain for a good hour. Non-stop, and I mean heavy, heavy." Police officers directed traffic while Public Works crews set up barricades and monitored conditions during the evening commute. Burke said flooding in the area has become a familiar problem during heavy downpours. "When it rains heavy like it did today, it's like this all the time, from that canal coming up," he said. Burke said standing water presents concerns beyond traffic issues. "We have a pond over there by Crosstown and Bayshore. It's got signs all around it saying there are gators in it. It's a long shot, but it could happen, and that's what worries me, with kids and the animals," he said. For some residents, the flooding disrupted everyday tasks. "She has her elderly brother, who's 83 years old, and she's in her 60s, and she was going to run out and get Chinese food, and now she's still sitting here waiting because she can't get to it," Burke said. Earlier in the day, Port St. Lucie police reported flooding at several intersections, including SE Evans Avenue and SE Airoso Boulevard, SE Eyerly Avenue and SE Airoso Boulevard, SW Bayshore Boulevard and SW Thornhill Drive, and NE Floresta Drive and NE Ardsley Drive. See also: Opponents, supporters clash over Palm Beach County Israel Bonds investments City officials said Public Works crews continued monitoring conditions as water slowly receded Tuesday evening. Officials also reminded residents not to walk or drive through flooded roadways because it can be difficult to determine how deep the water is.

entry.title: I-TEAM: A widow maps brain cancer cases in St. Lucie County - some just doors apart - WPEC
entry.summary: I-TEAM: A widow maps brain cancer cases in St. Lucie County - some just doors apart    WPEC
entry.article_text: Matt Elliott wants to know whether his brain cancer could be connected to other diagnoses on the Treasure Coast. He also knows he may not live long enough to get an answer. It might take them years to even figure out what the hell’s going on around here, Elliott said. I can’t expect myself to be around at the end of it. Lucie County have raised similar questions for years, pointing to diagnoses just houses apart and, in some cases, among unrelated residents of the same home decades apart. In June, I-Team reporter Katie Bente revisited families’ search for answers. In this second part of her investigation, Bente went street by street with a widow tracking the diagnoses and pressing health officials for updated findings. A few houses apart For Stephanie Ankiel , one stop on the drive through Fort Pierce brings the questions back to her own family. She pointed to her late husband’s childhood home, then another home a few houses away where she said a resident was diagnosed in 2025 with the same type of brain tumor. This is the house my late husband grew up in, Ankiel said. He was diagnosed with the same exact thing as that gentleman in 2025. Both men were initially diagnosed with oligodendroglioma, a different type of brain tumor from glioblastoma . Ankiel said her husband Mark Cunningham’s cancer later progressed to glioblastoma. A few streets away, she identified another home where she said two unrelated residents developed glioblastoma decades apart. This is the house where we’ve had two glioblastoma cases, 20 years apart, no family relation, she said. Elsewhere along the route, Ankiel pointed to neighboring homes where she said a woman and an 18-year-old had been diagnosed with brain cancer. The I-Team is withholding exact addresses to protect families’ privacy. PART 1: Brain cancer diagnoses leave St. Lucie County families searching for answers, again Ankiel helps patients through the Brain Cancer Foundation of the Treasure Coast , including a child who is just 3. She has spent years mapping where patients lived and looking for possible connections. Three additional brain cancer cases were confirmed in August alone in the areas families are tracking. Those diagnoses and the proximity of patients’ homes do not establish a cancer cluster or a common cause. But Ankiel wants officials to examine the range of brain cancers represented on her map, beyond glioblastoma alone. Regardless if it’s Glio at this point, we have too much brain cancer in this area. CDC guidance allows consideration of different cancer types when evidence suggests shared causes or exposures. No such connection has been established among the cases families are tracking. What the state studied and what is new The Florida Department of Health’s 2019 review examined glioblastoma diagnoses from 1998 through 2017 in ZIP codes 34952, 34982 and 34983. It found no statistically significant increase and did not designate a cancer cluster. That review did not include later diagnoses and focused on glioblastoma rather than the range of brain tumors represented on Ankiel’s map. Her husband’s initial diagnosis is one reason she wants officials to examine that broader picture. The I-Team asked whether the department had analyzed cases diagnosed since 2017 and what would trigger new environmental testing. Lucie County Health Officer Clint Sperber said officials have been reviewing cancer registry data and environmental influences. Our latest analysis, which includes data through 2023, shows no indication of higher rates in St. Lucie County or in the specific zip codes people have asked about, Sperber wrote. Lucie’s rates are in line with nearby counties and with the state as a whole. The updated report was not available when he responded. Sperber said officials were finishing a summary to release online. His response did not explain how the analysis handled tumors initially classified as another type and later diagnosed as glioblastoma, or whether other brain cancers were examined separately. It also did not specify what would trigger additional environmental testing. No environmental factor questioned by families has been established as a cause of these cancers. A call for another look Rep. Brian Mast said he has again asked the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to examine the concerns and provide the data behind its conclusions. You need to give us the receipts, Mast said. Give us the data of where these took place, how many of them took place. The CDC said state and local health departments lead examinations of unusual cancer patterns. It confirmed that it assisted Florida’s investigation in 2018, but did not specifically address whether it had received Mast’s latest request or would open a new review. In a statement to the I-Team, a CDC spokesperson said: CDC is prepared to provide additional assistance upon the Florida Department of Health’s request. Making the most of the time left Elliott was diagnosed this year with glioblastoma, an aggressive, fast-growing grade 4 brain cancer. The former bar manager described struggling to speak after surgery and initially believing his diagnosis was an isolated case. Meeting other local patients changed that. I thought I was the only one, he said. He has decided not to continue treatment, choosing to spend his remaining time with friends and family, going to the beach and swimming. While he wants investigators to find answers, he is focused on the life he still has. I’m not going to be that person that lives to be 65, 70, 80 years old, Elliott said. But I get to hang out with my friends. I get to go take a swim, have some fun.

entry.title: Could Kansas and Florida be in play? Why the battle for Congress may be expanding
entry.summary: With less than a month until Election Day, Democrats are looking beyond the traditional battlegrounds as new signs emerge that the fight for control of Congress could be spreading into states Republicans once had little reason to worry about. Kansas and Florida are among the states receiving new attention, while President Donald Trumps own campaign schedule is taking him into reliably Republican territory. RELATED STORY | Trump holds Ohio midterm rally, urging voters to consider him on the ballot during 32-day campaign tour The shift can also be seen in campaign spending. Conservative groups have recently moved money from North Carolina, where the Senate contest was expected to be one of the years most competitive races, to Kansas as Democrats perform better in both states. Kansas has not elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century. Since Labor Day, the numbers have only gotten worse for Republicans, said Kyle Kondik, a nonpartisan election analyst with the University of Virginia Center for Politics. Florida is another state to watch. Democrats are increasingly campaigning there even though the state appeared on relatively few lists of major battlegrounds earlier this year. RELATED STORY | Trump takes midterm push to Nebraska amid economic concerns among farmers Kondik said Florida could become an important early indicator on election night if Democrats are having an especially strong showing. Thats a state that counts very quickly, Kondik said. Trump, meanwhile, campaigned this week in Nebraska, a state he carried by nearly 200,000 votes two years ago. The president frequently calls polls fake, and Kondik cautioned that the current political picture could still be affected by inaccurate polling. I am always concerned about there being some systematic polling error, he said. Republicans currently hold 218 seats in the House, while the Senate has 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats. Democrats need 51 Senate votes to hold a majority, while Republicans need 50 because the vice president breaks ties. The final weeks of the campaign will help determine whether the activity in Kansas, Florida and other states marks a genuine expansion of the political battlefield or whether the fight for Congress ultimately returns to more familiar battlegrounds.

entry.article_text: Viewer-submitted videos are showing the extent of flooding across Port St. Lucie after heavy rain covered roads and created difficult driving conditions in several neighborhoods. Mita Duran sent CBS12 News video showing vehicles moving through water-covered streets, with some appearing to get stuck. In the Bayshore Heights neighborhood, Shirley Landis recorded heavy rain falling between Burlington Street and Brisbane. Landis said a canal runs through backyards in the area. Another video from Julien Clarke showed standing water covering a neighborhood roadway. Lucie has received about 4 inches of rain over the past 48 hours, and another 2 to 4 inches could fall by the end of the week. City crews are continuing to monitor conditions as water recedes. Officials are also reminding people to avoid driving or walking through flooded roads because it can be difficult to determine how deep the water is.

entry.article_text: Lucie County Supervisor of Elections is alerting voters in precincts 39 and 52 about a temporary change in their polling location ahead of the general election, which is less than a month away. Voters in these precincts will move from the Spanish Lakes Country Club clubhouse to Lakewood Park Church, located at 5405 Turnpike Feeder Road in Fort Pierce. Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker said the move is necessary because of renovations at the clubhouse. "I encourage voters to take advantage of early voting at Lakewood Park Library, our newest early voting site, to help avoid long lines on Election Day," Walker said. entry.title: U.S Senate candidate Angie Nixon campaigns in Fort Pierce, talks economy and reproductive health - WPBF
entry.summary: U.S Senate candidate Angie Nixon campaigns in Fort Pierce, talks economy and reproductive health    WPBF
entry.article_text: Senate candidate Angie Nixon visited Fort Pierce on Tuesday to speak with voters about reproductive health care, the economy, and other issues as part of her campaign across Florida ahead of the general election. Nixon, who represents a Jacksonville-area district in the Florida House of Representatives and describes herself as a Democratic Socialist, is holding town hall meetings across the state to connect with voters. Planned Parenthood President and CEO Alexis McGill Johnson hosted the Fort Pierce town hall, focusing on reproductive freedom and Florida's maternal mortality crisis. McGill Johnson and Nixon outlined the leadership they believe Florida families need, including protecting abortion access and expanding comprehensive health care services statewide. "Representative Nixon is a true champion for reproductive freedom," McGill Johnson said. "In the Senate, she is going to stand up for affordable health care and our right to make our own decisions about our own bodies." During the event, Nixon addressed a question about a proposed Islamic center approved for construction in Palm Beach County. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "This is a country where folks should have freedom of religion," Nixon said. "I would speak out against that type of opposition and hate if it was directed at a synagogue being built, if it was directed at a church being built, if it was directed at any other spiritual facility." Nixon also discussed the state of reproductive health care in Florida and other issues raised by voters. "Gas is high, people are struggling to get to and from work, and then they can't even afford the food anymore, let alone taking their children to the movies or out to eat, that's null and void now," one voter said. Nixon won the Democratic primary in St. Lucie County with about 54% of the vote. When asked how she plans to close the gap between herself and Republican incumbent Ashley Moody, Nixon said she intends to continue engaging with voters, including those who may disagree with her. "They have someone who is going to put them first," Nixon said when asked about the message she hopes attendees took away from Tuesday's event. She added that her campaign for U.S. Senate is focused on putting money back in people's pockets. Nixon spoke with voters for about an hour. Her next stop is in the Orlando area. entry.title: Susan Collins touts independence from Trump in first Maine Senate debate
entry.summary: Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins distanced herself from President Donald Trump during her first Maine Senate debate with Democrat Troy Jackson, arguing she has maintained her political independence by repeatedly voting against Trump's agenda and saying that she's not exactly his favorite senator. Democrats are trying to flip the Maine Senate seat as they work to win control of the Senate. Trump lost the state in 2024, giving Democrats hope of defeating the five-term moderate Republican, who has been targeted by Democrats in previous elections and survived. RELATED STORY | Senate Republicans move cash from purple North Carolina to red Kansas as battle for majority shifts During the hourlong debate, Jackson focused largely on attempting to connect Collins to Trump. He kicked off the night by pointing out she cast a critical vote to confirm Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh, a Trump nominee who eventually helped overturn the constitutional right to abortion. Collins supports abortion rights and said Kavanaugh assured her it was settled law, but she has said recently that she does not regret her vote to confirm him. Would you trust her to pick the next Supreme Court justice? asked Jackson, a former state lawmaker and logger. He also repeatedly brought up her procedural vote to advance the presidents 2025 tax and spending bill though Collins ultimately broke with her party to vote against it. Collins countered that she has voted against Trump more than she did Joe Biden when the Democrat was president, and has pushed back against Trump on tariffs, immigration enforcement and the war in Iran. I voted against my party more than another other senator on either side of the aisle, Collins said. The attention on Trump comes as only 31% of U.S. adults approved of how the Republican is handling the presidency, according to a September AP-NORC poll. Thats well below where his approval stood when he took office last year. entry.title: Changing Lives Monster Dash 5K in Boca Raton supports hope, housing, mental health
entry.summary: A Boca Raton nonprofit dedicated to helping people move from homelessness to self-sufficiency is inviting the community to support its mission during the Monster Dash 5K Run for Hope on Saturday, Oct. 17. Changing Lives serves people in Boca Raton and Delray Beach by connecting them with housing resources, recovery programs, employment assistance, mentorship and other support services designed to help individuals rebuild their lives. WATCH BELOW: Monster Dash 5K to be held in Boca Raton From homelessness to hope: Monster Dash 5K to be held in Boca Raton Executive director Jerry Pagan said the organization's goal is to do more than meet immediate needs. 'Changing Lives, it's an opportunity for us to not just feed the homeless but help them to rebuild their lives from street to self-sufficiency so they can be self-supporting and be part of the community,' Pagan said. He said the organization helps restore dignity through mental health support, housing opportunities and employment programs. 'They get a second chance at life,' Pagan said. Monster Dash 5K raises funds and awareness The nonprofit's upcoming Monster Dash 5K Run for Hope will take place at Florida Atlantic University in Boca Raton. According to Changing Lives, the event will feature a 5K run and walk, a Kids Pumpkin Dash and opportunities for participants to wear Halloween costumes while supporting a meaningful cause. Director of Operations Lesly Morales said the event helps fund mental health services and increase awareness about the organization's mission. 'We're gonna have a 5K dash starting at 7:30 a.m. Families, strollers, walkers, wheelchairs, we're all welcome,' Morales said. She said proceeds support the nonprofit's mental health continuum of care program and services that help people achieve long-term stability. A success story of hope and independence One of the strongest examples of the organization's impact comes from Susana, a former client who shared her story of overcoming homelessness. 'My journey was from going striving and thriving to homelessness to finding a program called Changing Lives,' she said. entry.title: Panthers forward Brad Marchand sustains left leg injury in second period against Kings
entry.summary: Florida Panthers forward Brad Marchand sustained a left leg injury in the second period of their 2-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Tuesday night. Marchand was not on the bench for the third period, and coach Paul Maurice did not have an update on his condition afterward. 'We'll get him looked at probably Thursday,' Maurice said. Marchand was hurt after taking a stick to the face from Kings defenseman Brandt Clarke with 52.6 seconds remaining, which caused him to twist around and collide with the right post before his left leg bent back in an awkward way. Marchand was down on the ice for several minutes being examined by an athletic trainer before teammates Brady Tkachuk and Niko Mikkola helped him to the bench, with Marchand unable to put any weight on his leg. He was then helped back to the dressing room. Marchand, 38, is in his third season with the Panthers after playing his first 16 seasons with the Boston Bruins. He was traded to Florida in March 2025 and helped them win their second straight Stanley Cup that season. But the defense of those titles last season was scuttled by injuries, and now the Panthers have seen two key players injured on their four-game West Coast trip to start this season. Aleksander Barkov, one of the top two-way centers in hockey, hurt his left leg in an overtime loss at San Jose on Thursday. Maurice said earlier Tuesday that Barkov is expected to miss six to eight weeks and will not require surgery. 'I mean, we have a little experience with Sasha going down, so it wasn't quite as shocking the second time it happened,' Maurice said. 'We know we have good depth. And there's a threshold for any team, a number of injuries you just can't survive, and we passed that early last year. So, real good resolve here. The tank is deep right now. We had a big summer off, so we're strong.' Clarke received a four-minute double-minor penalty. It was the second penalty of the game for Clarke, who was called for interference against Eetu Luostarinen earlier in the period. Luostarinen was shaken up on a cross-check from Clarke, sustaining a stinger, but was able to return to the game.

entry.title: Florida captain Aleksander Barkov will not need surgery, out 6-8 weeks, Panthers say
entry.summary: Florida center Aleksander Barkov is expected to miss six to eight weeks with a left leg injury and will not require surgery, Panthers coach Paul Maurice said Tuesday. Barkov was hurt in the Panthers' overtime loss at San Jose on Thursday. It appeared his left knee not the knee that needed to be surgically rebuilt last year buckled on the play, and the Finnish captain immediately left the ice in obvious discomfort. WATCH: Barkov won't need surgery, out 6-8 weeks, Panthers say Aleksander Barkov will not need surgery, out 6-8 weeks The timetable would suggest that Barkov will probably be out somewhere between 20 and 25 games before he could return. 'Thats our best window,' Maurice said. 'Could be a little less, could be a little more. But we think six to eight (weeks) is the right rehab time.' Florida plays at Los Angeles on Tuesday to end a season-opening four-game road trip. Maurice revealed the timetable after the Panthers' morning skate in advance of that game. The Panthers placed Barkov on long-term injured reserve over the weekend, after it became clear his absence would last longer than 10 games. The Panthers weighed multiple options on how to proceed and Barkov saw team doctors Monday before a final plan was agreed upon. Barkov was injured 20 minutes into the teams first training camp practice for the 2025-26 season and missed the entire campaign, one of many injury issues that played a role in Florida going from a back-to-back Stanley Cup champion to a team that missed the playoffs. If there is a silver lining, its that Florida is well-versed in how to play without Barkov who isnt just the team captain, but is generally considered to be the teams best player. 'If he hadnt been injured last year we would have thought, Gee, six to eight weeks is a long time,' Maurice said. 'I think last year was six to eight months, so were taking it.' Over his most recent 10 seasons excluding when he missed last season Barkov had 722 points, 485 hits and 463 blocked shots. entry.title: Port St. Lucie streets flood after downpour, stranding vehicles and disrupting commutes - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie streets flood after downpour, stranding vehicles and disrupting commutes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Heavy rain flooded roads across Port St. Lucie Tuesday afternoon, leaving some vehicles stranded, forcing children to walk through standing water after school and prompting a response from police officers and city crews. According to the City of Port St. Lucie , a large amount of rain fell in a short period of time, leading to temporary road closures and flooding in multiple areas. Public Works crews responded to flooding near Savona Boulevard and California Boulevard, closing the roadway until it was safe for travel. The city also reported high-water conditions near Thornhill Drive and Floresta Drive, where Phase 3 construction is underway. On Southwest Thornhill Drive, school buses continued dropping off students despite flooded streets. CBS12 News saw children step off buses carrying their shoes and walk barefoot through standing water to reach home. Along Southwest Broadview Avenue near Crosstown Parkway, residents watched as water spilled across the roadway, making it difficult for drivers to tell where the street ended and floodwater began. "If you didn't see the grass here, you wouldn't know where the road is," resident Kevin Burke told CBS12 News. "It was steady sheets of rain for a good hour. Non-stop, and I mean heavy, heavy." Police officers directed traffic while Public Works crews set up barricades and monitored conditions during the evening commute. Burke said flooding in the area has become a familiar problem during heavy downpours. "When it rains heavy like it did today, it's like this all the time, from that canal coming up," he said. Burke said standing water presents concerns beyond traffic issues. "We have a pond over there by Crosstown and Bayshore. It's got signs all around it saying there are gators in it. It's a long shot, but it could happen, and that's what worries me, with kids and the animals," he said. For some residents, the flooding disrupted everyday tasks. "She has her elderly brother, who's 83 years old, and she's in her 60s, and she was going to run out and get Chinese food, and now she's still sitting here waiting because she can't get to it," Burke said. Earlier in the day, Port St. Lucie police reported flooding at several intersections, including SE Evans Avenue and SE Airoso Boulevard, SE Eyerly Avenue and SE Airoso Boulevard, SW Bayshore Boulevard and SW Thornhill Drive, and NE Floresta Drive and NE Ardsley Drive. See also: Opponents, supporters clash over Palm Beach County Israel Bonds investments City officials said Public Works crews continued monitoring conditions as water slowly receded Tuesday evening. Officials also reminded residents not to walk or drive through flooded roadways because it can be difficult to determine how deep the water is.

entry.title: UF study finds dengue-linked mosquito common in Indian River County yards - WPEC
entry.summary: UF study finds dengue-linked mosquito common in Indian River County yards    WPEC
entry.article_text: Florida has reported nearly 500 dengue cases this year, including more than 250 infections acquired within the state, as new University of Florida research points to residential yards in Indian River County as a key place to understand mosquito-bite exposure. The Florida Department of Health’s latest weekly surveillance report , covering Sept. 20-26, lists 252 locally acquired dengue cases and 245 travel-associated cases statewide 497 total. The locally acquired cases were reported in Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco, Pinellas and Polk counties. Palm Beach County had one locally acquired case and 12 travel-associated cases; St. Lucie County had six travel-associated cases. No locally acquired dengue cases were listed for Indian River County in the report. The state’s locally acquired total includes 223 cases in Hillsborough County, the center of Florida’s outbreak. Health officials also reported 20 mosquito pools testing positive for dengue statewide. Nationally, the CDC’s most recent weekly provisional report counted 690 dengue cases among U.S. Florida accounted for 403 of those cases in the CDC reporting system, though the state’s more current surveillance report lists a higher total because reporting systems update on different schedules. Against that backdrop, researchers at UF/IFAS’ Florida Medical Entomology Laboratory in Vero Beach found a surprising mosquito pattern in suburban Indian River County. The team expected residential yards to be dominated by Aedes albopictus , also known as the Asian tiger mosquito. Instead, researchers found relatively high numbers of Aedes aegypti the yellow fever mosquito and one of the two species most closely associated with dengue transmission worldwide. The finding does not mean dengue is circulating in Indian River County . But it underscores why backyard mosquito control and personal bite prevention matter, researchers said. See also: Florida stages emergency supplies as Tropical Storm Isaias strengthens in Gulf The first-of-its-kind study paired mosquito trapping at homes with a smartphone-based Bite Diary that let residents document when and where they were bitten. Researchers collected 3,788 female mosquitoes from 78 yards. Of 70 reported bites, nearly 93% happened outdoors and nearly 74% happened at home, according to the peer-reviewed study . The number of mosquitoes trapped in a yard was not associated with the number of bites residents reported. Instead, people who spent more time outside during the evening, from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m., reported more bites. Gardening and walking dogs were among activities commonly reported when bites occurred. Dengue is spread when an infected mosquito bites a person; it does not spread directly from person to person. Symptoms can include fever, severe muscle and joint pain, rash, nausea and pain behind the eyes. People with symptoms should contact a health care provider, especially after travel to an area where dengue is common. Health officials urge residents to use EPA-registered insect repellent, wear long sleeves and pants when practical, repair window and door screens, and dump standing water from containers such as buckets, flowerpots, toys, tires and pool covers.

The president is expected to make a second stop in a matter of weeks to the border state of Texas Wednesday. It comes as the economy and immigration enforcement weigh on some Hispanic voters, but republicans maintain confidence in support. entry.title: Palm Beach County voters weigh pros and cons of Amendment 3 at WPTV town hall
entry.summary: As Florida voters prepare to decide Amendment 3 on Nov. 3, residents, elected officials and policy experts gathered in Palm Beach County to discuss how the proposed constitutional amendment could affect homeowners, local governments and public services. WATCH: WPTV Let's Hear It: Property Tax Town Hall on Amendment 3 (Part 1) WPTV Let's Hear It: Property Tax Town Hall - Part 1 The discussion took place during WPTV's 'Let's Hear It' community event and town hall at Palm Beach State College's Lake Worth Beach campus, where attendees asked questions and heard arguments from both supporters and opponents of the referendum. For many voters, the amendment could have significant financial implications. Supporters argue it would provide property tax relief for homeowners, while critics warn it could reduce funding for local services and shift key decisions to future lawmakers. WATCH: WPTV Let's Hear It: Property Tax Town Hall on Amendment 3 (Part 2) WPTV Let's Hear It: Property Tax Town Hall - Part 2Community members seek answers The evening began with WPTV's 'Let's Hear It' event, giving residents an opportunity to learn more about the amendment before voting. Rich Bartholomew, advocacy chair for the League of Women Voters, said he appreciated the effort to help residents better understand the proposal. 'I have been watching everything that WPTV has been doing on this,' Bartholomew said. 'I think this is a very important event.' Bartholomew also expressed concern that voters may not fully understand the long-term consequences of the amendment based solely on what appears on the ballot. 'There's nothing showing you on your ballot how all these things, these dominoes would fall,' he said. Supporters cite growing property tax bills Some residents in attendance said they support Amendment 3 because of rising property tax costs. John, a Palm Beach County resident, argued that continued increases in residential tax bills are becoming increasingly difficult for homeowners to manage. 'If you think about the tax we're paying now, where's it going to be in five years or 10 years at the rate we keep growing the tax on residences?' he said. 'It's unsustainable.' entry.title: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected - WFLX
entry.summary: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected    WFLX
entry.article_text: No arrests have been made in the shooting death of a 17-year-old at a teen meetup near Garcia’s Boat Ramp in Indian River County, with a self-defense claim expected in the case, Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Monday. “We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media,” Flowers said. The shooting occurred late Friday night when approximately 100 teens, ranging in age from 14 to 19, gathered at Garcia’s Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512, the sheriff said. Deputies had broken up a similar group earlier that evening before the crowd moved to the boat ramp. “The 17-year-old, and a group of his friends, are approaching a truck, and there are two people, both 18 years old, inside of that truck. The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch,” Flowers said. “He’s going to punch on the people that are inside of that truck. That shot is the shot that ultimately killed 17-year-old in this case.” The teen’s friends drove him away from the scene, east on County Road 512, while calling 911 and a dispatcher told them to stop at Fellsmere City Hall, where emergency crews performed CPR, the sheriff said. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries. The two individuals in the truck were identified using the sheriff’s office’s Flock technology, the sheriff said. Flowers said both have been cooperative with investigators, surrendering the weapon used in the shooting and the truck. Additional individuals involved in the incident have also been identified through Flock, though some remain unidentified. Investigators also recovered other weapons from the vehicle in which the 17-year-old was transported from the scene. Flowers said a warrant will be submitted in the case, but it will be up to the state to determine whether charges are filed. “There have been no arrests on this case at this time, because the preliminary investigation shows that the 17-year-old was opening the door to attempt to fight with the two that were inside of the vehicle. They had a history of fighting,” Flowers said. “Self defense plays a part in these, and when these kids go out and videotape these fights, and now guns are involved, there’s going to be more of this.” Names of those involved are not being released as the investigation continues, the sheriff said. Investigators believe at least four fights occurred at the boat ramp on the night of the shooting. Multiple shell casings and rounds were recovered from the scene. During Monday’s news conference, Flowers released video of the shooting, noting the footage had already circulated widely on social media and that the victim’s mother had seen it. One of the 18-year-olds involved in the shooting attends Vero Beach High School. The sheriff said teen meetups like the one at Garcia’s Boat Ramp are coordinated through Snapchat, making them difficult for law enforcement to track in advance. “When it’s Snapchat, it’s basically a private conversation,” Flowers said. “But it quickly can escalate to over 100, 150, 200 people there.” Flowers said the meetups, which have included alcohol, fighting, and firearms, have been taking place for years across Indian River County, Okeechobee, and surrounding areas, but that social media has intensified the danger. “Now we’re adding guns and alcohol into the mix, and we’re adding social media into the mix, and so what we’re seeing is an escalation of each one of these,” Flowers said. There’s guns, and those two just don’t mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead.” The sheriff said teens at these gatherings are motivated in part by a desire for online attention. “The kids like to fight, and they like to videotape it, and they like to get their likes and shares because of that,” Flowers said. Parents, you see these videos. You do not want your teens out at these meetups." With Vero Beach High School’s homecoming game scheduled for Friday and the dance on Saturday, Flowers said additional deputies will be on duty. Meanwhile, the sheriff urged parents to monitor their children’s whereabouts and report any information about planned meetups to the sheriff’s office. “Parents, if your kids are telling you that they’re headed out to one of these meetups, ask them where they’re going. Ask, find out the details. Share that with us,” Flowers said. He recommended parents use location-sharing apps such as Life360 to track their children and said a child appearing to be in a remote or unusual location can be an indicator that a meetup is taking place. The investigation remains active. Flowers said anyone who witnessed any of the events that night, including the shooting itself, and has not yet spoken to investigators is urged to come forward. “I can tell you, our investigation is not even remotely over, and if we are able to identify people that were involved in this, from underage drinking to fighting, hurting other people,” Flowers said. " If they did something wrong, they’re going to have to be accountable for that." Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

entry.title: Shooting death of Gabriella Hanley remains unsolved 5 years later, police seeking tips
entry.summary: Five years have passed, but the shooting death of 20-year-old Gabriella Hanley remains unsolved. No one has been charged with her death, and Port St. Lucie police are asking anyone with information to come forward. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie police investigating deadly shooting Mystery gunman fires shots into car in Port St. Lucie, killing woman On Oct. 5, 2021, at around 11:45 p.m., Port St. Lucie police said they responded to reports of multiple gunshots near Southeast Green River Parkway and Southeast Charleston Drive. Hanley was driving southbound on Southeast Green River Parkway in a black Kia Forte with her boyfriend, 21-year-old Darrick Mincey Jr., when another vehicle pulled alongside them and fired multiple rounds into their car, police said. Hanley was shot multiple times, police said. Officers and rescue personnel immediately attempted lifesaving measures, but she later died in the early morning hours on Oct. 6, 2021. Mincey was also struck by gunfire but survived. Investigators said they determined the Kia sustained 37 bullet impacts during the shooting. Numerous 9mm cartridge casings were recovered from the scene, and subsequent forensic examination determined they had been fired from two different firearms, police said. The suspect vehicle was described as a silver four-door sedan that fled southbound on Southeast Green River Parkway. In the years since Hanley's death, Port St. Lucie Police Department detectives have continued to investigate her death, conducting numerous interviews, examining forensic and digital evidence, and following up on investigative leads. As of Tuesday, no one has been charged with Hanley's death, and police continue to search for answers. If you know something about what happened to Hanley that night, no matter how insignificant you may think it is, Port St. Lucie police are asking you to come forward. You can call Port St. Lucie Police Department Major Crimes Division at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS (8477). Tips provided can remain anonymous.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie flooding problem renews focus on city's stormwater spending - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie flooding problem renews focus on city's stormwater spending    WPEC
entry.article_text: After viewer videos showed water covering roads and vehicles struggling through several Port St. Lucie neighborhoods, the city's own budget documents show where it plans to put money to reduce flooding. The city says that work is still in its early stages. Lucie has received about 4 inches of rain over the past 48 hours , and another 2 to 4 inches could fall by the end of the week. City crews are monitoring conditions as water recedes, and officials are reminding drivers and pedestrians to stay out of flooded roads because it is hard to tell how deep the water is. Frank Camarda, who has lived in the area for more than 20 years near SW California Boulevard and SW Plantation Terrace, said Tuesday night's flooding turned his street into a detour. He said drivers piled in while trying to bypass flooded roads, and he believes Savona Boulevard was also underwater. Camarda said he has not seen flooding on his own street before, but he has watched water pool near Oak Hammock a couple of times. He also said city crews used to clean the swale in front of his home about once a month, and he believes that has stopped. "I've been waiting for these guys to clean up. I haven't seen them," Camarda said. City spokesperson Scott Samples said the rain came in too fast for the system to keep up. He said the canals, swales and retention ponds were already full, which makes it harder for water to move. At one location the city monitored, he said, about two feet of water arrived in roughly 30 minutes. Samples said the water had receded from most roadways by about 8:30 p.m. Tuesday, and he described that as the stormwater system doing what it is designed to do. He said Public Works checks drainage before heavy rain and is working to keep swales, drains and canals clear, but there is only so much crews can do when that much water arrives at once. See also: Florida stages emergency supplies as Tropical Storm Isaias strengthens in Gulf Samples said residents who cannot get home should find another place to stay if they can, and that the city is working closely with police on safety. The city's proposed capital plan for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, submitted to City Council on April 13, includes the Oak Hammock Watershed Improvement Project. It would add new retention ponds, pump systems and upgraded valves. The plan shows $8 million in each of the first two years and $7 million in each of the next two, for $30 million in all, paid for through stormwater bond financing. Samples said the city has just begun early data analysis for Oak Hammock, which he placed in the California Boulevard area. He said that work will guide the design of a multi-phase project that could include new retention ponds, pumps for canals, or even raising the roadway at California and Savona boulevards so water drains off. He said it is hard to predict when residents will see construction or a finished project, because the city must first gather data, settle on a design and line up funding. He called Oak Hammock a priority for the city. "It will move as fast as it possibly can," Samples said. According to the city, the project covers a large area east of Interstate 95, north of the C-23 Canal and Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and west of Florida's Turnpike. The money would come partly from a $6 increase in the annual stormwater assessment, which the city's website lists as proposed. That would raise the assessment from $183 to $189. The city says the assessment helps pay for five projects aimed at flooding and water flow: Oak Hammock, the Elkcam Basin, the E-8 Canal, Hogpen Slough, and faster replacement of swales and culverts. The city says its drainage system includes about 200 miles of canals, 1,200 miles of swales, and more than 6,000 culverts. It also notes that maintaining swales and driveway culverts, from the edge of the pavement to the property line, is the property owner's responsibility under city code.

entry.title: New I-95 Oslo Road interchange opens in Indian River County over a year ahead of schedule - WFLX
entry.summary: New I-95 Oslo Road interchange opens in Indian River County over a year ahead of schedule    WFLX
entry.article_text: Governor Ron DeSantis was in Indian River County on Monday to celebrate the completion of a new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, a $100 million project state officials say will improve traffic flow, emergency response times and freight movement. The interchange, which opened about a year ahead of schedule, marks the first new I-95 interchange built in Indian River County in nearly 50 years. DeSantis said the project will provide a new direct connection to I-95 while easing congestion at nearby interchanges at Indrio Road and State Road 60. “This is going to bring a new critical connection to I-95 for a part of the state that has changed quite a bit,” DeSantis said. According to the governor, drivers using Oslo Road to access I-95 can expect travel times to be cut roughly in half. State transportation officials also project traffic along the corridor will continue growing through 2045. DeSantis said the project is expected to have significant public safety benefits as well. The state estimates emergency response times in the area could be reduced by as much as 56%, allowing first responders to reach crashes and other emergencies more quickly. “This will ultimately save some lives because time is of the essence in some of these situations,” DeSantis said. Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue said improved access to I-95 for first responders was one of the project’s most important features. “Every single second counts when it comes to saving lives, and this is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially,” Perdue said. The new interchange is also expected to improve freight movement for businesses in southern Indian River County by providing a more direct route to the interstate for trucks and commercial traffic. State officials said the project was accelerated through Florida’s Moving Florida Forward initiative, a transportation funding program launched by the DeSantis administration to speed up major road projects across the state. Perdue said FDOT worked with contractors through a “voluntary acceleration” program that rewarded construction teams for finding ways to complete projects more quickly. As a result, the Oslo Road interchange was finished approximately 400 days ahead of schedule. In addition to transportation improvements, FDOT acquired land near the interchange to establish a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat. State officials said the site will serve as the only relocation area of its kind in Southeast Florida, allowing protected tortoises to be moved while infrastructure projects continue. The Oslo Road interchange is part of nearly $1 billion in planned transportation investments across Florida’s Treasure Coast region. “This interchange sets a clear example of how Florida delivers infrastructure that improves quality of life today while building more capacity for the future,” DeSantis said.

entry.title: Westlake approves school zone speed cameras at Seminole Ridge High School
entry.summary: The city of Westlake is moving forward with plans to install school zone speed cameras at Seminole Ridge High School after city council members unanimously approved the measure during a final hearing. WPTV reporter Christy Waite has been tracking speed cameras that are popping up across western Palm Beach County. WATCH BELOW: Westlake approves school zone speed cameras Westlake unanimously approves speed cameras in school zones Westlake City Council voted 5-0 to authorize the cameras along Seminole Pratt Whitney Road, making Seminole Ridge High School the first and only school in the city to have the technology at this time. City Manager Howard Brown Jr. said the cameras are being implemented to improve safety around students and provide law enforcement with another tool to enforce speed limits in school zones. According to city leaders, a recent speed zone study found a need for additional enforcement in the area, helping drive the decision to move forward with the program. 'That's an area where we really want to protect our children and provide law enforcement with additional tools,' Brown said. The city says children's safety is the top priority. They hope the cameras will encourage drivers to slow down and pay closer attention when traveling through active school zones. 'We are just trying to correct behavior in those school zones because people are busy, they are not paying attention that they are even going through a school zone,' Brown said. Under the program, drivers caught traveling more than 10 mph over the posted speed limit in the school zone will receive a $100 citation. The city will partner with RedLine to operate the speed camera system. City leaders said there was no public comment submitted either for or against the cameras during the hearing. The city also says they are discussing the program and have included topics such as safety, security and privacy. Westlake expects the cameras to be installed by the end of the year. Once activated, the city plans to offer a 30-day warning period before citations are issued to drivers.

entry.title: UF study finds dengue-linked mosquito common in Indian River County yards - WPEC
entry.summary: UF study finds dengue-linked mosquito common in Indian River County yards    WPEC
entry.article_text: Florida has reported nearly 500 dengue cases this year, including more than 250 infections acquired within the state, as new University of Florida research points to residential yards in Indian River County as a key place to understand mosquito-bite exposure. The Florida Department of Health’s latest weekly surveillance report , covering Sept. 20-26, lists 252 locally acquired dengue cases and 245 travel-associated cases statewide 497 total. The locally acquired cases were reported in Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco, Pinellas and Polk counties. Palm Beach County had one locally acquired case and 12 travel-associated cases; St. Lucie County had six travel-associated cases. No locally acquired dengue cases were listed for Indian River County in the report. The state’s locally acquired total includes 223 cases in Hillsborough County, the center of Florida’s outbreak. Health officials also reported 20 mosquito pools testing positive for dengue statewide. Nationally, the CDC’s most recent weekly provisional report counted 690 dengue cases among U.S. Florida accounted for 403 of those cases in the CDC reporting system, though the state’s more current surveillance report lists a higher total because reporting systems update on different schedules. Against that backdrop, researchers at UF/IFAS’ Florida Medical Entomology Laboratory in Vero Beach found a surprising mosquito pattern in suburban Indian River County. The team expected residential yards to be dominated by Aedes albopictus , also known as the Asian tiger mosquito. Instead, researchers found relatively high numbers of Aedes aegypti the yellow fever mosquito and one of the two species most closely associated with dengue transmission worldwide. The finding does not mean dengue is circulating in Indian River County . But it underscores why backyard mosquito control and personal bite prevention matter, researchers said. See also: Florida stages emergency supplies as Tropical Storm Isaias strengthens in Gulf The first-of-its-kind study paired mosquito trapping at homes with a smartphone-based Bite Diary that let residents document when and where they were bitten. Researchers collected 3,788 female mosquitoes from 78 yards. Of 70 reported bites, nearly 93% happened outdoors and nearly 74% happened at home, according to the peer-reviewed study . The number of mosquitoes trapped in a yard was not associated with the number of bites residents reported. Instead, people who spent more time outside during the evening, from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m., reported more bites. Gardening and walking dogs were among activities commonly reported when bites occurred. Dengue is spread when an infected mosquito bites a person; it does not spread directly from person to person. Symptoms can include fever, severe muscle and joint pain, rash, nausea and pain behind the eyes. People with symptoms should contact a health care provider, especially after travel to an area where dengue is common. Health officials urge residents to use EPA-registered insect repellent, wear long sleeves and pants when practical, repair window and door screens, and dump standing water from containers such as buckets, flowerpots, toys, tires and pool covers.

The investigation revealed the victim went to South Sixth Street to speak with her boyfriend about their relationship. Upon her arrival, several people ran out of the residence and began attacking her. See also: Opponents, supporters clash over Palm Beach County Israel Bonds investments Police said the victim was able to escape, get into her vehicle, and drive away. As she fled, one of the suspects grabbed a gun from the property and began shooting at her, according to police. A second person was arrested for allegedly driving the shooter away from the scene. The two suspects arrested were identified as Keibin Lopez-Godoy, 18, and Kailee Yurubi, 18. Godoy faces a charge of first-degree attempted homicide. Yurubi faces a charge of accessory after the fact.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie flooding problem renews focus on city's stormwater spending - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie flooding problem renews focus on city's stormwater spending    WPEC
entry.article_text: After viewer videos showed water covering roads and vehicles struggling through several Port St. Lucie neighborhoods, the city's own budget documents show where it plans to put money to reduce flooding. The city says that work is still in its early stages. Lucie has received about 4 inches of rain over the past 48 hours , and another 2 to 4 inches could fall by the end of the week. City crews are monitoring conditions as water recedes, and officials are reminding drivers and pedestrians to stay out of flooded roads because it is hard to tell how deep the water is. Frank Camarda, who has lived in the area for more than 20 years near SW California Boulevard and SW Plantation Terrace, said Tuesday night's flooding turned his street into a detour. He said drivers piled in while trying to bypass flooded roads, and he believes Savona Boulevard was also underwater. Camarda said he has not seen flooding on his own street before, but he has watched water pool near Oak Hammock a couple of times. He also said city crews used to clean the swale in front of his home about once a month, and he believes that has stopped. "I've been waiting for these guys to clean up. I haven't seen them," Camarda said. City spokesperson Scott Samples said the rain came in too fast for the system to keep up. He said the canals, swales and retention ponds were already full, which makes it harder for water to move. At one location the city monitored, he said, about two feet of water arrived in roughly 30 minutes. Samples said the water had receded from most roadways by about 8:30 p.m. Tuesday, and he described that as the stormwater system doing what it is designed to do. He said Public Works checks drainage before heavy rain and is working to keep swales, drains and canals clear, but there is only so much crews can do when that much water arrives at once. See also: Florida stages emergency supplies as Tropical Storm Isaias strengthens in Gulf Samples said residents who cannot get home should find another place to stay if they can, and that the city is working closely with police on safety. The city's proposed capital plan for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, submitted to City Council on April 13, includes the Oak Hammock Watershed Improvement Project. It would add new retention ponds, pump systems and upgraded valves. The plan shows $8 million in each of the first two years and $7 million in each of the next two, for $30 million in all, paid for through stormwater bond financing. Samples said the city has just begun early data analysis for Oak Hammock, which he placed in the California Boulevard area. He said that work will guide the design of a multi-phase project that could include new retention ponds, pumps for canals, or even raising the roadway at California and Savona boulevards so water drains off. He said it is hard to predict when residents will see construction or a finished project, because the city must first gather data, settle on a design and line up funding. He called Oak Hammock a priority for the city. "It will move as fast as it possibly can," Samples said. According to the city, the project covers a large area east of Interstate 95, north of the C-23 Canal and Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and west of Florida's Turnpike. The money would come partly from a $6 increase in the annual stormwater assessment, which the city's website lists as proposed. That would raise the assessment from $183 to $189. The city says the assessment helps pay for five projects aimed at flooding and water flow: Oak Hammock, the Elkcam Basin, the E-8 Canal, Hogpen Slough, and faster replacement of swales and culverts. The city says its drainage system includes about 200 miles of canals, 1,200 miles of swales, and more than 6,000 culverts. It also notes that maintaining swales and driveway culverts, from the edge of the pavement to the property line, is the property owner's responsibility under city code.

entry.title: St. Lucie County Fire Board continues law firm search in effort to create complaint policy amid hazing fallout - WPTV
entry.summary: St. Lucie County Fire Board continues law firm search in effort to create complaint policy amid hazing fallout    WPTV
entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District has hit a snag in its effort to create a new policy for handling complaints against its own top leaders as fallout continues from a controversial hazing investigation. During a Fire District Board workshop Wednesday morning, board members had hoped to hear from outside law firms about helping draft a new complaint policy.Instead, St. Lucie County Commissioner and Fire District Board Member Jamie Fowler said one of the law firms contacted never returned her calls, while another disclosed a potential conflict of interest."I appreciated her honesty and forthrightness on that issue," Fowler said of the attorney during the meeting. "That being said, she did provide two references, both on the West Coast." The board discussed now reaching out to additional law firms in hopes of securing outside legal help ahead of its next meeting Oct. 21."I think we'd be doing ourselves an injustice if we at least we don't have a courtesy conversation with these other firms, so that we're at least prepared just in case these two firms aren't available, non-responsive," Board Member and Fort Pierce City Commissioner Curtis Johnson said. "I think we all have some sense of urgency of getting this thing closed, and and I don't want to delay any further." The effort follows a heated special board meeting Sept. 30, when members publicly acknowledged what they described as a significant gap in district policy: There is no clear process for independently handling complaints made against some of the district's own contract employees. "Since this district's inception, we have not had a policy on how they handle complaints against themselves," Fowler said during that meeting. "They — being those positions — have essentially been able to investigate themselves."Those positions include the fire chief, district attorney, clerk treasurer and medical director.The issue came under increased scrutiny amid fallout from a hazing investigation involving three veteran firefighters.A third-party investigator concluded that videos showing firefighters using a modified bug zapper to shock probationary firefighters depicted hazing.Three veteran firefighters — Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin — were fired as a result.Hutchinson and Boudrias previously told WPTV they did not consider the conduct hazing and said there was no intent to hurt anyone."It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun," Hutchinson said."We're all still friends," Boudrias said. "Us and the victims, there was no ill intent."The controversy has also raised questions about how complaints involving district leadership have been handled.Months before the hazing incident came to light, Baldwin and Hutchinson filed a complaint against Fire Chief Jeff Lee and then-District Attorney Kim Sabol in September 2025. District officials ultimately denied it. Baldwin and Hutchinson later filed additional complaints, including an amended complaint to investigators alleging the hazing investigation and their subsequent terminations were part of a broader pattern of retaliation. Lucie County Fire District told WPTV it is not currently in receipt of any official retaliation complaint from any party involved in this matter."That's not a good process," Fowler previously told WPTV.Sabol submitted her notice of retirement Sept. 30, just minutes after the special board meeting, effective 90 days from her notice. The District stated she will continue to provide services during that 90-day period. Lee previously acknowledged the district lacks a clear complaint process and told WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey that he welcomed outside scrutiny."I'm glad this board is finally taking this as a serious issue," Lee said, adding that he "welcomes any investigation from any agency."Lee also defended Sabol following her notice of retirement, calling it a "sad day" and saying she had been a "tremendous attorney for the district."Meanwhile, firefighters have been casting ballots in a union vote of no confidence in Lee."It basically says whether or not they trust and believe in him to lead this district," Fowler previously said. "So that is a huge thing if you have the majority of the men and women underneath you saying they can no longer serve under you, that's a pretty impactful message."Lee previously said he would wait for the results before commenting further on the vote."We'll see what the men and women decide," Lee said. "I came up on the labor side; I've always fought for our men and women on the line."The union is also continuing its legal fight to reinstate Boudrias, Hutchinson and Baldwin.During the Sept. 30 meeting, Fowler questioned whether the fire board itself may have the authority to bring the three firefighters back rather than waiting for the arbitration process to play out."I think we might actually," Fowler said at the time.Board members are expected to continue searching for an outside law firm to help develop the new policy before the Fire District Board meets again Oct.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie flooding problem renews focus on city's stormwater spending - cw34.com
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie flooding problem renews focus on city's stormwater spending    cw34.com
entry.article_text: After viewer videos showed water covering roads and vehicles struggling through several Port St. Lucie neighborhoods, the city's own budget documents show where it plans to put money to reduce flooding. The city says that work is still in its early stages. Lucie has received about 4 inches of rain over the past 48 hours , and another 2 to 4 inches could fall by the end of the week. City crews are monitoring conditions as water recedes, and officials are reminding drivers and pedestrians to stay out of flooded roads because it is hard to tell how deep the water is. Frank Camarda, who has lived in the area for more than 20 years near SW California Boulevard and SW Plantation Terrace, said Tuesday night's flooding turned his street into a detour. He said drivers piled in while trying to bypass flooded roads, and he believes Savona Boulevard was also underwater. Camarda said he has not seen flooding on his own street before, but he has watched water pool near Oak Hammock a couple of times. He also said city crews used to clean the swale in front of his home about once a month, and he believes that has stopped. "I've been waiting for these guys to clean up. I haven't seen them," Camarda said. City spokesperson Scott Samples said the rain came in too fast for the system to keep up. He said the canals, swales and retention ponds were already full, which makes it harder for water to move. At one location the city monitored, he said, about two feet of water arrived in roughly 30 minutes. Samples said the water had receded from most roadways by about 8:30 p.m. Tuesday, and he described that as the stormwater system doing what it is designed to do. He said Public Works checks drainage before heavy rain and is working to keep swales, drains and canals clear, but there is only so much crews can do when that much water arrives at once. See also: Florida stages emergency supplies as Tropical Storm Isaias strengthens in Gulf Samples said residents who cannot get home should find another place to stay if they can, and that the city is working closely with police on safety. The city's proposed capital plan for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, submitted to City Council on April 13, includes the Oak Hammock Watershed Improvement Project. It would add new retention ponds, pump systems and upgraded valves. The plan shows $8 million in each of the first two years and $7 million in each of the next two, for $30 million in all, paid for through stormwater bond financing. Samples said the city has just begun early data analysis for Oak Hammock, which he placed in the California Boulevard area. He said that work will guide the design of a multi-phase project that could include new retention ponds, pumps for canals, or even raising the roadway at California and Savona boulevards so water drains off. He said it is hard to predict when residents will see construction or a finished project, because the city must first gather data, settle on a design and line up funding. He called Oak Hammock a priority for the city. "It will move as fast as it possibly can," Samples said. According to the city, the project covers a large area east of Interstate 95, north of the C-23 Canal and Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and west of Florida's Turnpike. The money would come partly from a $6 increase in the annual stormwater assessment, which the city's website lists as proposed. That would raise the assessment from $183 to $189. The city says the assessment helps pay for five projects aimed at flooding and water flow: Oak Hammock, the Elkcam Basin, the E-8 Canal, Hogpen Slough, and faster replacement of swales and culverts. The city says its drainage system includes about 200 miles of canals, 1,200 miles of swales, and more than 6,000 culverts. It also notes that maintaining swales and driveway culverts, from the edge of the pavement to the property line, is the property owner's responsibility under city code.

entry.title: Could Kansas and Florida be in play? Why the battle for Congress may be expanding
entry.summary: With less than a month until Election Day, Democrats are looking beyond the traditional battlegrounds as new signs emerge that the fight for control of Congress could be spreading into states Republicans once had little reason to worry about. Kansas and Florida are among the states receiving new attention, while President Donald Trumps own campaign schedule is taking him into reliably Republican territory. RELATED STORY | Trump holds Ohio midterm rally, urging voters to consider him on the ballot during 32-day campaign tour The shift can also be seen in campaign spending. Conservative groups have recently moved money from North Carolina, where the Senate contest was expected to be one of the years most competitive races, to Kansas as Democrats perform better in both states. Kansas has not elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century. Since Labor Day, the numbers have only gotten worse for Republicans, said Kyle Kondik, a nonpartisan election analyst with the University of Virginia Center for Politics. Florida is another state to watch. Democrats are increasingly campaigning there even though the state appeared on relatively few lists of major battlegrounds earlier this year. RELATED STORY | Trump takes midterm push to Nebraska amid economic concerns among farmers Kondik said Florida could become an important early indicator on election night if Democrats are having an especially strong showing. Thats a state that counts very quickly, Kondik said. Trump, meanwhile, campaigned this week in Nebraska, a state he carried by nearly 200,000 votes two years ago. The president frequently calls polls fake, and Kondik cautioned that the current political picture could still be affected by inaccurate polling. I am always concerned about there being some systematic polling error, he said. Republicans currently hold 218 seats in the House, while the Senate has 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats. Democrats need 51 Senate votes to hold a majority, while Republicans need 50 because the vice president breaks ties. The final weeks of the campaign will help determine whether the activity in Kansas, Florida and other states marks a genuine expansion of the political battlefield or whether the fight for Congress ultimately returns to more familiar battlegrounds.

entry.title: Ex-CIA agent who stole $194M used $102M to buy Palm Beach, Hobe Sound properties - WPEC
entry.summary: Ex-CIA agent who stole $194M used $102M to buy Palm Beach, Hobe Sound properties    WPEC
entry.article_text: A former CIA agent convicted Tuesday of defrauding the government of $194 million reportedly used the majority of the money to acquire properties in Palm Beach and Hobe Sound. According to CBS Miami , court filings say 49-year-old David J. Rush of Virginia, a former high-ranking federal employee, directed $145 million to a holding company he controlled, and that $102 million was used to purchase four Florida properties: Two Palm Beach homes: $21.9 million and $27 million One Palm Beach parcel: $13.65 million One Hobe Sound parcel: $40 million Prosecutors allege Rush intended to eventually resell the properties for a profit. How the scheme unfolded According to the Department of Justice , Rush, of Ashburn, Virginia, pleaded guilty Tuesday, Oct. 6, to wire fraud in federal court in Alexandria, Virginia. According to prosecutors, Rush used his senior-level government position and "Top Secret" clearance to create fictitious government authorities and obtain federal money for his own benefit. Between November 2025 and March 2026, he directed approximately $145 million to a holding company established at his direction, according to court documents. The money was then used to purchase the properties. The Justice Department says Rush fraudulently obtained approximately $193.6 million in government funds. The South Florida real estate was only part of the alleged scheme. Gold bars Prosecutors say Rush separately created a fake "sensitive government activity" to justify acquiring hundreds of gold bars. On May 19, 2026, FBI agents searched Rush's Virginia home and recovered 298 gold bars, approximately $2.1 million in cash, €104,795, and numerous luxury watches. The gold had cost the government approximately $46 million, according to the Justice Department. Rush has agreed to forfeit the gold bars and cash, the Florida properties, luxury watches, and two 2026 BMW Alpina vehicles as part of his plea agreement. What's next Rush is scheduled to be sentenced Jan. He faces a maximum of 20 years in federal prison, along with possible restitution, forfeiture and a fine. The Justice Department said its investigation is continuing. The Director of National Intelligence has also requested an investigation by the Intelligence Community's inspector general. The allegations and admissions are detailed in federal court documents filed as part of Rush's guilty plea.
