entry.title: Vero Beach remembers 17-year-old Sulli Bah as family seeks justice - WFLX
entry.summary: Vero Beach remembers 17-year-old Sulli Bah as family seeks justice    WFLX
entry.article_text: Family, friends, teachers and classmates gathered at Farm Flame in Vero Beach on Wednesday to remember 17-year-old Sulliman “Sulli” Bah, who was fatally shot during a meetup at Garcia Boat Ramp last week, according to the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. No arrests have been made, and investigators are examining whether the shooting may have involved self-defense. The celebration of life was held at the Vero Beach restaurant where Bah worked. Through tears and memories, those who knew him described the Sebastian River High School student as kind, funny, hardworking and someone who could light up a room. As rain poured down Wednesday evening, flowers, candles and photographs filled Farm Flame while people who knew Bah stood together to honor his life. Isaac Rodriguez, who knew Bah, said Bah made an impact on everyone around him. “He touched everybody’s heart and he was just really kind and he always lit up the room,” Rodriguez said. Bah’s close friends told WPTV he was focused on his future and enjoyed spending time with the people closest to him. Alex Cortez said he and Bah boxed together, spent time together and shared many memories. “He was a very positive guy. He was always about working, he was intelligent, he had a big future,” Cortez said. Friend Xavi Espinosa remembered Bah as someone who could immediately make others feel welcome. “Even when I first met him, I felt he was such a good soul,” Espinosa said. The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office said Bah was at a meetup at Garcia Boat Ramp on Friday when shots were fired. The sheriff’s office said investigators are looking into whether the shooting was self-defense . No arrests have been made. Bah’s mother, Chelynn Godfrey, described her son as a loving and caring teenager who had his entire life ahead of him. She said she wants investigators to consider all the facts as they determine what happened. “I just ask that law enforcement truly looks at the big picture. I just want them to really look at the facts and I hope that they get this right,” Godfrey said. “I hope his shooter is arrested and I hope he goes to jail.” During the celebration, people took turns sharing memories of Bah and the impact he had on their lives. Angela Sanders, one of Bah’s former sixth grade teachers, remembered his personality and smile. “His personality is amazing, his smile lit up a room,” Sanders said. Myan Agosto said Bah was the type of friend who regularly checked on the people around him. “He never failed to make sure everybody was okay,” Agosto said. “He was just a really good friend.” Another friend, Zani Zoutten, remembered spending time with Bah during sixth period and described him as a happy person. The memories shared Wednesday showed how many people Bah touched during his 17 years. “He may not have lived so many years in this room, but the days he made on this earth — look at this room,” another speaker said during the celebration. Bah’s funeral is scheduled for Saturday.

entry.title: Martin County's MARTY bus transit abruptly shuts down, leaving riders stranded and 29 workers jobless
entry.summary: Martin County's contracted transit provider walked away from its agreement Thursday, halting all MARTY bus service and laying off 29 employees with no warning to riders or county leaders. There should have been more transparency and the people should have had some kind of notice so they could have made other plans," Argudo said.George Stokus, Martin County's Assistant County Administrator, said county officials are working urgently to restore service."We're doing everything we can humanly due to restore service as soon as we can," George Stokus said.In the meantime, the United Way of Martin County is stepping in through its Ride United program, which provides free, pre-scheduled Lyft rides to eligible residents for trips to work, grocery stores, medical appointments and other essential services.The organization said it was already facing financial challenges due to increased demand and other funding reductions before the MARTY service interruption and is now anticipating even greater need.Carol G. Houwaart-Diez, president and CEO of United Way of Martin County, emphasized the critical importance of transportation access for those who depend on it."Transportation isn't a luxury for the people who depend on it. It's how they get to work, receive medical care and put food on the table. entry.title: Vero Beach remembers 17-year-old Sulli Bah as family seeks justice
entry.summary: Family, friends, teachers and classmates gathered at Farm Flame in Vero Beach on Wednesday to remember 17-year-old Sulliman Sulli Bah, who was fatally shot during a meetup at Garcia Boat Ramp last week, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. No arrests have been made, and investigators are examining whether the shooting may have involved self-defense. The celebration of life was held at the Vero Beach restaurant where Bah worked. Through tears and memories, those who knew him described the Sebastian River High School student as kind, funny, hardworking and someone who could light up a room. Friends remember Sulli as a positive person As rain poured down Wednesday evening, flowers, candles and photographs filled Farm Flame while people who knew Bah stood together to honor his life. Isaac Rodriguez, who knew Bah, said Bah made an impact on everyone around him. He touched everybodys heart and he was just really kind and he always lit up the room, Rodriguez said. Bah's close friends told WPTV he was focused on his future and enjoyed spending time with the people closest to him. Alex Cortez said he and Bah boxed together, spent time together and shared many memories. He was a very positive guy. He was always about working, he was intelligent, he had a big future, Cortez said. Friend Xavi Espinosa remembered Bah as someone who could immediately make others feel welcome. Even when I first met him, I felt he was such a good soul, Espinosa said. Family seeks justice as investigation continues The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Bah was at a meetup at Garcia Boat Ramp on Friday when shots were fired. The sheriff's office said investigators are looking into whether the shooting was self-defense . No arrests have been made. Bah's mother, Chelynn Godfrey, described her son as a loving and caring teenager who had his entire life ahead of him. She said she wants investigators to consider all the facts as they determine what happened. I just ask that law enforcement truly looks at the big picture. I just want them to really look at the facts and I hope that they get this right, Godfrey said. I hope his shooter is arrested and I hope he goes to jail. Teachers and friends share memories During the celebration, people took turns sharing memories of Bah and the impact he had on their lives. Angela Sanders, one of Bah's former sixth grade teachers, remembered his personality and smile. His personality is amazing, his smile lit up a room, Sanders said.

entry.title: 'We are doing everything we can': Martin County works to find solutions after MARTY suspended - WPBF
entry.summary: 'We are doing everything we can': Martin County works to find solutions after MARTY suspended    WPBF
entry.article_text: MARTY public transit service in Martin County came to an abrupt halt Thursday, leaving residents who depend on the transit system without regular transportation as county officials scramble to find a solution. Martin County officials told WPBF's Caleb Califano they were given no advance warning that service would stop Thursday. According to the county, MARTY’s operator, Martin County Transit LLC, had requested a significant increase in its contract. The company says rising insurance, fuel and maintenance costs have led to significant financial losses since it began operating the service in July 2025. Despite negotiations with the county, the two sides were unable to reach an agreement. County officials said the company provided a 180-day notice to terminate its contract approximately two weeks ago. However, Thursday morning, Martin County Transit LLC notified the county that it was immediately discontinuing service. The sudden shutdown has left residents who rely on MARTY to get around the county without their regular transportation option. George Stokus, assistant Martin County administrator, said officials are now exploring both short-term and long-term solutions to restore service. "We are doing everything we can humanly do right now to restore service as soon as we can," Stokus said. "It’s just not an easy operation or switch to turn it back on. It’s going to take some time, and we are working to get to that." In the meantime, county officials say they are working with community partners, including United Way, to help residents impacted by the shutdown. The county has not provided a timeline for when MARTY operations could resume. Officials say they will continue posting updates on social media and will notify residents as soon as a solution is reached. Riders react Leticia Chaclan, of Martin County, waited for the bus in Stuart on Thursday, but it never came. She was unaware that the MARTY bus had been suspended until WPBF's Jasimine Yasmine Julmisse informed her. Chaclain says she's been riding the bus for years and that it's a staple for many members of the community. "We really need the bus," she said. "Especially people within the Hispanic community, who don’t have a driver’s license, and need it to go to places like the clinic, to go to the hospital, and for other things we need. It’s very necessary, and we use the bus a lot. In my case, I don’t drive. But I really need the bus, and I use it a lot. I don’t drive, and we go everywhere to shop." The sudden suspension of service impacted riders including Steven Godell, who said he was on his bicycle Thursday because he didn't see the MARTY bus come Thursday morning. "It's crazy, but I will move on and do something different," he said. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: ]Port St. Lucie Assisted-Living Project Raises Contamination Concerns - WPEC
entry.summary: ]Port St. Lucie Assisted-Living Project Raises Contamination Concerns    WPEC
entry.article_text: A proposed 150-unit assisted-living facility in Port St. Lucie is moving through the development process as nearby residents question whether enough is known about the environmental history of a neighboring property with petroleum contamination. The project, known as PSL Westmoreland ALF, is planned for 7.1 acres within the Rivella planned unit development, along Southeast Morningside Boulevard near Southeast Westmoreland Boulevard. The three-story facility would include assisted-living units and a memory care component. Lucie City Council approved the project’s major site plan on Sept. Construction has not begun, and the developer must still submit construction plans for technical review and additional agency reviews. A group of residents opposes the project, citing concerns about the neighboring property’s contamination history and the potential implications for people who could eventually live at the facility. It’s not about what is being built there, resident David Lipps said, arguing that nearby businesses and other facilities could also be affected by environmental concerns. Resident Charlie D’Agata said residents have raised objections at City Council meetings for about two years. He questioned why a developer would be allowed to build near a property he described as contaminated. Residents say they have contacted outside organizations, including the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Florida Department of Health, in an effort to get answers about the site. An engineering letter provides some context for their concerns. In a letter discussing a March 2026 meeting with environmental officials about the neighboring property, BTEX Engineering said the proposed remediation approach should be changed because of concerns about surrounding properties, including the planned assisted-living facility. The letter said vapors would need to be captured during remediation. The environmental history of the neighboring property and the extent of any potential impact on surrounding land remain central questions for residents seeking more information. The city has approved the major site plan, but the project must clear additional steps before construction can begin. The developer is expected to submit construction plans for technical review, followed by reviews involving the South Florida Water Management District and other agencies. Residents say they want clearer answers about the neighboring property’s environmental history and how any potential risks would be addressed as the project advances.

entry.article_text: Two women in Fort Pierce are accused of animal neglect after a dog died on their watch, according to arrest reports from the Fort Pierce Police Department . FPPD says that Samya Shanice Bryant, 25, and Danielle Amanda Potts, 28, were arrested on Oct. 2 in connection with the neglect and death of a dog at Pine Creek Apartments. Officers found the dog days before on Sept. 29 lying outside an apartment. The dog was severely underweight with visible ribs, infected sores on his paws, and no food or water. Bryant told the officers that the dog was hers, and that he had been sick for weeks after another man allegedly poured boiling water on him. FPPD says that both women who each lived in the apartment had control of the dog but did not get him veterinary treatment. entry.title: Treasure Coast HS student critically injured after being struck by SUV on way to school in Port St. Lucie - WPTV
entry.summary: Treasure Coast HS student critically injured after being struck by SUV on way to school in Port St. Lucie    WPTV
entry.article_text: A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student is in critical condition after being struck by a vehicle while walking to school Wednesday morning, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.Police said the crash happened around 6 a.m. near the intersection of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Southwest Squirrel Avenue.WATCH BELOW: Student critically injured after being struck by SUVInvestigators said the freshman was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard on his way to school and was near the edge of the roadway alongside construction barrels in the area when he was struck from behind by a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man.According to police, the driver initially believed he had hit a construction barrel and did not realize he had struck a person. Authorities said the driver later made a U-turn at the next location where it was safe to do so and returned to the scene.Once back in the area, the driver activated his hazard lights and found the teen unconscious on the side of the roadway. Police said he immediately called 911 and has remained cooperative throughout the investigation.The student suffered life-threatening injuries and remains hospitalized in critical condition, according to police.Investigators said there were no apparent signs of impairment involving the driver, though they noted the assessment is preliminary and could change as the investigation continues.The crash remains under investigation.Police are asking anyone who witnessed the incident or who may have dash camera, surveillance or other video footage from the area around the time of the crash to come forward.Anyone with information is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.Howard Shapiro lives across the street from where the crash occurred.Shapiro said this stretch of Port St. Lucie Boulevard can be dangerous."I don't walk around here is no lighting outside at nighttime," said Shapiro. "Kids walk along all the time because there's school back there, school down there."Though crews are improving the roadway, Shapiro said lights would make it safer."They are putting in a sidewalk, so that's going to be helpful. But streetlights need to follow," said Shapiro.Celine Gabriel lives off nearby Becker Road and said she avoids Port St. Lucie Boulevard altogether."I don't even come down this road no more," said Gabriel. "I go all the way down to I-95, come up on Gatlin to take my child to school.

entry.title: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say
entry.summary: A Martin County woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after deputies say she buried several cats alive in her yard at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, 37-year-old Alba Chavez told deputies she buried at least four of her cats alive at her home in the 11000 block of Southeast Federal Highway because she believed the animals were demons. Deputies immediately began searching the property in an effort to locate and rescue the animals. Investigators found two cats alive and rescued them, while two others were found dead. Chavez was taken into custody and is expected to face multiple counts of aggravated animal cruelty. The investigation remains active, and deputies are continuing to search the property for additional evidence.

Ball is in Paxton’s court.”RELATED STORY | Trump faces hecklers while making high-profile Texas campaign pushTalarico revealed his flu diagnosis September 30 when he spoke virtually with the United States Hispanic Business Council, an event he was supposed to attend in person.“I was starting to feel kind of under the weather a few days ago and last night it got so bad that I went to the urgent care here in Dallas, and I was diagnosed with the flu,” Talarico told the crowd gathered in Edinburg, Texas, over video conference. “I’m running a fever, and I’m at my most contagious right now, and I guess I’ve been shaking too many hands on the campaign trail and so I want to keep everybody safe.”Talarico’s last public appearance in Texas took place on September 26 when he held a press conference on suspending the federal gas and diesel tax and ending the war with Iran.“This is the kind of immediate action we need to provide Texans some relief at the pump in the middle of this affordability crisis,” Talarico said at a gas station in Carrollton, Texas.After publication of this story, a Talarico campaign source noted the candidate attended a private fundraiser in New York City featuring actor Robert De Niro on September 28.During this time stretch, Paxton has made several campaign trail stops, including speaking at Trump’s rally in San Antonio on Wednesday. Paxton has spoken at four other campaign events, including a conversation with the USHBC, and was on hand at the president’s event in Denton. At that stop, Trump said he didn’t even know Paxton was there and jokingly called him a “pain in the ass.”In a Truth Social post Wednesday night, Trump questioned Talarico’s whereabouts and called for a debate between the two Senate candidates.“He should immediately report to a Debate Stage against Ken Paxton, who is ready, willing, and able,” Trump wrote.The Paxton campaign did not respond to a request for comment about Trump’s proposed debate between the two candidates. Talarico has challenged Paxton to several debates, including one on Fox News, but the window for debates is narrowing with Election Day less than four weeks away.Talarico will appear at a town hall hosted by CNN and Jubilee Media on Wednesday, October 14 in Fort Worth, Texas. The media outlets have also extended a town hall invitation to Paxton.The two candidates are locked in a tight battle for the US Senate seat currently occupied by GOP Sen. John Cornyn, who Paxton defeated in a bruising Republican primary in May.RELATED STORY | Republicans fret as Talarico bombards airwaves and Paxton awaits Trump team’s cashA recent New York Times/Siena University poll showed Talarico with a six-point lead over Paxton.The close nature of the race in a state Trump won by double digits in 2024 is causing anxiety for Republicans, who are flooding the Texas airwaves in the final stretch. GOP ad spending in the state from September to November currently stands at more than $190 million compared to $52 million spent by Democrats during the same time period.

entry.article_text: A 33-year-old man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in connection with the August shooting death of a woman in Vero Beach, according to the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on an active warrant and is being held without bond. The warrant accuses him of killing Dawn Marie Kriskewic on Aug. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 According to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, deputies responded to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. Deputies found Kriskewic with injuries that appeared consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR. She was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead. Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death. The coworker also told investigators that Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the area around the time of the shooting. Investigators also recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch near the crime scene. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit. Additional surveillance footage cited by investigators showed Waggle walking through the area before and after the shooting. Detectives said footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which investigators later recovered. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle on Aug. He was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Jury convicts former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms of official misconduct - cw34.com
entry.summary: Jury convicts former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms of official misconduct    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie County jury convicted former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms of official misconduct Thursday, finding he improperly obstructed, delayed or prevented information about a possible felony involving the city from being communicated. Jurors found Mimms not guilty of bid tampering, the first count he faced. But they found him guilty on the official-misconduct count and specifically determined the misconduct involved obstructing, delaying or preventing communication of information related to a possible felony that directly involved or affected the government entity he served. The verdict followed a trial that began Sept. 29 and centered on allegations that Mimms improperly influenced the city’s bidding process for two vacant Lincoln Park-area lots. Prosecutors alleged Mimms steered the process toward Lincoln Park Young Professionals , a nonprofit whose board included his niece and another city employee. The organization sought a lease involving the properties, near the Lincoln Theater. During trial, FDLE Agent Derek Brisky testified about emails, city records and the request-for-proposals process. Prosecutors pointed to communications showing Mimms continued to discuss the RFP’s evaluation criteria and committee after the matter had been referred to the city’s purchasing department. The defense argued the purchasing department controlled the RFP’s publication and administration, and challenged the state’s claim that the process amounted to an improper sole-source arrangement. See also: 4 people arrested after drugs, 26 firearms found at North Palm Beach home Court records show Circuit Judge Michael James Linn denied the state’s request to have Mimms taken into custody pending sentencing. Mimms was allowed to remain free on bond. Sentencing is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. Lucie County Circuit Court.

entry.title: Former city manager Nick Mimms found guilty of misconduct charge, not guilty of bid tampering
entry.summary: Former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms was found guilty of a third-degree felony of official misconduct and not guilty of a second-degree felony of bid tampering on Thursday. Mimms was arrested in 2024 on charges of bid tampering and official misconduct. WATCH BELOW: Former Fort Pierce city manager found guilty of official misconduct Former city manager found guilty of official misconduct According to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, Mimms was accused of rigging the bidding process for two vacant parcels of land along Avenue D, adjacent to the Lincoln Theater, in favor of a local nonprofit, Lincoln Park Young Professionals. Among that nonprofit's board was Caleta Scott, Mimms' niece, and also a city employee. The nonprofit had been awarded a $500,000 grant from Allegheny Franciscan Ministries for a community center project, but nothing was ever built. Johnathan Bridges, special assistant state attorney and Brandon White, major crimes attorney for the 19th Circuit, said there was a mountain of evidence, including emails and city documents that incriminated Mimms. 'What we learned is millions of dollars have been wasted by this city hall under the leadership of Nick Mimms, and for too long, it went unchecked, said White. The people of Ft. Pierce deserve better, and I think this verdict shows the corruption that was happening under Nick Mimms. It's about time someone was held accountable.' WPTV pressed Mimms and his attorney for comment as they left the courtroom but did not get a response. Mimms was granted a pre-sentencing investigation and is scheduled to be sentenced on Dec. 11 at the St. Lucie County Courthouse. Prosecutors said he could face a maximum of five years in prison.

entry.title: Boynton Beach soup kitchen sees increase in demand as rising costs squeeze South Florida families
entry.summary: The Soup Kitchen in Boynton Beach is seeing a surge in demand, with need up about 25% as residents struggle with rising gas prices, medical bills, and other monthly expenses. The Soup Kitchen sees need for food assistance Marlene Mejia, CEO and executive director of The Soup Kitchen, said the need is increasing. 'I would say it's about 25% higher need,' she said. People are telling the kitchen that tough times are getting tougher. 'They're telling us that the gas prices are killing them, that medication and the bills that they have to pay at the end of the month, it's not enough,' Mejia said. 'So, that's why we're coming in and filling in the gap.' The Soup Kitchen is filling in the gap for every walk of life, including employed residents, who have homes and cars but are still not making ends meet at the end of the month. 'You can see people from all over and we call them the household person, which is asset limited income constrained,' Mejia said. 'But they're employed, so they have cars, they may have a house, they may have an apartment, and it's just not adding up at the end of the month.' Yolanda Marcellus was among the dozens of people standing in a long line and walking through The Soup Kitchen for food. 'I just come here. I pick up the food. They have good food every day. Everybody comes in. So, I'm thank God I'm here,' Marcellus said. The kitchen is able to distribute hundreds of pounds of food every day through faithful volunteers, like Mary Webb. 'You just feel good helping out other people and it comes back to you,' Webb said. 'The goodness comes back to you.' The Soup Kitchen is located at 8655 W. Boynton Beach Blvd. and they can be contacted at 561-732-7595.

entry.title: Martin County's MARTY bus transit abruptly shuts down, leaving riders stranded and 29 workers jobless
entry.summary: Martin County's contracted transit provider walked away from its agreement Thursday, halting all MARTY bus service and laying off 29 employees with no warning to riders or county leaders. Martin County issued an official statement acknowledging the disruption and pledging to work toward a solution. 'Martin County is actively working to identify solutions to restore transit service as quickly as possible and minimize the impact on our riders,' Martin County officials said in the statement. Martin County Transit, the company contracted to operate the MARTY system, blamed rising operating costs for the decision. In a statement, CEO Karen Deigl said, 'we entered this contract in good faith and made every effort to find a path forward. We understand how important MARTY is to its riders and the community, and this decision was not made lightly. Martin County Transit also acknowledged the abruptness of the shutdown. 'We understand that this news may feel sudden to riders and residents. As strong advocates for reliable public transportation, we are disappointed that we are unable to continue to operate the MARTY system,' Martin County Transit said. In an afternoon press conference, county leaders explained they were in negotiations after the vendor asked for a significant increase in the cost of the contract. Two weeks ago, the company gave notice it planned to leave in 180 days and instead, it walked away Thursday, according to the county. Jim Gordon, Martin County's Public Works Director, said the county had no warning the cancellation was coming. 'We were not given advanced notice that they were going to cancel service today,' Gordon said. For Joe, a 67-year-old veteran and Martin County resident, losing MARTY service means losing his lifeline. Joe sat at the bus stop Thursday expecting his regular pickup, but no buses came. He relies on the transit system daily. '[I use it] to go to work sometimes and to go down to the homeless place, the church that feeds us food,' Joe said. Joe said he received no notice before service was cut. 'No warning at all, nothing, zero.' Joe said. Physical limitations make alternative transportation all but impossible for Joe. 'I've had two broken necks, three broken backs, I can't feel my feet, so I'm not getting anywhere,' Joe said. As strong advocates for reliable public transportation, we are disappointed that we are unable to continue to operate the MARTY system," Martin County Transit said.In an afternoon press conference, county leaders explained they were in negotiations after the vendor asked for a significant increase in the cost of the contract. Two weeks ago, the company gave notice it planned to leave in 180 days and instead, it walked away Thursday, according to the county.Jim Gordon, Martin County's Public Works Director, said the county had no warning the cancellation was coming."We were not given advanced notice that they were going to cancel service today," Gordon said.For Joe, a 67-year-old veteran and Martin County resident, losing MARTY service means losing his lifeline. Joe sat at the bus stop Thursday expecting his regular pickup, but no buses came. He relies on the transit system daily."[I use it] to go to work sometimes and to go down to the homeless place, the church that feeds us food," Joe said.Joe said he received no notice before service was cut."No warning at all, nothing, zero." Joe said.Physical limitations make alternative transportation all but impossible for Joe."I've had two broken necks, three broken backs, I can't feel my feet, so I'm not getting anywhere," Joe said.Tony Argudo, a Martin County resident, said the transit company's handling of the shutdown lacked transparency."I don't think letting people go first thing this morning was a good idea. There should have been more transparency and the people should have had some kind of notice so they could have made other plans," Argudo said.George Stokus, Martin County's Assistant County Administrator, said county officials are working urgently to restore service."We're doing everything we can humanly due to restore service as soon as we can," George Stokus said.In the meantime, the United Way of Martin County is stepping in through its Ride United program, which provides free, pre-scheduled Lyft rides to eligible residents for trips to work, grocery stores, medical appointments and other essential services.The organization said it was already facing financial challenges due to increased demand and other funding reductions before the MARTY service interruption and is now anticipating even greater need.Carol G. Houwaart-Diez, president and CEO of United Way of Martin County, emphasized the critical importance of transportation access for those who depend on it."Transportation isn't a luxury for the people who depend on it. It's how they get to work, receive medical care and put food on the table. When a critical service like this disappears, the need doesn't disappear with it," Houwaart-Diez said.Houwaart-Diez said the United Way is committed to being there for riders during the disruption."This is important for people to be able to get to the doctor's, to get to wherever they need to go so we want to be there," Houwaart-Diez said.Ashley Capital has committed an initial $2,500 donation to help support the Ride United program's response, alongside a contribution from another donor. Since launching in September 2022, Ride United has provided thousands of rides for Martin County residents facing transportation barriers. However, United Way emphasized that the program cannot fully replace MARTY's fixed-route bus and paratransit services and that its response is only a temporary solution dependent on available funding.Martin County said it will continue providing updates as it works to restore public transit service. Information about MARTY can be found on the county's transit website.Residents seeking transportation assistance can call the United Way of Martin County at 772-283-4800 or click here to visit their website.Residents seeking paratransit transportation assistance can call 772-463-2822.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.summary: Dog lovers from across South Florida are heading to Fort Pierce this weekend for the Treasure Coast Kennel Club's Pirate Cluster, a four-day event featuring dock diving, FastCAT racing, agility, frisbee competitions, and other canine sports. The event is taking place Oct. 8-11 at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds, where visitors can watch trained canine athletes compete or give their own dogs an opportunity to try several activities. According to Treasure Coast Kennel Club President Lisa Root, many of the events offer same-day participation. 'It has to do with all kinds of sporting events that we do with our dogs, so dock diving, FastCAT, agility, UpDog (frisbee catching). Visitors can watch dogs leap into a pool during dock-diving competitions, sprint down a FastCAT course while chasing a lure, navigate agility obstacles, and participate in frisbee events. Root said the event is designed to be welcoming for both dog owners and spectators. 'It's a really family day. It's fun,' she said. Admission and parking are free for spectators. Fees apply for participants entering dogs into individual events. Dock diving showcases canine athleticism One of the most popular attractions is dock diving, where dogs run down a platform and launch themselves into a pool in pursuit of a toy. Competitors say many dogs recognize the venue before they even leave the vehicle. 'Once they start competing, they know what this dock means,' said dock-diving participant Janet. entry.article_text: A Flood Advisory is in effect for St. Lucie County until 4:30 p.m. A flood watch is in effect until 11 p.m. Thursday for parts of the Treasure Coast and Central Florida, including Indian River, Martin, St. Lucie and Okeechobee counties. The National Weather Service said numerous showers and thunderstorms are expected to develop Thursday afternoon and continue into the early evening. Some storms could bring 2 to 4 inches of rain, with isolated totals of 5 to 7 inches possible. Forecasters warned the heavy rain could lead to flash flooding, particularly in areas that have already received significant rainfall recently. Excessive runoff could flood rivers, creeks, streams and other low-lying areas. Urban locations and places with poor drainage may also see flooding, while storm drains and ditches could become clogged with debris. Residents should avoid driving through flooded roadways and be prepared for rapidly changing conditions through Thursday night.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie assisted-living project raises contamination concerns - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie assisted-living project raises contamination concerns    WPEC
entry.article_text: A proposed 150-unit assisted-living facility in Port St. Lucie is moving through the development process as nearby residents question whether enough is known about the environmental history of a neighboring property with petroleum contamination. The project, known as PSL Westmoreland ALF , is planned for 7.1 acres within the Rivella planned unit development, along Southeast Morningside Boulevard near Southeast Westmoreland Boulevard. The three-story facility would include assisted-living units and a memory care component. Lucie City Council approved the project’s major site plan on Sept. Construction has not begun, and the developer must still submit construction plans for technical review and additional agency reviews. A group of residents opposes the project, citing concerns about the neighboring property’s contamination history and the potential implications for people who could eventually live at the facility. See also: 'It's not safe': Treasure Coast neighbors raise concerns after teen hit walking to school It’s not about what is being built there, resident David Lipps said, arguing that nearby businesses and other facilities could also be affected by environmental concerns. Resident Charlie D’Agata said residents have raised objections at City Council meetings for about two years. He questioned why a developer would be allowed to build near a property he described as contaminated. Residents say they have contacted outside organizations, including the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Florida Department of Health , in an effort to get answers about the site. An engineering letter provides some context for their concerns. In a letter discussing a March 2026 meeting with environmental officials about the neighboring property, BTEX Engineering said the proposed remediation approach should be changed because of concerns about surrounding properties, including the planned assisted-living facility. The letter said vapors would need to be captured during remediation. The environmental history of the neighboring property and the extent of any potential impact on surrounding land remain central questions for residents seeking more information. The city has approved the major site plan, but the project must clear additional steps before construction can begin. The developer is expected to submit construction plans for technical review, followed by reviews involving the South Florida Water Management District and other agencies. Residents say they want clearer answers about the neighboring property’s environmental history and how any potential risks would be addressed as the project advances

entry.article_text: A Hobe Sound woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after deputies say she killed and buried several kittens because she believed they were possessed by demons.The Martin County Sheriff's Office (MCSO) arrested 36-year-old Alba Chavez on Thursday after responding to reports of animal cruelty at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park.WATCH BELOW: Woman buried cats alive, thought they were demons, deputies sayAccording to MCSO Sheriff John Budensiek, three youths living in the home called 911 after they discovered several of their kittens had disappeared. The children told deputies they believed Chavez had killed two kittens earlier in the week and were worried about the remaining animals.Budensiek said the children had attempted to protect three kittens by locking them inside a bedroom before going out to dinner Thursday evening. When they returned, they found the door had been forced open and the kittens were gone."When deputies arrived, she admitted she thought the kittens had demons and said she didn't want black cats or brown cats in her residence," Budensiek said during a Friday news conference.Investigators said Chavez told deputies she had killed two kittens on Monday, thrown them into the trash, later removed them and buried them in the backyard.Deputies said she then led them to a burial site behind the home and told them to bring gloves, shovels and bags if they wanted to find the missing kittens.Despite heavy rain and lightning, deputies began digging in the backyard."As they were digging, they could hear cries from the kittens," Budensiek said.Deputies rescued two kittens that were buried alive inside a plastic Publix bag. The two kittens killed earlier in the week were also recovered deceased from the burial site.A fifth kitten remains missing. Budensiek said deputies and investigators extensively searched the backyard and mobile home but have not located the animal.The two surviving kittens were rushed to a veterinary emergency clinic, where they are being treated for dehydration and monitored for potential long-term effects from being buried underground."If they survive, they'll eventually be taken to the Humane Society and go through the adoption process," Budensiek said.Chavez was arrested on four counts of animal cruelty involving torture, inflicting pain, serious injury or death to an animal. Authorities said additional charges could follow if the missing kitten is found dead.The arrest marks at least the third animal cruelty or neglect case in Martin County since late July. Asked whether the trend surprised him, Sheriff John Budensiek said reports of violence against animals often mirror broader societal problems."We've seen society kind of going downward and we see more violence with interactions with humans and then that translates into animals," Budensiek said. "In fact, a lot of times it starts with animals and then moves over to humans. So unfortunately, based on the trends and societal trends that we're seeing, it does not surprise me, but when we see it, it's extremely alarming.Budensiek said Chavez is being held without bond at the Martin County Jail and is also subject to an immigration hold. The sheriff identified her as a Venezuelan national who he said is in the United States illegally.According to the sheriff, deputies had previously responded to the home for incidents involving Chavez's mental health but had never received complaints related to animal cruelty.When asked about Chavez's motive, Budensiek said investigators still aren't certain whether mental health issues played a role."She said they were demonic. She said she didn't want those cats in her house," Budensiek said. "I don't know whether it was a mental health issue or she just didn't like the cats."Budensiek said the three youths who reported the incident were emotional but showed courage by contacting law enforcement."I applaud them for reaching out, calling 911 and letting us save the two kittens," he said.The children were taken into the custody of the Florida Department of Children and Families before being turned over to their father, who lives locally, according to investigators.Other adult cats found at the home were examined by animal services and determined to be healthy.Budensiek called the case "extremely alarming" and praised the responding deputies for their efforts to rescue the buried animals."We're going to aggressively pursue criminal charges on her to make sure she pays for the damage that she did to these animals," he said.

entry.title: Deputies hear cries underground, rescue 2 kittens buried alive in Hobe Sound - WPEC
entry.summary: Deputies hear cries underground, rescue 2 kittens buried alive in Hobe Sound    WPEC
entry.article_text: Deputies digging through a rain-soaked backyard in Martin County heard the cries of kittens buried up to 3 feet underground, leading to the rescue of two animals while two others were found dead, the sheriff revealed Friday. During a news conference, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek provided new details about the arrest of 36-year-old Alba Chavez, who is accused of killing two kittens and burying two others alive at a mobile home park in Hobe Sound. According to the sheriff's office, deputies responded to the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park on Thursday night after several minors inside the home called 911 to report that Chavez had allegedly killed two kittens Monday, placed them in the trash and later buried them in the backyard. The children, who feared for the safety of three remaining kittens, attempted to protect them by locking them inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday night. Budensiek said that when the children returned home, they discovered the bedroom door had been forced open and the kittens were missing. The children then called law enforcement to report the incident. When deputies arrived, Chavez was standing in the roadway and reportedly admitted to killing the two kittens. While speaking with deputies, Chavez said she believed the kittens had demons, described them as ugly and said she did not want black or brown cats inside the home. Chavez then led deputies to the backyard, where the kittens had allegedly been buried. "She took them to the backyard where our deputies started digging frantically trying to recover what they believed to be three live kittens and two dead kittens," Budensiek said. See also: Hurricane Isaias strengthens into major Category 3 storm near Florida Panhandle As deputies dug through the backyard, they heard cries coming from underground. Two kittens were recovered alive, while the two kittens Chavez allegedly killed Monday were found dead. A fifth kitten remains missing despite repeated searches of the property. Budensiek said the two surviving kittens were immediately taken to an emergency veterinary facility, where they were being treated for dehydration. The sheriff said veterinarians were also concerned about possible injuries caused by a lack of oxygen while the kittens were buried. Despite being rescued, the kittens could still die from their injuries. Chavez was arrested and charged with four counts of animal torture involving pain, serious injury or death, according to the sheriff's office. The four charges correspond to the two kittens found dead and the two rescued alive. The sheriff said Chavez was being held without bond at the Martin County Jail and also had an immigration hold. Investigators have not determined exactly how the first two kittens died. The sheriff said Chavez initially cooperated with deputies and led them to the burial site but later stopped answering questions about how the animals were killed. Authorities also have not determined her motive. Budensiek said deputies had previously responded to calls involving Chavez's mental health but had received no prior animal cruelty complaints at the residence. Additional charges could be filed if the fifth kitten is found dead, according to the sheriff. Following the incident, the Florida Department of Children and Families became involved, and the children were later released to their father, who lives locally. Officials said resources were available to help the children cope with what happened.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie assisted-living project raises contamination concerns - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie assisted-living project raises contamination concerns    WPEC
entry.article_text: A proposed 150-unit assisted-living facility in Port St. Lucie is moving through the development process as nearby residents question whether enough is known about the environmental history of a neighboring property with petroleum contamination. The project, known as PSL Westmoreland ALF , is planned for 7.1 acres within the Rivella planned unit development, along Southeast Morningside Boulevard near Southeast Westmoreland Boulevard. The three-story facility would include assisted-living units and a memory care component. Lucie City Council approved the project’s major site plan on Sept. Construction has not begun, and the developer must still submit construction plans for technical review and additional agency reviews. A group of residents opposes the project, citing concerns about the neighboring property’s contamination history and the potential implications for people who could eventually live at the facility. See also: 'It's not safe': Treasure Coast neighbors raise concerns after teen hit walking to school It’s not about what is being built there, resident David Lipps said, arguing that nearby businesses and other facilities could also be affected by environmental concerns. Resident Charlie D’Agata said residents have raised objections at City Council meetings for about two years. He questioned why a developer would be allowed to build near a property he described as contaminated. Residents say they have contacted outside organizations, including the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Florida Department of Health , in an effort to get answers about the site. An engineering letter provides some context for their concerns. In a letter discussing a March 2026 meeting with environmental officials about the neighboring property, BTEX Engineering said the proposed remediation approach should be changed because of concerns about surrounding properties, including the planned assisted-living facility. The letter said vapors would need to be captured during remediation. The environmental history of the neighboring property and the extent of any potential impact on surrounding land remain central questions for residents seeking more information. The city has approved the major site plan, but the project must clear additional steps before construction can begin. The developer is expected to submit construction plans for technical review, followed by reviews involving the South Florida Water Management District and other agencies. Residents say they want clearer answers about the neighboring property’s environmental history and how any potential risks would be addressed as the project advances

entry.title: Boynton Beach Community High School set to launch school district's only choice sports academy
entry.summary: A first of its kind program is coming to Boynton Beach High School. The school is launching the Palm Beach County School Districts only choice Sports Academy, giving students a chance to turn their passion for sports into a career opportunities that go far beyond the field. WATCH BELOW: Principal Dr. Moody Fuller speaks with WPTV's Todd Wilson how the academy came to fruition Boynton Beach High to launch school district's only sports academy The idea came from just taking a look of our student interests, Principal Dr. Moody Fuller said. That closer look revealed something important, Boynton Beach students have a real passion for sports and the Boynton Beach Sports Academy was born. 'What we wanted to do was teach them that sports are more than just being an athlete, Fuller said. Fuller said the world of sports extends far beyond the playing field, with countless career opportunities. The academy gives students six different pathways to explore those careers. 'The six areas that we are focusing on, number one is going to be performance, culinary, hospitality, nutrition,' he said. 'Were going to offer e-sports, photography, and broadcasting. We also have turf management coming soon and the last one is sports medical science.' The sports academy is also bringing some big changes to campus, including new turf on the football field, along with a new weight room and training room. 'Were really hoping we have something to show fall of '27,' he said. 'We are expecting to break ground on our stadium this spring, were also looking at the weight room as soon as possible. Some of these facility upgrades will be in as soon as Aug. 27. And the school isnt waiting to get started. Boynton Beach high is already accepting students for the sports academy for the fall of 2027.

entry.title: Haverhill Road near Greenacres Elementary to become designated school zone after WPTV investigation
entry.summary: A busy stretch of Haverhill Road across from Greenacres Elementary School will become a designated school zone after parents raised concerns about children crossing the road. WPTV reporter Christy Waite has been pressing the county, city and the Palm Beach County School District for answers. WATCH BELOW: School zone, crosswalk coming to Greenacres Elementary Big safety changes are coming outside Greenacres Elementary Brandon and Lynn Pote reached out to Waite after growing increasingly concerned about student safety. The couple lives across from Greenacres Elementary School, where the speed limit along Haverhill Road is 40 mph, and there is currently no designated school zone or crosswalk. 'Right here on Haverhill Road there is no crosswalk and no school zone, and cars are going 40 mph,' Brandon Pote said. entry.title: Boynton Beach Community High School set to launch school district's only choice sports academy
entry.summary: A first-of-its-kind program is coming to Boynton Beach High School. The school is launching the Palm Beach County School Districts only choice Sports Academy, giving students a chance to turn their passion for sports into a career opportunities that go far beyond the field. WATCH BELOW: Principal Dr. Moody Fuller speaks with WPTV's Todd Wilson how the academy came to fruition Boynton Beach High to launch school district's only sports academy 'The idea came from just taking a look of our student interests,' Principal Dr. Moody Fuller said. That closer look revealed something important, Boynton Beach students have a real passion for sports and the Boynton Beach Sports Academy was born. 'What we wanted to do was teach them that sports are more than just being an athlete,' Fuller said. Fuller said the world of sports extends far beyond the playing field, with countless career opportunities. The academy gives students six different pathways to explore those careers. 'The six areas that we are focusing on, number one is going to be performance, culinary, hospitality, nutrition,' he said. 'Were going to offer e-sports, photography, and broadcasting. We also have turf management coming soon, and the last one is sports medical science.' The sports academy is also bringing some big changes to campus, including new turf on the football field, along with a new weight room and training room. 'We're really hoping we have something to show fall of '27,' he said. 'We are expecting to break ground on our stadium this spring, we're also looking at the weight room as soon as possible. Some of these facility upgrades will be in as soon as Aug. 27. And the school isnt waiting to get started. Boynton Beach High is already accepting students for the sports academy for the fall of 2027.

entry.summary: Port St. Lucie assisted-living project raises contamination concerns    WPEC
entry.article_text: A proposed 150-unit assisted-living facility in Port St. Lucie is moving through the development process as nearby residents question whether enough is known about the environmental history of a neighboring property with petroleum contamination. The project, known as PSL Westmoreland ALF , is planned for 7.1 acres within the Rivella planned unit development, along Southeast Morningside Boulevard near Southeast Westmoreland Boulevard. The three-story facility would include assisted-living units and a memory care component. Lucie City Council approved the project’s major site plan on Sept. Construction has not begun, and the developer must still submit construction plans for technical review and additional agency reviews. A group of residents opposes the project, citing concerns about the neighboring property’s contamination history and the potential implications for people who could eventually live at the facility. See also: 'It's not safe': Treasure Coast neighbors raise concerns after teen hit walking to school It’s not about what is being built there, resident David Lipps said, arguing that nearby businesses and other facilities could also be affected by environmental concerns. Resident Charlie D’Agata said residents have raised objections at City Council meetings for about two years. He questioned why a developer would be allowed to build near a property he described as contaminated. Residents say they have contacted outside organizations, including the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Florida Department of Health , in an effort to get answers about the site. An engineering letter provides some context for their concerns. In a letter discussing a March 2026 meeting with environmental officials about the neighboring property, BTEX Engineering said the proposed remediation approach should be changed because of concerns about surrounding properties, including the planned assisted-living facility. The letter said vapors would need to be captured during remediation. The environmental history of the neighboring property and the extent of any potential impact on surrounding land remain central questions for residents seeking more information. The city has approved the major site plan, but the project must clear additional steps before construction can begin. The developer is expected to submit construction plans for technical review, followed by reviews involving the South Florida Water Management District and other agencies. Residents say they want clearer answers about the neighboring property’s environmental history and how any potential risks would be addressed as the project advances

entry.title: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say - WFLX
entry.summary: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say    WFLX
entry.article_text: A Martin County woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after deputies say she buried several cats alive in her yard at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office arrested 37-year-old Alba Luz Chavez on four counts of aggravated animal cruelty after investigators said they discovered two live kittens and two dead kittens buried on a property in Hobe Sound. Deputies were called to the home Thursday night for what family members described as a mental health crisis. Family members told deputies Chavez believed the cats were demons and had killed several animals earlier in the week. According to the affidavit, deputies learned that Chavez had allegedly told residents of the home she killed two kittens on Monday, Oct. Three juveniles living at the residence told deputies Chavez had appeared to be experiencing a mental health episode for most of the week. The juveniles said they locked three surviving kittens inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday evening. When they returned around 6 p.m., they discovered Chavez had forced her way into the room and the kittens were gone. Investigators said Chavez initially refused to tell family members where the animals were. However, while speaking with deputies, Chavez allegedly said, “If you want the cats, you will need gloves, a red bag and a shovel,” and directed them to an area on the property. Deputies began digging and found two live kittens buried underground inside plastic Publix bags, according to the affidavit. Investigators later uncovered two deceased kittens that appeared to be in the early stages of decomposition. Detectives searched for a third missing kitten but were unable to locate it. During an interview, Chavez told investigators she had been cleaning her house and referred to the cats as “very ugly,” according to the affidavit. Investigators wrote that Chavez also made statements indicating she did not want black cats and suggested kittens of different colors “had different fates.” The affidavit states Chavez later began singing instead of answering additional questions. The two surviving kittens were taken to a pet emergency center for treatment. A veterinarian told investigators the kittens were about three weeks old and very weak. The veterinarian said it was too early to determine whether a lack of oxygen while confined inside the plastic bags had caused brain damage or other medical complications. The two deceased kittens are expected to undergo necropsies to determine their exact causes of death. Chavez was arrested and booked into the Martin County Jail on four felony counts of aggravated animal cruelty and is being held without bond.

"I'm going to have you back float in the tail — I'll kind of help you float there."The lesson even included a dive completely underwater."3.2.1. breathe out — we dive down and then pop up," Anthony said. "That was so good — that was fun — and that's how we shoot video underwater."For Anthony, the joy of mermaiding as an adult goes far beyond the water itself. "I think that's what mermaiding as an adult feels like is you don't have to act like a kid but you can be an adult that plays," she said. "And that's where it can be fun or it can be more — some people just want to feel empowered. Or good in their skin and they do a photo shoot or a bucket list thing."This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.article_text: Hurricane Isaias continues to churn toward the Florida Panhandle, packing winds of 120 mph midday Friday as a Category 3 storm.Florida officials urged residents across the Panhandle to complete preparations immediately on Friday as Isaias moved toward an expected late-night landfall along Florida's northwest coast.During an afternoon news conference, Gov. Ron DeSantis said the hurricane is expected to make landfall around 11 p.m. and could bring sustained winds of 115 to 120 mph, dangerous storm surge, widespread power outages, flooding and tornadoes."We think it's going to land potentially as a Category 3," DeSantis said. "This is really your last chance. If you don't do it right now, then you're probably going to be running into hazardous conditions later tonight."The governor warned that storm surge would impact a large stretch of the Gulf Coast, extending well beyond the immediate landfall area.While residents in areas such as Destin and neighboring communities face the greatest surge threat, officials said coastal flooding could reach as far east as Apalachicola and potentially affect portions of the Tampa Bay region because of the storm's large size."You're going to see water across the entire region of the Florida Panhandle," DeSantis said.Officials cautioned that hazards will not be limited to communities near the eye of the storm. Tornadoes could develop far from the center, including in Tallahassee and other parts of North Florida, while heavy rain bands are expected to continue through Saturday."There will be impacts from this far, far outside the National Hurricane Center's cone," DeSantis said.State Emergency Management Executive Director Jared Perdue said dangerous conditions had already begun for some communities."The time to prepare has passed," Perdue said. "For many of you, if you're there, it's time to shelter in place and stay safe."Evacuation orders remain in effect across multiple Panhandle counties, particularly for barrier islands, low-lying areas and RV parks. Officials urged residents who are still able to leave evacuation zones to do so immediately.State crews have staged significant resources ahead of the storm, including more than 1,400 generators, fuel, food and water supplies and thousands of emergency responders.The state has also positioned 16,000 utility workers to begin restoring power once conditions are safe."We do anticipate extensive power outages here," DeSantis said.The Florida National Guard has mobilized 5,000 service members and more than 1,300 high-water vehicles. Search-and-rescue teams, helicopters, boats and other specialized equipment have been pre-positioned throughout the region.More than 6,000 linemen and restoration personnel are standing by to support power restoration efforts following Hurricane Isaias.The Florida State Guard has deployed nearly 400 soldiers to assist with pre-landfall and post-landfall efforts, including preliminary damage assessments, route clearance, points of distribution operations, and air, ground, and maritime search and rescue support.Transportation disruptions are also expected. Officials said Florida Highway Patrol may close portions of Interstate 10 and other major roadways and bridges once winds exceed 39 mph. Multiple airports, including Pensacola International Airport and airports in Destin and Fort Walton Beach, have announced closures.State officials also warned residents not to drive through flooded roadways and to stay away from downed power lines after the storm passes.Attorney General James Uthmeier warned that looting and price gouging during the emergency will be aggressively prosecuted."Don't even try it," Uthmeier said. "During emergencies, there's heightened penalties."Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia encouraged residents to document their homes and belongings before the storm by taking photos and videos and storing records digitally for insurance purposes.Officials emphasized that residents should be prepared to be self-sufficient for at least 72 hours after the storm and reminded generator users never to operate generators inside homes because of the risk of carbon monoxide poisoning.As Isaias approaches, emergency managers are asking Floridians to follow local evacuation orders, monitor weather alerts, and avoid travel once conditions deteriorate."We're ready for it," DeSantis said. "We just got to get through it."Currently, 27 Florida counties are under a state of emergency.

entry.title: Martin County's MARTY bus transit abruptly shuts down, leaving riders stranded and 29 workers jobless - WFLX
entry.summary: Martin County's MARTY bus transit abruptly shuts down, leaving riders stranded and 29 workers jobless    WFLX
entry.article_text: Martin County’s contracted transit provider walked away from its agreement Thursday, halting all MARTY bus service and laying off 29 employees with no warning to riders or county leaders. Martin County issued an official statement acknowledging the disruption and pledging to work toward a solution. “Martin County is actively working to identify solutions to restore transit service as quickly as possible and minimize the impact on our riders,” Martin County officials said in the statement. Martin County Transit, the company contracted to operate the MARTY system, blamed rising operating costs for the decision. In a statement, CEO Karen Deigl said, “we entered this contract in good faith and made every effort to find a path forward. We understand how important MARTY is to its riders and the community, and this decision was not made lightly.” Martin County Transit also acknowledged the abruptness of the shutdown. “We understand that this news may feel sudden to riders and residents. As strong advocates for reliable public transportation, we are disappointed that we are unable to continue to operate the MARTY system,” Martin County Transit said. In an afternoon press conference, county leaders explained they were in negotiations after the vendor asked for a significant increase in the cost of the contract. Two weeks ago, the company gave notice it planned to leave in 180 days and instead, it walked away Thursday, according to the county. Jim Gordon, Martin County’s Public Works Director, said the county had no warning the cancellation was coming. “We were not given advanced notice that they were going to cancel service today,” Gordon said. For Joe, a 67-year-old veteran and Martin County resident, losing MARTY service means losing his lifeline. Joe sat at the bus stop Thursday expecting his regular pickup, but no buses came. He relies on the transit system daily. “[I use it] to go to work sometimes and to go down to the homeless place, the church that feeds us food,” Joe said. Joe said he received no notice before service was cut. “No warning at all, nothing, zero.” Joe said. Physical limitations make alternative transportation all but impossible for Joe. “I’ve had two broken necks, three broken backs, I can’t feel my feet, so I’m not getting anywhere,” Joe said. Tony Argudo, a Martin County resident, said the transit company’s handling of the shutdown lacked transparency. “I don’t think letting people go first thing this morning was a good idea. There should have been more transparency and the people should have had some kind of notice so they could have made other plans,” Argudo said. George Stokus, Martin County’s Assistant County Administrator, said county officials are working urgently to restore service. “We’re doing everything we can humanly due to restore service as soon as we can,” George Stokus said. In the meantime, the United Way of Martin County is stepping in through its Ride United program, which provides free, pre-scheduled Lyft rides to eligible residents for trips to work, grocery stores, medical appointments and other essential services. The organization said it was already facing financial challenges due to increased demand and other funding reductions before the MARTY service interruption and is now anticipating even greater need. Houwaart-Diez, president and CEO of United Way of Martin County, emphasized the critical importance of transportation access for those who depend on it. “Transportation isn’t a luxury for the people who depend on it. It’s how they get to work, receive medical care and put food on the table. When a critical service like this disappears, the need doesn’t disappear with it,” Houwaart-Diez said. Region Martin County Houwaart-Diez said the United Way is committed to being there for riders during the disruption. “This is important for people to be able to get to the doctor’s, to get to wherever they need to go so we want to be there,” Houwaart-Diez said. Ashley Capital has committed an initial $2,500 donation to help support the Ride United program’s response, alongside a contribution from another donor. Since launching in September 2022, Ride United has provided thousands of rides for Martin County residents facing transportation barriers. However, United Way emphasized that the program cannot fully replace MARTY’s fixed-route bus and paratransit services and that its response is only a temporary solution dependent on available funding. Martin County said it will continue providing updates as it works to restore public transit service. Information about MARTY can be found on the county’s transit website . Residents seeking transportation assistance can call the United Way of Martin County at 772-283-4800 or click here to visit their website. Residents seeking paratransit transportation assistance can call 772-463-2822. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Port St. Lucie intersection floods so badly a pizza shop 'lost thousands'; city says fix will take time
entry.summary: WPTV is continuing to follow flooding issues at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards in Port St. Lucie.   The water has receded, but earlier this week , the intersection looked like a lake. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie flooding hits pizza shop hard as city works on fix Flooding issues continue at this Port St. Lucie intersection WPTV is pressing city leaders about any solution to keep the water levels down. Neighbors shared video of the roadways, looking like a river. 'We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke,' said Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria right of the intersection. 'It becomes like an island around here.' That island is a shopping plaza where the pizza shop is located. Due to the flooding on Thursday, Dascoli said they had to close early. 'It's an ongoing thing that you know should be resolved,' said Dascoli. Dascoli told WPTV customers couldn't go in and orders couldn't go out during this weeks flooding. 'We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in,' said Dascoli. 'Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries.' WPTV pressed the city of Port St. Lucie about any solutions to the flooding. Scott Samples with the city said it's starting a pilot program for water level sensors at flood-prone areas in the city. 'There'll be alerts that'll be able to go to Public Works and the police to say, 'Hey, this area is seeing rapid flooding,' so they might be able to respond quicker,' said Samples. Samples said long-term solutions include a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood. The project includes two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect runoff, and even raising sections of the roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Right now, Samples said the project is in the data collection phase before moving on to design. 'This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time,' said Samples.

entry.title: Florida property tax increases explained ahead of Amendment 3 vote
entry.summary: The WPTV Town Hall on Amendment 3 has led to some more questions about the referendum facing voters on raising the Homestead Exemption to lower property taxes and reduce revenue for cities and counties. One question attendees posed was why are our property taxes increasing every year. Palm Beach County Administrator Joe Abruzzo talked about it at the town hall, saying inflation is a big factor. This is a national problem not even a Florida problem, its not a Palm Beach County problem,' Abruzzo said. 'What it costs for traffic arms where our lights go: 700 thousand five years ago. Now, theyre at 1.5 million. The cost of labor, asphalt, concrete, the things we actually use in government is just skyrocketing, so we have to budget appropriately to be able to afford the things we need to buy,' Another email asked why municipal workers get raises every three years. 'Theyre not coming in and saying we want to take a pay cut,' said West Palm Beach Mayor Keith James, talking about negotiating with police, fire and labor unions. 'Every three years were looking at increases, and we also want to pay our employees so theyre competitive with the market otherwise we lose them to the private sector and other cities and theyre living in a city where affordability is an issue,' James said. Another question asked about the impact on apartment living. Over 50% of the occupied housing units in West Palm Beach are renters,' the mayor said. 'There is no dispute that the rents are going to increase, because those are not homesteaders and so the taxes will go up on those units and the landlords will pass those expenses on to the renters,' he said.

entry.title: Police searching for driver in hit-and-run crash that injured 63-year-old man in Port St. Lucie
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie police confirmed that a man found unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries early Friday morning was the victim of a hit-and-run crash. WATCH BELOW: Police seek driver after man found unconscious in Port St. Lucie The victim has been identified as a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie resident, police said. The incident occurred at about 12:56 a.m. near the intersection of NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. The 63-year-old man was unconscious and suffering from severe head trauma and significant bleeding, police said. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for medical treatment and remains in critical condition. Police said detectives obtained surveillance video from a nearby business that captured the incident and are continuing to collect and evaluate additional video footage as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the crash and identify the vehicle and driver involved. Authorities are asking anyone who was driving in the area around the time of the crash, may have witnessed the incident, or has dashcam or other video footage from the area to come forward. Even information that may seem insignificant could assist investigators in identifying the driver and bringing this investigation to a resolution. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. The investigation remains active and ongoing.

entry.title: 'EXTREMELY ALARMING': Hobe Sound woman buried kittens alive, believing they were demons
entry.summary: A Hobe Sound woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after deputies say she killed and buried several kittens because she believed they were possessed by demons. The Martin County Sheriff's Office (MCSO) arrested 36-year-old Alba Chavez on Thursday after responding to reports of animal cruelty at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. WATCH BELOW: Woman buried cats alive, thought they were demons, deputies say Hobe Sound woman buries kittens alive, believes they were demons According to MCSO Sheriff John Budensiek, three youths living in the home called 911 after they discovered several of their kittens had disappeared. The children told deputies they believed Chavez had killed two kittens earlier in the week and were worried about the remaining animals. Budensiek said the children had attempted to protect three kittens by locking them inside a bedroom before going out to dinner Thursday evening. When they returned, they found the door had been forced open, and the kittens were gone. 'When deputies arrived, she admitted she thought the kittens had demons and said she didn't want black cats or brown cats in her residence,' Budensiek said during a Friday news conference. Investigators said Chavez told deputies she had killed two kittens on Monday, thrown them into the trash, later removed them and buried them in the backyard. Deputies said she then led them to a burial site behind the home and told them to bring gloves, shovels and bags if they wanted to find the missing kittens. Despite heavy rain and lightning, deputies began digging in the backyard. 'As they were digging, they could hear cries from the kittens,' Budensiek said. Deputies rescued two kittens that were buried alive inside a plastic Publix bag. The two kittens killed earlier in the week were also recovered deceased from the burial site. A fifth kitten remains missing. Budensiek said deputies and investigators extensively searched the backyard and mobile home but have not located the animal.
