entry.article_text: A Hobe Sound woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after deputies say she killed and buried several kittens because she believed they were possessed by demons.The Martin County Sheriff's Office (MCSO) arrested 36-year-old Alba Chavez on Thursday after responding to reports of animal cruelty at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park.WATCH BELOW: Woman buried cats alive, thought they were demons, deputies sayAccording to MCSO Sheriff John Budensiek, three youths living in the home called 911 after they discovered several of their kittens had disappeared. The children told deputies they believed Chavez had killed two kittens earlier in the week and were worried about the remaining animals.Budensiek said the children had attempted to protect three kittens by locking them inside a bedroom before going out to dinner Thursday evening. When they returned, they found the door had been forced open, and the kittens were gone."When deputies arrived, she admitted she thought the kittens had demons and said she didn't want black cats or brown cats in her residence," Budensiek said during a Friday news conference.Investigators said Chavez told deputies she had killed two kittens on Monday, thrown them into the trash, later removed them and buried them in the backyard.Deputies said she then led them to a burial site behind the home and told them to bring gloves, shovels and bags if they wanted to find the missing kittens.Despite heavy rain and lightning, deputies began digging in the backyard."As they were digging, they could hear cries from the kittens," Budensiek said.Deputies rescued two kittens that were buried alive inside a plastic Publix bag. The two kittens killed earlier in the week were also recovered deceased from the burial site.A fifth kitten remains missing. Budensiek said deputies and investigators extensively searched the backyard and mobile home but have not located the animal.The two surviving kittens were rushed to a veterinary emergency clinic, where they are being treated for dehydration and monitored for potential long-term effects from being buried underground."If they survive, they'll eventually be taken to the Humane Society and go through the adoption process," Budensiek said.Chavez was arrested on four counts of animal cruelty involving torture, inflicting pain, serious injury or death to an animal. Authorities said additional charges could follow if the missing kitten is found dead.The arrest marks at least the third animal cruelty or neglect case in Martin County since late July. Asked whether the trend surprised him, Budensiek said reports of violence against animals often mirror broader societal problems."We've seen society kind of going downward and we see more violence with interactions with humans, and then that translates into animals," Budensiek said. "In fact, a lot of times it starts with animals and then moves over to humans. So unfortunately, based on the trends and societal trends that we're seeing, it does not surprise me, but when we see it, it's extremely alarming.Budensiek said Chavez is being held without bond at the Martin County Jail and is also subject to an immigration hold. The sheriff identified her as a Venezuelan national who he said is in the United States illegally.According to the sheriff, deputies had previously responded to the home for incidents involving Chavez's mental health but had never received complaints related to animal cruelty.When asked about Chavez's motive, Budensiek said investigators still aren't certain whether mental health issues played a role."She said they were demonic. She said she didn't want those cats in her house," Budensiek said. "I don't know whether it was a mental health issue or she just didn't like the cats."Budensiek said the three youths who reported the incident were emotional but showed courage by contacting law enforcement."I applaud them for reaching out, calling 911 and letting us save the two kittens," he said.The children were taken into the custody of the Florida Department of Children and Families before being turned over to their father, who lives locally, according to investigators.Other adult cats found at the home were examined by animal services and determined to be healthy.Budensiek called the case "extremely alarming" and praised the responding deputies for their efforts to rescue the buried animals."We're going to aggressively pursue criminal charges on her to make sure she pays for the damage that she did to these animals," he said.

entry.article_text: A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student remains in critical condition after police say he was struck by an SUV while walking to school along a construction zone in Port St. Lucie Police, the crash happened around 6 a.m. Wednesday on Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue. Investigators say the freshman was walking along the roadway, which does not have sidewalks, when a 72-year-old driver hit him from behind with an SUV. The area is currently under construction as crews work to widen a portion of Port St. Police say the driver initially believed he had struck a construction barrel. After turning around and returning to the scene, officers say he found the teen unconscious on the side of the road and called 911. Neighbors who live near the crash site say the lack of sidewalks has long been a concern, especially for students who walk or bike to school. "It's not safe to walk around here," said neighbor Kendry Portal. "We need those sidewalks." Neighbors told CBS12 News they have seen multiple crashes involving pedestrians along the busy stretch of road since construction began a few years ago. See also: Jury convicts former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms of official misconduct The Florida Department of Transportation is widening the southern portion of Port St. Lucie Boulevard into a four-lane road and adding sidewalks as part of the ongoing project. Neighbors say the safety improvements cannot come soon enough. "I want to see this street finished as soon as possible," Portal said. Police do not believe the driver was impaired, and it remains unclear whether any charges will be filed. Authorities are asking anyone with dashcam or surveillance video from the area around the time of the crash to contact Port St. As of Thursday morning, the 14-year-old remains hospitalized in critical condition. "I just hope that he gets well soon and hope for the family in this situation," said Portal.

entry.title: Vero Beach remembers 17-year-old Sulli Bah as family seeks justice - WFLX
entry.summary: Vero Beach remembers 17-year-old Sulli Bah as family seeks justice    WFLX
entry.article_text: Family, friends, teachers and classmates gathered at Farm Flame in Vero Beach on Wednesday to remember 17-year-old Sulliman “Sulli” Bah, who was fatally shot during a meetup at Garcia Boat Ramp last week, according to the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. No arrests have been made, and investigators are examining whether the shooting may have involved self-defense. The celebration of life was held at the Vero Beach restaurant where Bah worked. Through tears and memories, those who knew him described the Sebastian River High School student as kind, funny, hardworking and someone who could light up a room. As rain poured down Wednesday evening, flowers, candles and photographs filled Farm Flame while people who knew Bah stood together to honor his life. Isaac Rodriguez, who knew Bah, said Bah made an impact on everyone around him. “He touched everybody’s heart and he was just really kind and he always lit up the room,” Rodriguez said. Bah’s close friends told WPTV he was focused on his future and enjoyed spending time with the people closest to him. Alex Cortez said he and Bah boxed together, spent time together and shared many memories. “He was a very positive guy. He was always about working, he was intelligent, he had a big future,” Cortez said. Friend Xavi Espinosa remembered Bah as someone who could immediately make others feel welcome. “Even when I first met him, I felt he was such a good soul,” Espinosa said. The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office said Bah was at a meetup at Garcia Boat Ramp on Friday when shots were fired. The sheriff’s office said investigators are looking into whether the shooting was self-defense . No arrests have been made. Bah’s mother, Chelynn Godfrey, described her son as a loving and caring teenager who had his entire life ahead of him. She said she wants investigators to consider all the facts as they determine what happened. “I just ask that law enforcement truly looks at the big picture. I just want them to really look at the facts and I hope that they get this right,” Godfrey said. “I hope his shooter is arrested and I hope he goes to jail.” During the celebration, people took turns sharing memories of Bah and the impact he had on their lives. Angela Sanders, one of Bah’s former sixth grade teachers, remembered his personality and smile. “His personality is amazing, his smile lit up a room,” Sanders said. Myan Agosto said Bah was the type of friend who regularly checked on the people around him. “He never failed to make sure everybody was okay,” Agosto said. “He was just a really good friend.” Another friend, Zani Zoutten, remembered spending time with Bah during sixth period and described him as a happy person. The memories shared Wednesday showed how many people Bah touched during his 17 years. “He may not have lived so many years in this room, but the days he made on this earth — look at this room,” another speaker said during the celebration. Bah’s funeral is scheduled for Saturday.

entry.title: Palm Beach County officials explain what's driving Florida property tax increases ahead of Amendment 3 vote
entry.summary: The WPTV Town Hall on Amendment 3 has led to more questions about the referendum facing voters on raising the homestead exemption to lower property taxes and reduce revenue for cities and counties. One question attendees posed was: Why are our property taxes increasing every year? WATCH BELOW: Florida property tax increases explained ahead of Amendment 3 vote Florida property tax increases explained ahead of Amendment 3 vote Palm Beach County Administrator Joe Abruzzo talked about it at the town hall, saying inflation is a big factor. 'This is a national problem, not even a Florida problem; it's not a Palm Beach County problem,' Abruzzo said. 'What it cost for traffic arms where our lights go: $700,000 five years ago. Now, they're at 1.5 million. The cost of labor, asphalt, concrete, the things we actually use in government is just skyrocketing, so we have to budget appropriately to be able to afford the things we need to buy.' Another email asked why municipal workers get raises every three years. 'They're not coming in and saying we want to take a pay cut,' said West Palm Beach Mayor Keith James, talking about negotiating with police, fire and labor unions. 'Every three years we're looking at increases, and we also want to pay our employees so theyre competitive with the market; otherwise we lose them to the private sector and other cities, and they're living in a city where affordability is an issue.' Another question asked about the impact on apartment living. 'Over 50% of the occupied housing units in West Palm Beach are renters,' James said. 'There is no dispute that the rents are going to increase, because those are not homesteaders and so the taxes will go up on those units and the landlords will pass those expenses on to the renters.'

entry.title: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say - WFLX
entry.summary: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say    WFLX
entry.article_text: A Martin County woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after deputies say she buried several cats alive in her yard at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office arrested 37-year-old Alba Luz Chavez on four counts of aggravated animal cruelty after investigators said they discovered two live kittens and two dead kittens buried on a property in Hobe Sound. Deputies were called to the home Thursday night for what family members described as a mental health crisis. Family members told deputies Chavez believed the cats were demons and had killed several animals earlier in the week. According to the affidavit, deputies learned that Chavez had allegedly told residents of the home she killed two kittens on Monday, Oct. Three juveniles living at the residence told deputies Chavez had appeared to be experiencing a mental health episode for most of the week. The juveniles said they locked three surviving kittens inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday evening. When they returned around 6 p.m., they discovered Chavez had forced her way into the room and the kittens were gone. Investigators said Chavez initially refused to tell family members where the animals were. However, while speaking with deputies, Chavez allegedly said, “If you want the cats, you will need gloves, a red bag and a shovel,” and directed them to an area on the property. Deputies began digging and found two live kittens buried underground inside plastic Publix bags, according to the affidavit. Investigators later uncovered two deceased kittens that appeared to be in the early stages of decomposition. Detectives searched for a third missing kitten but were unable to locate it. During an interview, Chavez told investigators she had been cleaning her house and referred to the cats as “very ugly,” according to the affidavit. Investigators wrote that Chavez also made statements indicating she did not want black cats and suggested kittens of different colors “had different fates.” The affidavit states Chavez later began singing instead of answering additional questions. The two surviving kittens were taken to a pet emergency center for treatment. A veterinarian told investigators the kittens were about three weeks old and very weak. The veterinarian said it was too early to determine whether a lack of oxygen while confined inside the plastic bags had caused brain damage or other medical complications. The two deceased kittens are expected to undergo necropsies to determine their exact causes of death. Chavez was arrested and booked into the Martin County Jail on four felony counts of aggravated animal cruelty and is being held without bond.

entry.summary: A Martin County employee helped rescue three girls who were struggling in a rip current Thursday afternoon at Bob Graham Beach in Jensen Beach. Watch report: Martin County employee rescues 3 girls caught in rip current at Bob Graham Beach Amy Offenbach said she arrived at the beach around 2 p.m. to surf when she noticed three girls about 25 yards offshore holding onto the same surfboard. Offenbach, who works in Martin County's Growth and Development Department and is an avid surfer, said something about the situation immediately caught her attention. 'The ocean could be very gentle and calm, but it can also be very heavy and crash very hard,' Offenbach said. Rescue unfolds offshore Offenbach said she became concerned when one of the girls appeared distressed. 'That kind of struck me as strange,' she said. 'The other one seemed a little agitated.' Moments later, a girl on the beach told Offenbach she believed her friends needed help. 'By that time the girls were waving in the water like they needed help, so immediately I just went into rescue mode,' Offenbach said. Offenbach and a friend went into the water and paddled toward the girls. Bringing the girls to safety When Offenbach reached the group, she said one of the girls appeared to be in serious distress. 'I looked at her, and she seemed kind of dazed and confused,' Offenbach said. 'I said, 'Get up on the board.'' Offenbach said she gave the surfboard she was riding to two of the girls and instructed them to hold on and kick toward shore. She then placed the third girl on her soft-top surfboard and paddled her back to the beach. entry.summary: Martin County employee rescues girl from rip current at Stuart beach    WPBF
entry.article_text: A Martin County employee is being praised for her quick actions after rescuing a girl from drowning at Bob Graham Beach in Stuart on Thursday afternoon. Amy Offenbach, who came to the beach to surf, said the day took an unexpected turn. "It was just by chance that we were here and thank God that we were at the right time," Offenbach said. Offenbach, who has years of lifeguard training, said her instincts kicked in when she saw three girls struggling in the water. "I took off my clothes, grabbed the board, and started paddling," she said. "I immediately went into rescue mode." Authorities said one of the girls was choking on water, and the beach had no lifeguards on duty. Offenbach rushed in to help, using a surfboard to stabilize the girl. "Once she was on the board, she was kind of limp. Her body wasn't doing anything else," Offenbach said. Offenbach said the girl's forehead felt cold, prompting her to rush the child to the nearest lifeguard stand down the road. The girl was then taken to the hospital with minor drowning injuries. "I'm just really thankful that her parents have their child," Offenbach said. Offenbach, a Martin County employee, said she doesn’t feel the need for recognition. While some are calling her a hero, Offenbach said she was simply acting on her instincts as a mother. "I have a 14-year-old son myself, and I can't imagine him not coming back from hanging out at the beach with his friends," she said. The incident serves as a reminder to exercise caution at the beach, especially in areas without lifeguards. entry.title: Explosion inside Port St. Lucie home leaves family with little to salvage - WPBF
entry.summary: Explosion inside Port St. Lucie home leaves family with little to salvage    WPBF
entry.article_text: An explosion inside a Port St. Lucie home destroyed almost everything owned by a family of four. Lucie County Fire District, the initial call came in at 1:24 p.m. for a fire at a home in the 100 block of Carmelite Street Friday afternoon. Neighbors called 911 after noticing the home was on fire. "I looked, and there was all kinds of smoke going through the yard," said neighbor Rob Roadman. "I was outside in the backyard, and then I see very heavy smoke," said Marina Cheong, who lives a few doors down. Cheong said she ran toward the home to help but was stopped by the explosion. "And then there was explosion, very loud, loud explosion, and debris started flying everywhere," she said. "I heard a huge explosion. At first, I thought maybe it's a transformer or something, but it was much, much, much louder than that," Roadman said. Neighbors said the man who lives in the home told them he had been cooking when a grease fire started in the garage, where the propane tank was located. The explosion sent the propane tank flying out of the garage, across the street, and into the garage of a neighbor's home. "I thought it was an air raid. It was not a casual thing. My house shook," Roadman said. "I thought that the whole house had exploded. It was very loud," Cheong added. Roadman said he spoke to the man shortly after the explosion. "I asked the dad if he was OK, and he goes, 'Yeah.' But you could tell he wasn't. Who wouldn't be?" Roadman said. The man was briefly hospitalized but returned to the house a few hours later to join family and friends in going through the debris to see what could be salvaged. They said there wasn’t much left. However, a family member told WPBF 25 News that they consider themselves lucky that nobody was seriously injured. She said the family has a strong community and a strong church to help them persevere. entry.title: 'A strong support system': Community helps injured father after Port St. Lucie house fire - WPEC
entry.summary: 'A strong support system': Community helps injured father after Port St. Lucie house fire    WPEC
entry.article_text: A fire that spread through the garage of a Port St. Lucie home Friday afternoon left a father injured and displaced a family, while neighbors and church members rallied to help them begin the cleanup process. The fire happened on Carmelite Street in the Northport Village neighborhood near St. According to the family, the fire started in the kitchen before spreading through the garage. They say a propane tank later exploded, causing additional damage and impacting a neighbor's garage doors across the street. Lucie County Fire District responded to the home around 1:30 p.m. Crews arrived to find heavy fire coming from the garage. When firefighters extinguished the flames, significant damage was left behind, including a charred garage door, blackened walls and belongings covered in soot. Renter Nigel Laidlow was inside the home when the fire broke out. He suffered burns to his legs and was transported for medical treatment. "I don't even know how to describe it. It was really surreal," Laidlow said. "I would've never thought a little fire would turn into this." By Saturday, family photos, furniture and other belongings were spread across the front yard as loved ones worked to salvage what they could. Members of the Fort Pierce Seventh-day Adventist Church spent the day helping move and sort through damaged items. "We have a really strong support system, especially from my church," Laidlow said. Despite the loss, Laidlow said he is grateful his family survived. "This right here is something not anybody would like to deal with. Not in a lifetime," he said. See also: MCSO warns scam emails may trick development applicants into wiring money The family is now focused on recovering and determining its next steps. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.

entry.title: Treasure Coast HS student critically injured after being struck by SUV on way to school in Port St. Lucie
entry.summary: A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student is in critical condition after being struck by a vehicle while walking to school Wednesday morning, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Police said the crash happened around 6 a.m. near the intersection of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Southwest Squirrel Avenue. WATCH BELOW: Student critically injured after being struck by SUV Port St Lucie student hit by vehicle while walking to school Investigators said the freshman was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard on his way to school and was near the edge of the roadway alongside construction barrels in the area when he was struck from behind by a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man. According to police, the driver initially believed he had hit a construction barrel and did not realize he had struck a person. Authorities said the driver later made a U-turn at the next location where it was safe to do so and returned to the scene. Once back in the area, the driver activated his hazard lights and found the teen unconscious on the side of the roadway. Police said he immediately called 911 and has remained cooperative throughout the investigation. The student suffered life-threatening injuries and remains hospitalized in critical condition, according to police. Investigators said there were no apparent signs of impairment involving the driver, though they noted the assessment is preliminary and could change as the investigation continues. The crash remains under investigation. Police are asking anyone who witnessed the incident or who may have dash camera, surveillance or other video footage from the area around the time of the crash to come forward. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. 'I Don't Walk Around Here' Howard Shapiro lives across the street from where the crash occurred. Shapiro said this stretch of Port St. Lucie Boulevard can be dangerous. 'I don't walk around here is no lighting outside at nighttime,' said Shapiro. 'Kids walk along all the time because there's school back there, school down there.' Though crews are improving the roadway, Shapiro said lights would make it safer. 'They are putting in a sidewalk, so that's going to be helpful. But streetlights need to follow,' said Shapiro. Celine Gabriel lives off nearby Becker Road and said she avoids Port St. Lucie Boulevard altogether. 'I don't even come down this road no more,' said Gabriel. '

entry.title: Indian River County sheriff investigates whether fatal shooting of teen at boat ramp was self-defense
entry.summary: A 17-year-old was killed in a shooting Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, and investigators are examining whether the shooting was an act of self-defense , according to Sheriff Eric Flowers. WATCH: WPTV'S Coverage of Teen killed in Garcia's Boat Ramp shooting 17-Year-Old Killed at Indian River County Boat Ramp; Sheriff Investigating Self-Defense Claim The shooting happened during a confrontation at the popular waterfront gathering spot, which authorities say has become a frequent meetup location for teenagers. According to Flowers, investigators reviewed video that showed the 17-year-old opening the door of a truck and throwing punches at people inside before a shot was fired. 'The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck,' Flowers said during a news conference. 'One shot is fired. That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case.' Video released by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office shows the confrontation moments before the shooting. Flowers said social media has played a role in drawing large groups of teens to locations like Garcia's Boat Ramp and warned that the presence of firearms is increasing the risks associated with those gatherings. 'We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media,' Flowers said. 'Now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these.' Authorities said both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and the vehicle involved in the incident. As of Monday, no arrests had been made. 'It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these,' Flowers said. The investigation remains active. The sheriff is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, as well as future teen meetup events, to contact investigators. Flowers also urged parents to know where their children are and suggested location-tracking tools as one way to help keep them safe.

entry.title: Panthers say Brad Marchand needs 6 weeks before he can resume play
entry.summary: Yes, the Florida Panthers are already seeing injuries piling up. And yes, the Panthers know things could be much, much worse. Florida forward Brad Marchand will need six weeks to recover from his left leg injury and should be able to resume play with the Panthers sometime in November, coach Paul Maurice confirmed Friday. That comes on the heels of forward Aleksander Barkov, who is expected to need a similar timetable before he can play again, also because of a left leg injury. Losing two stars isn't good. But Maurice sees the silver lining. 'Nobody said 'months' yet,' Maurice said. That's the difference between the injuries this season and what was happening to Florida at this point last season. By then, Barkov was already expected to be sidelined at least seven months with torn ligaments in his right knee and Matthew Tkachuk was also going to be out for multiple months while recovering from surgery to repair a sports hernia and torn adductor. Barkov wound up missing the entire season. Tkachuk didn't start his season until mid-January. The Panthers saw players miss a combined 544 games with injuries last season and missed the playoffs, an unceremonious end to their run as back-to-back Stanley Cup champions. So, yes, losing Barkov (who could be back by the end of November) and Marchand (who'll be back on the ice in three weeks, then is expected to need three more weeks to rehab and condition) for a few weeks now isn't ideal. But Florida has been there before. 'We're no stranger to guys going down the last few years and guys have done a great job of stepping up,' Tkachuk said. 'Worst case, you just got to win 1-0, 2-1.' There have been clear sighs of relief with the knowledge that Barkov and Marchand will both return in a few weeks. Florida was short-handed in all four games of its season-opening road trip Marchand missed the first two, Barkov missed the next two, and defenseman Aaron Ekblad also missed two because he and his wife were welcoming a baby and the Panthers went 2-0-2 anyway. entry.title: Power and rescue crews mobilize in Florida as Hurricane Isaias pushes north
entry.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the Florida Panhandle near Destin on Friday night with 105 mph winds. Gov. Ron DeSantis said in a news conference a short time later that power outages spanned from Pensacola to Panama City to Tallahassee. Watch update from Governor DeSantis: WATCH: Governor DeSantis discussed landfall of Hurricane Isaias '(Power) crews will be mobilizing once the storm passes, and they will be hard at work as soon as it's safe to do so and they have the light to be able to operate,' DeSantis said Friday night. Ahead of the storm, the governor on Friday warned that storm surge would impact a large stretch of the Gulf Coast, extending well beyond the immediate landfall area. While residents in areas such as Destin and neighboring communities faced the greatest surge threat, officials said coastal flooding could reach as far east as Apalachicola and potentially affect portions of the Tampa Bay region because of the storm's large size. 'You're going to see water across the entire region of the Florida Panhandle,' DeSantis said. Officials cautioned that hazards will not be limited to communities near the eye of the storm. Tornadoes could develop far from the center, including in Tallahassee and other parts of North Florida, while heavy rain bands are expected to continue through Saturday. 'There will be impacts from this far, far outside the National Hurricane Center's cone,' DeSantis said. State Emergency Management Executive Director Jared Perdue said dangerous conditions had already begun for some communities. 'The time to prepare has passed,' Perdue said. 'For many of you, if you're there, it's time to shelter in place and stay safe.' Evacuation orders remain in effect across multiple Panhandle counties, particularly for barrier islands, low-lying areas and RV parks. Officials urged residents who are still able to leave evacuation zones to do so immediately. entry.title: Gov. DeSantis issues state of emergency for 25 Florida counties ahead of Hurricane Isaias
entry.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis signed an executive order Tuesday issuing a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties ahead of Hurricane Isaias. The counties included are: Baker, Bay, Calhoun, Columbia, Dixie, Escambia, Franklin, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Gulf, Hamilton, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Leon, Liberty, Madison, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Suwannee, Taylor, Walton, Wakulla, and Washington. This order will allow the Florida Division of Emergency Management to stage critical preparedness resources and ensure Florida is ready to respond, DeSantis said. The governor urged Floridians to make disaster plans and check hurricane supplies. The current forecast indicates a tropical storm or hurricane could make landfall somewhere along the central Gulf Coast later this week, the governor said in a Tuesday statement. 'Impacts are expected to extend beyond the point of landfall, with heavy rainfall, strong winds, coastal flooding and isolated tornadoes possible across North Florida,' the statement said. entry.title: Gov. Ron DeSantis announces removal of 220 Medicaid providers amid fraud, abuse investigation
entry.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis announced Tuesday that Florida's intensified effort to root out fraud, waste and abuse in the state's Medicaid program has resulted in more than $1 billion in projected savings and the removal of hundreds of providers from the system. Speaking at the Healthcare District of Palm Beach County alongside Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) Secretary Shevaun Harris, DeSantis said the state has expanded oversight and enforcement measures to identify fraudulent billing and improper Medicaid payments. entry.title: Amendment 3 supporters outspent opponents 26-to-1 as Florida Realtors poured $18 million into the race
entry.summary: The political committee supporting Amendment 3 which would raise Florida's homestead tax exemption received an $18 million cash infusion in September, campaign finance records show. The two committees opposing the amendment raised a combined $680,000, a margin of more than 26 to 1. In the coming days and weeks, voters can expect to see significant messaging urging a 'yes' vote on the amendment. WATCH BELOW: Amendment 3 backers outraise opponents 26-to-1 Amendment 3 backers outraise opponents 26-to-1 Digging deeper into those campaign finance records, I found the 'No' committees received donations from numerous corporate, individual and nonprofit contributors. Yes on 3's $18 million came from a single source: Florida Realtors. Margy Grant is the chief executive of Florida Realtors and the sole contributor to 'Yes on 3.' 'As the voice of real estate, Florida Realtors is a longtime advocate for homeowners,' Grant said. 'Families are struggling with the affordability of so many things. When you go to the grocery store, when you go to the gas station, prices just continue to climb. The one thing we can possibly control is property taxes.' You're gonna end up paying more in other ways.' entry.title: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Jensen Beach residents frustrated by recurring septic backups after storms
entry.summary: WPTV is looking into drainage and septic issues on the Treasure Coast. Neighbor Daniel Fletchall reached out to our news team about septic issues in his community on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach. WATCH BELOW: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Neighbors demand septic solution Neighbors deal with septic back-ups following heavy rainfall Fletchall said after a heavy rain, he and his neighbors' septic backs up and comes up into their yards 'The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard,' said Fletchall. 'It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out.' Fletchall said they can't even flush their toilets for days. 'I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom,' said Fletchall. Fletchall added he can't shower or wash his clothes. 'Thankfully, my parents live nearby, so I can go take a shower,' said Fletchall. 'But it's just not happening here. Fletchall isn't the only one affected by this issue. Neighbors like Christie Berger are also having septic issues every time there's heavy rain. 'I go to McDonald's to use the bathroom if I have to,' Berger said. Neighbor Rachelle Kukan said it's becoming unacceptable. 'I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could,' said Kukan. Fletchall said he had septic companies come out to fix the drainage in his yard. Elevating the septic tank, Fletchall said, would be costly, and even then he's been told it might not solve the problem. Fletchall said he'd like the Martin County staff to extend the sewer lines into his neighborhood. 'I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but Im not getting any help here,' said Fletchall. WPTV reached out to Martin County about any solutions. Staff said the neighborhood on Northwest Sunset Boulevard is on the list to get septic-to-sewer conversions, but no date has been set yet. Staff said they're looking at ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems to convert.

entry.title: 2 women arrested after shooting at Martin County tow yard sparked a chase and crash, more charges possible
entry.summary: Two women are under arrest after a shooting at Garry's Towing and Recovery in Martin County triggered a school lockout, a police chase and a separate crash. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says more charges could be coming. Jade Rondon, a Miami resident, opened fire in the tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m. WATCH BELOW: Tow yard shooting leads to arrests; more charges possible Martin County tow yard shooting: 2 women arrested, more charges possible The sheriff's office says the car she came to retrieve had been involved in criminal activity Thursday evening, then reported stolen. Detectives recovered it Friday morning. Around 1 p.m., Rondon arrived at the tow yard accompanied by another woman, Valerie Valdes. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. 'They got into some type of argument about the belongings in the car which by the way the only thing really in the car was a couple guns,' Sheriff John Budensiek said. Rondon got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into the car and leaving the area. The individuals who were shot at also left the scene before deputies arrived. Garry Reed, the owner of Garry's Towing and Recovery, said his employee was left shaken by the ordeal. 'Young lady who works in my office she was terrorized,' Reed said. Reed told me they had helped the Martin County Sheriff's Office recover the car Friday morning, but when the owner came to pick it up this afternoon, things turned dangerous. 'The young lady went to see what was going on and all of a sudden she heard gunfire,' Reed said. '[Its] scary. I'm racing my heart is racing,' Reed said. entry.title: SLC seniors demand answers as Fort Pierce center prepares to close
entry.summary: A Fort Pierce senior center is expected to close, leaving some of the older adults who rely on it worried about losing a gathering place in their own community. The Council on Aging of St. Lucie confirmed the senior center at 1505 Orange Avenue in Fort Pierce is expected to close in the near future. The property is currently listed for sale for $2.2 million. The news came as a surprise to some seniors who use the center regularly, including 77-year-old Sandy Pietrewicz. She has relied on the center for nearly a decade. That's the community center that I go to for lunch and friendship and social activities with other elderly women, said Pietrewicz. After hearing the center could be closing, Pietrewicz said she and other seniors were left with questions about what would happen to the services they depend on. We were all talking about who we could contact, and I thought of WPTV immediately, she said. WPTV reporter Brooke Chau went to the center to get answers and hear directly from the seniors who use it. The Council on Aging said the closure will not mean an end to the services provided to seniors. You're going to get the same treatment. You're going to get the same love. You're going to get the same meals, said Trekina Smith with the Council on Aging. Once the property sells, seniors who currently use the Orange Avenue location are expected to transition to the Council on Aging's facility on Bayshore Boulevard in Port St. Lucie. The organization said transportation will be provided to help seniors get to the new location. But some seniors say the location itself is important. That makes us even angrier. We can't have something in our own community, Pietrewicz said. Geneira Lovett, who also uses the center, told WPTV that seniors in Fort Pierce want to be able to access services close to where they live. We live here, we want rights to do thing, besides trouble, Lovett said. The Council on Aging said it understands those concerns, but says change is necessary. For now, the Council on Aging says services at the Orange Avenue center are continuing. There is no finalized timeline for the closure because the transition is tied to the sale of the property. We understand the concerns, it's a change for us too. But hey, change comes, and you got to go with the change, Smith said. The organization said seniors will continue to have access to meals, activities, social opportunities and transportation once services move to the Port St. Lucie location.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys & Girls Clubs of America
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys Girls Clubs of America. Enrique Rosario Liz has been named the organizations 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, a recognition that celebrates outstanding leadership, academic achievement and service to others. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys Girls Clubs of America The honor marks the latest milestone in a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, advancing to the national level of competition. In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the exciting news during a special presentation. Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.title: No arrests after 17-year-old shot, killed at meetup in Indian River County, self-defense claim expected
entry.summary: No arrests have been made in the shooting death of a 17-year-old at a teen meetup near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, with a self-defense claim expected in the case, Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Monday. WATCH BELOW: Sheriff Eric Flowers give update on shooting death of teen Indian River County Sheriff's Office gives update on shooting death of teen 'We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media,' Flowers said. The shooting occurred late Friday night when approximately 100 teens, ranging in age from 14 to 19, gathered at Garcia's Boat Ramp in the 3700 block of County Road 512, the sheriff said. Deputies had broken up a similar group earlier that evening before the crowd moved to the boat ramp. 'The 17-year-old, and a group of his friends, are approaching a truck, and there are two people, both 18 years old, inside of that truck. The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch,' Flowers said. 'He's going to punch on the people that are inside of that truck. One shot is fired. That shot is the shot that ultimately killed 17-year-old in this case.' The teen's friends drove him away from the scene, east on County Road 512, while calling 911 and a dispatcher told them to stop at Fellsmere City Hall, where emergency crews performed CPR, the sheriff said. He was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries. The two individuals in the truck were identified using the sheriff's office's Flock technology, the sheriff said. Flowers said both have been cooperative with investigators, surrendering the weapon used in the shooting and the truck. Additional individuals involved in the incident have also been identified through Flock, though some remain unidentified. Investigators also recovered other weapons from the vehicle in which the 17-year-old was transported from the scene. They had a history of fighting," Flowers said. "Self defense plays a part in these, and when these kids go out and videotape these fights, and now guns are involved, there's going to be more of this." Names of those involved are not being released as the investigation continues, the sheriff said.Investigators believe at least four fights occurred at the boat ramp on the night of the shooting. Multiple shell casings and rounds were recovered from the scene.During Monday's news conference, Flowers released video of the shooting, noting the footage had already circulated widely on social media and that the victim's mother had seen it. One of the 18-year-olds involved in the shooting attends Vero Beach High School.The sheriff said teen meetups like the one at Garcia's Boat Ramp are coordinated through Snapchat, making them difficult for law enforcement to track in advance."When it's Snapchat, it's basically a private conversation," Flowers said. "But it quickly can escalate to over 100, 150, 200 people there."Flowers said the meetups, which have included alcohol, fighting, and firearms, have been taking place for years across Indian River County, Okeechobee, and surrounding areas, but that social media has intensified the danger."Now we're adding guns and alcohol into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these," Flowers said. There's guns, and those two just don't mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead."The sheriff said teens at these gatherings are motivated in part by a desire for online attention."The kids like to fight, and they like to videotape it, and they like to get their likes and shares because of that," Flowers said. Parents, you see these videos. You do not want your teens out at these meetups."With Vero Beach High School's homecoming game scheduled for Friday and the dance on Saturday, Flowers said additional deputies will be on duty. Meanwhile, the sheriff urged parents to monitor their children's whereabouts and report any information about planned meetups to the sheriff's office."Parents, if your kids are telling you that they're headed out to one of these meetups, ask them where they're going. Ask, find out the details. Share that with us," Flowers said.He recommended parents use location-sharing apps such as Life360 to track their children and said a child appearing to be in a remote or unusual location can be an indicator that a meetup is taking place.The investigation remains active. Flowers said anyone who witnessed any of the events that night, including the shooting itself, and has not yet spoken to investigators is urged to come forward."I can tell you, our investigation is not even remotely over, and if we are able to identify people that were involved in this, from underage drinking to fighting, hurting other people," Flowers said. " If they did something wrong, they're going to have to be accountable for that."Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS.

entry.title: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County
entry.summary: A 17-year-old died after being shot near a boat ramp in Indian River County late Friday night, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded to reports of a juvenile shot in the 3700 block of County Road 512, near Garcia's Boat Ramp, at approximately 11:24 p.m. WATCH: 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp 17-year-old dies after shooting near Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County The sheriff's office said deputies found the 17-year-old and began lifesaving measures until Indian River County Fire Rescue arrived. The teen was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center before being flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center, where he died from his injuries. Detectives with the sheriff's office's Criminal Investigations Division and crime scene personnel are processing the scene and interviewing multiple witnesses. Investigators said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public. No information about a possible suspect or what led up to the shooting has been released. Anyone with information is asked to call the Indian River County Sheriff's Office at 772-569-6700 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: Martin County employee, avid surfer rescues 3 girls from rip current at Bob Graham Beach
entry.summary: A Martin County employee helped rescue three girls who were struggling in a rip current Thursday afternoon at Bob Graham Beach near Jensen Beach. Amy Offenbach said she arrived at the beach around 2 p.m. to surf when she noticed three girls about 25 yards offshore holding onto the same surfboard. Watch report: Martin County employee rescues 3 girls caught in rip current at Bob Graham Beach Offenbach, who works in Martin County's Growth and Development Department and is an avid surfer, said something about the situation immediately caught her attention. 'The ocean could be very gentle and calm, but it can also be very heavy and crash very hard,' Offenbach said. Rescue unfolds offshore Offenbach said she became concerned when one of the girls appeared distressed. 'That kind of struck me as strange,' she said. 'The other one seemed a little agitated.' Moments later, a girl on the beach told Offenbach she believed her friends needed help. 'By that time the girls were waving in the water like they needed help, so immediately I just went into rescue mode,' Offenbach said. She then placed the third girl on her soft-top surfboard and paddled her back to the beach. entry.article_text: A 33-year-old man has been arrested on a first-degree murder charge in connection with the August shooting death of a woman in Vero Beach, according to the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. Matthew Allen Waggle was arrested Oct. 5 on an active warrant and is being held without bond. The warrant accuses him of killing Dawn Marie Kriskewic on Aug. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 According to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, deputies responded to the 500 block of 1st Street after 911 callers reported a woman lying in the roadway. Deputies found Kriskewic with injuries that appeared consistent with gunshot wounds and began CPR. She was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she was pronounced dead. Investigators identified Waggle as Kriskewic's former boyfriend. A coworker told detectives that Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle before her death. The coworker also told investigators that Waggle had previously threatened consequences if Kriskewic called police when he came to retrieve his belongings. Detectives said surveillance footage showed a person they identified as Waggle near the area around the time of the shooting. Investigators also recovered a rolling suitcase containing men's clothing and a tactical vest with a "security" patch near the crime scene. A Ruger pistol was found on a neighboring property along with a note stating that another person had given Waggle permission to use the firearm for firearm qualifications, according to the affidavit. Additional surveillance footage cited by investigators showed Waggle walking through the area before and after the shooting. Detectives said footage also showed him discarding a shirt, which investigators later recovered. A judge signed the first-degree murder warrant for Waggle on Aug. He was taken into custody at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say - WFLX
entry.summary: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say    WFLX
entry.article_text: A Martin County woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after deputies say she buried several cats alive in her yard at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office arrested 37-year-old Alba Luz Chavez on four counts of aggravated animal cruelty after investigators said they discovered two live kittens and two dead kittens buried on a property in Hobe Sound. Deputies were called to the home Thursday night for what family members described as a mental health crisis. Family members told deputies Chavez believed the cats were demons and had killed several animals earlier in the week. According to the affidavit, deputies learned that Chavez had allegedly told residents of the home she killed two kittens on Monday, Oct. Three juveniles living at the residence told deputies Chavez had appeared to be experiencing a mental health episode for most of the week. The juveniles said they locked three surviving kittens inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday evening. When they returned around 6 p.m., they discovered Chavez had forced her way into the room and the kittens were gone. Investigators said Chavez initially refused to tell family members where the animals were. However, while speaking with deputies, Chavez allegedly said, “If you want the cats, you will need gloves, a red bag and a shovel,” and directed them to an area on the property. Deputies began digging and found two live kittens buried underground inside plastic Publix bags, according to the affidavit. Investigators later uncovered two deceased kittens that appeared to be in the early stages of decomposition. Detectives searched for a third missing kitten but were unable to locate it. During an interview, Chavez told investigators she had been cleaning her house and referred to the cats as “very ugly,” according to the affidavit. Investigators wrote that Chavez also made statements indicating she did not want black cats and suggested kittens of different colors “had different fates.” The affidavit states Chavez later began singing instead of answering additional questions. The two surviving kittens were taken to a pet emergency center for treatment. A veterinarian told investigators the kittens were about three weeks old and very weak. The veterinarian said it was too early to determine whether a lack of oxygen while confined inside the plastic bags had caused brain damage or other medical complications. The two deceased kittens are expected to undergo necropsies to determine their exact causes of death. Chavez was arrested and booked into the Martin County Jail on four felony counts of aggravated animal cruelty and is being held without bond.

entry.title: Jury convicts former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms of official misconduct - WPEC
entry.summary: Jury convicts former Fort Pierce city manager Nick Mimms of official misconduct    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie County jury convicted former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms of official misconduct Thursday, finding he improperly obstructed, delayed or prevented information about a possible felony involving the city from being communicated. Jurors found Mimms not guilty of bid tampering, the first count he faced. But they found him guilty on the official-misconduct count and specifically determined the misconduct involved obstructing, delaying or preventing communication of information related to a possible felony that directly involved or affected the government entity he served. The verdict followed a trial that began Sept. 29 and centered on allegations that Mimms improperly influenced the city’s bidding process for two vacant Lincoln Park-area lots. Prosecutors alleged Mimms steered the process toward Lincoln Park Young Professionals , a nonprofit whose board included his niece and another city employee. The organization sought a lease involving the properties, near the Lincoln Theater. During trial, FDLE Agent Derek Brisky testified about emails, city records and the request-for-proposals process. Prosecutors pointed to communications showing Mimms continued to discuss the RFP’s evaluation criteria and committee after the matter had been referred to the city’s purchasing department. The defense argued the purchasing department controlled the RFP’s publication and administration, and challenged the state’s claim that the process amounted to an improper sole-source arrangement. See also: 4 people arrested after drugs, 26 firearms found at North Palm Beach home Court records show Circuit Judge Michael James Linn denied the state’s request to have Mimms taken into custody pending sentencing. Mimms was allowed to remain free on bond. Sentencing is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. Lucie County Circuit Court.

entry.title: Isaias weakens after Gulf Coast landfall, bringing flooding threat to South
entry.summary: Hurricane Isaias became the first hurricane to make direct landfall in the United States in more than two years when it came ashore late Friday as a Category 2 storm. By Saturday morning, Isaias had weakened into a post-tropical cyclone as it moved across Alabama. While no longer a hurricane, its remnants were expected to bring heavy rain and gusty winds across parts of the South on Saturday before spreading into the Great Lakes and Northeast on Sunday. As of 6 a.m. CT Saturday, more than 900,000 customers were without power. More than 400,000 outages were reported in Florida's Panhandle, while Alabama reported more than 320,000 outages and Georgia reported about 120,000. The storm also caused significant wind damage in the Pensacola area, where a hotel lost its roof as Isaias made landfall. RELATED STORY | Study: Super-sized El Nio could cause more than 450,000 heat deaths by February The hurricane pushed storm surge onto coastal roadways across the Florida Panhandle. No deaths or injuries associated with the storm had been reported as of early Saturday morning. Isaias marked a departure from what had been one of the quietest Atlantic hurricane seasons in recent years. It was also the first hurricane to form in the Atlantic basin in 2026. Forecasters had predicted a below-normal season because of a strong El Nio, which typically creates upper-level winds that can disrupt tropical cyclone development. Although Isaias was the ninth named storm of the season, all previous systems had peaked at tropical-storm strength. The same upper-level winds that limited hurricane activity this year also contributed to Isaias weakening before landfall. The storm maintained Category 3 strength for much of Friday before being downgraded to a Category 2 hurricane just hours before reaching the coast. RELATED STORY | El Nino keeps Atlantic hurricane season historically calm Behind Isaias, the National Hurricane Center said it was not tracking any additional systems. The Atlantic hurricane season typically peaks around Sept. 10 and begins to wind down by mid-October before ending Nov. 30. Since 2013, only two hurricanes have made U.S. landfall after Oct. 15. The most recent was Hurricane Nicole in 2022.

entry.title: Power and rescue crews mobilize in Florida as Isaias pushes north
entry.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the Florida Panhandle near Destin on Friday night with 105 mph winds. Gov. Ron DeSantis said in a news conference a short time later that power outages spanned from Pensacola to Panama City to Tallahassee. entry.title: Explosion inside Port St. Lucie home leaves family with little to salvage - WPBF
entry.summary: Explosion inside Port St. Lucie home leaves family with little to salvage    WPBF
entry.article_text: An explosion inside a Port St. Lucie home destroyed almost everything owned by a family of four. Lucie County Fire District, the initial call came in at 1:24 p.m. for a fire at a home in the 100 block of Carmelite Street Friday afternoon. Neighbors called 911 after noticing the home was on fire. "I looked, and there was all kinds of smoke going through the yard," said neighbor Rob Roadman. "I was outside in the backyard, and then I see very heavy smoke," said Marina Cheong, who lives a few doors down. Cheong said she ran toward the home to help but was stopped by the explosion. "And then there was explosion, very loud, loud explosion, and debris started flying everywhere," she said. "I heard a huge explosion. At first, I thought maybe it's a transformer or something, but it was much, much, much louder than that," Roadman said. Neighbors said the man who lives in the home told them he had been cooking when a grease fire started in the garage, where the propane tank was located. The explosion sent the propane tank flying out of the garage, across the street, and into the garage of a neighbor's home. "I thought it was an air raid. It was not a casual thing. My house shook," Roadman said. "I thought that the whole house had exploded. It was very loud," Cheong added. Roadman said he spoke to the man shortly after the explosion. "I asked the dad if he was OK, and he goes, 'Yeah.' But you could tell he wasn't. Who wouldn't be?" Roadman said. The man was briefly hospitalized but returned to the house a few hours later to join family and friends in going through the debris to see what could be salvaged. They said there wasn’t much left. However, a family member told WPBF 25 News that they consider themselves lucky that nobody was seriously injured. She said the family has a strong community and a strong church to help them persevere. entry.title: Deputies hear cries underground, rescue 2 kittens buried alive in Hobe Sound - cw34.com
entry.summary: Deputies hear cries underground, rescue 2 kittens buried alive in Hobe Sound    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Deputies digging through a rain-soaked backyard in Martin County heard the cries of kittens buried up to 3 feet underground, leading to the rescue of two animals while two others were found dead, the sheriff revealed Friday. During a news conference, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek provided new details about the arrest of 36-year-old Alba Chavez, who is accused of killing two kittens and burying two others alive at a mobile home park in Hobe Sound. According to the sheriff's office, deputies responded to the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park on Thursday night after several minors inside the home called 911 to report that Chavez had allegedly killed two kittens Monday, placed them in the trash and later buried them in the backyard. The children, who feared for the safety of three remaining kittens, attempted to protect them by locking them inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday night. Budensiek said that when the children returned home, they discovered the bedroom door had been forced open and the kittens were missing. The children then called law enforcement to report the incident. When deputies arrived, Chavez was standing in the roadway and reportedly admitted to killing the two kittens. While speaking with deputies, Chavez said she believed the kittens had demons, described them as ugly and said she did not want black or brown cats inside the home. Chavez then led deputies to the backyard, where the kittens had allegedly been buried. "She took them to the backyard where our deputies started digging frantically trying to recover what they believed to be three live kittens and two dead kittens," Budensiek said. See also: Hurricane Isaias strengthens into major Category 3 storm near Florida Panhandle As deputies dug through the backyard, they heard cries coming from underground. Two kittens were recovered alive, while the two kittens Chavez allegedly killed Monday were found dead. A fifth kitten remains missing despite repeated searches of the property. Budensiek said the two surviving kittens were immediately taken to an emergency veterinary facility, where they were being treated for dehydration. The sheriff said veterinarians were also concerned about possible injuries caused by a lack of oxygen while the kittens were buried. Despite being rescued, the kittens could still die from their injuries. Chavez was arrested and charged with four counts of animal torture involving pain, serious injury or death, according to the sheriff's office. The four charges correspond to the two kittens found dead and the two rescued alive. The sheriff said Chavez was being held without bond at the Martin County Jail and also had an immigration hold. Investigators have not determined exactly how the first two kittens died. The sheriff said Chavez initially cooperated with deputies and led them to the burial site but later stopped answering questions about how the animals were killed. Authorities also have not determined her motive. Budensiek said deputies had previously responded to calls involving Chavez's mental health but had received no prior animal cruelty complaints at the residence. Additional charges could be filed if the fifth kitten is found dead, according to the sheriff. Following the incident, the Florida Department of Children and Families became involved, and the children were later released to their father, who lives locally. Officials said resources were available to help the children cope with what happened.

entry.title: DeSantis: Nearly 450,000 without power after Hurricane Isaias, but no confirmed storm deaths in Florida
entry.summary: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said Saturday morning that nearly 450,000 utility customers remained without power across Northwest Florida after Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the Panhandle , but state officials had not confirmed any storm-related fatalities as recovery efforts continued. Speaking during a statewide briefing, DeSantis said the storm came ashore near Destin at 9:30 p.m. Friday as a Category 2 hurricane with sustained winds of about 105 mph. Wind gusts reached as high as 116 mph near Santa Rosa Sound, while storm surge pushed water levels approximately 5.5 feet above normal in some areas. WATCH BELOW: Santa Rosa County among hardest hit counties, DeSantis says DeSantis: Nearly 450,000 without power after Hurricane Isaias Although the storm has since weakened into a post-tropical cyclone and moved out of Florida, DeSantis warned that flooding remains a concern, particularly in parts of the Panhandle and Big Bend expected to receive 4 to 8 inches of rain through the weekend. 'As of now there have been no confirmed fatalities,' DeSantis said, noting reports of a possible death in Escambia County linked to a fallen tree had not yet been confirmed by the state. State officials said more than 16,000 linemen were staged ahead of the storm and began restoration efforts as early as 3 a.m. Saturday. By 7 a.m., approximately 448,000 customer accounts were without electricity statewide, including about 323,000 Florida Power Light customers and roughly 110,000 customers served by electric cooperatives. Some of the hardest-hit counties included Santa Rosa County, where about 90% of customers were without power, Holmes County at 89%, Washington County at 86%, Walton County at 85%, Escambia County at 75% and Okaloosa County at 53%, according to the governor. The Florida Department of Transportation and Florida Highway Patrol launched overnight 'cut and toss' operations to clear roads of fallen trees and debris. Officials said all state-owned bridges had been inspected and reopened by 6 a.m. Saturday. Interstate 10 and U.S. 98, two major transportation corridors in the region, were also reopened. Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport resumed commercial operations Saturday morning, while Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport and Pensacola International Airport remained closed. Despite the storm's impacts, state emergency officials said they had not received any requests for large-scale search and rescue deployments. Florida Division of Emergency Management

Officials said all state-owned bridges had been inspected and reopened by 6 a.m. 98, two major transportation corridors in the region, were also reopened.Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport resumed commercial operations Saturday morning, while Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport and Pensacola International Airport remained closed.Despite the storm's impacts, state emergency officials said they had not received any requests for large-scale search and rescue deployments.Florida Division of Emergency Management Executive Director Jared Perdue said state teams remain on standby as flood risks continue."We are going to keep search and rescue teams ready to go," Perdue said. "There could be continued flooding from all of the rainfall."Officials urged residents to avoid driving through flooded roadways, stay clear of downed power lines and limit unnecessary travel while utility crews and emergency workers continue recovery efforts.Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier also warned residents to watch for scams in the aftermath of the storm, including reports of fraudulent text messages offering tree-removal services and unlicensed contractors seeking repair work.State officials said damage assessments are underway and will help determine whether Florida qualifies for additional federal disaster aid beyond the pre-landfall emergency declaration already approved by FEMA.DeSantis said he planned to visit storm-damaged areas in the Panhandle later Saturday, including parts of Okaloosa County, to assess conditions and meet with local officials."We were ready for the worst," DeSantis said. "We'll get everything back up and running and let people go on with their lives as soon as possible."

entry.title: Isaias weakens after Gulf Coast landfall, bringing flooding threat to South
entry.summary: Hurricane Isaias became the first hurricane to make direct landfall in the United States in more than two years when it came ashore late Friday as a Category 2 storm. By Saturday morning, Isaias had weakened into a post-tropical cyclone as it moved across Alabama. While no longer a hurricane, its remnants were expected to bring heavy rain and gusty winds across parts of the South on Saturday before spreading into the Great Lakes and Northeast on Sunday. As of 6 a.m. CT Saturday, more than 900,000 customers were without power. More than 400,000 outages were reported in Florida's Panhandle, while Alabama reported more than 320,000 outages and Georgia reported about 120,000. The storm also caused significant wind damage in the Pensacola area, where a hotel lost its roof as Isaias made landfall. RELATED STORY | Study: Super-sized El Nio could cause more than 450,000 heat deaths by February The hurricane pushed storm surge onto coastal roadways across the Florida Panhandle. Escambia County Sheriff Chip W. Simmons confirmed one person died during the storm. He added that some roads were impassable due to downed trees and power lines. Away from the coast, a death was reported in Birmingham, Alabama, due to a fallen tree limb. Isaias marked a departure from what had been one of the quietest Atlantic hurricane seasons in recent years. It was also the first hurricane to form in the Atlantic basin in 2026. Forecasters had predicted a below-normal season because of a strong El Nio, which typically creates upper-level winds that can disrupt tropical cyclone development. Although Isaias was the ninth named storm of the season, all previous systems had peaked at tropical-storm strength. The same upper-level winds that limited hurricane activity this year also contributed to Isaias weakening before landfall. The storm maintained Category 3 strength for much of Friday before being downgraded to a Category 2 hurricane just hours before reaching the coast. RELATED STORY | El Nino keeps Atlantic hurricane season historically calm Behind Isaias, the National Hurricane Center said it was not tracking any additional systems. The Atlantic hurricane season typically peaks around Sept. 10 and begins to wind down by mid-October before ending Nov. 30. Since 2013, only two hurricanes have made U.S. landfall after Oct. 15. The most recent was Hurricane Nicole in 2022.

entry.article_text: A Martin County employee is being praised for her quick actions after rescuing a girl from drowning at Bob Graham Beach in Stuart on Thursday afternoon. Amy Offenbach, who came to the beach to surf, said the day took an unexpected turn. "It was just by chance that we were here and thank God that we were at the right time," Offenbach said. Offenbach, who has years of lifeguard training, said her instincts kicked in when she saw three girls struggling in the water. "I took off my clothes, grabbed the board, and started paddling," she said. "I immediately went into rescue mode." Authorities said one of the girls was choking on water, and the beach had no lifeguards on duty. Offenbach rushed in to help, using a surfboard to stabilize the girl. "Once she was on the board, she was kind of limp. Her body wasn't doing anything else," Offenbach said. Offenbach said the girl's forehead felt cold, prompting her to rush the child to the nearest lifeguard stand down the road. The girl was then taken to the hospital with minor drowning injuries. "I'm just really thankful that her parents have their child," Offenbach said. Offenbach, a Martin County employee, said she doesn’t feel the need for recognition. While some are calling her a hero, Offenbach said she was simply acting on her instincts as a mother. "I have a 14-year-old son myself, and I can't imagine him not coming back from hanging out at the beach with his friends," she said. The incident serves as a reminder to exercise caution at the beach, especially in areas without lifeguards. The investigation remains ongoing as detectives continue to examine the circumstances surrounding the crash. Investigators said the vehicle involved was a 2002 Ford Excursion. According to police, the driver initially believed he had struck a construction barrel and did not realize he had hit a person. The driver later made a U-turn at the next safe location, returned to the scene, activated his hazard lights and found the teenager unconscious on the side of the roadway. Lucie County Fire District, the initial call came in at 1:24 p.m. for a fire at a home in the 100 block of Carmelite Street Friday afternoon. Neighbors called 911 after noticing the home was on fire. "I looked, and there was all kinds of smoke going through the yard," said neighbor Rob Roadman. "I was outside in the backyard, and then I see very heavy smoke," said Marina Cheong, who lives a few doors down. Cheong said she ran toward the home to help but was stopped by the explosion. "And then there was explosion, very loud, loud explosion, and debris started flying everywhere," she said. "I heard a huge explosion. At first, I thought maybe it's a transformer or something, but it was much, much, much louder than that," Roadman said. Neighbors said the man who lives in the home told them he had been cooking when a grease fire started in the garage, where the propane tank was located. The explosion sent the propane tank flying out of the garage, across the street, and into the garage of a neighbor's home. "I thought it was an air raid. It was not a casual thing. My house shook," Roadman said. "I thought that the whole house had exploded. It was very loud," Cheong added. Roadman said he spoke to the man shortly after the explosion. "I asked the dad if he was OK, and he goes, 'Yeah.' But you could tell he wasn't. Who wouldn't be?" Roadman said. The man was briefly hospitalized but returned to the house a few hours later to join family and friends in going through the debris to see what could be salvaged. They said there wasn’t much left. However, a family member told WPBF 25 News that they consider themselves lucky that nobody was seriously injured. She said the family has a strong community and a strong church to help them persevere. The family has set up a GoFundMe account for donations. entry.summary: 'A strong support system': Community helps injured father after Port St. Lucie house fire    WPEC
entry.article_text: A fire that spread through the garage of a Port St. Lucie home Friday afternoon left a father injured and displaced a family, while neighbors and church members rallied to help them begin the cleanup process. The fire happened on Carmelite Street in the Northport Village neighborhood near St. According to the family, the fire started in the kitchen before spreading through the garage. They say a propane tank later exploded, causing additional damage and impacting a neighbor's garage doors across the street. Lucie County Fire District responded to the home around 1:30 p.m. Crews arrived to find heavy fire coming from the garage. When firefighters extinguished the flames, significant damage was left behind, including a charred garage door, blackened walls and belongings covered in soot. Renter Nigel Laidlow was inside the home when the fire broke out. He suffered burns to his legs and was transported for medical treatment. "I don't even know how to describe it. It was really surreal," Laidlow said. "I would've never thought a little fire would turn into this." By Saturday, family photos, furniture and other belongings were spread across the front yard as loved ones worked to salvage what they could. Members of the Fort Pierce Seventh-day Adventist Church spent the day helping move and sort through damaged items. "We have a really strong support system, especially from my church," Laidlow said. Despite the loss, Laidlow said he is grateful his family survived. "This right here is something not anybody would like to deal with. Not in a lifetime," he said. See also: MCSO warns scam emails may trick development applicants into wiring money The family is now focused on recovering and determining its next steps. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.
