entry.title: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say - WFLX
entry.summary: Hobe Sound woman buried cats alive because she believed they were demons, deputies say    WFLX
entry.article_text: A Martin County woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after deputies say she buried several cats alive in her yard at the Hobe Sound Mobile Home Park. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office arrested 37-year-old Alba Luz Chavez on four counts of aggravated animal cruelty after investigators said they discovered two live kittens and two dead kittens buried on a property in Hobe Sound. Deputies were called to the home Thursday night for what family members described as a mental health crisis. Family members told deputies Chavez believed the cats were demons and had killed several animals earlier in the week. According to the affidavit, deputies learned that Chavez had allegedly told residents of the home she killed two kittens on Monday, Oct. Three juveniles living at the residence told deputies Chavez had appeared to be experiencing a mental health episode for most of the week. The juveniles said they locked three surviving kittens inside a bedroom before leaving for dinner Thursday evening. When they returned around 6 p.m., they discovered Chavez had forced her way into the room and the kittens were gone. Investigators said Chavez initially refused to tell family members where the animals were. However, while speaking with deputies, Chavez allegedly said, “If you want the cats, you will need gloves, a red bag and a shovel,” and directed them to an area on the property. Deputies began digging and found two live kittens buried underground inside plastic Publix bags, according to the affidavit. Investigators later uncovered two deceased kittens that appeared to be in the early stages of decomposition. Detectives searched for a third missing kitten but were unable to locate it. During an interview, Chavez told investigators she had been cleaning her house and referred to the cats as “very ugly,” according to the affidavit. Investigators wrote that Chavez also made statements indicating she did not want black cats and suggested kittens of different colors “had different fates.” The affidavit states Chavez later began singing instead of answering additional questions. The two surviving kittens were taken to a pet emergency center for treatment. A veterinarian told investigators the kittens were about three weeks old and very weak. The veterinarian said it was too early to determine whether a lack of oxygen while confined inside the plastic bags had caused brain damage or other medical complications. The two deceased kittens are expected to undergo necropsies to determine their exact causes of death. Chavez was arrested and booked into the Martin County Jail on four felony counts of aggravated animal cruelty and is being held without bond.

entry.article_text: The man accused of crossing state lines and traveling to Indian River County to kill his ex-girlfriend was booked into the Indian River County Jail on Monday. According to Indian River County Jail records, Matthew Waggle, 33, was booked into the Indian River County Jail at around 5:20 a.m. He faces a charge of first-degree murder. CBS12 reported on the August shooting after authorities found the victim's body, identified as Dawn Kriskewic , in a roadway in the southern part of the county. Investigators say Waggle traveled to Vero Beach by bus and Uber before allegedly killing Kriskewic outside her home Sunday morning. See also: FHP: Wrong-way driver caused deadly I-95 crash Sunday near PB Lakes Boulevard Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said surveillance video captured Waggle walking through Kriskewic's neighborhood shortly after an Uber dropped him off. Investigators say Waggle then left the area, taking an Uber back to Orlando before boarding another Greyhound bus. He eventually made his way to West Virginia, where investigators say he hid at a motel. Flowers said at the time that Flock Safety cameras were instrumental in tracking down Waggle. Authorities had later tracked Waggle to a motel in West Virginia and taken him into custody. Authorities said Kriskewic had ended her relationship with Waggle before the shooting and had warned coworkers at the hair salon that she wanted no contact with him.

Hundreds of thousands of people lost power in the wake of the storm, and 430,000 customers remained without power Saturday morning. As of Sunday afternoon, more than 200,000 customers had power restored, DeSantis said. FLP is expected to be largely finished with power restoration efforts by Monday. 'I know its frustrating to lose power and some of you have been without it for a couple of days now... The state park was closed after a bridge washout, but DeSantis said the park was expected to reopen Sunday night after substantial recovery efforts. entry.title: Treasure Coast travelers say limited transportation options make it 'difficult to get around'
entry.summary: A recent change to a flight out of Vero Beach is sparking a bigger conversation about travel options on the Treasure Coast. Travelers tell WPTV limited flight schedules and a lack of convenient transportation alternatives can make getting in and out of the area difficult, sometimes forcing them to drive to larger airports or rearrange their plans. WATCH: Why Treasure Coast travelers say they need more options At the Vero Beach Regional Airport, travelers shared their frustrations with WPTV reporter Brooke Chau about the challenges of getting where they need to go. In the Treasure Coast area, Vero Beach specifically, it is difficult to get around, said Peter Masella. He pointed to the lack of a Brightline station in Vero Beach, saying people often have to travel to other cities to access additional transportation options. A recent schedule change to Breeze Airways' route between Vero Beach and the New York area has added to those concerns. The flight, which previously departed Vero Beach in the evening, now leaves in the morning. A New York City physician told WPTV the change has affected his work schedule. Im a physician working in New York City and because of the change of flight for Vero Beach, I have had to rearrange my patients schedule two days in a row, he said. Another traveler from Westchester, New York said the change can mean a longer trip. Then I have to take a taxi all the way down and around to Vero Beach. Its very inconvenient, she said. However, Breeze Airways has also been adding destinations from Vero Beach. Last month, the airline introduced nonstop service to Trenton, Baltimore, Pittsburgh and Atlantic City, expanding the airport's commercial flight options. Vero Beach Airport Director, Brandon Dambeck, says airlines regularly evaluate the performance of their routes, which can lead to new destinations as well as schedule or route changes. All of these airlines are monitoring the routes and their gauge of success,' Dambeck said. For travelers, more destinations are welcome, but they say flight times that fit their schedules are just as important.

entry.title: Martin County employee, avid surfer rescues 3 girls from rip current at Bob Graham Beach
entry.summary: A Martin County employee helped rescue three girls who were struggling in a rip current Thursday afternoon at Bob Graham Beach near Jensen Beach. Amy Offenbach said she arrived at the beach around 2 p.m. to surf when she noticed three girls about 25 yards offshore holding onto the same surfboard. Watch report: Martin County employee rescues 3 girls caught in rip current at Bob Graham Beach Offenbach, who works in Martin County's Growth and Development Department and is an avid surfer, said something about the situation immediately caught her attention. 'The ocean could be very gentle and calm, but it can also be very heavy and crash very hard,' Offenbach said. Rescue unfolds offshore Offenbach said she became concerned when one of the girls appeared distressed. 'That kind of struck me as strange,' she said. 'The other one seemed a little agitated.' Moments later, a girl on the beach told Offenbach she believed her friends needed help. 'By that time the girls were waving in the water like they needed help, so immediately I just went into rescue mode,' Offenbach said. Offenbach and a friend went into the water and paddled toward the girls. Bringing the girls to safety When Offenbach reached the group, she said one of the girls appeared to be in serious distress. 'I looked at her, and she seemed kind of dazed and confused,' Offenbach said. 'I said, 'Get up on the board.'' Offenbach said she gave the surfboard she was riding to two of the girls and instructed them to hold on and kick toward shore. She then placed the third girl on her soft-top surfboard and paddled her back to the beach. entry.title: Port St. Lucie intersection floods so badly a pizza shop 'lost thousands'; city says fix will take time
entry.summary: WPTV is continuing to follow flooding issues at the intersection of California and Savona boulevards in Port St. Lucie.   The water has receded, but earlier this week , the intersection looked like a lake. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie flooding hits pizza shop hard as city works on fix Flooding issues continue at this Port St. Lucie intersection WPTV is pressing city leaders about any solution to keep the water levels down. Neighbors shared video of the roadways, looking like a river. 'We were actually calling it the California River, as a joke,' said Joe Dascoli, who works at Estella Pizzaria right of the intersection. 'It becomes like an island around here.' That island is a shopping plaza where the pizza shop is located. Due to the flooding on Thursday, Dascoli said they had to close early. 'It's an ongoing thing that you know should be resolved,' said Dascoli. Dascoli told WPTV customers couldn't go in and orders couldn't go out during this weeks flooding. 'We've lost thousands of dollars just in revenue and people not being able to come in,' said Dascoli. 'Some of our drivers, their cars aren't capable of going through the floods, so we have to stop deliveries.' WPTV pressed the city of Port St. Lucie about any solutions to the flooding. Scott Samples with the city said it's starting a pilot program for water level sensors at flood-prone areas in the city. 'There'll be alerts that'll be able to go to Public Works and the police to say, 'Hey, this area is seeing rapid flooding,' so they might be able to respond quicker,' said Samples. Samples said long-term solutions include a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood. The project includes two new retention ponds, baffle boxes to collect runoff, and even raising sections of the roadway at California and Savona boulevards. Right now, Samples said the project is in the data collection phase before moving on to design. 'This is one of the highest priorities that we have in terms of capital investment projects, and so it's going to take time,' said Samples.

entry.title: Jupiter HarbourFest brings free music, food and community fun
entry.summary: Jupiter HarbourFest is returning to Harbourside Place this Friday and Saturday, offering two days of live music, local food, vendors and family-friendly fun along the Jupiter waterfront. The festival, presented by Jupiter Medical Center and organized by the Palm Beach North Chamber of Commerce, is free to attend for general admission guests this year. 'It's a great event,' said Brian of the Palm Beach North Chamber of Commerce. 'Thanks to our sponsors, we're able to put on the event for free for general admission.' In addition to free admission, attendees can purchase tickets for special experiences, including the festival's Tastings event and VIP areas. Organizers describe HarbourFest as a coastal country music festival featuring food trucks, local restaurants, vendors and performances spread across two stages. Among the participating restaurants are Tommy Bahama and the Wyndham, both of which showcased dishes ahead of the event. Tommy Bahama will offer some of its most popular menu items, including its coconut shrimp and house-made key lime pie. 'We're going to feature two dishes, kind of the fan favorites of Tommy Bahama,' said Kyle from Tommy Bahama. The Wyndham plans to feature a braised beef shank prepared with Mediterranean spices, saffron cream sauce and orzo pasta. Live music will also be a major part of the festival experience. Local band BOXELDER will perform during the event, bringing its signature sound to the waterfront celebration. Festival organizers say HarbourFest aims to combine music, food and community while highlighting the businesses, restaurants and attractions that make Jupiter a popular destination in northern Palm Beach County. More information, including VIP ticket options, can be found at JupiterHarbourFest.org . entry.title: LET'S HEAR IT: Okeechobee nonprofit hopes to bring Traveling Vietnam Wall to local veterans
entry.summary: At a Lets Hear It event in Okeechobee last month,, WPTV anchor and Navy veteran Mike Trim spoke with a local veteran dedicated to serving fellow vets. Gregg Maynard, an Army veteran and founder of the nonprofit Thank You For Your Service, helps disabled veterans through projects such as building wheelchair ramps and providing other assistance. WATCH: Okeechobee Traveling Vietnam Wall Now, Maynard is working to bring the Traveling Vietnam Memorial Wall to Okeechobee. He hopes the display will give local Vietnam veterans, especially those unable to travel to Washington, D.C., the opportunity to experience the memorial and reflect on their service. Not only does it help those veterans who may never make the trip to D.C., but I think these stories and what these guys went through can also be an educational experience for kids, Maynard told Trim. It gives them a chance to learn. Maynard said it costs thousands of dollars to bring the wall to the area and is raising funds through his nonprofit. Those interested in supporting the effort can contact him at thankyouforyourservice34972@gmail.com . Ultimately, Maynard hopes the memorial will have a meaningful impact on the local Vietnam veteran community. I want them to feel appreciated, Maynard said. But most importantly, if it helps just one Vietnam veteran, then all the work and effort that goes into making this happen will be worth it.

entry.title: Palm Beach Atlantic University celebrates Hispanic heritage through art, music festival
entry.summary: Palm Beach Atlantic University wrapped up its three-day Hispanic Heritage Festival on Saturday, celebrating Hispanic art, culture and music during Hispanic Heritage Month in South Florida. The annual festival featured a contemporary art exhibition and a series of musical performances designed to showcase the cultural contributions and artistic traditions of the Hispanic world. Organizers say the event continues to grow as it enters its 17th year. Palm Beach Atlantic University celebrates Hispanic heritage through art, music festival In a region with a large Hispanic population, organizers say the festival provides an opportunity for students and community members to engage with artists and musicians while learning more about the diversity of Hispanic cultures. Artists from across the Hispanic world The festival began Thursday with an art exhibition featuring artists representing more than 10 countries. Visitors viewed a wide range of artistic styles and mediums, including oil paintings, photography and metalwork. Among the featured artists was Franco Sotillo, a visual artist originally from Lima, Peru, who said his work combines mixed media and reflects both his heritage and personal experiences. 'I'm a visual artist and came from Lima, Peru,' Sotillo said. 'I moved to this country 12 years ago.' Sotillo said his work incorporates materials including oils, paper and other raw elements. He said sharing his art allows him to introduce audiences to Peruvian artistic expression. 'I'm an immigrant, but also bringing my culture to the states to show people how Peruvian art is expressed,' Sotillo said. entry.title: 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors
entry.summary: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico returned to the campaign trail over the weekend after a 12-day absence that fueled speculation about his whereabouts. His opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, and other Republicans questioned Talarico's explanation that he had been home with the flu. At one point, Paxton called for 'proof of life' in a social media post questioning Talarico's whereabouts. The speculation included unsubstantiated claims circulating online that Talarico had been receiving treatment at a mental health facility in Ohio. I had the flu,' Talarico insisted in an interview with MS Now on Sunday. 'This is the craziest thing Ive ever heard. Its wild that someone can just post something on the internet and then the media just runs with it.' The rumors prompted the Lindner Center of HOPE to publicly deny that Talarico had been a patient. 'Representative James Talarico has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope,' Lindner Center HOPE posted on X. Talarico responded to the post by saying, 'Ive never even been to Ohio ' Over the weekend, Talarico was seen meeting with potential voters at the Austin City Limits Music Festival. He also attended a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas on Saturday, where he met with the country singer. The Texas Senate contest is among the most closely watched races in the country as Democrats seek their first statewide election victory in more than 30 years.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 54-year-old Jupiter woman is facing felony charges after she allegedly removed fentanyl from a critically ill patient's IV infusion while working at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said Monday. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Investigators learned a family member reported witnessing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Pope was not assigned to the patient's care. The next evening, Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room and again approached the IV equipment, police said. The family member intervened. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the agency said in a news release. "We remain committed to thorough, evidence-based investigations and pursuing accountability when the evidence supports criminal charges." This remains an active criminal case. entry.title: Explosion inside Port St. Lucie home leaves family with little to salvage - WPBF
entry.summary: Explosion inside Port St. Lucie home leaves family with little to salvage    WPBF
entry.article_text: An explosion inside a Port St. Lucie home destroyed almost everything owned by a family of four. Lucie County Fire District, the initial call came in at 1:24 p.m. for a fire at a home in the 100 block of Carmelite Street Friday afternoon. Neighbors called 911 after noticing the home was on fire. "I looked, and there was all kinds of smoke going through the yard," said neighbor Rob Roadman. "I was outside in the backyard, and then I see very heavy smoke," said Marina Cheong, who lives a few doors down. Cheong said she ran toward the home to help but was stopped by the explosion. "And then there was explosion, very loud, loud explosion, and debris started flying everywhere," she said. "I heard a huge explosion. At first, I thought maybe it's a transformer or something, but it was much, much, much louder than that," Roadman said. Neighbors said the man who lives in the home told them he had been cooking when a grease fire started in the garage, where the propane tank was located. The explosion sent the propane tank flying out of the garage, across the street, and into the garage of a neighbor's home. "I thought it was an air raid. It was not a casual thing. My house shook," Roadman said. "I thought that the whole house had exploded. It was very loud," Cheong added. Roadman said he spoke to the man shortly after the explosion. "I asked the dad if he was OK, and he goes, 'Yeah.' But you could tell he wasn't. Who wouldn't be?" Roadman said. The man was briefly hospitalized but returned to the house a few hours later to join family and friends in going through the debris to see what could be salvaged. They said there wasn’t much left. However, a family member told WPBF 25 News that they consider themselves lucky that nobody was seriously injured. She said the family has a strong community and a strong church to help them persevere. The family has set up a GoFundMe account for donations. 'From a little hole in the wall in Lake Worth to now we've gotten to the point where we have six locations we have about five more in the pipeline,' he said. The expansion will reach beyond Palm Beach County, with Melbourne set to be next. Working 7 days a week and really trying to build a great life for the family," Abbenante said.He worked his way through every job in the restaurant."Dishwashing, washing tables, bartending, making pizzas, working with my mom in the line, just doing whatever had to be done," Abbenante said.I reviewed an original menu, a reminder of how it all began. A large pizza was priced at $3.65 to $4.70. Many of those early dishes are still on the menu today."Yeah, we have all the same dishes from our hoagies where we use the same bread to our eggplant parmesan to our chicken and veal parmesan," Abbenante said.Reflecting on 50 years, Abbenante said family unity and commitment to quality are what have set Lynora's apart."We didn't go out on weekends you know me and my brother it was like we were working and helping mom and helping Dad and when you get to that point you think about the business a little differently - we are really united and I think that is what has made Lynora's so special for the last 50 years. Is when you walk into these restaurants…you get that energy and you get that homemade food. And everything is made with love so it's been a great run and we're looking forward to the next 50 years," Abbenante said.The recipes have remained true to their origins, with bread, pasta, and sauces still made in-house."It really brings us back to how it all started right and the food has been the same, we still make our own bread we still make our own pasta and all the dishes we have created have really been from our mom the sauces," Abbenante said.Among Lynora's most distinctive preparations is its signature sauce."One of the things that is really true to us is how our sauces are made our sauces still take 8 hours to make," Abbenante said.The restaurant's famous meatballs carry the same recipes as when Lynora's first opened."These are actually the same recipes that my mom started 50 years ago, you can kind of see our sauce is a little different than most restaurants... our flavors are basically built into the sauce and our meatballs you know they really speak for themselves," Abbenante said.Quality and consistency, Abbenante says, are the foundation of the restaurant's longevity."It's about making sure that we have the quality ingredients, highest quality, and when you make the food - you have to make sure it's done consistent year in and year out, day in and day out, and when you do that, that's the secret sauce," Abbenante said.Each Lynora's location is designed to reflect the personality of its community."So, when you're Jupiter you get that little feel of Jupiter and when you're in Boca you get that feel of Boca," Abbenante said.Lynora's pizza is made in a wood-burning oven using a hybrid style that blends New York and classic Italian techniques."So we do a mixture of New York style and classic Napoletano pizza and so it's a hybrid and the reason we do that is, because of our oven - our oven is not a gas oven it's a wood burning oven," Abbenante said. Judge Jennifer Rochon granted a temporary restraining order requested by a coalition led by the nonprofit government watchdog group Common Cause, which had challenged the ad buys in a New York federal court. spent on the ad buys, and Mehringer and other officials did not indicate any plans for a refund.The White House Office of Management and Budget last month allocated $20 million in taxpayer money from CBP for what it called “OBBBA commemorative events.” (OBBBA is an abbreviation for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which Trump signed into law in 2025.)Mehringer emphasized in her declaration that that money “did not fund the creation or production of any videos or media” and “only funded the airing of preexisting media.”Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin was pressed during an appearance Sunday on CBS News’ “Face the Nation” on whether the taxpayer dollars would be refunded.“Anytime we can do a public service announcement and brag about America, I’m all about it,” Mullin said, taking aim at negative coverage of the Trump administration as he pointed to success in securing the border and lowering fentanyl-related deaths.“We should be bragging about what’s happening inside America,” he said, adding, “I commend the opportunity of President Trump to give us the opportunity to brag about America.”The-CNN-Wire™ & © 2026 Cable News Network, Inc., a Warner Bros.

entry.title: ICU nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from critically ill patient at Tradition hospital
entry.summary: A Jupiter woman who worked as an intensive care unit nurse at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital has been arrested after police say she stole fentanyl from a critically ill patient while on shift. The Port St. Lucie Police Department say 54-year-old Leslie Pope unlawfully removed fentanyl from a patient's IV infusion while working in the hospital's ICU. According to investigators, a family member of the patient reported seeing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion line, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Police said Pope was not assigned to care for the patient. Detectives said Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room the following evening and again approached the IV equipment. The family member intervened during the encounter. Investigators later reviewed surveillance footage that they say showed Pope manipulating protective caps on the IV equipment. Authorities said they were unable to determine whether any additional medication was removed during the second incident. On Oct. 8, Pope was arrested in Jupiter and now faces felony charges of grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance.

entry.title: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court - WPEC
entry.summary: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court    WPEC
entry.article_text: A legal battle has erupted in Martin County as the developer behind a massive data center project files a sprawling lawsuit against the Village of Indiantown, its village council, planning board, and local residents. Silver Fox 606 LLC filed the complaint and verified petition for a writ of prohibition, claiming local officials are illegally derailing its $25 million project. Silver Fox purchased the over 600-acre property at 13820 SW Silver Fox Lane in 2025 following zoning verifications confirming that computer and data processing facilities were permitted as an as-of-right use in Heavy Industrial districts. Following the 2026 municipal elections, a newly sworn-in village council attempted to stall or ban data center developments despite what the lawsuit alleges were prior municipal marketing efforts that actively recruited similar tech infrastructure. See also: ICU nurse accused of taking fentanyl from critically ill patient at PSL hospital Indiantown's Community and Economic Development Director administratively approved the Silver Fox plat on September 17. The lawsuit highlights a turbulent political climate, pointing to a September 1 emergency council meeting where the village manager and long-serving village attorney were ousted. Shortly after, an administrative appeal was filed by a local resident seeking to overturn the director's approvals. Silver Fox's legal team argues that the planning, zoning, and appeals board lacks the legal jurisdiction to review the plat approval, citing state statutes rendering recorded plats unassailable without landowner consent. Furthermore, the suit alleges that the Village Council violated Florida's Sunshine Law during the abrupt personnel changes. The developer is seeking emergency injunctive relief, a preliminary injunction halting any stop-work orders or retroactive reviews, and declaratory judgments affirming its vested development rights.

entry.title: 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors
entry.summary: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico returned to the campaign trail over the weekend after a 9-day absence that fueled speculation about his whereabouts. His opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, and other Republicans questioned Talarico's explanation that he had been home with the flu. At one point, Paxton called for 'proof of life' in a social media post questioning Talarico's whereabouts. The speculation included unsubstantiated claims circulating online that Talarico had been receiving treatment at a mental health facility in Ohio. I had the flu,' Talarico insisted in an interview with MS Now on Sunday. 'This is the craziest thing Ive ever heard. Its wild that someone can just post something on the internet and then the media just runs with it.' The rumors prompted the Lindner Center of HOPE to publicly deny that Talarico had been a patient. 'Representative James Talarico has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope,' Lindner Center HOPE posted on X. Talarico responded to the post by saying, 'Ive never even been to Ohio ' Over the weekend, Talarico was seen meeting with potential voters at the Austin City Limits Music Festival. He also attended a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas on Saturday, where he met with the country singer. The Texas Senate contest is among the most closely watched races in the country as Democrats seek their first statewide election victory in more than 30 years.

entry.title: Explosion inside Port St. Lucie home leaves family with little to salvage - WPBF
entry.summary: Explosion inside Port St. Lucie home leaves family with little to salvage    WPBF
entry.article_text: An explosion inside a Port St. Lucie home destroyed almost everything owned by a family of four. Lucie County Fire District, the initial call came in at 1:24 p.m. for a fire at a home in the 100 block of Carmelite Street Friday afternoon. Neighbors called 911 after noticing the home was on fire. "I looked, and there was all kinds of smoke going through the yard," said neighbor Rob Roadman. "I was outside in the backyard, and then I see very heavy smoke," said Marina Cheong, who lives a few doors down. Cheong said she ran toward the home to help but was stopped by the explosion. "And then there was explosion, very loud, loud explosion, and debris started flying everywhere," she said. "I heard a huge explosion. At first, I thought maybe it's a transformer or something, but it was much, much, much louder than that," Roadman said. Neighbors said the man who lives in the home told them he had been cooking when a grease fire started in the garage, where the propane tank was located. The explosion sent the propane tank flying out of the garage, across the street, and into the garage of a neighbor's home. "I thought it was an air raid. It was not a casual thing. My house shook," Roadman said. "I thought that the whole house had exploded. It was very loud," Cheong added. Roadman said he spoke to the man shortly after the explosion. "I asked the dad if he was OK, and he goes, 'Yeah.' But you could tell he wasn't. Who wouldn't be?" Roadman said. The man was briefly hospitalized but returned to the house a few hours later to join family and friends in going through the debris to see what could be salvaged. They said there wasn’t much left. However, a family member told WPBF 25 News that they consider themselves lucky that nobody was seriously injured. She said the family has a strong community and a strong church to help them persevere. The family has set up a GoFundMe account for donations. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. "We take these allegations very seriously," Cleveland Clinic spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF in a statement. "She individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the agency said in a news release. entry.article_text: Police are searching for a hit-and-run cargo van driver accused of fatally striking a man riding a gas scooter before he crashed into a nearby business and ran away in Fort Pierce. Police officers received multiple 911 calls just before 9 p.m. Sunday about a vehicle crash involving a motorcycle, which later was identified as a gas scooter, close to the intersection of Okeechobee Road and 25th Street, near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. entry.title: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon - WPEC
entry.summary: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon    WPEC
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. Police immediately established a perimeter and searched for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit, but were unable to locate him. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. The victim's identity has not been released as police work through the family notification process. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.

entry.title: Fort Pierce utility crews assist Panhandle recovery after Hurricane Isaias - WPBF
entry.summary: Fort Pierce utility crews assist Panhandle recovery after Hurricane Isaias    WPBF
entry.article_text: South Florida utility crews and first responders are aiding recovery efforts in Florida's Panhandle following Hurricane Isaias. On Saturday, the Fort Pierce Utilities Authority sent seven crew members and five trucks to the area to help restore power. The crew is working with Choctawhatchee Electric Cooperative, also known as CHELCO, alongside other utility companies from across Florida. They are rebuilding power lines, removing damaged equipment, and installing new transformers and distribution lines. The American Public Power Association said nearly 67,000 CHELCO customers lost power during the storm, affecting about 90% of its system. Fort Pierce Utilities said a statewide mutual-aid agreement allows utilities to quickly send crews to areas where they are most needed. This agreement has also brought outside crews to South Florida following previous hurricanes. "Because of the collaboration and the help provided by the mutual aid agreements, we're able to help each other out. And we couldn't do it on our own. It's too much damage, and it gets our customers back up in a shorter amount of time when there's power loss," said Keith Stephens, director of gas and electric for Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. The Fort Pierce crew is expected to remain in the Panhandle throughout this week or as long as the crew's assistance is required. Florida Power Light has also sent thousands of lineworkers to the Gulf Coast to help restore power. Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Delray Beach Fire Rescue have deployed crews as well, and they are expected to assist with recovery efforts for the next two weeks.

entry.title: Driver flees after fatal motorcycle crash in Fort Pierce, police say
entry.summary: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say fled after a crash that killed a motorcyclist Sunday night. The crash happened around 8:52 p.m. near South 25th Street and Okeechobee Road. Officers responded after receiving multiple 911 calls about a crash involving a motorcycle. According to preliminary information from the Fort Pierce Police Department, a white box van traveling east on Okeechobee Road struck a blue motorcycle and attempted to leave the scene. Police said the van's driver made a U-turn in the eastbound lanes while fleeing, crossed the westbound lanes and crashed into Kings and Queens Unisex Salon at 2508 Okeechobee Road. The driver then got out of the van and fled north on foot, police said. When officers arrived, they found the motorcyclist in the outside eastbound lane of Okeechobee Road and determined the person had died. St. Lucie County Fire Rescue also responded. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 and Aviation units assisted Fort Pierce police in searching for the driver, but police said he had not been located as of Monday. Two other vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene. Police described the driver as an adult Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top and light-colored pants or shorts. The identity of the person killed has not been confirmed. The Fort Pierce Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit and Crime Scene Investigations are investigating. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's identity or whereabouts is asked to contact Fort Pierce police at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

entry.title: Palm Beach County faith leaders sound alarm on housing affordability crisis
entry.summary: For many working families in Palm Beach County, having a job is no longer enough to guarantee they can afford a place to live. That was the message from faith leaders and community members with People Engaged in Active Community Efforts (PEACE), who gathered Monday at St. Ann Catholic Church to call attention to the countys housing affordability crisis and urge local leaders to take action. WATCH WPTV'S COVERAGE BELOW: Palm Beach County faith leaders sound alarm on housing affordability crisis We are gathered today because across our congregations and our community, we continue to hear the same concern, said the Rev. Latifah Griffin, a PEACE board of trustees member. People who are working here are struggling to live here. PEACE is a coalition of 31 congregations across Palm Beach County. Members say conversations within their congregations reveal a growing number of residents struggling with rising rents, stagnant wages and the possibility of being priced out of the communities where they work and raise their families. Palm Beach County data underscores those concerns. According to the countys January 2025 affordable housing report, the average rent for a two-bedroom apartment increased from $1,899 in 2021 to $2,833 in 2024 a 49.2% increase in three years. The cost of buying a home has also risen. The county report found the median price of a single-family home climbed from $425,000 in late 2020 to $600,000 in late 2024, an increase of 41.2%. Nationally, Redfin reported in August 2026 that households needed an annual income of nearly $110,000 to afford a typical U.S. home. For residents working in service and other modest-wage jobs, those costs can make independent living difficult even when they work consistently. Harry Wolin shared his family's experience at Mondays gathering. He said he and his wife, who are retired and living on a fixed income, help support their adult daughter, a waitress who lives in Lake Worth. Woolen said his daughter has worked in the restaurant industry for more than 20 years, but her income is not enough to afford housing without help from her parents. Shes doing everything that weve told people theyre supposed to do: get a job, work hard, help support your family, Wolin said. And it just doesnt work given the price of housing. He said he worries about workers in similar circumstances who do not have relatives able to help them financially. What do they do if they dont have a family who can help them? Wolin asked. entry.title: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court - WPEC
entry.summary: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court    WPEC
entry.article_text: A legal battle has erupted in Martin County as the developer behind a massive data center project files a sprawling lawsuit against the Village of Indiantown, its village council, planning board, and local residents. Silver Fox 606 LLC filed the complaint and verified petition for a writ of prohibition, claiming local officials are illegally derailing its $25 million project. Silver Fox purchased the over 600-acre property at 13820 SW Silver Fox Lane in 2025 following zoning verifications confirming that computer and data processing facilities were permitted as an as-of-right use in Heavy Industrial districts. Following the 2026 municipal elections, a newly sworn-in village council attempted to stall or ban data center developments despite what the lawsuit alleges were prior municipal marketing efforts that actively recruited similar tech infrastructure. See also: ICU nurse accused of taking fentanyl from critically ill patient at PSL hospital Indiantown's Community and Economic Development Director administratively approved the Silver Fox plat on September 17. The lawsuit highlights a turbulent political climate, pointing to a September 1 emergency council meeting where the village manager and long-serving village attorney were ousted. Shortly after, an administrative appeal was filed by a local resident seeking to overturn the director's approvals. Silver Fox's legal team argues that the planning, zoning, and appeals board lacks the legal jurisdiction to review the plat approval, citing state statutes rendering recorded plats unassailable without landowner consent. Furthermore, the suit alleges that the Village Council violated Florida's Sunshine Law during the abrupt personnel changes. The developer is seeking emergency injunctive relief, a preliminary injunction halting any stop-work orders or retroactive reviews, and declaratory judgments affirming its vested development rights.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 54-year-old Jupiter woman is facing felony charges after she allegedly removed fentanyl from a critically ill patient's IV infusion while working at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said Monday. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. "We take these allegations very seriously," Cleveland Clinic spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF in a statement. "She individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Investigators learned a family member reported witnessing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Pope was not assigned to the patient's care. The next evening, Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room and again approached the IV equipment, police said. The family member intervened. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the police agency said in a news release. "We remain committed to thorough, evidence-based investigations and pursuing accountability when the evidence supports criminal charges." This remains an active criminal case. "Cleveland Clinic doesn’t comment on caregivers," spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF. entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. entry.article_text: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously to end their lease with the former operator of Crabby's Dockside and begin searching for a new operator for the waterfront restaurant. The restaurant, located along Avenue A at the Fort Pierce Marina, closed in February. The city said its operator, Winking Starfish, owed more than $418,000 in rent, taxes, and late fees. After recalculating the balance, the city now says the amount owed is nearly $334,000. Winking Starfish identified a potential new operator for the restaurant, but city officials said the proposal sought favorable terms. City Manager Richard Chess told commissioners that the city would allow interested restaurateurs to compete for the location. The city plans to set requirements for potential operators, with the city commission making the final decision. "Our marina is very, very successful, and we're very proud of it, and that location, that Crabby's location, is a very critical part of the marina," Mayor Linda Hudson said. Chess also said during the meeting that a new agreement would combine rent and other payments into one amount, based on the property's market value. entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son , who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists. 'Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place,' Gray told WPTV. Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed. entry.title: 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors
entry.summary: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico returned to the campaign trail over the weekend after a 9-day absence that fueled speculation about his whereabouts. His opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, and other Republicans questioned Talarico's explanation that he had been home with the flu. Talarico returns to the campaign trail, and midterm spending heats up At one point, Paxton called for 'proof of life' in a social media post questioning Talarico's whereabouts. The speculation included unsubstantiated claims circulating online that Talarico had been receiving treatment at a mental health facility in Ohio. I had the flu,' Talarico insisted in an interview with MS Now on Sunday. 'This is the craziest thing Ive ever heard. Its wild that someone can just post something on the internet and then the media just runs with it.' The rumors prompted the Lindner Center of HOPE to publicly deny that Talarico had been a patient. 'Representative James Talarico has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope,' Lindner Center HOPE posted on X. Talarico responded to the post by saying, 'Ive never even been to Ohio ' Over the weekend, Talarico was seen meeting with potential voters at the Austin City Limits Music Festival. He also attended a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas on Saturday, where he met with the country singer. The Texas Senate contest is among the most closely watched races in the country as Democrats seek their first statewide election victory in more than 30 years.

Obtained 911 recordings capture the frantic moments following the crash. In one call, a person inside the Toyota pickup truck described the aftermath. "We got hit, and it's like, there's blood all over our car," the caller told a dispatcher. Another caller reported seeing the white van crash into the nearby building while trying to get away. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. According to a police news release, the driver ran northbound after crashing into the salon, located at 2508 Okeechobee Road. Police responded to multiple 911 calls reporting the crash around 8:52 p.m. and immediately established a perimeter, searching for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit. Despite their efforts, they were unable to locate him. Two additional vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene, according to police. The department's Traffic Homicide Unit, Crime Scene Investigations and other personnel processed the scene as part of the ongoing investigation. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. Police said the victim's identity had not yet been confirmed as of Monday, and confirmation was still pending before next of kin could be notified. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's whereabouts is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or submit a tip through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers .

entry.article_text: A 54-year-old Jupiter woman is facing felony charges after she allegedly removed fentanyl from a critically ill patient's IV infusion while working at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said Monday. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. "We take these allegations very seriously," Cleveland Clinic spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF in a statement. "She individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Investigators learned a family member reported witnessing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Pope was not assigned to the patient's care. The next evening, Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room and again approached the IV equipment, police said. The family member intervened. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the police agency said in a news release. "We remain committed to thorough, evidence-based investigations and pursuing accountability when the evidence supports criminal charges." This remains an active criminal case. "Cleveland Clinic doesn’t comment on caregivers," spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF. entry.title: Teen identified after deadly Fellsmere shooting involving 100-plus teens - WPEC
entry.summary: Teen identified after deadly Fellsmere shooting involving 100-plus teens    WPEC
entry.article_text: A 17-year-old was killed in a Fellsmere shooting Friday night after a meetup of more than 100 teens turned violent, according to the sheriff. The shooting happened around 11:24 p.m. at Garcia’s Boat Ramp , where a large crowd had gathered. Sheriff Eric Flowers said the group included teens ages 14 to 19, with drinking and fighting reported. These have been happening since before I was in high school, since before many of you were in high school. This has been going on for a long time. But now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix. CBS12 confirmed with the family that the slain 17-year-old was Sulliman Bah, a senior at Sebastian River High School. He and a group of friends approached a pickup truck with two 18-year-olds inside. Detectives say Bah opened the door and attempted to punch someone inside when the passenger fired a single shot at Bah. See also: What Florida voters need to know about the 3 constitutional amendments on the Nov. ballot Bah was taken by friends toward Fellsmere. Deputies and EMS met them at Fellsmere City Hall and performed CPR before he was taken to Sebastian River Medical Center and later transported to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he succumbed to his injuries. No arrests have been made. Flowers said the driver and passenger inside the truck have cooperated with investigators and turned over the truck and firearm. The sheriff said the preliminary investigation indicates a self-defense claim may apply. We will be submitting a warrant in the case, but at this time it looks as though there will be a self-defense claim as a result, Flowers said. The sheriff said the state will ultimately decide whether charges are filed. Investigators used Flock technology to identify people connected to the truck and shooting. Deputies also recovered additional guns and multiple shell casings. Flowers said investigators believe the meetup was part of a growing trend of teens gathering at remote locations arranged through Snapchat , where fights are recorded and shared online. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," he said. "We've got kids out here losing their lives trying to go viral on social media." He said there may have been as many as four fights at the boat ramp that night, and investigators are still working to identify people who were there. "They had a history of fighting," Flowers said. "This has been an ongoing thing." The sheriff urged parents to ask their children whether they attended the meetup and encouraged anyone who witnessed the shooting or recorded it to contact investigators. "It's not safe," Flowers said. There's guns, and those two just don't mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead." In a statement, the Indian River School District gave its condolences to the teen's family: The School District of Indian River County is heartbroken by this young person’s death. Our hearts are with his family, friends, and the students and staff who knew and cared about him. Grief support was in place over the weekend, including counselors at Sebastian River High School’s Homecoming Dance, and continues today as students and staff return to school. Our teams will remain available in the days ahead, offering care and responding to the needs of those affected. A spokesperson for SDIRC said the student had recently withdrawn from Sebastian River High School to be home schooled.

entry.article_text: Police are searching for a hit-and-run cargo van driver accused of fatally striking a man riding a gas scooter before he crashed into a nearby business and ran away in Fort Pierce. Police officers received multiple 911 calls just before 9 p.m. Sunday about a vehicle crash involving a motorcycle, which later was identified as a gas scooter, close to the intersection of Okeechobee Road and 25th Street, near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. A white cargo van was behind the scooter, traveling east on Okeechobee Road, Maj. Michael Santiago told WPBF's Angela Rozier at a briefing Monday afternoon. The van driver fled the scene and made a U-turn to drive in the wrong direction across the median on Okeechobee Road, but he crashed into the side of a building, the Kings Queens Unisex Salon. The man then ran from the scene. Salon owner Sheila Hampton showed the damage, and is thankful no one was inside at the time. Hampton said she feels for the victim and his family. "His family told me he was just leaving from one of his friend's houses and just going home," she said. A second vehicle, a Toyota pickup truck, was also struck, but no one was injured. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit and Aviation Unit assisted Fort Pierce police and the K-9 Unit in efforts to locate the driver. They are in possession of the van. Police described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top with light-colored pants or shorts. "So, that in itself proves intent that that person knew exactly what they were doing at the time and was just trying to simply get away," Santiago said. Anyone with information should call the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco
entry.summary: On Monday, Port St. Lucie City Council approved three major site plans for projects along the Southern Grove, a developing jobs corridor in the city. One of those plans: the long-awaited Costco retail store. 'This is something that we have been looking forward to for a long time, Scott Samples with the City of Port St. Lucie said. Samples and Wes McCurry, president and CEO of St. Lucie County Economic Development Council said the 163,000-square-foot store is just the beginning for a new phase of growth in western Port St. Lucie. 'This is getting closer to the finish line, Samples said. The Costco will join other companies like Amazon, Tamco and Cheney Brothers, calling the Southern Grove area home. McCurry said since the jobs are now here, new commercial development will follow. 'They see all the all the development that's occurring here, along with the demographics that they like to see, said McCurry. It only makes sense that Costco opens a retail store here.' City council approved two other major site plans for the area, including a 5.5-acre site making up the first phase of the Tradition Entertainment District set to bring restaurants and retail. This area has historically been largely under-served by restaurants and retail, and especially entertainment facilities, McCurry said. It's kind of catching up to the rooftops that are happening. You know, rooftops always drive that demand, but there's more to come. The other plan is space for an acute care rehabilitation hospital, featuring inpatient and outpatient services with 42 beds in a more than 55 thousand square foot building. 'Growing area needs services, and that's just another component of services that are coming into the area is expanded healthcare access, McCurry said. McCurry said the plans for retail, healthcare and entertainment is fulfilling the citys master plan for what Southern Grove was destined to become. 'The plan is coming together. The vision is coming together. What everyone saw 20 years ago is now starting to happen, McCurry said. Samples said Costco still must close on the land, move on to construction design planning and permitting before any shovels hit the ground.

entry.title: ATF drops registration requirements for suppressors, short-barreled firearms
entry.summary: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives announced Friday it will no longer enforce National Firearms Act registration and approval requirements for suppressors, short-barreled rifles and short-barreled shotguns. The move eliminates what was often a months-long process that required buyers to obtain federal approval, register the items with the government and pay a tax stamp before taking possession. Federal background checks are still required. For firearm retailers in West Palm Beach, the change is already having an impact. At We Kick Brass, owner Mike Perez said customers previously had to navigate a lengthy approval process to legally purchase suppressors and certain firearms regulated under the National Firearms Act. 'People were legally able to own these firearms,' Perez said. 'They just had to wait a longer process. It had to get ATF approval.' ATF drops registration requirements for suppressors, short-barreled firearmsWhat changed? For decades, suppressors and short-barreled rifles and shotguns were subject to National Firearms Act requirements that included registration, federal approval and a tax stamp. The ATF announced Friday it will no longer enforce those requirements for those items. The move follows a federal court ruling in Texas involving National Firearms Act registration requirements and comes after Congress reduced the tax stamp fee from $200 to zero. Perez said the biggest change is the amount of paperwork buyers no longer have to complete. 'The biggest change is less paperwork,' Perez said. 'It's a lot easier for someone to come in here and purchase a firearm and feel safe about it and secure about it.' He said some customers who once faced waits stretching nine months, 14 months or longer may now be able to take possession much sooner. 'They no longer have to wait 14 months, or nine months, or even more than a day if they have a concealed weapon firearm permit,' Perez said. entry.title: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court - WPEC
entry.summary: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court    WPEC
entry.article_text: A legal battle has erupted in Martin County as the developer behind a massive data center project files a sprawling lawsuit against the Village of Indiantown, its village council, planning board, and local residents. Silver Fox 606 LLC filed the complaint and verified petition for a writ of prohibition, claiming local officials are illegally derailing its $25 million project. Silver Fox purchased the over 600-acre property at 13820 SW Silver Fox Lane in 2025 following zoning verifications confirming that computer and data processing facilities were permitted as an as-of-right use in Heavy Industrial districts. Following the 2026 municipal elections, a newly sworn-in village council attempted to stall or ban data center developments despite what the lawsuit alleges were prior municipal marketing efforts that actively recruited similar tech infrastructure. See also: ICU nurse accused of taking fentanyl from critically ill patient at PSL hospital Indiantown's Community and Economic Development Director administratively approved the Silver Fox plat on September 17. The lawsuit highlights a turbulent political climate, pointing to a September 1 emergency council meeting where the village manager and long-serving village attorney were ousted. Shortly after, an administrative appeal was filed by a local resident seeking to overturn the director's approvals. Silver Fox's legal team argues that the planning, zoning, and appeals board lacks the legal jurisdiction to review the plat approval, citing state statutes rendering recorded plats unassailable without landowner consent. Furthermore, the suit alleges that the Village Council violated Florida's Sunshine Law during the abrupt personnel changes. The developer is seeking emergency injunctive relief, a preliminary injunction halting any stop-work orders or retroactive reviews, and declaratory judgments affirming its vested development rights.

entry.title: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon - WPEC
entry.summary: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon    WPEC
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Obtained 911 recordings capture the frantic moments following the crash. In one call, a person inside the Toyota pickup truck described the aftermath. "We got hit, and it's like, there's blood all over our car," the caller told a dispatcher. Another caller reported seeing the white van crash into the nearby building while trying to get away. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. According to a police news release, the driver ran northbound after crashing into the salon, located at 2508 Okeechobee Road. Police responded to multiple 911 calls reporting the crash around 8:52 p.m. and immediately established a perimeter, searching for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit. Despite their efforts, they were unable to locate him. Two additional vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene, according to police. The department's Traffic Homicide Unit, Crime Scene Investigations and other personnel processed the scene as part of the ongoing investigation. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. Police said the victim's identity had not yet been confirmed as of Monday, and confirmation was still pending before next of kin could be notified. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's whereabouts is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or submit a tip through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers .
