entry.title: Treasure Coast travelers say limited transportation options make it 'difficult to get around'
entry.summary: A recent change to a flight out of Vero Beach is sparking a bigger conversation about travel options on the Treasure Coast. Travelers tell WPTV limited flight schedules and a lack of convenient transportation alternatives can make getting in and out of the area difficult, sometimes forcing them to drive to larger airports or rearrange their plans. WATCH: Why Treasure Coast travelers say they need more options At the Vero Beach Regional Airport, travelers shared their frustrations with WPTV reporter Brooke Chau about the challenges of getting where they need to go. In the Treasure Coast area, Vero Beach specifically, it is difficult to get around, said Peter Masella. He pointed to the lack of a Brightline station in Vero Beach, saying people often have to travel to other cities to access additional transportation options. A recent schedule change to Breeze Airways' route between Vero Beach and the New York area has added to those concerns. The flight, which previously departed Vero Beach in the evening, now leaves in the morning. A New York City physician told WPTV the change has affected his work schedule. Im a physician working in New York City and because of the change of flight for Vero Beach, I have had to rearrange my patients schedule two days in a row, he said. Another traveler from Westchester, New York said the change can mean a longer trip. Then I have to take a taxi all the way down and around to Vero Beach. Its very inconvenient, she said. However, Breeze Airways has also been adding destinations from Vero Beach. Last month, the airline introduced nonstop service to Trenton, Baltimore, Pittsburgh and Atlantic City, expanding the airport's commercial flight options. Vero Beach Airport Director, Brandon Dambeck, says airlines regularly evaluate the performance of their routes, which can lead to new destinations as well as schedule or route changes. All of these airlines are monitoring the routes and their gauge of success,' Dambeck said. For travelers, more destinations are welcome, but they say flight times that fit their schedules are just as important.

entry.title: Treasure Coast High School freshman dies after being hit by car while walking to school
entry.summary: A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student who was hit by a vehicle while walking to school last week has died from his injuries, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Police said the crash happened the morning of Oct. 7 near the intersection of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Southwest Squirrel Avenue. According to police, the freshman was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near the edge of the roadway when he was struck from behind by a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man. The teen suffered critical injuries and was transported to a local hospital. Police said he was pronounced clinically deceased on Oct. 9 shortly after 4 p.m. Investigators said the crash remains under investigation as detectives continue to examine the circumstances surrounding what happened. Amid the tragedy, the student's family made the decision to donate his organs in hopes of helping others and honoring their son's memory. 'In the midst of their grief, their decision offers the possibility of hope and healing for other families and individuals whose lives may be changed through this extraordinary gift,' police said in a statement. Treasure Coast High School will provide grief counseling services for students and staff as the school community copes with the loss. The Port St. Lucie Police Department extended its condolences to the student's family, friends, classmates and the entire Treasure Coast High School community. 'We recognize that no words can ease the pain of losing a child, and our thoughts remain with everyone affected by this heartbreaking tragedy,' the department said.

entry.title: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death - WPEC
entry.summary: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie Boulevard say more needs to be done to protect pedestrians as construction continues on the busy road. Their concerns come after a 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student died from injuries he suffered when he was hit by an SUV while walking to school. Police say the freshman was walking along the edge of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on the morning of Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He was pronounced clinically deceased two days later. His family chose to donate his organs . Much of the roadway remains under construction, and there are no sidewalks along large sections of the corridor. Recent heavy rain also left portions of the shoulder flooded, further limiting space for pedestrians. "He was just going to school," said neighbor Irene Ange. "He was just starting his high school year. He had the right to be safe." Irene Ange, who has lived near the boulevard for more than two decades, says students often walk or bike close to traffic, sometimes before sunrise. The stretch of road is dangerous, Ange said. It’s very dark, and drivers are not following the speed limits. Ange said she saw first responders rushing to the crash site and was heartbroken for the student and his family. See also: Suspect booked into Martin County Jail after undercover drug sting, sheriff says The teen’s mother told CBS12 by phone that her son was a people person who made friends easily. She said the family does not want this to happen to another child. The Florida Department of Transportation is widening the southern portion of Port St. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four and adding sidewalks on both sides of the road. FDOT says the sidewalks will be eight to 10 feet wide. The project is expected to be completed in winter 2028, with an estimated cost of about $25.6 million. CBS 12 saw crews building sidewalks several blocks from where the crash happened. FDOT did not respond to questions about what pedestrian safety measures are in place while construction continues. entry.title: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death - WPEC
entry.summary: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie Boulevard say more needs to be done to protect pedestrians as construction continues on the busy road. Their concerns come after a 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student died from injuries he suffered when he was hit by an SUV while walking to school. Police say the freshman was walking along the edge of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on the morning of Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He was pronounced clinically deceased two days later. His family chose to donate his organs . Much of the roadway remains under construction, and there are no sidewalks along large sections of the corridor. Recent heavy rain also left portions of the shoulder flooded, further limiting space for pedestrians. "He was just going to school," said neighbor Irene Ange. "He was just starting his high school year. He had the right to be safe." Irene Ange, who has lived near the boulevard for more than two decades, says students often walk or bike close to traffic, sometimes before sunrise. The stretch of road is dangerous, Ange said. It’s very dark, and drivers are not following the speed limits. Ange said she saw first responders rushing to the crash site and was heartbroken for the student and his family. See also: Suspect booked into Martin County Jail after undercover drug sting, sheriff says The teen’s mother told CBS12 by phone that her son was a people person who made friends easily. She said the family does not want this to happen to another child. The Florida Department of Transportation is widening the southern portion of Port St. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four and adding sidewalks on both sides of the road. FDOT says the sidewalks will be eight to 10 feet wide. The project is expected to be completed in winter 2028, with an estimated cost of about $25.6 million. CBS 12 saw crews building sidewalks several blocks from where the crash happened. FDOT did not respond to questions about what pedestrian safety measures are in place while construction continues. "No accountability with that response because now there's another death," Ange said. Ange says more needs to be done now to keep children safe on their way to school. "This did not have to happen to this family," Ange said. The family now have to mourn him." The driver initially told officers he believed he had struck a construction barrel and has been cooperating with investigators. It remains unclear whether any charges will be filed.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie family demands answers after dog killed in hit-and-run - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie family demands answers after dog killed in hit-and-run    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie family is seeking justice after their German shepherd, Titus, was struck and killed by a truck in a hit-and-run incident last Tuesday on Goodman Avenue. "I want justice served because you didn’t stop; you killed my dog after you hit him," Michelle Baker, Titus' owner, said. Michelle and Dillon Baker, parents of two young children, are struggling to explain the loss to their 11-year-old son and 2-year-old daughter. The incident occurred around noon when the family’s dogs hopped the fence and ran down the road. Despite efforts to track them using GPS collars, the Bakers were unable to locate the dogs in time. "He knew he hit something because he stopped, then he kept going," Dillon Baker said. Surveillance footage shows a silver truck hitting Titus, stopping briefly, and then continuing to drag the dog down the road before running him over. "My dog did not deserve to go out like that," Michelle Baker said. The driver did not return to the scene, and animal control is investigating the incident as a hit-and-run. The family believes the act constitutes animal cruelty. "That’s a crime, that’s a full-on crime, it’s murder," Michelle Baker said. Back at the Baker home, Gypsy, who witnessed the incident, has not been the same since Titus’ death. The family has a message for the driver. "Pay attention, pay attention and care about what’s on the road in front of you," Michelle Baker said. WPBF contacted animal control for further comment on the incident; as of Monday night, they have not responded. entry.title: Cats & Dogs exhibit opens in West Palm Beach
entry.summary: If you've ever wondered what the world looks like through your dog's eyes or how your cat experiences its surroundings, a new exhibit at the Cox Science Center Aquarium in West Palm Beach aims to provide answers. entry.title: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death - WPEC
entry.summary: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie Boulevard say more needs to be done to protect pedestrians as construction continues on the busy road. Their concerns come after a 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student died from injuries he suffered when he was hit by an SUV while walking to school. Police say the freshman was walking along the edge of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on the morning of Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He was pronounced clinically deceased two days later. His family chose to donate his organs . Much of the roadway remains under construction, and there are no sidewalks along large sections of the corridor. Recent heavy rain also left portions of the shoulder flooded, further limiting space for pedestrians. "He was just going to school," said neighbor Irene Ange. "He was just starting his high school year. He had the right to be safe." Irene Ange, who has lived near the boulevard for more than two decades, says students often walk or bike close to traffic, sometimes before sunrise. The stretch of road is dangerous, Ange said. It’s very dark, and drivers are not following the speed limits. Ange said she saw first responders rushing to the crash site and was heartbroken for the student and his family. See also: Suspect booked into Martin County Jail after undercover drug sting, sheriff says The teen’s mother told CBS12 by phone that her son was a people person who made friends easily. She said the family does not want this to happen to another child. The Florida Department of Transportation is widening the southern portion of Port St. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four and adding sidewalks on both sides of the road. FDOT says the sidewalks will be eight to 10 feet wide. The project is expected to be completed in winter 2028, with an estimated cost of about $25.6 million. CBS 12 saw crews building sidewalks several blocks from where the crash happened. FDOT did not respond to questions about what pedestrian safety measures are in place while construction continues. "No accountability with that response because now there's another death," Ange said. Ange says more needs to be done now to keep children safe on their way to school. "This did not have to happen to this family," Ange said. The family now have to mourn him." The driver initially told officers he believed he had struck a construction barrel and has been cooperating with investigators. It remains unclear whether any charges will be filed.

entry.title: ICU nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from critically ill patient at Tradition hospital
entry.summary: A Jupiter woman who worked as an intensive care unit nurse at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital has been arrested after police say she stole fentanyl from a critically ill patient while on shift. The Port St. Lucie Police Department say 54-year-old Leslie Pope unlawfully removed fentanyl from a patient's IV infusion while working in the hospital's ICU. According to investigators, a family member of the patient reported seeing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion line, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Police said Pope was not assigned to care for the patient. Detectives said Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room the following evening and again approached the IV equipment. The family member intervened during the encounter. Investigators later reviewed surveillance footage that they say showed Pope manipulating protective caps on the IV equipment. Authorities said they were unable to determine whether any additional medication was removed during the second incident. On Oct. 8, Pope was arrested in Jupiter and now faces felony charges of grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance.

entry.title: Treasure Coast travelers say limited transportation options make it 'difficult to get around'
entry.summary: A recent change to a flight out of Vero Beach is sparking a bigger conversation about travel options on the Treasure Coast. Travelers tell WPTV limited flight schedules and a lack of convenient transportation alternatives can make getting in and out of the area difficult, sometimes forcing them to drive to larger airports or rearrange their plans. WATCH: Why Treasure Coast travelers say they need more options At the Vero Beach Regional Airport, travelers shared their frustrations with WPTV reporter Brooke Chau about the challenges of getting where they need to go. In the Treasure Coast area, Vero Beach specifically, it is difficult to get around, said Peter Masella. He pointed to the lack of a Brightline station in Vero Beach, saying people often have to travel to other cities to access additional transportation options. A recent schedule change to Breeze Airways' route between the New York area and Vero Beach has added to those concerns. The flight, which previously departed from Westchester, New York in the evening, now leaves in the morning. A New York City physician told WPTV the change has affected his work schedule. Im a physician working in New York City and because of the change of flight for Vero Beach, I have had to rearrange my patients schedule two days in a row, he said. Another traveler from Westchester, New York said the change can mean a longer trip. Then I have to take a taxi all the way down and around to Vero Beach. Its very inconvenient, she said. However, Breeze Airways has also been adding destinations from Vero Beach. Last month, the airline introduced nonstop service to Trenton, Baltimore, Pittsburgh and Atlantic City, expanding the airport's commercial flight options. Vero Beach Airport Director, Brandon Dambeck, says airlines regularly evaluate the performance of their routes, which can lead to new destinations as well as schedule or route changes. All of these airlines are monitoring the routes and their gauge of success,' Dambeck said. For travelers, more destinations are welcome, but they say flight times that fit their schedules are just as important.

entry.title: The Kings Academy volleyball team eyes 7th straight district title while chasing state championship
entry.summary: With an 18-5 record heading into the playoffs, The Kings Academy volleyball team in Palm Beach County is one of the favorites to win the Florida state championship and could also claim a seventh straight district title. Coming into this volleyball season, few teams in the state were talked about more than The Kings Academy, and for good reason. WATCH BELOW: Kings Academy volleyball team eyes state title Kings Academy volleyball chases state title, 7th district crown 'This year has been a year of expectations to win some stuff because our team is so well-rounded,' setter Jordan Molnar said. Winning 'some stuff' might be an understatement. The girls opened the season as one of the top teams in Palm Beach County and one of the favorites to win the state crown. Instead of feeding into the hype, the team came together with shared expectations. 'It's called the core covenant, and anytime they get a little sidetracked, we go back and refocus on those things that they said they wanted to do,' head coach Bethafor Avila said. They wanted to get over the hump of losing in regional play and win a state championship, and while they're primed to do just that, the girls are taking it one day at a time and focusing on district play, where they could win their seventh straight district title. 'A lot of the girls on the team have been for a while, so we've got to experience a lot of those district wins. It's just special that we get to do it for such an amazing school,' middle hitter Ava Maldonado said. At 18-5, the school might be amazing, but so are the Kings Academy volleyball team, who fully expect to put the entire state on notice. 'It's a lot of energy around because we know that we can do something big this year and were all just working hard to get to that,' Molnar said. 'It's been fun; we have a great group of girls put together, and I think it's really nice to come together and compete with them,' Maldonado said.

entry.title: Florida to execute a prisoner who killed his cellmate in hopes of getting a death sentence
entry.summary: A Florida prisoner who claimed he killed his cellmate so he could be moved to death row is set to be executed Tuesday, nearly 18 years after the fatal attack. James Robertson, 63, pleaded guilty to first-degree murder and waived all appeals in the 2008 strangling of Frank Hart. Robertson is set to receive a three-drug injection at Florida State Prison near Starke starting at noon. Robertson was supposed to be one of two executions carried out by Florida on Tuesday, but Gov. Ron DeSantis withdrew a death warrant last week for William Lee Thompson. The Republican governor did not provide a reason for withdrawing Thompsons death warrant but had temporarily stayed his execution last month pending a psychiatric evaluation. Records show that this is the first time DeSantis has withdrawn a death warrant, which does not technically change Thompsons sentence. He will remain on death row, and a new death warrant could be signed for him in the future. Robertson's execution comes at a time of escalating attention on the death penalty in the U.S. In Tennessee, Christa Pike survived an execution attempt two weeks ago despite receiving two lethal doses of pentobarbital. And last week, the Pentagon announced that the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan would be livestreamed. Robertson wanted to be on death row According to court records, Robertson was incarcerated at Charlotte Correctional Institution, north of Fort Myers, in December 2008 when he tied several socks together and strangled Hart while the other man slept. Robertson told investigators that the attack was unprovoked and that he killed his cellmate so that he would be sentenced to death, rather than having to live out his days in prison. Robertson was 17 years old when he went to prison in 1980 for burglary and assault. Years of convictions for escape, battery and weapons while in prison kept adding time to his total sentence. Hart was sent to prison in 2003 following a sexual battery conviction. Robertson pleaded guilty and waived a penalty phase, where a jury would recommend the death penalty or life in prison. A judge sentenced Robertson to death, and he later waived all post-conviction proceedings. Robertson reiterated his position during a hearing earlier this month, telling a judge that he understood his execution had been scheduled and that he didn't want to make any final appeals to the Florida Supreme Court or U.S. Supreme Court. Death penalty opponents question its deterrent

Ron DeSantis withdrew a death warrant last week for William Lee Thompson. The Republican governor did not provide a reason for withdrawing Thompson’s death warrant but had temporarily stayed his execution last month pending a psychiatric evaluation.Records show that this is the first time DeSantis has withdrawn a death warrant, which does not technically change Thompson’s sentence. He will remain on death row, and a new death warrant could be signed for him in the future.Robertson's execution comes at a time of escalating attention on the death penalty in the U.S. In Tennessee, Christa Pike survived an execution attempt two weeks ago despite receiving two lethal doses of pentobarbital. And last week, the Pentagon announced that the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan would be livestreamed.According to court records, Robertson was incarcerated at Charlotte Correctional Institution, north of Fort Myers, in December 2008 when he tied several socks together and strangled Hart while the other man slept. Robertson told investigators that the attack was unprovoked and that he killed his cellmate so that he would be sentenced to death, rather than having to live out his days in prison.Robertson was 17 years old when he went to prison in 1980 for burglary and assault. Years of convictions for escape, battery and weapons while in prison kept adding time to his total sentence. Hart was sent to prison in 2003 following a sexual battery conviction.Robertson pleaded guilty and waived a penalty phase, where a jury would recommend the death penalty or life in prison. A judge sentenced Robertson to death, and he later waived all post-conviction proceedings. Robertson reiterated his position during a hearing earlier this month, telling a judge that he understood his execution had been scheduled and that he didn't want to make any final appeals to the Florida Supreme Court or U.S. Supreme Court.While proponents of the death penalty have long claimed that it is a deterrent, Floridians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty released a statement saying that this case demonstrates the opposite."Frank Hart deserved to be safe in state custody, and his loved ones deserve our compassion," the group's legal and policy director, Maria DeLiberato, said in the statement. "When someone commits murder to try to secure his own execution, we have to confront the conditions that contributed to that decision and the reality that the existence of the death penalty may have caused the very violence it purportedly prevents."Meanwhile, DeSantis is the third Florida governor to sign a death warrant for Thompson. Bob Graham and Bob Martinez both scheduled executions for Thompson in the 1980s, but years of appeals and stays allowed him to avoid the electric chair, the state's method of execution at the time. The 74-year-old death row inmate was convicted of first-degree murder, kidnapping and sexual battery in the 1976 killing of 23-year-old Sally Ivester.Thompson will remain on Florida’s death row, and a new death warrant could be signed for him in the future. His attorneys have said he suffers from dementia, and his health is failing. They said he should be relocated to an adequate medical facility to get the care he needs.Only one other Florida inmate remains alive following a death warrant signed by DeSantis. James Dailey, 80, was scheduled to die in late 2019 for the murder of a 14-year-old girl, but a federal judge halted the execution as attorneys argued against his guilt. The stay was eventually lifted, but DeSantis didn't sign a new death warrant. The state halted all executions during the COVID-19 pandemic and didn't restart until 2023.DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw 19 executions in 2025, more than any other Florida governor in a single year since the death penalty was reinstated in 1976. Robertson would be the state's 17th execution of 2026, with two more already scheduled, not counting Thompson.William Reaves, 77, is scheduled to be executed on Oct. 20, followed by Jesse Guardado, 64, on Nov. Reaves was convicted of fatally shooting a deputy after dropping a gun in front of the law enforcement officer in 1986. Guardado was convicted of robbing and killing a woman in order to buy drugs in 2004.If Robertson, Reaves and Guardado are all executed as planned, that would match the state's 2025 total, with eight weeks remaining in 2026.DeSantis has made few public comments about the unprecedented number of executions but explained previously that his goal is to bring justice to victims’ families who have waited decades for the death sentences to be carried out."I felt I owed it to them to make sure this ran very smoothly. If I honestly thought someone was innocent, I would not pull the trigger," the governor said last year.A total of 47 people were executed in the U.S. Besides leading all other states last year, Florida has carried out more than half of the 30 total executions in the U.S. In July, Florida executed two prisoners in one day, the first state in nearly a decade to do so.All Florida executions are carried out via lethal injection of a sedative, a paralytic and a drug that stops the heart, according to the Department of Corrections.

entry.title: Martin County commissioners unanimously move forward with 1-year moratorium on data centers
entry.summary: Martin County commissioners voted Tuesday unanimously to move forward with a one-year moratorium on data centers as county leaders consider how to handle future development of the facilities. Tuesday's vote marked the first of two hearings scheduled this month on the proposed moratorium. PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Martin County eyes pause on data center development Martin County eyes pause on data center development Commissioners are expected to take up the issue again on Oct. 27, when another vote will be required. The discussion comes as Martin County has already received an application for a data center. The county received the application Monday, one day before commissioners considered the moratorium. Because the application was submitted before the proposed moratorium, it would not be affected by the measure. The proposal comes amid concerns from residents about the future of data center development in Martin County. WPTV is continuing to hear from residents about those concerns as commissioners consider what restrictions, if any, should be placed on future data center development. Stay with WPTV.com and WPTV News for updates on this development story.

entry.title: Trinity United Methodist Church in West Palm Beach offers free hot breakfast for students and families
entry.summary: A West Palm Beach church is helping make sure students start their school day with a hot meal while also providing food to families and people experiencing homelessness. Trinity United Methodist Church offers free breakfast every Tuesday and Friday from 6 a.m. to 8 a.m. during the school year. Students and families can stop by for a hot, balanced breakfast before heading to school. WATCH BELOW: Church serves free hot breakfast to students and families West Palm Beach church serves free hot breakfast to students and families For one student, that morning's menu was simple: 'Eggs, sausage, and grits.' Willie Miller II, co-coordinator of the church's feeding ministry, said the effort is about recognizing and responding to hunger within the community. 'As we look back over the years and trace the heartbeat of our community, our response to hunger has always been to pay attention to the quiet struggles happening right next door,' Miller said. The breakfast ministry started in 2016. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the program shifted from dine-in meals to a grab-and-go format, which continues today. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with neighbors like Agatha Bythwood and her daughter. She says the meals provide help before the school day begins. 'It's very helpful,' Bythwood said. 'It's great that they do all of this and feed the kids before they go off to school.' Miller said the ministry is about more than serving food. The church also wants to provide a welcoming place for people who may be struggling. 'Trinity United Methodist doors are wide open as a welcoming refuge for seniors navigating isolation and students carrying quiet morning burdens,' Miller said. 'You will feel seen, welcomed, valued by the community and our church,' Miller said.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco
entry.summary: On Monday, Port St. Lucie City Council approved three major site plans for projects along the Southern Grove, a developing jobs corridor in the city. One of those plans: the long-awaited Costco retail store. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie City Council approves site plan for Costco Port St Lucie approves site plan for Costco 'This is something that we have been looking forward to for a long time, Scott Samples with the City of Port St. Lucie said. Samples and Wes McCurry, president and CEO of the St. Lucie County Economic Development Council, said the 163,000-square-foot store is just the beginning for a new phase of growth in western Port St. Lucie. 'This is getting closer to the finish line,' Samples said. The Costco will join other companies like Amazon, Tamco and Cheney Brothers, calling the Southern Grove area home. McCurry said since the jobs are now here, new commercial development will follow. 'They see all the development that's occurring here, along with the demographics that they like to see, said McCurry. 'It only makes sense that Costco opens a retail store here.' City council approved two other major site plans for the area, including a 5.5-acre site making up the first phase of the Tradition Entertainment District set to bring restaurants and retail. 'This area has historically been largely underserved by restaurants and retail, and especially entertainment facilities, McCurry said. 'It's kind of catching up to the rooftops that are happening. You know, rooftops always drive that demand, but there's more to come.' The other plan is space for an acute care rehabilitation hospital, featuring inpatient and outpatient services with 42 beds in a more than 55,000-square-foot building. 'A growing area needs services, and that's just another component of services that are coming into the area is expanded healthcare access,' McCurry said. McCurry said the plans for retail, healthcare and entertainment are fulfilling the citys master plan for what Southern Grove was destined to become. 'The plan is coming together. The vision is coming together. What everyone saw 20 years ago is now starting to happen,' McCurry said. Samples said Costco still must close on the land, move on to construction design planning and permitting before any shovels hit the ground.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy - WPTV
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy    WPTV
entry.article_text: Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son, who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police.Port St. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later.WATCH: Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through DonationNow, the family's decision to donate his organs could help multiple people waiting for lifesaving transplants while creating a lasting legacy in his memory.Organ donation advocates say the family's choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists.The teen's family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families."It's a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it's the right thing," said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft.Craft has worked with Donate Life Florida through the tax collector's office to encourage organ donor registration and raise awareness about the need for donors.For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family's decision carries special meaning."Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place," Gray told WPTV.Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed."I know for a fact that I wouldn't be here without a family making that election in their deepest moment of despair," he said.Gray described years of uncertainty while waiting for a match."That's five years of uncertainty, five years of being paralyzed, five years of not being able to grow," he said.Organ donation advocates say the need for donors continues across Florida and the United States.Gray noted that a single donor has the potential to save multiple lives and help many more patients through tissue donation."One donor is to save upwards to nine lives and to be able to heal another 75 lives," Gray said.Behind those numbers are people awaiting a second chance, he said."Let's all be heroes and save lives," Gray added.Advocates say organ donation often allows families to find meaning during some of life's most difficult moments."I would hope that they could see the lasting impact that a selfless act can make on others," Craft said. "If you can help somebody else, it's an amazing thing."For transplant recipients, organ donation can mean more time with family, additional milestones and opportunities.In the midst of tragedy, one Port St. Lucie family's decision could now help save lives and ensure their son's legacy continues through the people he may help.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Driver flees after fatal motorcycle crash in Fort Pierce, police say
entry.summary: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say fled after a crash that killed a motorcyclist Sunday night. The crash happened around 8:52 p.m. near South 25th Street and Okeechobee Road. Officers responded after receiving multiple 911 calls about a crash involving a motorcycle. According to preliminary information from the Fort Pierce Police Department, a white box van traveling east on Okeechobee Road struck a blue motorcycle and attempted to leave the scene. Police said the van's driver made a U-turn in the eastbound lanes while fleeing, crossed the westbound lanes and crashed into Kings and Queens Unisex Salon at 2508 Okeechobee Road. The driver then got out of the van and fled north on foot, police said. When officers arrived, they found the motorcyclist in the outside eastbound lane of Okeechobee Road and determined the person had died. St. Lucie County Fire Rescue also responded. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 and Aviation units assisted Fort Pierce police in searching for the driver, but police said he had not been located as of Monday. Two other vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene. Police described the driver as an adult Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top and light-colored pants or shorts. The identity of the person killed has not been confirmed. The Fort Pierce Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit and Crime Scene Investigations are investigating. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's identity or whereabouts is asked to contact Fort Pierce police at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

entry.title: Treasure Coast travelers say limited transportation options make it 'difficult to get around'
entry.summary: A recent change to a flight out of Vero Beach is sparking a bigger conversation about travel options on the Treasure Coast. Travelers tell WPTV that limited flight schedules and a lack of convenient transportation alternatives can make getting in and out of the area difficult, sometimes forcing them to drive to larger airports or rearrange their plans. WATCH: Why Treasure Coast travelers say they need more options At the Vero Beach Regional Airport, travelers shared their frustrations with WPTV reporter Brooke Chau about the challenges of getting where they need to go. 'In the Treasure Coast area, Vero Beach specifically, it is difficult to get around,' said Peter Masella. He pointed to the lack of a Brightline station in Vero Beach, saying people often have to travel to other cities to access additional transportation options. A recent schedule change to Breeze Airways' route between the New York area and Vero Beach has added to those concerns. The flight, which previously departed from Westchester, New York in the evening, now leaves in the morning. A New York City physician told WPTV the change has affected his work schedule. 'I'm a physician working in New York City, and because of the change of flight for Vero Beach, I have had to rearrange my patients' schedules two days in a row, he said. Another traveler from Westchester, New York said the change can mean a longer trip. 'Then I have to take a taxi all the way down and around to Vero Beach. Its very inconvenient,' she said. However, Breeze Airways has also been adding destinations from Vero Beach. Last month, the airline introduced nonstop service to Trenton, Baltimore, Pittsburgh and Atlantic City, expanding the airport's commercial flight options. Vero Beach Airport Director Brandon Dambeck says airlines regularly evaluate the performance of their routes, which can lead to new destinations as well as schedule or route changes. All of these airlines are monitoring the routes and their gauge of success,' Dambeck said. For travelers, more destinations are welcome, but they say flight times that fit their schedules are just as important.

entry.title: Miami Dolphins at 0-5 using bye week to regroup before divisional matchup with the New York Jets
entry.summary: The Miami Dolphins are not treating their bye week as a throwaway. The team hit the practice field Tuesday at Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens to regroup after an 0-5 start to the season. After the break, the Dolphins will head north to take on divisional rival New York Jets (2-3) on Oct. 25. Players say the focus right now is on health and coming back locked in. Running back Ollie Gordon III said the team is using the time to get right and come together. 'Everybody is getting their legs back and everybody getting everything back together and everybody getting 100 percent and us getting out there and getting healthy while we get back and work together,' Gordon said. Offensive lineman Kadyn Proctor said the message from the coaching staff has been clear about what the team needs heading out of the bye. 'We have to have that fire in us. That's all coach has been saying. Just come back and be locked in, because if you ain't, we going to keep going like this,' Proctor said. While the Dolphins lost 31-24 last week to the Bengals, the team showed some positive signs, including a run game that continues to progress and Malik Willis' ability to keep plays alive with his legs. entry.title: Martin County advances proposed data center moratorium - WPEC
entry.summary: Martin County advances proposed data center moratorium    WPEC
entry.article_text: Martin County commissioners are moving forward with a proposed one-year moratorium on large-scale data centers, giving the county more time to study their potential impact before allowing new projects to move forward. The Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the proposal on its first reading Tuesday, Oct. A second public hearing is scheduled for Oct. 27 before the moratorium can receive final approval. The proposed ordinance would temporarily stop the county from accepting new applications for large-scale data centers in unincorporated areas of Martin County. It would not apply to municipalities. Under the proposal, large-scale data centers are defined as facilities with an anticipated peak electrical demand of 50 megawatts or more. County officials say the pause would give them time to study concerns surrounding data centers, including noise, water usage, electricity consumption, wastewater disposal and potential environmental impacts. During Tuesday's meeting, officials also revealed that the county received an application for a data center on Monday, just one day before the hearing. See also: Florida drug trafficking bust leads to 19 arrests, 6 more suspects sought Applications deemed complete before the moratorium takes effect would be allowed to move forward under existing regulations. Commissioner Sarah Heard questioned whether 365 days would be enough time for the county to complete the necessary research. She also asked whether the moratorium could apply to smaller facilities using 20 megawatts or more of electricity. County staff explained that the 50-megawatt threshold comes from state law defining large-scale data centers. Commissioner Edward Campi said the county needs to hear from experts on both sides of the issue before making long-term decisions. Campi referenced a recent visit to Virginia, where he toured an area with approximately 120 data centers and observed their appearance and noise levels. He said the proposed moratorium would provide an opportunity for supporters and opponents to share their perspectives. Blake Capps also supported the proposal, saying the county needs to carefully consider where data centers could be located, including areas within its urban services boundaries. Commissioner Heatherington was absent from Tuesday's meeting. The county first directed its attorney to draft the moratorium in August as concerns grew over the potential impact of large-scale data centers. The proposal will return to commissioners for a second public hearing on Tuesday, Oct. If approved, the moratorium would give Martin County up to a year to review its regulations before accepting new applications for large-scale data centers.

It's about the controls of the vessel," said Michael Meekins, executive director of the Port of Palm Beach.Meekins said newer ships can come equipped with advanced propulsion systems that make them easier to maneuver than traditional vessels.The debate also centers on proposed mooring dolphins, offshore structures that allow ships to tie up beyond the existing dock.Meekins described the structures as a common maritime tool that can accommodate different vessel configurations without constructing an entirely new dock."You have the normal pier and then out from the pier you just have a catwalk, and then there's a concrete anchorage system with some moorings on it, and that allows the ship to tie up out there without having to build an entire dock," Meekins said.He said no final approval has been made on how many mooring dolphins will be installed or how far out from the port they will be.I addressed Gary's concerns about larger ships with boaters, swimmers and snorkelers near Peanut Island, and Meekins pushed back."The cruise line really has zero impact on the local tourists who are going out to Peanut Island or anything else," Meekins said. entry.summary: A 54-year-old man suspected of robbing a pizza delivery driver was fatally shot by a Palm Beach County sheriff's deputy Tuesday after a pursuit ended near Jog and Woolbright roads, Sheriff Ric Bradshaw said. Bradshaw said the investigation began after a pizza delivery driver was robbed around 10 p.m. Monday. The suspect allegedly ordered a pizza to a location and told the driver he only had a $100 bill. When the driver pulled out money to make change, the suspect allegedly grabbed him, and the two struggled over the cash. Investigators entered that information into license plate readers and received an alert Tuesday that the vehicle was in the Lake Park area. PBSO tactical units located the vehicle and conducted surveillance to confirm the registered owner was driving, according to Bradshaw. When deputies attempted a traffic stop, the driver fled, Bradshaw said. entry.title: Martin County commissioners unanimously move forward with 1-year moratorium on data centers
entry.summary: Martin County commissioners voted Tuesday unanimously to move forward with a one-year moratorium on data centers as county leaders consider how to handle future development of the facilities. Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi explained it's, 'an opportunity to say, 'pause,' let's hear from people, lets have the opportunity for experts to come and speak to us on both sides. Commissioners explained they would consider extending the moratorium later if they need more time. If it takes a year, a year and a half, two years, whatever it takes, whatever it takes, we should be doing this, said Martin County Commissioner Eileen Vargas. Tuesday's vote marked the first of two hearings scheduled this month on the proposed moratorium. PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Martin County eyes pause on data center development Martin County eyes pause on data center development Commissioners are expected to take up the issue again on Oct. 27, when another vote will be required. Residents are now hoping the county will use the time to consider their concerns. For me its wildlife so these areas are in largely rural or large plots of land and so you take that area and develop it and these facilities are massivemillions and millions of square feet, no animals can live there anymore, or the hum is going to affect the animals, said Sergei Kelley, who spoke at the meeting. Martin County resident, Scott Butler added, 'The fear of the use of all this water we have [...] and understanding what these data center are going to use. The discussion comes as Martin County has already received an application for a data center. The county received the application Monday, one day before commissioners considered the moratorium. Its the first data center proposed in unincorporated Martin County. The application is considered a hyper-scale data center, at over 950-thousand square feet proposed on a lot off Kanner Highway west of I-95. Because the application was submitted before the proposed moratorium, it would not be affected by the measure. The proposal comes amid concerns from residents about the future of data center development in Martin County. entry.title: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 54-year-old Jupiter woman is facing felony charges after she allegedly removed fentanyl from a critically ill patient's IV infusion while working at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said Monday. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. "We take these allegations very seriously," Cleveland Clinic spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF in a statement. "She individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Investigators learned a family member reported witnessing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Pope was not assigned to the patient's care. The next evening, Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room and again approached the IV equipment, police said. The family member intervened. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the police agency said in a news release. "We remain committed to thorough, evidence-based investigations and pursuing accountability when the evidence supports criminal charges." This remains an active criminal case. entry.title: Miami Dolphins at 0-5 using bye week to regroup before divisional matchup with the New York Jets
entry.summary: The Miami Dolphins are not treating their bye week as a throwaway. The team hit the practice field Tuesday at Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens to regroup after an 0-5 start to the season. After the break, the Dolphins will head north to take on divisional rival New York Jets (2-3) on Oct. 25. Players say the focus right now is on health and coming back locked in. WATCH BELOW: Dolphins use bye week to get healthy, prep for Jets Dolphins use bye week to get healthy, prep for Jets Running back Ollie Gordon III said the team is using the time to get right and come together. 'Everybody is getting their legs back and everybody getting everything back together and everybody getting 100 percent and us getting out there and getting healthy while we get back and work together,' Gordon said. Offensive lineman Kadyn Proctor said the message from the coaching staff has been clear about what the team needs heading out of the bye. 'We have to have that fire in us. That's all coach has been saying. Just come back and be locked in, because if you ain't, we going to keep going like this,' Proctor said. While the Dolphins lost 31-24 last week to the Bengals, the team showed some positive signs, including a run game that continues to progress and Malik Willis' ability to keep plays alive with his legs. Gordon said the team has embraced the run game. 'I feel like it's been good; the team we have is good to be able to run behind them and play with them,' Gordon said. entry.title: Martin County advances proposed data center moratorium - WPEC
entry.summary: Martin County advances proposed data center moratorium    WPEC
entry.article_text: Martin County commissioners are moving forward with a proposed one-year moratorium on large-scale data centers, giving the county more time to study their potential impact before allowing new projects to move forward. The Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the proposal on its first reading Tuesday, Oct. A second public hearing is scheduled for Oct. 27 before the moratorium can receive final approval. The proposed ordinance would temporarily stop the county from accepting new applications for large-scale data centers in unincorporated areas of Martin County. It would not apply to municipalities. Under the proposal, large-scale data centers are defined as facilities with an anticipated peak electrical demand of 50 megawatts or more. County officials say the pause would give them time to study concerns surrounding data centers, including noise, water usage, electricity consumption, wastewater disposal and potential environmental impacts. During Tuesday's meeting, officials also revealed that the county received an application for a data center on Monday, just one day before the hearing. See also: Florida drug trafficking bust leads to 19 arrests, 6 more suspects sought Applications deemed complete before the moratorium takes effect would be allowed to move forward under existing regulations. Commissioner Sarah Heard questioned whether 365 days would be enough time for the county to complete the necessary research. She also asked whether the moratorium could apply to smaller facilities using 20 megawatts or more of electricity. County staff explained that the 50-megawatt threshold comes from state law defining large-scale data centers. Commissioner Edward Campi said the county needs to hear from experts on both sides of the issue before making long-term decisions. Campi referenced a recent visit to Virginia, where he toured an area with approximately 120 data centers and observed their appearance and noise levels. He said the proposed moratorium would provide an opportunity for supporters and opponents to share their perspectives. Blake Capps also supported the proposal, saying the county needs to carefully consider where data centers could be located, including areas within its urban services boundaries. Commissioner Heatherington was absent from Tuesday's meeting. The county first directed its attorney to draft the moratorium in August as concerns grew over the potential impact of large-scale data centers. The proposal will return to commissioners for a second public hearing on Tuesday, Oct. If approved, the moratorium would give Martin County up to a year to review its regulations before accepting new applications for large-scale data centers.

entry.title: Florida executes a prisoner who killed his cellmate in hopes of getting a death sentence

James Robertson, 63, declined to offer any last words before receiving a three-drug injection and was pronounced dead about 10 minutes later. It was a stark contrast to the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee two weeks ago, where she was rushed to the hospital after surviving two lethal doses of pentobarbital . Robertsons execution, the first in Florida since Pike, comes at a time of escalating attention on the death penalty in the United States. The Pentagon said last week that it would livestream the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan, drawing criticism from both Republican and Democratic lawmakers. entry.article_text: A Florida prisoner who said he killed his cellmate specifically to get on death row was executed Tuesday, nearly 18 years after the attack.James Robertson, 63, declined to offer any last words before receiving a three-drug injection and was pronounced dead about 10 minutes later. It was a stark contrast to the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee two weeks ago, where she was rushed to the hospital after surviving two lethal doses of pentobarbital.Robertson’s execution, the first in Florida since Pike, comes at a time of escalating attention on the death penalty in the United States. The Pentagon said last week that it would livestream the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan, drawing criticism from both Republican and Democratic lawmakers.“Florida has a sound lethal injection process and protocol,” Jordan Kirkland, a state Department of Corrections spokesperson, said at a news conference before the execution. Although he couldn’t speak to Tennessee’s lethal injection procedure, he said Florida would make sure its process was “humane and dignified.”Florida executes people by injecting them with a sedative, a paralytic, and a drug that stops the heart, according to the Department of Corrections.Robertson had pleaded guilty to first-degree murder for strangling Frank Hart while he slept in 2008, and waived all appeals. He told investigators that he did it so he wouldn't have to live out his days in prison.Hart was killed just eight days before he was due to be released, his daughter, Rebecca Hart, told reporters at Florida State Prison. She stressed that her father was not just a piece of Robertson’s story.“When someone you love is taken from you in such a violent way, the world keeps moving, even when a part of yours feels like it has stopped,” she read. “Other people go on with their lives, but you carry your loss into every tomorrow.”Robertson was 17 years old when he went to prison in 1980 for burglary and assault. Years of convictions for escape, battery and weapons while in prison kept adding time to his total sentence. Hart had been sent to prison in 2003 following a sexual battery conviction.Robertson was supposed to be one of two executions carried out by Florida on Tuesday, but Gov. Ron DeSantis withdrew a death warrant last week for William Lee Thompson. The Republican governor did not provide a reason but had temporarily stayed the execution last month pending a psychiatric evaluation.Records show this was the first time DeSantis withdrew a death warrant. Thompson, 74, will remain on death row, and a new death warrant could be signed in the future. His attorneys say he has dementia and failing health, and they want him transferred to a medical facility.DeSantis is the third Florida governor to sign a death warrant for Thompson. Bob Graham and Bob Martinez both scheduled executions for Thompson in the 1980s, but years of appeals and stays allowed him to avoid the electric chair, the state's method of execution at the time.Thompson was convicted of first-degree murder, kidnapping and sexual battery in the 1976 killing of 23-year-old Sally Ivester.DeSantis oversaw 19 executions in 2025, more than any other Florida governor in a single year since the death penalty was reinstated in 1976. Robertson was the state’s 17th execution of 2026, with two more already scheduled, not counting Thompson.DeSantis, who leaves office in January, has made few public comments about the unprecedented number of executions but explained previously that his goal is to bring justice to victims’ families who have waited decades for the death sentences to be carried out.William Reaves, 77, is scheduled to be executed on Oct. 20, followed by Jesse Guardado, 64, on Nov. Reaves was convicted of fatally shooting a deputy after dropping a gun in front of the law enforcement officer in 1986. Guardado was convicted of robbing and killing a woman in order to buy drugs in 2004.A total of 47 people were executed in the U.S. Besides leading all other states last year, Florida has carried out more than half the 31 total executions in the U.S. In July, Florida executed two prisoners in one day, the first state in nearly a decade to do so.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag    WPBF
entry.article_text: A nurse at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie is under investigation after allegedly stealing fentanyl from a critically ill patient’s IV bag on June 24 and 25, according to police. "They did an internal investigation where the Department of Health was then notified, in turn notifying PSLPD where we started our investigation in early August," said Officer Brittany McNally, public information officer for the Port St. Police said a family member of the patient reported seeing 54-year-old Leslie Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient’s fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket, and leave the room. "That’s not standard procedure, from what I understand at the hospital," McNally said. "But again, she’s not even assigned that patient. And there was no initial justification for her to even be in that room at the time." Investigators said Pope returned the following evening and approached the IV equipment again, but the family member intervened and stopped her. Hospital video reportedly showed Pope manipulating protective caps on the IV equipment, but investigators said she did not remove any fluid during the second incident. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 "The patient was on a specific monitor for the situation that he was in the ICU. And this individual had this monitor that had video recordings, which was a key piece of evidence in this case and completely contradicted what her recollection was," McNally said. Police said Pope denied the allegations and did not admit to using the fentanyl for personal consumption. "From my understanding, she did not admit that she was using it for personal consumption and essentially denied all the allegations that were made, but there was an overwhelming amount of evidence to prove otherwise," McNally said. Cleveland Clinic released a statement regarding the arrest, saying, "We take these allegations very seriously. The individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." The investigation remains ongoing.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy    WFLX
entry.article_text: Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son , who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later. Now, the family’s decision to donate his organs could help multiple people waiting for lifesaving transplants while creating a lasting legacy in his memory. Organ donation advocates say the family’s choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists. The teen’s family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families. “It’s a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it’s the right thing,” said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft. Craft has worked with Donate Life Florida through the tax collector’s office to encourage organ donor registration and raise awareness about the need for donors. For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family’s decision carries special meaning. “Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place,” Gray told WPTV. Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed. “I know for a fact that I wouldn’t be here without a family making that election in their deepest moment of despair,” he said. Gray described years of uncertainty while waiting for a match. “That’s five years of uncertainty, five years of being paralyzed, five years of not being able to grow,” he said. Organ donation advocates say the need for donors continues across Florida and the United States. Gray noted that a single donor has the potential to save multiple lives and help many more patients through tissue donation. “One donor is to save upwards of nine lives and to be able to heal another 75 lives,” Gray said. Behind those numbers are people awaiting a second chance, he said. “Let’s all be heroes and save lives,” Gray added. Advocates say organ donation often allows families to find meaning during some of life’s most difficult moments. “I would hope that they could see the lasting impact that a selfless act can make on others,” Craft said. “If you can help somebody else, it’s an amazing thing.” For transplant recipients, organ donation can mean more time with family, additional milestones and opportunities. In the midst of tragedy, one Port St. Lucie family’s decision could now help save lives and ensure their son’s legacy continues through the people he may help. entry.summary: Local leaders joined housing advocates in West Palm Beach on Tuesday to discuss rising homeowners association fees and condo assessments that they say are putting financial pressure on residents, particularly seniors and people struggling to remain in their homes. Condo costs create affordability concerns Florida condominium owners have faced increased financial pressures following reforms adopted in response to the 2021 Surfside condominium collapse. entry.title: City council approves lease agreement to bring hotel to Vero Beach Regional Airport area
entry.summary: WPTV has been reporting extensively on the growth at the Vero Beach Regional Airport when it comes to flights. But on Tuesday, Vero Beach City Council approved a lease agreement to bring a four-story, 116-room Marriott hotel to the airport. 'We've been in negotiations with this for the last three years, Brian Dembeck, interim airport director, said. 'This is something that is going to dramatically improve the passenger experience.' Dembeck took WPTV to the site, which sits just outside the gates of the terminal along Aviation Boulevard. 'They're going to have a hotel right next door that they can come, they can stay, wait for their flight, and then go right over to the terminal.' But the lodging is more than just for passengers. Brian Cartland, vice-president of economic development for the Indian River County Chamber of Commerce, said the hotel could attract more businesses to the city of Vero Beach and beyond. 'The hotel is going to serve multiple purposes, said Cartland. 'This hotel is going to help target industry growth by giving those companies that are looking at the area some additional alternatives for some great high-end options.' While the hotel is close to the airport, Chad Maxey, senior vice president of Diversified Companies, the developer of the project, said one big need for the extra lodging is just down the street at the Jackie Robinson Training Complex. 'We feel this is a great location to have a hotel that's going to be able to provide amenities to the airport and also to the families and kids that are going to play baseball, Maxey said. Maxey said the hotel will also feature a homerun dugout amenity for families. 'Kids can play virtual baseball in the hotel as they're getting ready to go across the street and actually hit the diamond over there and play with the major league baseball players, Maxey said. Developers said the hotel will break ground next year and expected to be completed by end of 2028.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco
entry.summary: On Monday, Port St. Lucie City Council approved three major site plans for projects along the Southern Grove, a developing jobs corridor in the city. One of those plans: the long-awaited Costco retail store. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie City Council approves site plan for Costco Port St Lucie approves site plan for Costco 'This is something that we have been looking forward to for a long time, Scott Samples with the City of Port St. Lucie said. Samples and Wes McCurry, president and CEO of the St. Lucie County Economic Development Council, said the 163,000-square-foot store is just the beginning for a new phase of growth in western Port St. Lucie. 'This is getting closer to the finish line,' Samples said. The Costco will join other companies like Amazon, Tamco and Cheney Brothers, calling the Southern Grove area home. McCurry said since the jobs are now here, new commercial development will follow. 'They see all the development that's occurring here, along with the demographics that they like to see, said McCurry. 'It only makes sense that Costco opens a retail store here.' City council approved two other major site plans for the area, including a 5.5-acre site making up the first phase of the Tradition Entertainment District set to bring restaurants and retail. 'This area has historically been largely underserved by restaurants and retail, and especially entertainment facilities, McCurry said. 'It's kind of catching up to the rooftops that are happening. You know, rooftops always drive that demand, but there's more to come.' The other plan is space for an acute care rehabilitation hospital, featuring inpatient and outpatient services with 42 beds in a more than 55,000-square-foot building. 'A growing area needs services, and that's just another component of services that are coming into the area is expanded healthcare access,' McCurry said. McCurry said the plans for retail, healthcare and entertainment are fulfilling the citys master plan for what Southern Grove was destined to become. 'The plan is coming together. The vision is coming together. What everyone saw 20 years ago is now starting to happen,' McCurry said. Samples said Costco still must close on the land, move on to construction design planning and permitting before any shovels hit the ground.

entry.title: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Just days after MARTY public bus services abruptly shut down in Martin County, county commissioners voted unanimously Tuesday to allow the county administrator to negotiate a new contract with a company that could restore service. The vote gives county administration the green light to begin negotiations with MTM Transit, a company that previously operated the county’s public bus system. For former MARTY bus driver Bill Lawrence, Tuesday’s decision offered a sign of hope after he and several other drivers suddenly lost their jobs last Thursday. “I’m hoping that we get this back on the road soon. We need our employees, our drivers, to get back to work,” Lawrence said. Lawrence was among the drivers impacted when Martin County Transit LLC, the company previously operating MARTY, abruptly stopped services last Thursday. The company cited rising operating costs, including fuel and maintenance, as reasons for its decision to discontinue service. During Tuesday’s county commission meeting, Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton explained that county officials had spent the past several days exploring options to restore service. “We reached out to a number of vendors; a number of vendors reached out to us,” Gorton said. According to Gorton, the county evaluated several proposals before identifying MTM Transit as its preferred option. Under the county’s emergency procurement rules, the proposed agreement would be a one-year contract costing approximately $3 million. During that year, county officials would work toward establishing a standard multi-year contract through the county’s normal competitive bidding process. One of the county’s priorities during negotiations is bringing back the drivers who lost their jobs following last week’s shutdown. “We absolutely want to use those same drivers and get them back to work as quickly as possible,” Gorton said. Commissioners also authorized county administration to move forward with terminating its previous contract with Martin County Transit LLC. County officials say they are hopeful negotiations with MTM Transit can be finalized by the end of this week, potentially allowing buses to begin operating again next week. entry.title: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon - cw34.com
entry.summary: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Obtained 911 recordings capture the frantic moments following the crash. In one call, a person inside the Toyota pickup truck described the aftermath. "We got hit, and it's like, there's blood all over our car," the caller told a dispatcher. Another caller reported seeing the white van crash into the nearby building while trying to get away. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. According to a police news release, the driver ran northbound after crashing into the salon, located at 2508 Okeechobee Road. Police responded to multiple 911 calls reporting the crash around 8:52 p.m. and immediately established a perimeter, searching for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit. Despite their efforts, they were unable to locate him. Two additional vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene, according to police. The department's Traffic Homicide Unit, Crime Scene Investigations and other personnel processed the scene as part of the ongoing investigation. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. Police said the victim's identity had not yet been confirmed as of Monday, and confirmation was still pending before next of kin could be notified. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's whereabouts is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or submit a tip through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers .

entry.summary: A St. Lucie County Fire District board member is calling on Fire Chief Jeff Lee to resign after firefighters delivered an overwhelming vote of no confidence in district leadership, the latest fallout from a hazing investigation that led to the firing of three veteran firefighters. More than 74% of firefighters who participated in the union vote said they had no confidence in Lee. About 92% said they had no confidence in Assistant Chief Brian Gonzalez, while 97% said the same of district attorney Kim Sabol. 'They've sent their message, and now it's, again, up for the board to take action.' entry.title: City council approves lease agreement to bring hotel to Vero Beach Regional Airport area
entry.summary: WPTV has been reporting extensively on the growth at the Vero Beach Regional Airport when it comes to flights. But on Tuesday, Vero Beach City Council approved a lease agreement to bring a four-story, 116-room Marriott hotel to the airport. 'We've been in negotiations with this for the last three years, Brian Dembeck, interim airport director, said. 'This is something that is going to dramatically improve the passenger experience.' Dembeck took WPTV to the site, which sits just outside the gates of the terminal along Aviation Boulevard. 'They're going to have a hotel right next door that they can come, they can stay, wait for their flight, and then go right over to the terminal.' But the lodging is more than just for passengers.
