entry.title: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Just days after MARTY public bus services abruptly shut down in Martin County, county commissioners voted unanimously Tuesday to allow the county administrator to negotiate a new contract with a company that could restore service. The vote gives county administration the green light to begin negotiations with MTM Transit, a company that previously operated the county’s public bus system. For former MARTY bus driver Bill Lawrence, Tuesday’s decision offered a sign of hope after he and several other drivers suddenly lost their jobs last Thursday. “I’m hoping that we get this back on the road soon. We need our employees, our drivers, to get back to work,” Lawrence said. Lawrence was among the drivers impacted when Martin County Transit LLC, the company previously operating MARTY, abruptly stopped services last Thursday. The company cited rising operating costs, including fuel and maintenance, as reasons for its decision to discontinue service. During Tuesday’s county commission meeting, Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton explained that county officials had spent the past several days exploring options to restore service. “We reached out to a number of vendors; a number of vendors reached out to us,” Gorton said. According to Gorton, the county evaluated several proposals before identifying MTM Transit as its preferred option. Under the county’s emergency procurement rules, the proposed agreement would be a one-year contract costing approximately $3 million. During that year, county officials would work toward establishing a standard multi-year contract through the county’s normal competitive bidding process. One of the county’s priorities during negotiations is bringing back the drivers who lost their jobs following last week’s shutdown. “We absolutely want to use those same drivers and get them back to work as quickly as possible,” Gorton said. Commissioners also authorized county administration to move forward with terminating its previous contract with Martin County Transit LLC. County officials say they are hopeful negotiations with MTM Transit can be finalized by the end of this week, potentially allowing buses to begin operating again next week. entry.title: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag    WPBF
entry.article_text: A nurse at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie is under investigation after allegedly stealing fentanyl from a critically ill patient’s IV bag on June 24 and 25, according to police. "They did an internal investigation where the Department of Health was then notified, in turn notifying PSLPD where we started our investigation in early August," said Officer Brittany McNally, public information officer for the Port St. Police said a family member of the patient reported seeing 54-year-old Leslie Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient’s fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket, and leave the room. "That’s not standard procedure, from what I understand at the hospital," McNally said. "But again, she’s not even assigned that patient. And there was no initial justification for her to even be in that room at the time." Investigators said Pope returned the following evening and approached the IV equipment again, but the family member intervened and stopped her. Hospital video reportedly showed Pope manipulating protective caps on the IV equipment, but investigators said she did not remove any fluid during the second incident. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 "The patient was on a specific monitor for the situation that he was in the ICU. And this individual had this monitor that had video recordings, which was a key piece of evidence in this case and completely contradicted what her recollection was," McNally said. Police said Pope denied the allegations and did not admit to using the fentanyl for personal consumption. "From my understanding, she did not admit that she was using it for personal consumption and essentially denied all the allegations that were made, but there was an overwhelming amount of evidence to prove otherwise," McNally said. Cleveland Clinic released a statement regarding the arrest, saying, "We take these allegations very seriously. The individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." The investigation remains ongoing.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco    WFLX
entry.article_text: Lucie City Council approved three major site plans for projects along the Southern Grove, a developing jobs corridor in the city. One of those plans: the long-awaited Costco retail store. “This is something that we have been looking forward to for a long time,” Scott Samples with the City of Port St. Samples and Wes McCurry, president and CEO of the St. Lucie County Economic Development Council, said the 163,000-square-foot store is just the beginning for a new phase of growth in western Port St. “This is getting closer to the finish line,” Samples said. The Costco will join other companies like Amazon, Tamco and Cheney Brothers, calling the Southern Grove area home. McCurry said since the jobs are now here, new commercial development will follow. “They see all the development that’s occurring here, along with the demographics that they like to see,” said McCurry. “It only makes sense that Costco opens a retail store here.” City council approved two other major site plans for the area, including a 5.5-acre site making up the first phase of the Tradition Entertainment District set to bring restaurants and retail. “This area has historically been largely underserved by restaurants and retail, and especially entertainment facilities,” McCurry said. “It’s kind of catching up to the rooftops that are happening. You know, rooftops always drive that demand, but there’s more to come.” The other plan is space for an acute care rehabilitation hospital, featuring inpatient and outpatient services with 42 beds in a more than 55,000-square-foot building. “A growing area needs services, and that’s just another component of services that are coming into the area is expanded healthcare access,” McCurry said. McCurry said the plans for retail, healthcare and entertainment are fulfilling the city’s master plan for what Southern Grove was destined to become. “The plan is coming together. The vision is coming together. What everyone saw 20 years ago is now starting to happen,” McCurry said. Samples said Costco still must close on the land, move on to construction design planning and permitting before any shovels hit the ground.

entry.title: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death - WPEC
entry.summary: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie Boulevard say more needs to be done to protect pedestrians as construction continues on the busy road. Their concerns come after a 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student died from injuries he suffered when he was hit by an SUV while walking to school. Police say the freshman was walking along the edge of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on the morning of Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He was pronounced clinically deceased two days later. His family chose to donate his organs . Much of the roadway remains under construction, and there are no sidewalks along large sections of the corridor. Recent heavy rain also left portions of the shoulder flooded, further limiting space for pedestrians. "He was just going to school," said neighbor Irene Ange. "He was just starting his high school year. He had the right to be safe." Irene Ange, who has lived near the boulevard for more than two decades, says students often walk or bike close to traffic, sometimes before sunrise. The stretch of road is dangerous, Ange said. It’s very dark, and drivers are not following the speed limits. Ange said she saw first responders rushing to the crash site and was heartbroken for the student and his family. See also: Suspect booked into Martin County Jail after undercover drug sting, sheriff says The teen’s mother told CBS12 by phone that her son was a people person who made friends easily. She said the family does not want this to happen to another child. The Florida Department of Transportation is widening the southern portion of Port St. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four and adding sidewalks on both sides of the road. FDOT says the sidewalks will be eight to 10 feet wide. The project is expected to be completed in winter 2028, with an estimated cost of about $25.6 million. CBS 12 saw crews building sidewalks several blocks from where the crash happened. FDOT did not respond to questions about what pedestrian safety measures are in place while construction continues. "No accountability with that response because now there's another death," Ange said. Ange says more needs to be done now to keep children safe on their way to school. "This did not have to happen to this family," Ange said. The family now have to mourn him." The driver initially told officers he believed he had struck a construction barrel and has been cooperating with investigators. It remains unclear whether any charges will be filed.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son , who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police. Port St. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later. Organ donation advocates say the family's choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists. Family's decision offers hope to others The teen's family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families. Transplant recipient shares personal perspective For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family's decision carries special meaning. entry.title: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Just days after MARTY public bus services abruptly shut down in Martin County, county commissioners voted unanimously Tuesday to allow the county administrator to negotiate a new contract with a company that could restore service. The vote gives county administration the green light to begin negotiations with MTM Transit, a company that previously operated the county’s public bus system. For former MARTY bus driver Bill Lawrence, Tuesday’s decision offered a sign of hope after he and several other drivers suddenly lost their jobs last Thursday. “I’m hoping that we get this back on the road soon. We need our employees, our drivers, to get back to work,” Lawrence said. Lawrence was among the drivers impacted when Martin County Transit LLC, the company previously operating MARTY, abruptly stopped services last Thursday. The company cited rising operating costs, including fuel and maintenance, as reasons for its decision to discontinue service. During Tuesday’s county commission meeting, Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton explained that county officials had spent the past several days exploring options to restore service. “We reached out to a number of vendors; a number of vendors reached out to us,” Gorton said. According to Gorton, the county evaluated several proposals before identifying MTM Transit as its preferred option. Under the county’s emergency procurement rules, the proposed agreement would be a one-year contract costing approximately $3 million. During that year, county officials would work toward establishing a standard multi-year contract through the county’s normal competitive bidding process. One of the county’s priorities during negotiations is bringing back the drivers who lost their jobs following last week’s shutdown. “We absolutely want to use those same drivers and get them back to work as quickly as possible,” Gorton said. Commissioners also authorized county administration to move forward with terminating its previous contract with Martin County Transit LLC. County officials say they are hopeful negotiations with MTM Transit can be finalized by the end of this week, potentially allowing buses to begin operating again next week. entry.title: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag    WPBF
entry.article_text: A nurse at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie is under investigation after allegedly stealing fentanyl from a critically ill patient’s IV bag on June 24 and 25, according to police. "They did an internal investigation where the Department of Health was then notified, in turn notifying PSLPD where we started our investigation in early August," said Officer Brittany McNally, public information officer for the Port St. Police said a family member of the patient reported seeing 54-year-old Leslie Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient’s fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket, and leave the room. "That’s not standard procedure, from what I understand at the hospital," McNally said. "But again, she’s not even assigned that patient. And there was no initial justification for her to even be in that room at the time." Investigators said Pope returned the following evening and approached the IV equipment again, but the family member intervened and stopped her. Hospital video reportedly showed Pope manipulating protective caps on the IV equipment, but investigators said she did not remove any fluid during the second incident. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 "The patient was on a specific monitor for the situation that he was in the ICU. And this individual had this monitor that had video recordings, which was a key piece of evidence in this case and completely contradicted what her recollection was," McNally said. Police said Pope denied the allegations and did not admit to using the fentanyl for personal consumption. "From my understanding, she did not admit that she was using it for personal consumption and essentially denied all the allegations that were made, but there was an overwhelming amount of evidence to prove otherwise," McNally said. Cleveland Clinic released a statement regarding the arrest, saying, "We take these allegations very seriously. The individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." The investigation remains ongoing.

entry.title: Van driver sought after fleeing fatal crash involving scooter in Fort Pierce - WPBF
entry.summary: Van driver sought after fleeing fatal crash involving scooter in Fort Pierce    WPBF
entry.article_text: Police are searching for a hit-and-run cargo van driver accused of fatally striking a 44-year-old man riding a gas scooter before he crashed into a nearby business and ran away in Fort Pierce. On Tuesday, the victim was identified as Andy Ramon Martinez-Pantoja. Police officers received multiple 911 calls just before 9 p.m. Sunday about a vehicle crash involving a motorcycle, which later was identified as a gas scooter, close to the intersection of Okeechobee Road and 25th Street, near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. A white cargo van was behind the scooter, traveling east on Okeechobee Road, Maj. Michael Santiago told WPBF's Angela Rozier at a briefing Monday afternoon. The van driver fled the scene and made a U-turn to drive in the wrong direction across the median on Okeechobee Road, but he crashed into the side of a building, the Kings Queens Unisex Salon. The man then ran from the scene. Salon owner Sheila Hampton showed the damage, and is thankful no one was inside at the time. Hampton said she feels for the victim and his family. "His family told me he was just leaving from one of his friend's houses and just going home," she said. A second vehicle, a Toyota pickup truck, was also struck, but no one was injured. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit and Aviation Unit assisted Fort Pierce police and the K-9 Unit in efforts to locate the driver. They are in possession of the van. Police described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top with light-colored pants or shorts. "So, that in itself proves intent that that person knew exactly what they were doing at the time and was just trying to simply get away," Santiago said. Anyone with information should call the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon - cw34.com
entry.summary: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Obtained 911 recordings capture the frantic moments following the crash. In one call, a person inside the Toyota pickup truck described the aftermath. "We got hit, and it's like, there's blood all over our car," the caller told a dispatcher. Another caller reported seeing the white van crash into the nearby building while trying to get away. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. According to a police news release, the driver ran northbound after crashing into the salon, located at 2508 Okeechobee Road. Police responded to multiple 911 calls reporting the crash around 8:52 p.m. and immediately established a perimeter, searching for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit. Despite their efforts, they were unable to locate him. Two additional vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene, according to police. The department's Traffic Homicide Unit, Crime Scene Investigations and other personnel processed the scene as part of the ongoing investigation. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. Police said the victim's identity had not yet been confirmed as of Monday, and confirmation was still pending before next of kin could be notified. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's whereabouts is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or submit a tip through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers .

entry.title: Road, flight restrictions set to take effect near Mar-a-Lago this weekend
entry.summary: A major stretch of South Ocean Boulevard in Palm Beach is scheduled to close Friday morning until further notice, prompting traffic changes for residents and commuters in the area. According to the Town of Palm Beach's website, South Ocean Boulevard (State Road A1A) will close between South County Road and Southern Boulevard beginning at 5 a.m. Friday, Oct. 16. The closure will remain in effect until further notice. Town officials said information about traffic checkpoints, modified bridge-opening schedules and temporary marine security zones is available on the town's Planned Traffic Impacts webpage . The closure announcement comes as federal aviation officials issued a Temporary Flight Restriction, or TFR, for VIP movement in the West Palm Beach area. The notice is scheduled to take effect Saturday, Oct. 17, and remain in place through Sunday, Oct. 18. Similar road and airspace restrictions have been implemented in the past during visits by former President Donald Trump to his Mar-a-Lago residence. At this time, neither the Town of Palm Beach nor federal authorities have publicly confirmed whether Trump is expected to be in Palm Beach this weekend. Motorists are encouraged to plan ahead and expect delays in the area surrounding the closure.

entry.title: Scripps News poll: 40% of voters say they’ve been fooled by AI ads this campaign
entry.summary: Many Americans say theyve been confused or even fooled by political ads using artificial intelligence this campaign season, and want more rules governing how the technology is used, according to a new Scripps News/Talker Research poll. More than four-in-ten registered voters say theyve seen something they thought was real in a political ad, only to later find it was AI-generated. Another 30% said they saw something they werent sure was real or AI. Some of the most talked about ads of the campaign have featured AI-generated candidates like Sen. Jon Ossoff in a beauty salon , James Talarico reciting old quotes out of context , and Sherrod Brown overstaying his welcome at a birthday party . More than half of survey respondents (56%) said they have seen Republicans using AI ads, compared with 49% saying they have seen ads for Democrats. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors And more than three-quarters of voters say there should be rules around how the technology is used in politics. In the absence of federal regulation, states have passed their own laws aimed at curbing the influence of AI or deepfakes in campaign advertising. Some states require disclosures or bar deepfake videos from being published in the weeks leading up to Election Day. But many of the regulations fail to keep up with the evolving use of what can be a cheap and effective new tool. An analysis from the Wesleyan Media Project from early September found AI tools had been used in at least 164 ads, 69% of which did not disclose AI was used. Eighty percent were from Republicans or Republican-leaning groups. Still, a similar amount of voters in both parties say there should be rules around how the technology is used, according to the Scripps News/Talker Research poll, including 77% of Democrats and 79% of Republicans. Concerns about how AI could impact areas outside politics also cut across party lines. Large swaths of the country worry about the impact AI could have on their jobs (61%), government institutions (83%), financial institutions (81%), and their physical safety (57%). Nearly 80% say they see content they believe was generated by AI at least once per day. This random double-opt-in online survey of 1,000 U.S. registered voters was commissioned by Scripps News and conducted by market research company Talker Research, in accordance with the Market Research Societys code of conduct. Data was collected from Sept. 30-Oct. 1, 20

entry.title: Republicans are flooding Senate races with ad money, but paying a premium
entry.summary: Republicans are spending hundreds of millions of dollars on advertising in battleground Senate races as they scramble to defend increasingly competitive GOP seats in the final stretch of the midterms. But when it comes to how far they can stretch a dollar, theyre effectively paying premium prices at Whole Foods while Democrats are shopping deals at Costco. RELATED STORY | Trump is heading all the way to Alaska in a sign of just how close its Senate race may be Across nine of the most competitive Senate races last month, Republicans cumulatively outspent Democrats on broadcast TV ads by nearly 100% more, $233 million to $121 million, according to AdImpact data, but only saw about 40% more rating points. The disparity comes down to a difference in strategy. Republicans are relying heavily on outside groups, like super PACs, that pay elevated rates for ads and are making big buys late in the campaign, when inventory is stretched. By contrast, Democrats are taking advantage of discounted rates for candidates and earlier, less expensive reservations. At this stage in the game, Republicans are spending more to get less, which means the shock and awe of their massive dollar advantage isnt necessarily translating to an actual impact on the ground, according to veteran Republican strategist John Thomas. A better metric, he said, is to consider the gross rating points, or GRPs, a unit advertisers use to measure the reach and frequency of an ad campaign, independent of how much was paid for it. entry.article_text: Republicans are spending hundreds of millions of dollars on advertising in battleground Senate races as they scramble to defend increasingly competitive GOP seats in the final stretch of the midterms.But when it comes to how far they can stretch a dollar, they’re effectively paying premium prices at Whole Foods while Democrats are shopping deals at Costco.RELATED STORY | Trump is heading all the way to Alaska in a sign of just how close its Senate race may beAcross nine of the most competitive Senate races last month, Republicans cumulatively outspent Democrats on broadcast TV ads by nearly 100% more, $233 million to $121 million, according to AdImpact data, but only saw about 40% more rating points.The disparity comes down to a difference in strategy. Republicans are relying heavily on outside groups, like super PACs, that pay elevated rates for ads and are making big buys late in the campaign, when inventory is stretched.By contrast, Democrats are taking advantage of discounted rates for candidates and earlier, less expensive reservations.At this stage in the game, Republicans are spending more to get less, which means the “shock and awe” of their massive dollar advantage isn’t necessarily translating to an actual impact on the ground, according to veteran Republican strategist John Thomas.A better metric, he said, is to consider the gross rating points, or GRPs, a unit advertisers use to measure the reach and frequency of an ad campaign, independent of how much was paid for it.In those nine races – where outside groups accounted for about 9 in 10 Republican ad dollars, compared to about half for Democrats – Democrats paid $201 per GRP, while Republicans paid about $274.In some races in September, Democrats actually outpaced Republicans in GRPs, completely overcoming their spending edge.In North Carolina, for example, Republicans outspent Democrats by about $17 million to $14 million on TV ads in September, as former Gov. Roy Cooper poses a major threat to former RNC Chair Michael Whatley and the GOP chances of holding Sen. But Democrats got more than 71,000 GRPs from their spend while Republicans got about 58,000. And at the beginning of October – recognizing the costly, difficult road ahead for Whatley – Republicans actually began cutting their remaining ad bookings by about $15 million.Democrats were also outspent last month by Republicans in Maine by about 32%, another premier battleground race where former state Sen. Troy Jackson is looking to unseat veteran GOP incumbent Sen. Susan Collins, who has received major backing from national Republicans. But here, again, despite being outspent, Democrats got 6% more GRPs for their money.Even in Texas – where Democrats were blasted by Republican ad money in September, outspent more than 4 times over – the GRP gap was proportionally much smaller. Republicans got only 2.6 times more GRPs.A GOP super PAC had to spend more than $22 million to air its top ad, touting Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton’s record as a prosecutor, about 15,500 times in September. Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico’s campaign spent a little under $4 million to air its most aired ad, casting Paxton as “the most corrupt politician in Texas,” about 8,000 times. That amounts to less than one-fifth the spending for about half the airtime.Lauren French, communications director for Senate Majority PAC, a leading Democratic super PAC, also emphasized that buying TV late in the cycle becomes exorbitantly expensive. “The nitty-gritty of campaigning is that not all ad space costs the same,” she said.“If you are buying something in February, it’s going to be a lot cheaper, and you’re going to get a lot more bang for your buck than, say, if you’re buying it in September. So that’s why you’re seeing this huge disconnect between what Republicans are paying and what Democrats are paying on average in some of these races,” French said.In seven of the top nine Senate races by total TV and radio ad spending in September, Democrats paid less per GRP than Republicans.The two exceptions were New Hampshire and Alaska. Confident in their nominees, Republicans were able to secure comparable or better rates in both states’ key markets. In New Hampshire, this was reinforced by Republicans allocating relatively more to cheaper secondary markets.“Broadly speaking, Republicans are using their money pretty ineffectively, and public polling is saying that people are not seeing their ads as much as one would expect. So, by that definition alone, some of their money is being set on fire. We are being outspent in a lot of these states, which means we have to make more strategic decisions,” French said.Thomas said that Texas, in particular, was emblematic of this effect, with GOP outside groups mounting an urgent rescue effort for Paxton and pouring money into the state. He noted that Paxton allies had taken to buying ad time on national NFL broadcasts because local markets had grown so crowded. That’s why people across the country are seeing Texas Senate ads in games that don’t include the Dallas Cowboys or Houston Texans.RELATED STORY | Barack Obama to campaign with Ohio Democrats as he expands his outreach ahead of Election Day“In some cases, because the commercial rate is so high in a local, like a Houston spot, it actually sometimes can be cheaper to buy a national spot,” he said.Democrats’ efficiency advantage might have been much greater, given their candidates have consistently raised more money their Republican opponents on a campaign-to-campaign basis, allowing them to spend more directly on their own ads at cheap rates.But thanks to a recent Supreme Court ruling, for the first time this year, national party committees can take advantage of candidate ad rates through coordinated buys.This means well-funded national committees like the National Republican Congressional Committee or National Republican Senate Committee can team up with candidates – like Mike Rogers in Michigan or Sen. Jon Husted in Ohio – and foot the bill for pricey ad campaigns while getting candidate discounts.The expansion of coordinated buying has allowed Republicans to blunt the Democratic candidate fundraising advantage. Democrats can do the same, but the GOP has taken to it far more aggressively: In September, GOP advertisers spent more than $30 million on coordinated ad buys, compared to about $5 million from Democrats.Outside groups like super PACs still play a dominant role, however, due to their unique ability to accept unlimited donations and make unlimited expenditures.“The money is actually very, very inefficient, but the benefit, even with the inefficiency of a super PAC, is one or two people can cut checks and fund the whole thing,” Thomas said.

entry.title: Local non-profit all about recycling gets community boost
entry.summary: WPTV Morning Anchor Ashley Glass is following up at the Resource Depot in West Palm Beach, which is the site of a Let's Hear It community meet-up, and learning that the non-profit, all about recycling and repurposing everyday items, just received a big boost of community support. 'This place is amazing,' Craig Goldenfarb, Esq., Founder and CEO of GOLDLAW, said. WATCH Local non-profit all about recycling gets community boost Resource Depot gets community boost The Resource Depot is one of 65 local non-profit organizations benefiting from the law firm's GOLDEN 100 program, in which $100,000 in funding was donated. 'To support my community is really special,' Goldenfarb said. 'Putting money back into the non-profit is something that strikes me close to the heart. Staff at the Resource Depot take in 20,000 pounds of donated materials each month and repurpose them for sale. Glass asked the Resource Depot's Executive Director, Jennifer O'Brien, how the funding will be used. 'AI training for our staff,' she responded. 'We have a small but mighty staff, and were looking for ways we might work more efficiently. O'Brien also told Glass that when the community is invested, it gives her entire staff the energy to keep pushing forward with their non-profit work and saving an immeasurable amount of what could be trash from landfills.

entry.title: City council approves lease agreement to bring hotel to Vero Beach Regional Airport area - WPTV
entry.summary: City council approves lease agreement to bring hotel to Vero Beach Regional Airport area    WPTV
entry.article_text: WPTV has been reporting extensively on the growth at the Vero Beach Regional Airport when it comes to flights.But on Tuesday, Vero Beach City Council approved a lease agreement to bring a four-story, 116-room Marriott hotel to the airport."We've been in negotiations with this for the last three years,” Brian Dembeck, interim airport director, said. "This is something that is going to dramatically improve the passenger experience."Dembeck took WPTV to the site, which sits just outside the gates of the terminal along Aviation Boulevard."They're going to have a hotel right next door that they can come, they can stay, wait for their flight, and then go right over to the terminal."But the lodging is more than just for passengers.Brian Cartland, vice-president of economic development for the Indian River County Chamber of Commerce, said the hotel could attract more businesses to the city of Vero Beach and beyond."The hotel is going to serve multiple purposes,” said Cartland. "This hotel is going to help target industry growth by giving those companies that are looking at the area some additional alternatives for some great high-end options."While the hotel is close to the airport, Chad Maxey, senior vice president of Diversified Companies, the developer of the project, said one big need for the extra lodging is just down the street at the Jackie Robinson Training Complex."We feel this is a great location to have a hotel that's going to be able to provide amenities to the airport and also to the families and kids that are going to play baseball,” Maxey said.Maxey said the hotel will also feature a “homerun dugout amenity” for families."Kids can play virtual baseball in the hotel as they're getting ready to go across the street and actually hit the diamond over there and play with the Major League Baseball players,” Maxey said.Developers said the hotel will break ground next year and is expected to be completed by the end of 2028.

entry.title: Martin County commissioners unanimously move forward with 1-year moratorium on data centers
entry.summary: Martin County commissioners voted Tuesday unanimously to move forward with a one-year moratorium on data centers as county leaders consider how to handle future development of the facilities. Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi explained it's 'an opportunity to say, 'pause,' let's hear from people, lets have the opportunity for experts to come and speak to us on both sides. Watch report from Cassandra Garcia: Martin County commissioners unanimously move forward with 1-year moratorium on data centers Commissioners explained they would consider extending the moratorium later if they need more time. If it takes a year, a year and a half, two years, whatever it takes, whatever it takes, we should be doing this, said Martin County Commissioner Eileen Vargas. Tuesday's vote marked the first of two hearings scheduled this month on the proposed moratorium. PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Martin County eyes pause on data center development Martin County eyes pause on data center development Commissioners are expected to revisit the issue on Oct. 27, when another vote will be required. Residents are now hoping the county will use the time to consider their concerns. For me its wildlife so these areas are in largely rural or large plots of land and so you take that area and develop it and these facilities are massivemillions and millions of square feet, no animals can live there anymore, or the hum is going to affect the animals, said Sergei Kelley, who spoke at the meeting. Martin County resident Scott Butler added, 'The fear of the use of all this water we have [...] and understanding what these data center[s] are going to use. The discussion comes as Martin County has already received an application for a data center. The county received the application Monday, one day before commissioners considered the moratorium. Its the first data center proposed in unincorporated Martin County. The application is considered a hyper-scale data center, at over 950-thousand square feet proposed on a lot off Kanner Highway west of I-95. Because the application was submitted before the proposed moratorium, it would not be affected by the measure. The proposal comes amid residents' concerns about the future of data center development in Martin County. One resident at the meeting told commissioners, 'Once land is converted into industrial use, the consequences can remain long after.' entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son , who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police. Port St. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later. WATCH: Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through Donation Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through Donation | WPTV Now, the family's decision to donate his organs could help multiple people waiting for lifesaving transplants while creating a lasting legacy in his memory. Organ donation advocates say the family's choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists. Family's decision offers hope to others The teen's family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families. 'It's a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it's the right thing,' said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft. Craft has worked with Donate Life Florida through the tax collector's office to encourage organ donor registration and raise awareness about the need for donors. Transplant recipient shares personal perspective For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family's decision carries special meaning. 'Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place,' Gray told WPTV. Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed. 'I know for a fact that I wouldn't be here without a family making that election in their deepest moment of despair,' he said. Gray described years of uncertainty while waiting for a match. 'That's five years of uncertainty, five years of being paralyzed, five years of not being able to grow,' he said. entry.title: Suspected fentanyl supplier linked to overdose death arrested after chase on I-95
entry.summary: A suspected drug trafficker linked to a deadly fentanyl overdose investigation is behind bars after investigators say he fled from detectives, hit a law enforcement vehicle and led authorities on a high-speed chase on I-95 in St. Lucie and Martin counties. Investigators said the arrest of James Arthur Green, 43, came after a weeks-long narcotics investigation that also uncovered a suspected connection to a fatal fentanyl overdose. According to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, detectives with the Special Investigations Division conducted multiple undercover purchases of drugs, gathering evidence during those operations that identified Green as the suspected supplier of fentanyl to a person who later died from an overdose. On Oct. 13, detectives used the deceased victim's cellphone during another controlled narcotics operation and placed an order for fentanyl. Investigators said Green returned to the victim's residence, delivered about two grams of fentanyl and sent a photograph showing where he left the drugs. Later that day, detectives conducted a separate undercover operation in which Green allegedly participated in a transaction involving about two ounces of fentanyl and one pound of methamphetamine. When detectives attempted to arrest him, Green fled, allegedly hitting a sheriff's office vehicle and fleeing onto southbound I-95. Authorities said the pursuit reached speeds of approximately 115 mph. During the chase, detectives reported seeing Green throw suspected narcotics and a cellphone out of his vehicle. The Florida Highway Patrol and Martin County Sheriff's Office joined the pursuit as it entered Martin County. Troopers deployed stop sticks before performing a PIT maneuver near Kanner Highway, bringing the chase to an end. Investigators recovered the one pound of methamphetamine and two ounces of fentanyl associated with the controlled purchase, along with an additional 22 grams of methamphetamine, two grams of crack cocaine and one gram of fentanyl. As part of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office investigation, Green faces charges including trafficking of fentanyl, trafficking of cocaine, four counts of trafficking methamphetamine, sale of cocaine and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. 'Public officials are held to an even higher standard,' Uthmeier said. 'If you work in a city hall, serve on a commission, if you hold public office or work for a state agency, you have a duty to serve the public and not use your job to enrich yourself.' entry.title: Road, flight restrictions set to take effect near Mar-a-Lago this weekend
entry.summary: A major stretch of South Ocean Boulevard in Palm Beach is scheduled to close Friday morning until further notice, prompting traffic changes for residents and commuters in the area. According to the Town of Palm Beach's website, South Ocean Boulevard (State Road A1A) will close between South County Road and Southern Boulevard beginning at 5 a.m. Friday, Oct. 16. The closure will remain in effect until further notice. Town officials said information about traffic checkpoints, modified bridge-opening schedules and temporary marine security zones is available on the town's Planned Traffic Impacts webpage . The closure announcement comes as federal aviation officials issued a Temporary Flight Restriction, or TFR, for VIP movement in the West Palm Beach area. The notice is scheduled to take effect Saturday, Oct. 17, and remain in place through Sunday, Oct. 18. Similar road and airspace restrictions have been implemented in the past during visits by President Donald Trump to his Mar-a-Lago residence. At this time, neither the Town of Palm Beach nor federal authorities have publicly confirmed whether Trump is expected to be in Palm Beach this weekend. Motorists are encouraged to plan ahead and expect delays in the area surrounding the closure.

entry.title: Scripps News poll: 43% of voters say they’ve been fooled by AI ads this campaign
entry.summary: Many Americans say theyve been confused or even fooled by political ads using artificial intelligence this campaign season, and want more rules governing how the technology is used, according to a new Scripps News/Talker Research poll. More than four-in-ten registered voters say theyve seen something they thought was real in a political ad, only to later find it was AI-generated. Another 30% said they saw something they werent sure was real or AI. Some of the most talked about ads of the campaign have featured AI-generated candidates like Sen. Jon Ossoff in a beauty salon , James Talarico reciting old quotes out of context , and Sherrod Brown overstaying his welcome at a birthday party . More than half of survey respondents (56%) said they have seen Republicans using AI ads, compared with 49% saying they have seen ads for Democrats. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors And more than three-quarters of voters say there should be rules around how the technology is used in politics. In the absence of federal regulation, states have passed their own laws aimed at curbing the influence of AI or deepfakes in campaign advertising. Some states require disclosures or bar deepfake videos from being published in the weeks leading up to Election Day. But many of the regulations fail to keep up with the evolving use of what can be a cheap and effective new tool. An analysis from the Wesleyan Media Project from early September found AI tools had been used in at least 164 ads, 69% of which did not disclose AI was used. Eighty percent were from Republicans or Republican-leaning groups. Still, a similar amount of voters in both parties say there should be rules around how the technology is used, according to the Scripps News/Talker Research poll, including 77% of Democrats and 79% of Republicans. Concerns about how AI could impact areas outside politics also cut across party lines. Large swaths of the country worry about the impact AI could have on their jobs (61%), government institutions (83%), financial institutions (81%), and their physical safety (57%). Nearly 80% say they see content they believe was generated by AI at least once per day. entry.title: West Palm Beach nonprofit all about recycling gets community boost
entry.summary: WPTV Morning Anchor Ashley Glass is following up at the Resource Depot in West Palm Beach, home to a Let's Hear It community meet-up, and learning that the non-profit, which focuses on recycling and repurposing everyday items, just received a major boost in community support. 'This place is amazing,' Craig Goldenfarb, Esq., Founder and CEO of GOLDLAW, said. WATCH Local non-profit all about recycling gets community boost Resource Depot gets community boost The Resource Depot is one of 65 local non-profit organizations benefiting from the law firm's GOLDEN 100 program, in which $100,000 in funding was donated. 'To support my community is really special,' Goldenfarb said. 'Putting money back into the non-profit is something that strikes me close to the heart. Staff at the Resource Depot take in 20,000 pounds of donated materials each month and repurpose them for sale. O'Brien also told Glass that when the community is invested, it gives her entire staff the energy to keep pushing forward with their non-profit work and saving an immeasurable amount of what could be trash from landfills.

According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists.The teen's family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families."It's a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it's the right thing," said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft.Craft has worked with Donate Life Florida through the tax collector's office to encourage organ donor registration and raise awareness about the need for donors.For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family's decision carries special meaning."Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place," Gray told WPTV.Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed."I know for a fact that I wouldn't be here without a family making that election in their deepest moment of despair," he said.Gray described years of uncertainty while waiting for a match."That's five years of uncertainty, five years of being paralyzed, five years of not being able to grow," he said.Organ donation advocates say the need for donors continues across Florida and the United States.Gray noted that a single donor has the potential to save multiple lives and help many more patients through tissue donation."One donor is to save upwards of nine lives and to be able to heal another 75 lives," Gray said.Behind those numbers are people awaiting a second chance, he said."Let's all be heroes and save lives," Gray added.Advocates say organ donation often allows families to find meaning during some of life's most difficult moments."I would hope that they could see the lasting impact that a selfless act can make on others," Craft said. "If you can help somebody else, it's an amazing thing."For transplant recipients, organ donation can mean more time with family, additional milestones and opportunities.In the midst of tragedy, one Port St. Lucie family's decision could now help save lives and ensure their son's legacy continues through the people he may help.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.summary: Driver flees after fatal motorcycle crash in Fort Pierce, police say    WPTV
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say fled after a crash that killed a motorcyclist Sunday night.The crash happened around 8:52 p.m. near South 25th Street and Okeechobee Road. Officers responded after receiving multiple 911 calls about a crash involving a motorcycle.According to preliminary information from the Fort Pierce Police Department, a white box van traveling east on Okeechobee Road struck a blue motorcycle and attempted to leave the scene.Police said the van's driver made a U-turn in the eastbound lanes while fleeing, crossed the westbound lanes and crashed into Kings and Queens Unisex Salon at 2508 Okeechobee Road.The driver then got out of the van and fled north on foot, police said.When officers arrived, they found the motorcyclist in the outside eastbound lane of Okeechobee Road and determined the person had died. Lucie County Fire Rescue also responded.The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 and Aviation units assisted Fort Pierce police in searching for the driver, but police said he had not been located as of Monday. Two other vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene.Police described the driver as an adult Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top and light-colored pants or shorts.The identity of the person killed has not been confirmed.The Fort Pierce Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit and Crime Scene Investigations are investigating.Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's identity or whereabouts is asked to contact Fort Pierce police at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

entry.title: Trump made Alaska push for Sullivan with Senate control at stake
entry.summary: Its a long way from Washington, has a small population and hasn't backed a Democrat for Senate in nearly 20 years. Yet President Donald Trump on Tuesday devoted a big chunk of his dwindling time ahead of crucial midterm elections to head to Alaska attempting to bolster a Republican incumbent senator in another sign of GOP fears about retaining control of Congress after Election Day on Nov. 3. Trump headlined a rally for Sen. Dan Sullivan in Wasilla, about 45 miles north of Anchorage famous for being the hometown of former Republican vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin and the headquarters of the Iditarod sled dog race across the state. Trump's stop is part of a western swing also taking him to rallies in Arizona and Montana on Wednesday. The president noted to the crowd that he had flown eight hours to rally for Sullivan, whom he called one of the best and most respected senators in D.C. Sullivan, seeking a third term, faces Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman who is running to put Alaska first and emphasizing cost-of-living issues. During Tuesday's rally, Trump announced that Taiwan would purchase gas from a proposed mega-gas project that he has been highlighting amid Sullivan's campaign and that it would invest more than $4 billion. entry.article_text: It’s a long way from Washington, has a small population and hasn't backed a Democrat for Senate in nearly 20 years.Yet President Donald Trump on Tuesday devoted a big chunk of his dwindling time ahead of crucial midterm elections to head to Alaska — attempting to bolster a Republican incumbent senator in another sign of GOP fears about retaining control of Congress after Election Day on Nov. 3.Trump headlined a rally for Sen. Dan Sullivan in Wasilla, about 45 miles north of Anchorage — famous for being the hometown of former Republican vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin and the headquarters of the Iditarod sled dog race across the state.Trump's stop is part of a western swing also taking him to rallies in Arizona and Montana on Wednesday.The president noted to the crowd that he had flown eight hours to rally for Sullivan, whom he called “one of the best and most respected senators in D.C.” Sullivan, seeking a third term, faces Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman who is running to put “Alaska first” and emphasizing cost-of-living issues.During Tuesday's rally, Trump announced that Taiwan would purchase gas from a proposed mega-gas project that he has been highlighting amid Sullivan's campaign and that it would invest more than $4 billion. There was no immediate confirmation from Taiwan, the self-governing island that China claims as its own. The White House did not immediately provide further details.Trump also said the Federal Communications Commission would vote in the coming weeks on investing an additional $162 million in expanding high-speed internet access in Alaska. And he announced pardons for two men who had pleaded guilty in 2022 to Clean Air Act violations for tampering with federally mandated monitoring devices on certain vehicles.Trump and Vance have been trying to boost Sullivan repeatedlyDemocrats last won a Senate seat in Alaska in 2008, and the state hasn’t elected a governor from that party since 1998. The only time Alaska didn’t vote Republican for president was during Lyndon B. Johnson’s landslide 1964 reelection.Yet high gasoline prices from the Iran war and persistently elevated inflation have damaged Trump’s approval ratings enough to leave Democrats dreaming of Alaska upsets.Alaska pollster Ivan Moore said he's seen a decline in Trump's support statewide that mirrors the president's falling approval ratings nationally. That means the Senate race may be decided by Trump 2024 voters who are now unsure they still back him.“The visit is certainly appropriate. Whether the visit will be effective or not is another matter," said Moore, who said when he first heard that Trump would visit Alaska, he didn't believe it would actually happen.The Trump administration has prioritized expanding oil and gas drilling in the state. Vice President JD Vance last week campaigned in Fairbanks for Sullivan and Republican Rep. Nick Begich.Sullivan recently joined Trump in the Oval Office, where the president announced a $54 billion investment by South Korea's government into the proposed Alaska gas project. That's despite South Korea saying the deal, and its total value, haven't been finalized.Versions of a gas project have been proposed in Alaska for decades.Trump trekking four time zones west to get to Sullivan’s home turf — an unusually long trip so close to the midterms — is his strongest show of support for the incumbent.Trump last campaigned in Alaska to try to defeat a fellow RepublicanAlaska is home to around 740,000 people, making it slightly less populous than Denver. It ranks 48th out of 50 states in population, smaller than all but Vermont and Wyoming.Trump nonetheless headlined a 2022 rally in Anchorage opposing Republican Alaska Sen. Lisa Murkowski after she voted to convict him on a charge of incitement of insurrection during his second impeachment trial, following the attack on the U.S. Capitol by a mob of his supporters on Jan. 6, 2021.Trump endorsed Kelly Tshibaka, who challenged Murkowski that year, but that didn't stop incumbent Murkowski from winning reelection.In Wasilla, Max Christensen was waiting in line for the rally and said he hoped to hear more specifics from Trump about the natural gas project, and said he was “really curious just to see how he’s going to handle things like inflation and gas prices and things like that.”Christensen, 22, said he thinks Trump has been a great president “despite all his flaws and stuff," adding, “I think he really does genuinely care about the people of the United States of America.”This year, there are two Dan Sullivans on the ballotTrump has complained about Alaska’s unique elections system. The state has open primaries, in which the four top vote-getters — regardless of party affiliation — advance to the general election, which uses ranked choice voting.RELATED STORY | Republicans are flooding Senate races with ad money, but paying a premiumThat's led to a scenario where there also will be another Dan Sullivan on the November ballot: retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan, whom Trump and other allies of Sen. Sullivan have called a sham candidate. Sullivan has denied this, but Trump continued to hammer the other Sullivan at his rally.“They found a guy named Dan Sullivan, they put him up to get things a little confused,” Trump said, as he repeatedly urged his supporters to vote for “the real Dan Sullivan.”Trump also touted Begich, who is facing a competitive challenge from Bill Hill, an independent.Alaska has a history of rewarding candidates with an independent streak — something Vance acknowledged during his trip to Fairbanks last week."In very deep red years, Alaska is competitive. In very deep blue years, Alaska is still competitive,” Vance said. “I think it’s just a reality of the politics of the state.”Independence has been hard to find in the Republican Party, where Trump for years has had total control. Some Republicans facing tough elections have begun tiptoeing away from the president on key issues such as Iran and tariffs, but not Sullivan, who has been vocal in supporting both.Trump also questioned why three Republicans were running against a Democrat for governor and endorsed Bernadette Wilson, who finished third in the August primary but was the top vote-getting Republican. This came at the same time state GOP leaders — including outgoing Gov. Mike Dunleavy — are urging voters to rank Republicans on the ballot.Many Republicans — despite reservations with ranked voting — have seen a ranking strategy in that race as crucial for Republicans trying to win the seat.Trump's trade war with Canada may also be a factorTrump has also triggered a trade war with Canada, which shares a 1,500-plus-mile border with Alaska and is among the state's most important trading partners.The U.S. banned nearly $1 billion worth of imports from its neighbor — including alcoholic beverages, dairy products and motorcycles — after previously imposing 50% tariffs on about $20 billion in Canadian products. Canada has responded with reciprocal bans and its own import levies, and the back-and-forth could raise prices for Alaska consumers.RELATED STORY | 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumorsMaking Canada an enemy of sorts is "discomforting" for many Alaskans, said pollster Moore.“We associate, I think, probably more closely with the Canadians — more than a lot of the Lower 48," he said.

entry.title: Martin County approves emergency transit plan to restore MARTY bus service after abrupt shutdown
entry.summary: Martin County commissioners have approved emergency measures aimed at restoring MARTY bus service after an abrupt shutdown last week left hundreds of riders without transportation and dozens of drivers without jobs. County leaders voted Tuesday to terminate their contract with Martin County Transit and begin negotiating an emergency one-year operating agreement with MTM Transit, a company that previously operated the county's transit system. County moves forward with emergency contract The emergency action follows last week's sudden shutdown of MARTY bus service, which county officials say disrupted transportation across the community. 'We're doing it under our emergency procurement rules, and we will have a one-year contract,' said Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton. The proposed agreement with MTM Transit would serve as a temporary solution while county leaders develop a longer-term plan for public transportation service. County officials say restoring service is a top priority. 'The next vendor needs to have a contract to be able to hire the drivers back,' Gorton said. Drivers hope to return to work The shutdown has created uncertainty for employees who suddenly found themselves without work. 'It was shocking. This company has pulled out and left 28 employees unemployed, and not knowing what tomorrow is going to be like is very devastating,' said Joey Acevedo, president of ATU Local 1577. Former MARTY bus driver Bill Lawrence said workers are eager to get back behind the wheel and resume serving the community. 'I'm very hopeful. I've always been hopeful. We have people behind us that give us hope,' Lawrence said. entry.title: Van driver sought after fleeing fatal crash involving scooter in Fort Pierce - WPBF
entry.summary: Van driver sought after fleeing fatal crash involving scooter in Fort Pierce    WPBF
entry.article_text: Police are searching for a hit-and-run cargo van driver accused of fatally striking a 44-year-old man riding a gas scooter before he crashed into a nearby business and ran away in Fort Pierce. On Tuesday, the victim was identified as Andy Ramon Martinez-Pantoja. Police officers received multiple 911 calls just before 9 p.m. Sunday about a vehicle crash involving a motorcycle, which later was identified as a gas scooter, close to the intersection of Okeechobee Road and 25th Street, near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. A white cargo van was behind the scooter, traveling east on Okeechobee Road, Maj. Michael Santiago told WPBF's Angela Rozier at a briefing Monday afternoon. The van driver fled the scene and made a U-turn to drive in the wrong direction across the median on Okeechobee Road, but he crashed into the side of a building, the Kings Queens Unisex Salon. The man then ran from the scene. Salon owner Sheila Hampton showed the damage, and is thankful no one was inside at the time. Hampton said she feels for the victim and his family. "His family told me he was just leaving from one of his friend's houses and just going home," she said. A second vehicle, a Toyota pickup truck, was also struck, but no one was injured. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit and Aviation Unit assisted Fort Pierce police and the K-9 Unit in efforts to locate the driver. They are in possession of the van. Police described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top with light-colored pants or shorts. "So, that in itself proves intent that that person knew exactly what they were doing at the time and was just trying to simply get away," Santiago said. Anyone with information should call the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: Jupiter Goodwill employee celebrates 19 years on the job during Disability Employment Awareness Month
entry.summary: October marks National Disability Employment Awareness Month, an annual observance recognizing the contributions people with disabilities make to workplaces across the country. The observance dates back to 1945, when it began as a weeklong national recognition of the contributions of people with physical disabilities. WATCH BELOW: Jupiter Goodwill employee celebrates 19 years on the job National Disability Employment Awareness Month highlights value and talent in the workplace In 1988, Congress expanded the commemoration to a month, and it evolved to recognize the importance of increasing employment opportunities for people with disabilities, including those with mental health conditions and other nonobvious disabilities. The U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Disability Employment Policy, created in 2001, now leads the annual observance. At a Goodwill store in Jupiter, that message can be seen through an employee who has spent nearly two decades putting his own talents to work. WPTV reporter Christy Waite spoke with Jeffrey McFadden Jr., who has worked at the Jupiter Goodwill for 19 years, but for him, going to work is about much more than earning a paycheck. 'I like to smile at others, uplift people and make other people smile,' McFadden said. Staying with the same employer for nearly two decades is something he and his family take pride in. 'My dad said that is a big achievement, to be in a job for so long, and it's a blessing to be a part of this atmosphere and get to meet really nice people,' McFadden said. He said his path into the workforce included attending Goodwill's transition school, where he received job training. 'I went to the Goodwill transition school where we get job training, and it helped us get jobs,' McFadden said. Abra Joseph, the director of donated goods, said Goodwill's programs are aimed at helping people who face barriers to employment find and maintain jobs. 'Sixty percent of our team members self-identify as having some type of barrier to employment,' Joseph said. She said the goal is to 'create an environment where our team members feel valued, respected, and supported.' But McFadden's talents extend far beyond his job. entry.title: Florida AG vows public corruption crackdown after Fort Pierce city manager Nicholas Mimms conviction - WPBF
entry.summary: Florida AG vows public corruption crackdown after Fort Pierce city manager Nicholas Mimms conviction    WPBF
entry.article_text: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier is promising a broader crackdown on public corruption following the conviction of former Fort Pierce City Manager Nicholas Mimms. Lucie County jury found Mimms guilty of official misconduct but acquitted him of bid tampering. The case centered on two vacant, city-owned parcels in Fort Pierce and a nonprofit connected to Mimms’ niece. Prosecutors said Mimms used his position to benefit the nonprofit and later concealed his involvement. Mimms’ niece served on the nonprofit’s board. The organization received a $500,000 grant from a Catholic charitable organization for a community center that was never built. Uthmeier pointed to the conviction as an example of the state’s efforts to hold public officials accountable. “We want to ensure the public that we are protecting their trust, that we are protecting taxpayers and that we are going to hold public officials to the oaths that they take,” Uthmeier said. Uthmeier said the evidence showed that “shenanigans took place” to ensure the nonprofit received the award and that Mimms ultimately covered up his involvement. “He will be punished for abusing his office,” Uthmeier said. Uthmeier said his office’s Public Corruption Unit has more than 25 active investigations or cases underway and described the Mimms case as the first of many public corruption cases the state expects to announce. Florida Department of Law Enforcement Commissioner Larry Keefe said his agency is making public corruption investigations a priority. “No one is too big, no one is too powerful to be held accountable,” Keefe said. Uthmeier declined to comment on what sentence Mimms should receive. Official misconduct is a third-degree felony punishable by up to five years in prison. Mimms is scheduled to be sentenced Dec. entry.title: Scripps News poll: 43% of voters say they’ve been fooled by AI ads this campaign
entry.summary: Many Americans say theyve been confused or even fooled by political ads using artificial intelligence this campaign season, and want more rules governing how the technology is used, according to a new Scripps News/Talker Research poll. Political Roundtable: AI and political campaign ads More than four-in-ten registered voters say theyve seen something they thought was real in a political ad, only to later find it was AI-generated. Another 30% said they saw something they werent sure was real or AI. Some of the most talked about ads of the campaign have featured AI-generated candidates like Sen. Jon Ossoff in a beauty salon , James Talarico reciting old quotes out of context , and Sherrod Brown overstaying his welcome at a birthday party . More than half of survey respondents (56%) said they have seen Republicans using AI ads, compared with 49% saying they have seen ads for Democrats. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors And more than three-quarters of voters say there should be rules around how the technology is used in politics. In the absence of federal regulation, states have passed their own laws aimed at curbing the influence of AI or deepfakes in campaign advertising. Some states require disclosures or bar deepfake videos from being published in the weeks leading up to Election Day. But many of the regulations fail to keep up with the evolving use of what can be a cheap and effective new tool. An analysis from the Wesleyan Media Project from early September found AI tools had been used in at least 164 ads, 69% of which did not disclose AI was used. Eighty percent were from Republicans or Republican-leaning groups. Still, a similar amount of voters in both parties say there should be rules around how the technology is used, according to the Scripps News/Talker Research poll, including 77% of Democrats and 79% of Republicans. Concerns about how AI could impact areas outside politics also cut across party lines. Large swaths of the country worry about the impact AI could have on their jobs (61%), government institutions (83%), financial institutions (81%), and their physical safety (57%). Nearly 80% say they see content they believe was generated by AI at least once per day. Officials said next year's tournament will also return to a traditional food and beverage model, allowing fans to purchase what they want throughout the venue rather than having it included in the admission price. We want more people to be part of it and these changes are an important step in making that happen.' The offer ends Oct. 29. entry.summary: Fort Pierce police investigate after body found in Lincoln Park lake    WPEC
entry.article_text: A man in his 30s was found dead in a lake at Lincoln Park in Fort Pierce Wednesday morning, and police are investigating how he ended up in the water. An officer was flagged down by a citizen just after 9 a.m. who reported seeing a body floating in the lake near the 400 block of North 13th Street, Fort Pierce Police Major Michael Santiago said. Officers say they arrived and found a man face down in the water. Rescue crews pulled him out, but he was pronounced dead. Police identified the man but are waiting to notify his next of kin. Santiago described him as a Black man believed to be between 30 and 32 years old. Investigators are working to determine how the man entered the water and what he was doing before his death. See also: Man fatally shot by PBSO deputy after Boynton Beach pursuit identified There were no apparent signs of trauma to the man's body, Santiago said, but he noted the body appeared to have been in the water for some time. Police are canvassing the area, speaking with potential witnesses and looking for surveillance footage that could help investigators determine how the man ended up in the lake, per FPPD. Santiago said investigators are also looking into whether currents in the waterway could have played a role in where the body was found. It is too early to determine whether foul play or drugs were involved. Investigators are waiting for the medical examiner's findings, including autopsy and toxicology results, to help determine the cause of death. CBS12 News will provide updates as more information becomes available.

entry.title: Court records reveal man shot by PBSO deputies had a lengthy criminal history
entry.summary: Palm Beach County sheriff's deputies shot and killed a 51-year-old man Tuesday afternoon following a strong-arm robbery report and a pursuit that began in Lake Park, which continued along Interstate 95 and ended in a deadly confrontation near Boynton Beach. On Wednesday, PBSO identified Gregory Dobkins as the man who was fatally shot. Court records show his final encounter with law enforcement was not his first. WATCH BELOW: Man shot by deputies had lengthy criminal history, records show Court records reveal man shot by PBSO deputies had a lengthy criminal history Deputies said Dobkins was a suspect in a strong-arm robbery that happened Monday night when they located him in Lake Park using license plate readers. Deputies and state troopers then pursued him down I-95 before a confrontation in Boynton Beach ended in the shooting. At the scene Tuesday, Sheriff Ric Bradshaw described the moment his deputy fired. 'He was actually in a kneeling position and raised up his hands in the shooting position, and that's when our deputy fired, struck him, and he was neutralized right there,' Bradshaw said. 'During this whole time, he's yelling too at the officers, right? 'You're gonna have to kill me. You're gonna have to kill me, you're gonna have to kill me.'' At the scene, Bradshaw told reporters Dobkins had a lengthy criminal history. 'He's obviously a serious bad guy,' Bradshaw said. WPTV dug through court records across Florida and found a history of theft, assault, drug convictions and other charges that go back decades. Arrest affidavits repeatedly reference a battle with addiction. Most recently in 2025, Dobkins was accused of stealing merchandise from a Walgreens in Sarasota. Deputies wrote that when they confronted Dobkins, he was acting erratically, so they Baker Acted him. Court records show Dobkins pleaded guilty to petit theft and paid a fine. Tuesday's deadly confrontation is still actively under investigation by state and county law enforcement. We're going to keep digging into this to better understand what happened, and will bring details as they are uncovered.
