entry.title: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award - WPBF
entry.summary: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award    WPBF
entry.article_text: A water tank at Jaycee Park has been transformed into a colorful tribute to Florida’s native wildlife thanks to Stuart-born and raised artist Christian Stanley and his wife, Jessica. "We keep an eye on the happenings that are going on here in Fort Pierce and saw that there was an open call to artists and put together a design that we thought was a strong submission and submitted it, and we're fortunately selected to come out here and paint the tank," said Stanley, co-owner of C. The decades-old, 22-foot-tall tank that can hold a million gallons of water is owned by Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. It was once a bright shade of white; now it features colorful paintings of manatees, dolphins, turtles, fish and pelicans, along with a sunset. "The great joy that I get out of being of mural artist is taking stuff from the ocean, from the forest, whatever, and bringing it out to the streets for people to see in a much larger-than-life fashion," he said. "So, when I knew the call was interested in being kind of native Florida wildlife, I knew that we could really bring something together that would be really impactful for the community." On Tuesday, Stanley and his wife traveled from Central Florida to the Treasure Coast to apply a UV clear coat to help protect the artwork against the harsh environment of the shore. The two originally began painting the tank in August, completing the mural within a month. He said they then decided to enter their work into Tnemec Company, Inc.'s 2026 Tank of the Year, not expecting much. But became the only South Florida water tank in the running against dozens across the state and the country. "We're so excited," Stanley said.

entry.title: Young Stuart divers take a leap toward college scholarships, international competition and Olympic dreams
entry.summary: In life, they say, take a leap of faith. Well, a group of kids in Stuart are doing just that on a diving board. WATCH BELOW: Stuart divers take leap toward big dreams Stuart's Atlantic Diving Team teaches the Olympic sport of diving to kids of all ages,experience levels 'There are different things for different people. Some people prefer platform diving, which is much higher but fun, which I prefer. Something Ive grown to love is all the friendships that I make throughout the years,' said Grace Erickson, a local diver, who admits diving has always been her passion. 'On my preschool poster I wrote what I wanted to be when I got older was a diver,' Erickson said. That preschooler who could only dream of being a diver is fulfilling her dream as an eighth grader. 'Its been really exciting; it's new things every twist and turn, both in your head and diving off the board,' Erickson said. Her longtime coach, Osvaldo 'Pito' Alberty, thanks her for her courage and wants to see Erickson and her teammates take the sport to new levels. 'We are like a family here. We treat each other with respect and courtesy, and we push each other to do better than everyone else,' said Pito, whose passion is sharing his experience, knowledge and love for diving with young athletes with the Atlantic Diving Team in Stuart. Atlantic takes divers of all ages, backgrounds and experience levels and teaches them the Olympic sport of diving. 'The younger we get them, the better it is because over time they can get scholarships. If they want to do international diving, they can qualify for international competitions or even the Olympics,' Pito said. For divers like Erickson, she wants to take her talents to the college level, but there's a new diver whos just learning the sport, Carissa Smith. 'I was recently a gymnast and just about two months ago I started diving,' said Smith. Smith is a natural-born acrobat. At 14, she hasn't participated in her first competition because she wants to learn the basics. But for now, she admits diving is pretty fun. 'It feels like you're flying; it's exhilarating just being able to get better at my diving,' said Smith.

entry.title: Prima Vista Boulevard safety plan in St. Lucie County would add raised median after 578 crashes since 2020
entry.summary: WPTV is learning that potential road improvements are coming to a busy road in Port St. Lucie. St. Lucie County staff are sharing designs and want to hear input from neighbors about a proposed project on Prima Vista Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Neighbors weigh in on Prima Vista Boulevard changes St. Lucie County wants input on improvements to this busy road They plan to improve a section of the roadway from Airoso Boulevard to U.S. Highway 1 by removing the center left turn lanes Dan Zrallack, county engineer, said their plan is to replace the center left-turn lanes with a raised median. 'The center turn lane is often referred to as a suicide lane,' Zrallack said. 'The more turning movements you have, the more chances you have for accidents by restricting access and putting in the median turn lanes. We can kind of control where those turning movements are and protect the drivers as well as pedestrians walking along the roadway.'  According to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, there have been 578 crashes on that section of the Prima Vista Boulevard since 2020.  Zrallack said the median will make the road safer.  'Statistically, the safety improves by up to like 40 percent or more,' Zrallack said.  But not every neighbor is sold on the improvements.  Kadaysha Wilkins lives on Prima Vista Boulevard and told WPTV the median will make traveling more complicated.  'Adding medians or anything else is going to cause more chaos than good,' Wilkins said. 'Ten to 12 years of living here, I've never seen an issue with our turning lane.'  Wilkins said it'll make it more difficult to take her niece and nephew to school by using the median instead of driving across the street.  'A five-minute ride has turned into a 15-minute travel,' Wilkins said. Wilkins said trying to come home could also be an issue. 'Turning into my driveway, which could have taken two seconds, is that now going to take 15 minutes? Wilkins said.   Zrallack said he hears the concerns and hopes they can address them on Thursday night during their public meeting. 'We're hoping to get more of that by hearing from the community again and seeing what else we can do to refine the design,' Zrallack said. A second in-person public meeting for the project was held Thursday at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center.

entry.title: How to find your polling place in Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast
entry.summary: Before heading to the polls for Florida's 2026 general election, voters should confirm where they are assigned to vote. Polling places can change between election cycles, and election officials recommend checking your polling location well before Election Day. Voters in Palm Beach County, St. Lucie County, Martin County, Indian River County and Okeechobee County can visit their local supervisor of elections website to verify registration information, view their sample ballot and locate their assigned polling place. How do I find my polling place? Most county election offices offer online voter lookup tools that allow voters to: Verify voter registration status View a sample ballot Find their precinct Locate their Election Day polling site Confirm district assignments Can I vote at any polling place? On Election Day, voters must generally cast a ballot at their assigned polling location. During early voting, voters may use any authorized early voting location within their county. What should I bring? Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those who arrive without acceptable identification may be eligible to cast a provisional ballot.

entry.title: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills - WFLX
entry.summary: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills    WFLX
entry.article_text: A program that has worked with thousands of Martin County children is returning after a brief hiatus, with a renewed focus on helping young students strengthen their reading skills. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County is celebrating the return of its AmeriCorps program, which places volunteers directly with students to provide individualized and small-group academic support. WATCH BELOW: Literacy program returns to Martin County after hiatus “We missed it. It was an extremely important piece to our success and moving the district forward,” Martin County Schools Superintendent Michael Maine said. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County first introduced the federal mentorship program to the area in 2019. For six years, AmeriCorps volunteers worked with thousands of local students before federal funding shortfalls forced the program to pause. Now, program leaders have set new goals for its return. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with AmeriCorps Program Director for Martin County Boys and Girls Club, Russell Lamberti. “We want to serve 575 students, and we want to see an increase of 65% growth, and that can be in vocabulary, fluency and grammar,” AmeriCorps Program Director Russell Lamberti said. AmeriCorps volunteers will work one-on-one and in small groups with kindergarten through fifth-grade students at four Boys Girls Club locations, with an emphasis on literacy. For AmeriCorps Volunteer Experience Specialist Abelard Cesar, the mission also has a personal connection. I learned English at 13 years old, and I had mentors that helped me grow,” Cesar said. The Boys Girls Clubs says the program delivered significant academic results during its previous six-year run. In some cases, as many as eight in 10 participating students moved their reading from Level 1 to Level 4. About the same percentage maintained or improved their English Language Arts grades, according to the organization. The organization said students also showed improvements in literacy rates, assessment scores, school attendance and behavioral patterns. AmeriCorps members’ work previously extended beyond the classroom. According to the Boys Girls Clubs, volunteers completed nearly 50 service projects in Martin County and contributed more than 60,000 hours to community cleanup efforts and other acts of service. The return comes as literacy remains a focus across the county. Earlier this year, the Martin County School District reported that local kindergarten students tied for fourth place statewide in readiness scores and literacy assessments. The AmeriCorps program is part of a broader academic effort by the Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County, which serves more than 1,000 members ages 6 to 18 in its daily programs. The organization also provides after-school academic assistance through certified teachers. Beyond its Clubs, the organization runs or manages several programs serving local children, including Reading Buddies, Character Counts!, career training using virtual reality technology, culinary programs and skilled-trades programs. With AmeriCorps volunteers returning, the Boys Girls Clubs says it hopes to build on the program’s previous results while giving more Martin County students the individual attention and support they need.

entry.title: Martin County deputies investigate whether fatal Hobe Sound shooting was Stand Your Ground
entry.summary: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot by a man investigators say was his friend on SE Citrus Way in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound. The Martin County Sheriff's Office is now working to determine whether the shooting qualifies as a Stand Your Ground case. The victim has been identified as Jarvis Preston. No one has been arrested. The Martin County Sheriff is still weighing whether the facts point to a homicide charge or a Stand Your Ground defense. WATCH BELOW: Shooting investigated as possible Stand Your Ground case Martin County Sheriff's Office investigates deadly Hobe Sound shooting among friends The sheriff's office says the two men had been drinking together Wednesday afternoon. Detectives believe Preston continued to drink into the evening, then attempted to rob his friend, who investigators have not publicly identified. The friend got away, but investigators say Preston followed him home and threatened him. 'The deceased starts to pull out a handgun. Shooter pulls out his AR-15 rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there,' John Budensiek of the Martin County Sheriff's Office said. After the shooting, Preston's friend allegedly dropped his weapon, unarmed Preston, and started to render aid until deputies arrived. Investigators are searching for surveillance video and speaking with several witnesses to determine whether Florida's Stand Your Ground law applies. 'We're really not ready to make that determination. But I want to make sure we do it the right way to send the right messages to the right people, so this doesn't happen again,' Budensiek said. The shooting has shaken the tight-knit Banner Lake community. Neighbor Stephanie Rose described the loss. 'It's just sad, really sad,' Stephanie Rose said. Rose said she knew both men. 'They were good kids, I mean, they got along perfectly. ... They were friends. I don't know what happened,' Rose said. As Preston's family and neighbors grieve, the community is coming to terms with the loss of a young life. 'Unbelievable, and it's just sad. I was just on my way to give them my condolences,' Rose said. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.article_text: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot Wednesday night in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound, and authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Martin County sheriff's deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way, where they found Jarvis Preston with three gunshot wounds to the chest. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand your ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek explained that Preston and the shooter were friends. Witnesses reported that Preston had been drinking heavily throughout the day and began threatening the shooter and others while armed with a gun. "He's talking, I'm going to shoot you, I'm going to hurt you. The shooter walks towards him, now they're at the edge of the road, at which point the deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Budensiek said. The sheriff said the shooter called 911 and attempted life-saving efforts before Preston was flown to St. Mary’s Hospital, where he died. Preston’s grandmother, Harriet Ford Gregg, said she heard the gunshots and later saw her grandson lying on the ground. "It was Jarvis laying on the ground out there, and the police officer was reviving him," Gregg said. She shared her grief over losing Preston, who lived with her, saying his empty bedroom is now too painful to face. I'm not going in there," Gregg said. Reservations are available through Avelo Airlines .

entry.title: Martin County deputies investigate whether fatal Hobe Sound shooting was Stand Your Ground
entry.summary: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot by a man investigators say was his friend on SE Citrus Way in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound. The Martin County Sheriff's Office is now working to determine whether the shooting qualifies as a Stand Your Ground case. The victim has been identified as Jarvis Preston. No one has been arrested. The Martin County Sheriff is still weighing whether the facts point to a homicide charge or a Stand Your Ground defense. WATCH BELOW: Shooting investigated as possible Stand Your Ground case Martin County Sheriff's Office investigates deadly Hobe Sound shooting among friends The sheriff's office says the two men had been drinking together Wednesday afternoon. Detectives believe Preston continued to drink into the evening, then attempted to rob his friend, who investigators have not publicly identified. The friend got away, but investigators say Preston followed him home and threatened him. 'The deceased starts to pull out a handgun. Shooter pulls out his AR-15 rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there,' John Budensiek of the Martin County Sheriff's Office said. After the shooting, Preston's friend allegedly dropped his weapon, unarmed Preston, and started to render aid until deputies arrived. Investigators are searching for surveillance video and speaking with several witnesses to determine whether Florida's Stand Your Ground law applies. 'We're really not ready to make that determination. But I want to make sure we do it the right way to send the right messages to the right people, so this doesn't happen again,' Budensiek said. The shooting has shaken the tight-knit Banner Lake community. Neighbor Stephanie Rose described the loss. 'It's just sad, really sad,' Stephanie Rose said. Rose said she knew both men. 'They were good kids, I mean, they got along perfectly. ... They were friends. I don't know what happened,' Rose said. As Preston's family and neighbors grieve, the community is coming to terms with the loss of a young life. 'Unbelievable, and it's just sad. I was just on my way to give them my condolences,' Rose said. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.article_text: A welfare check on an 88-year-old Okeechobee County veteran led to the discovery of a homicide and the arrest of the victim's grandson following an early-morning police chase in Indian River County, Sheriff Eric Flowers and Chief Deputy Michael Hazellief said Thursday during a press conference.WATCH BELOW: Sheriffs announce arrest of wanted suspectPaul Eugene Baker, a longtime Okeechobee County resident and veteran, was found dead on his property after his daughter-in-law called for a welfare check. His grandson, 35-year-old Earl Douglas Wadlington III, was taken into custody after deputies pursued him through a Walmart parking lot at approximately 4 a.m."What started off as a simple welfare check of an 88-year-old veteran in our county has turned into a tragedy and a family tragedy," Hazellief said.Baker's daughter-in-law had not seen or heard from him in several days. She went to his residence and found the house in disarray, which investigators said was highly unusual."She hadn't seen him or talked to him in several days. She went by to check on the residence. She found the house in disarray, became concerned, and it was highly unusual for him to not be around or for the house to be in this manner," Hazellief said.Law enforcement obtained and executed a search warrant for the property. Baker was found dead on the property. Investigators said the manner and location of his death made it immediately evident that it was a homicide.Baker's only vehicle was also missing from the residence, along with other property. Investigators learned that Wadlington had recently been living with Baker.The daughter-in-law told investigators that Wadlington had a history with the criminal justice system and that no other family member would allow him to live with them. Wadlington has over 800 felonies in his criminal background, the chief deputy said."The daughter-in-law also explained to us that he had been in and out of prison, that he had challenges that nobody else in the family would allow him to live with him, but the grandfather had allowed him to stay there," Hazellief said.Because the daughter-in-law also held power of attorney for Baker, law enforcement was able to enter the missing vehicle into the ALPR system — a license plate reader network connected to partner agencies across the Treasure Coast area — as stolen. The vehicle was flagged as connected to a homicide suspect. Investigators tracked the vehicle leaving the area but chose not to issue a public alert."We didn't put anything out publicly at that time because we did not want to startle. We wanted the suspect to stay in the vehicle. Quite honestly, we wanted to keep driving," Hazellief said.WATCH BELOW: Dashcam video of chase, bodycam video of arrest in Indian River CountyInvestigators noted that while the agency was required this past month to remove Flock cameras from state roads and permitted locations per a state DOT order, cameras in other qualifying locations remained operational and allowed investigators to move forward with the case."To be specific with the language, we still have them in place in places that don't meet that criteria, and because of that, we were able to really move forward with this case," Hazellief said.Senior detective Ashley Rojas and her team led the investigation, the chief deputy said.The stolen vehicle was detected by Indian River County's Flock camera system this morning, leading investigators to the suspect's location.Indian River County Sheriff Flowers described the early-morning pursuit caught on video, in which Wadlington fled from deputies through a Walmart parking lot."One of the particular things that's interesting is it's 4 o'clock in the morning. He's running from our deputies. He's running through the Walmart parking lot. You see that our deputies were able to deploy stop sticks. The reason that he ultimately stopped and got out and ran is because his truck was going to stop working. That stolen vehicle is going to stop working," Flowers said.Sebastian Police Department also responded and assisted Indian River County deputies throughout the pursuit."Doesn't matter if the uniform is green or blue, doesn't matter what color it is. We're all going to go after the bad guys," Flowers said.Flowers praised the Flock camera system and said the county will continue using it despite public criticism."For all the naysayers and all the people who don't like flock and who don't like it, we're going to continue to use it. We're going to continue to put bad guys in jail because of it," Flowers said.Flowers noted that Indian River County cameras not covered by the state DOT order remain in operation. He said the Flock system has aided in other cases, including one involving a missing elderly woman.Wadlington was arrested on fleeing and eluding charges, deputies said, in addition to driving a stolen a vehicle. Both agencies said they are working very closely with the state attorney's office to obtain a warrant for his arrest for the homicide very soon."This guy is the definition of somebody who needs to stay behind bars," Flowers said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Martin County sheriff's deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way, where they found Jarvis Preston with three gunshot wounds to the chest. The sheriff said the shooter called 911 and attempted life-saving efforts before Preston was flown to St. Mary’s Hospital, where he died. "It was Jarvis laying on the ground out there, and the police officer was reviving him," Gregg said. She shared her grief over losing Preston, who lived with her, saying his empty bedroom is now too painful to face. I'm not going in there," Gregg said. entry.title: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills - WFLX
entry.summary: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills    WFLX
entry.article_text: A program that has worked with thousands of Martin County children is returning after a brief hiatus, with a renewed focus on helping young students strengthen their reading skills. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County is celebrating the return of its AmeriCorps program, which places volunteers directly with students to provide individualized and small-group academic support. WATCH BELOW: Literacy program returns to Martin County after hiatus “We missed it. It was an extremely important piece to our success and moving the district forward,” Martin County Schools Superintendent Michael Maine said. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County first introduced the federal mentorship program to the area in 2019. For six years, AmeriCorps volunteers worked with thousands of local students before federal funding shortfalls forced the program to pause. Now, program leaders have set new goals for its return. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with AmeriCorps Program Director for Martin County Boys and Girls Club, Russell Lamberti. “We want to serve 575 students, and we want to see an increase of 65% growth, and that can be in vocabulary, fluency and grammar,” AmeriCorps Program Director Russell Lamberti said. AmeriCorps volunteers will work one-on-one and in small groups with kindergarten through fifth-grade students at four Boys Girls Club locations, with an emphasis on literacy. For AmeriCorps Volunteer Experience Specialist Abelard Cesar, the mission also has a personal connection. I learned English at 13 years old, and I had mentors that helped me grow,” Cesar said. The Boys Girls Clubs says the program delivered significant academic results during its previous six-year run. In some cases, as many as eight in 10 participating students moved their reading from Level 1 to Level 4. About the same percentage maintained or improved their English Language Arts grades, according to the organization. The organization said students also showed improvements in literacy rates, assessment scores, school attendance and behavioral patterns. AmeriCorps members’ work previously extended beyond the classroom. According to the Boys Girls Clubs, volunteers completed nearly 50 service projects in Martin County and contributed more than 60,000 hours to community cleanup efforts and other acts of service. The return comes as literacy remains a focus across the county. Earlier this year, the Martin County School District reported that local kindergarten students tied for fourth place statewide in readiness scores and literacy assessments. The AmeriCorps program is part of a broader academic effort by the Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County, which serves more than 1,000 members ages 6 to 18 in its daily programs. The organization also provides after-school academic assistance through certified teachers. Beyond its Clubs, the organization runs or manages several programs serving local children, including Reading Buddies, Character Counts!, career training using virtual reality technology, culinary programs and skilled-trades programs. With AmeriCorps volunteers returning, the Boys Girls Clubs says it hopes to build on the program’s previous results while giving more Martin County students the individual attention and support they need.

entry.summary: Suspected fentanyl trafficker arrested after 115 mph chase on I-95 in St. Lucie County    WPBF
entry.article_text: A suspected fentanyl trafficker is behind bars after investigators say he sold drugs to a person who later died of an overdose, then led law enforcement on a high-speed chase that reached 115 mph and ended in Martin County. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro identified the suspect as 43-year-old James Arthur Green, who he said is a 10-time convicted felon. According to the sheriff, the investigation began after a fatal fentanyl overdose on Oct. Detectives used the victim’s phone to contact Green, who allegedly returned to the victim’s home Tuesday to deliver more fentanyl. Investigators say Green even sent a picture to the victim’s phone showing where he had left the drugs, unaware that he had been communicating with law enforcement the entire time. "Obviously, he didn’t know that this person had passed away. We were communicating with them," Del Toro said. Later that day, investigators say Green attempted to sell more fentanyl during an undercover operation. When detectives moved in to arrest him, Green fled, striking an unmarked St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office cruiser before leading law enforcement on a pursuit down Interstate 95. Authorities say the chase reached speeds of 115 mph and continued into Martin County. The pursuit eventually ended near Kanner Highway after Florida Highway Patrol troopers deployed stop sticks and performed a PIT maneuver to stop Green’s vehicle. Del Toro emphasized the dangers of fentanyl and the importance of removing suspected traffickers from the community. This is killing our citizens and our community and preying upon people that have substance abuse problems," Del Toro said. "So I’m very, very happy this person’s off the streets right now." Green now faces multiple drug-related charges, along with additional charges connected to the pursuit. He is being held on a $440,000 bond. entry.title: Dreyfoos seniors build free AI platform for student entrepreneurs
entry.summary: Three seniors at Alexander W. Dreyfoos School of the Arts have created Prodigy Pro, a free artificial intelligence platform designed to help students turn their ideas into real-world ventures. Co-founders Aiden Azoy and Anthony Tan and Head of Design Mia Rubio developed the platform after attending South Florida business networking events and realizing how few students were in the room. WATCH: Dreyfoos seniors build free AI platform for student entrepreneurs These Dreyfoos seniors built an AI platform used in 20 countries We attended networking events and we noticed, why are we the youngest people in the room? Azoy said. There are so many talented students in our communities where theyre able to pursue their professional careers outside of school. The students said they wanted to give young people a way to explore their interests, develop practical ideas and participate in West Palm Beachs growing business community. Creating opportunities for young entrepreneurs The founders attend Dreyfoos in downtown West Palm Beach, where new development and the arrival of major companies have fueled the areas growing reputation as Wall Street South. We go to Dreyfoos, and literally hundreds of feet away are these huge constructions of Related Ross, companies like ServiceNow or even Citadel moving down to South Florida, Tan said. Were right at the forefront of this new business center that is becoming West Palm Beach. Tan said the students attempted to connect with professionals at local gatherings but struggled to find opportunities intended for people their age. We tried to go to these meetings, and a lot of the time there wouldnt be any opportunity for us, Tan said. So thats why we wanted to create our own. Prodigy Pro was built to help students take the first steps toward developing projects and businesses. Prodigy Pro is a free AI entrepreneurship platform that helps a student take their idea from an idea to the final product, Tan said. entry.article_text: Three seniors at Alexander W. Dreyfoos School of the Arts have created Prodigy Pro, a free artificial intelligence platform designed to help students turn their ideas into real-world ventures.Co-founders Aiden Azoy and Anthony Tan and Head of Design Mia Rubio developed the platform after attending South Florida business networking events and realizing how few students were in the room.WATCH: Dreyfoos seniors build free AI platform for student entrepreneurs“We attended networking events and we noticed, why are we the youngest people in the room?” Azoy said. “There are so many talented students in our communities where they’re able to pursue their professional careers outside of school.”The students said they wanted to give young people a way to explore their interests, develop practical ideas and participate in West Palm Beach’s growing business community.The founders attend Dreyfoos in downtown West Palm Beach, where new development and the arrival of major companies have fueled the area’s growing reputation as “Wall Street South.”“We go to Dreyfoos, and literally hundreds of feet away are these huge constructions of Related Ross, companies like ServiceNow or even Citadel moving down to South Florida,” Tan said. “We’re right at the forefront of this new business center that is becoming West Palm Beach.”Tan said the students attempted to connect with professionals at local gatherings but struggled to find opportunities intended for people their age.“We tried to go to these meetings, and a lot of the time there wouldn’t be any opportunity for us,” Tan said. “So that’s why we wanted to create our own.”Prodigy Pro was built to help students take the first steps toward developing projects and businesses.“Prodigy Pro is a free AI entrepreneurship platform that helps a student take their idea from an idea to the final product,” Tan said.Azoy said the team created the platform after noticing that many students were not taking their ideas beyond the classroom.“Prodigy Pro is a way for students to build real ventures outside of school and be able to pursue their professional interests,” Azoy said. “We noticed that not enough students are getting out there and really putting their ideas out into the world. We gave them the ability to do that.”Users enter information about an idea and the problem they hope to solve. The platform’s AI then helps organize the concept and identify potential next steps.Rubio designed the user interface and worked to make the process understandable for students who may have little or no previous business experience.“You upload your information and the idea that you really want to pursue,” Rubio said. “And the AI will help you guide and shape and really tell you what your next step is, as well as create roadmaps, reminders and just really help your venture get off the ground.”The platform divides the development process into smaller sections and tasks.“With Prodigy [Pro], we wanted to make the next step super easy and attainable,” Rubio said. “So we grouped things into different sections and made each task super easy for the user to understand, so they know what to do next with their venture.”During a demonstration, the students used concerns about a school bus route to show how a user could enter a problem and explore possible efficiencies. “You input your information, and it really gives you the next steps, what you should do, and you can ask the AI to help develop your venture,” Rubio said.The founders said making Prodigy Pro free was central to their mission. Azoy said students should have access to the same entrepreneurial tools regardless of their school or community’s resources.“It’s completely free for students, and we want to stress that because we want to basically give the message that a student in an underprivileged school or community should have the same exact resources as, you know, a student in a resourced school,” Azoy said.According to the students, Prodigy Pro has grown to more than 15,000 users in 20 countries.The team also competed in the Mott Million Dollar Challenge, a national student entrepreneurship competition.“A few months ago in May, we competed in the Mott Million Dollar Challenge, where we won $7,500 for our venture,” Tan said.Tan said the prize money was reinvested into Prodigy Pro.“A lot of it went into the development of the platform, going through the UI, the back end, also enabling the AI to be free for other students,” he said.The three founders are seniors preparing for life after high school, but they said Prodigy Pro will continue.Asked whether the platform would remain after graduation, Rubio responded, “Yes, of course. It’ll remain to be a free platform for our users.”For Azoy, the larger goal is to show young people that they do not have to wait to begin developing their professional interests.“We really think that it’s important for them to be showing up and, you know, building ventures that really matter because every student has creativity in an underprivileged or privileged school,” Azoy said.The students’ work comes as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into education, business and everyday problem-solving. entry.title: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award - WPBF
entry.summary: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award    WPBF
entry.article_text: A water tank at Jaycee Park has been transformed into a colorful tribute to Florida’s native wildlife thanks to Stuart-born and raised artist Christian Stanley and his wife, Jessica. "We keep an eye on the happenings that are going on here in Fort Pierce and saw that there was an open call to artists and put together a design that we thought was a strong submission and submitted it, and we're fortunately selected to come out here and paint the tank," said Stanley, co-owner of C. The decades-old, 22-foot-tall tank that can hold a million gallons of water is owned by Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. It was once a bright shade of white; now it features colorful paintings of manatees, dolphins, turtles, fish and pelicans, along with a sunset. "The great joy that I get out of being of mural artist is taking stuff from the ocean, from the forest, whatever, and bringing it out to the streets for people to see in a much larger-than-life fashion," he said. "So, when I knew the call was interested in being kind of native Florida wildlife, I knew that we could really bring something together that would be really impactful for the community." On Tuesday, Stanley and his wife traveled from Central Florida to the Treasure Coast to apply a UV clear coat to help protect the artwork against the harsh environment of the shore. The two originally began painting the tank in August, completing the mural within a month. He said they then decided to enter their work into Tnemec Company, Inc.'s 2026 Tank of the Year, not expecting much. But became the only South Florida water tank in the running against dozens across the state and the country. "We're so excited," Stanley said.

entry.title: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound - WPBF
entry.summary: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot Wednesday night in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound, and authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Martin County sheriff's deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way, where they found Jarvis Preston with three gunshot wounds to the chest. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand your ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek explained that Preston and the shooter were friends. Witnesses reported that Preston had been drinking heavily throughout the day and began threatening the shooter and others while armed with a gun. "He's talking, I'm going to shoot you, I'm going to hurt you. The shooter walks towards him, now they're at the edge of the road, at which point the deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Budensiek said. The sheriff said the shooter called 911 and attempted life-saving efforts before Preston was flown to St. Mary’s Hospital, where he died. Preston’s grandmother, Harriet Ford Gregg, said she heard the gunshots and later saw her grandson lying on the ground. "It was Jarvis laying on the ground out there, and the police officer was reviving him," Gregg said. She shared her grief over losing Preston, who lived with her, saying his empty bedroom is now too painful to face. I'm not going in there," Gregg said. entry.title: Investigators question if fatal shooting in Hobe Sound falls under stand-your-ground law - WPBF
entry.summary: Investigators question if fatal shooting in Hobe Sound falls under stand-your-ground law    WPBF
entry.article_text: Investigators in Martin County are working to determine whether a fatal shooting in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound was a crime or if the shooter acted within Florida's stand-your-ground law. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office said the shooter told them he and his friend were on Southeast Citrus Way on Wednesday night when an argument escalated. According to the shooter, his friend repeatedly threatened to shoot him and even showed him a gun. "The deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Family members identified the deceased as Jarvis Preston. The sheriff’s office has not released the identity of the shooter. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand-your-ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Budensiek said. Dave Aronberg, the former Palm Beach County state attorney who is not involved in this case but has experience with stand-your-ground cases, said the shooter’s account suggests it could fall under the law. "The shooter must have reasonably believed that firing the weapon was immediately necessary to prevent imminent death or great bodily harm," Aronberg said. However, Aronberg noted that if Preston did not pull a gun, never had a gun, or if the shooter was the aggressor, the stand your ground defense would not apply. "You can't start a fight, provoke the confrontation and then shoot your way out of it," Aronberg said. The sheriff said investigators are still working to locate and interview witnesses to the shooting. He added that the final decision on whether charges will be filed will be made in collaboration with the state attorney’s office. entry.summary: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie community members had a chance to learn more about and comment on proposed safety changes to Prima Vista Boulevard during a county information session at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center Thursday. The proposal focuses on the stretch between Aroso Boulevard and U.S. It would replace the center turn lane with a raised median and add landscaping designed to make the road feel narrower and encourage drivers to slow down. A majority of the community members spoke out against the plan, saying they don't believe the changes would improve safety. County officials say the changes are intended to improve safety, reduce crashes, and help slow traffic along the corridor. "We understand it's not popular. That's why we have these," said St. Lucie County engineer Dan Zrallack. "We're taking away the ease of access for people who live along this corridor. There's a lot of driveways. There's a lot of residences that have historically been able to turn directly into their driveway. It's no longer safe to do that. We have to control the traffic so that we have less accidents." County staff estimate the project could cost about $6.1 million dollars, but don't know where that money would come from yet. See also: Jupiter woman sues DoorDash, alleges delivery driver sexually assaulted her County leaders said feedback from the meeting will help shape the project. The proposal is in the early stages. Lucie County still needs to design the roadway, and identify funding sources before any work can move forward. Residents who couldn’t attend the workshop can review plans and submit comments to Christopher.arnold@stlucieco.gov.

entry.title: Woman charged with animal cruelty after bringing 'severely emaciated' dog to veterinarian
entry.summary: A West Palm Beach woman is facing a felony animal cruelty charge after investigators said her Yorkshire terrier was so severely malnourished that veterinarians gave the dog the lowest possible body condition score before it was euthanized. The investigation began Oct. 2 when Palm Beach County Animal Care and Control officers responded to Access Specialty Animal Hospital in Royal Palm Beach after staff reported a suspected animal cruelty case involving a 7-year-old Yorkshire terrier named King. Veterinary staff told investigators King arrived in critical condition suffering from severe emaciation, a heavy flea infestation and signs of prolonged neglect. According to the affidavit, veterinarians assigned King a 1 out of 9 body condition score on the Purina Body Condition Scale, the lowest possible rating, indicating extreme emaciation. The attending veterinarian told investigators the dog was non-responsive, severely hypothermic and in respiratory and cardiac distress when he arrived. According to the affidavit, the Yorkie was unable to breathe on his own. The veterinarian determined King's condition was the result of a chronic deterioration that developed over weeks or months rather than a sudden illness. Despite emergency lifesaving measures, including intubation and assisted ventilation, the dog's condition remained poor due to the severity of his condition. The veterinarian said the dog's emaciation as among the most severe she had encountered in her veterinary career and concluded King's suffering was most likely caused by prolonged neglect and a lack of adequate care. The affidavit states Marseille and another individual declined an advanced stabilization treatment recommended by the hospital because they could not afford the cost. Hospital staff identified Charlynn Marseille, 33, as the person who brought King to the veterinary hospital. Investigators later confirmed ownership through animal records and an interview at Marseille's West Palm Beach residence, where she acknowledged owning the dog. Investigators also referenced a 2023 complaint involving the same dog. According to the affidavit, a caller reported concerns that King had been left alone for days without food and was crying. Marseille was arrested Oct. 14 and charged with aggravated animal cruelty causing excessive pain or suffering. She is being held at the Palm Beach County

entry.title: Lake Worth neighbors fear deteriorating private road could cut off emergency access
entry.summary: Residents along Brooklyn Lane in Lake Worth say their only road in and out of the neighborhood is deteriorating, raising concerns about whether emergency vehicles will be able to reach their homes. 'You know it's one way in, one way out, so we're in trouble,' resident Gerald Hruby said. WATCH: Lake Worth neighbors fear deteriorating private road could cut off emergency access Residents along Brooklyn Lane say their only road in and out is deteriorating For neighbor Doug Rua, a former EMT and police officer, the biggest concern is public safety. 'I'm concerned about fire trucks being able to maneuver around it or over it, along with ambulances,' Rua said. 'So its really, its really a public safety issue.' Residents say the problem involves a pipe underneath the road. 'The road is corroding away because of a hole in the pipe under the road,' resident Richard Scott said. 'The county won't fix it, and we've had this problem since, uh, 2019.' Residents said the worsening conditions have also affected trash collection. They said garbage pickup stopped when the road became too damaged for trucks to safely navigate. WPTV has been following the neighbors concerns. During a recent return to Brooklyn Lane, WPTV traffic reporter Johann Hoffend saw county workers assessing the damage and performing temporary work that allowed trash pickup to resume. 'We reached out to WPTV earlier this month and actually last month, and theyve really been a help to us,' Rua said. But those temporary repairs are already showing signs of deterioration following recent heavy rain. The county has said it cannot repair the road because Brooklyn Lane is private. That leaves residents questioning what a permanent solution might look like and who ultimately bears responsibility for fixing the deteriorating roadway. WPTV reached out to the county about whether there are options to address the damage along Brooklyn Lane. The county said it is looking into the issue.

entry.article_text: A welfare check on an 88-year-old Okeechobee County veteran led to the discovery of a homicide and the arrest of the victim's grandson following an early-morning police chase in Indian River County, Sheriff Eric Flowers and Chief Deputy Michael Hazellief said Thursday during a press conference.WATCH BELOW: Sheriff, chief deputy announce arrest of wanted suspectPaul Eugene Baker, a longtime Okeechobee County resident and veteran, was found dead on his property after his daughter-in-law called for a welfare check. His grandson, 35-year-old Earl Douglas Wadlington III, was taken into custody after deputies pursued him through a Walmart parking lot at approximately 4 a.m."What started off as a simple welfare check of an 88-year-old veteran in our county has turned into a tragedy and a family tragedy," Hazellief said.Baker's daughter-in-law had not seen or heard from him in several days. She went to his residence and found the house in disarray, which investigators said was highly unusual."She hadn't seen him or talked to him in several days. She went by to check on the residence. She found the house in disarray, became concerned, and it was highly unusual for him to not be around or for the house to be in this manner," Hazellief said.Law enforcement obtained and executed a search warrant for the property. Baker was found dead on the property. Investigators said the manner and location of his death made it immediately evident that it was a homicide.Baker's only vehicle was also missing from the residence, along with other property. Investigators learned that Wadlington had recently been living with Baker.The daughter-in-law told investigators that Wadlington had a history with the criminal justice system and that no other family member would allow him to live with them. Wadlington has over 800 felonies in his criminal background, the chief deputy said."The daughter-in-law also explained to us that he had been in and out of prison, that he had challenges that nobody else in the family would allow him to live with him, but the grandfather had allowed him to stay there," Hazellief said.Because the daughter-in-law also held power of attorney for Baker, law enforcement was able to enter the missing vehicle into the ALPR system — a license plate reader network connected to partner agencies across the Treasure Coast area — as stolen. The vehicle was flagged as connected to a homicide suspect. Investigators tracked the vehicle leaving the area but chose not to issue a public alert."We didn't put anything out publicly at that time because we did not want to startle. We wanted the suspect to stay in the vehicle. Quite honestly, we wanted to keep driving," Hazellief said.WATCH BELOW: Dashcam video of chase, bodycam video of arrest in Indian River CountyInvestigators noted that while the agency was required this past month to remove Flock cameras from state roads and permitted locations per a state DOT order, cameras in other qualifying locations remained operational and allowed investigators to move forward with the case."To be specific with the language, we still have them in place in places that don't meet that criteria, and because of that, we were able to really move forward with this case," Hazellief said.Senior detective Ashley Rojas and her team led the investigation, the chief deputy said.The stolen vehicle was detected by Indian River County's Flock camera system this morning, leading investigators to the suspect's location.Indian River County Sheriff Flowers described the early-morning pursuit caught on video, in which Wadlington fled from deputies through a Walmart parking lot."One of the particular things that's interesting is it's 4 o'clock in the morning. He's running from our deputies. He's running through the Walmart parking lot. You see that our deputies were able to deploy stop sticks. The reason that he ultimately stopped and got out and ran is because his truck was going to stop working. That stolen vehicle is going to stop working," Flowers said.Sebastian Police Department also responded and assisted Indian River County deputies throughout the pursuit."Doesn't matter if the uniform is green or blue, doesn't matter what color it is. We're all going to go after the bad guys," Flowers said.Flowers praised the Flock camera system and said the county will continue using it despite public criticism."For all the naysayers and all the people who don't like flock and who don't like it, we're going to continue to use it. We're going to continue to put bad guys in jail because of it," Flowers said.Flowers noted that Indian River County cameras not covered by the state DOT order remain in operation. He said the Flock system has aided in other cases, including one involving a missing elderly woman.Wadlington was arrested on fleeing and eluding charges, deputies said, in addition to driving a stolen a vehicle. Both agencies said they are working very closely with the state attorney's office to obtain a warrant for his arrest for the homicide very soon."This guy is the definition of somebody who needs to stay behind bars," Flowers said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award - WPBF
entry.summary: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award    WPBF
entry.article_text: A water tank at Jaycee Park has been transformed into a colorful tribute to Florida’s native wildlife thanks to Stuart-born and raised artist Christian Stanley and his wife, Jessica. "We keep an eye on the happenings that are going on here in Fort Pierce and saw that there was an open call to artists and put together a design that we thought was a strong submission and submitted it, and we're fortunately selected to come out here and paint the tank," said Stanley, co-owner of C. The decades-old, 22-foot-tall tank that can hold a million gallons of water is owned by Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. It was once a bright shade of white; now it features colorful paintings of manatees, dolphins, turtles, fish and pelicans, along with a sunset. "The great joy that I get out of being of mural artist is taking stuff from the ocean, from the forest, whatever, and bringing it out to the streets for people to see in a much larger-than-life fashion," he said. "So, when I knew the call was interested in being kind of native Florida wildlife, I knew that we could really bring something together that would be really impactful for the community." On Tuesday, Stanley and his wife traveled from Central Florida to the Treasure Coast to apply a UV clear coat to help protect the artwork against the harsh environment of the shore. The two originally began painting the tank in August, completing the mural within a month. He said they then decided to enter their work into Tnemec Company, Inc.'s 2026 Tank of the Year, not expecting much. But became the only South Florida water tank in the running against dozens across the state and the country. "We're so excited," Stanley said.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie community members had a chance to learn more about and comment on proposed safety changes to Prima Vista Boulevard during a county information session at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center Thursday. The proposal focuses on the stretch between Aroso Boulevard and U.S. It would replace the center turn lane with a raised median and add landscaping designed to make the road feel narrower and encourage drivers to slow down. A majority of the community members spoke out against the plan, saying they don't believe the changes would improve safety. County officials say the changes are intended to improve safety, reduce crashes, and help slow traffic along the corridor. "We understand it's not popular. That's why we have these," said St. Lucie County engineer Dan Zrallack. "We're taking away the ease of access for people who live along this corridor. There's a lot of driveways. There's a lot of residences that have historically been able to turn directly into their driveway. It's no longer safe to do that. We have to control the traffic so that we have less accidents." County staff estimate the project could cost about $6.1 million dollars, but don't know where that money would come from yet. See also: Jupiter woman sues DoorDash, alleges delivery driver sexually assaulted her County leaders said feedback from the meeting will help shape the project. The proposal is in the early stages. Lucie County still needs to design the roadway, and identify funding sources before any work can move forward. Residents who couldn’t attend the workshop can review plans and submit comments to Christopher.arnold@stlucieco.gov.

entry.title: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients
entry.summary: Having access to a gym is one thing. Actually using it is another. For Jennifer Fink, working out at home means avoiding some of the things she dislikes about going to a traditional gym. WATCH BELOW: Fitness at Your Door brings fitness trainers to your doorstep Fitness at Your Door: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients 'I don't really like the gym, and I usually work out at home,' Fink said. 'You don't have to wait for machines or deal with people at the gym if you don't want to.' It's one of the barriers Kashawn Fraser is trying to address through Fitness at Your Door, a South Florida wellness company that brings personal trainers directly to clients. Fraser said the company has grown to more than 250 certified personal trainers who undergo background checks, serving clients from Miami to Jupiter. The program is also expanding to the Treasure Coast. 'You can order Uber food to your door ... but to have someone show up for you where it matters the most, that's why this company was born,' Fraser said. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with Fraser to learn why he founded the organization. After playing professional football in the Canadian Football League and having multiple knee surgeries, he shifted his focus from his own fitness to helping others with theirs. 'I had three reconstructive knee surgeries back to back,' Fraser said. 'I have been in your shoes. I've been hurt, I've been down, I've been out of shape, I've been in shape.' For clients like Fink, having a trainer come to them can also take some of the anxiety out of going to a gym. 'You don't want to be on one of those YouTube videos where you are doing it wrong, and people are laughing at you,' Fink said. The program also works with people living in 55-and-older communities. Fraser said staying active can be especially meaningful for people approaching retirement who want the energy to enjoy time with their families. 'You work so hard to get to retirement to enjoy your kids and grandkids and have the best energy you can,' Fraser said. Across residential communities, gyms, fitness centers and clubhouses can go underused, even though residents have those amenities close to home. Fraser saw an opportunity to bring the workout into those spaces by having personal trainers meet clients where they already live.

entry.title: Palm Beach County school district to hold meeting on attendance zone changes for new Westlake school
entry.summary: The Palm Beach County School District's Advisory Boundary Committee (ABC) will hold a public meeting on Thursday, Oct. 22 to discuss proposed attendance zone changes affecting several elementary schools beginning in the 2027-2028 school year. WATCH: New $48 million school coming to Westlake, set to open August 2027 New $48 million school coming to Westlake, set to open August 2027 The meeting begins at 6:30 p.m. at the Fulton-Holland Educational Services Center Board Room located at 3300 Forest Hill Boulevard in West Palm Beach. The proposed changes include establishing an attendance zone for a new elementary school Elementary School '23-H' in the city of Westlake, by adjusting portions of the Golden Grove Elementary and Loxahatchee Groves Elementary boundaries, the district said. Additionally, a portion of the Crystal Lakes Elementary attendance zone is proposed to be shifted to Sunset Palms Elementary. The district said the public may attend the meeting in person or offer input virtually. To register to give public comments virtually, visit the district's website and click the dropdown '2026-27 Advisory Boundary Committee (ABC) Meetings with Community Input.' Meeting information, including the agenda and supporting documents, is also available on the district's website . The meeting will be livestreamed, recorded and posted here .

entry.title: Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office seeks public's help on homicide suspect's movements before arrest
entry.summary: The Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office is asking for the public's assistance in gathering additional information regarding the movements of homicide suspect Earl Douglas Wadlington III prior to his arrest . WATCH: Sheriff, chief deputy announce arrest of wanted suspect Indian River, Okeechobee sheriffs announce apprehension of suspect Wadlington was arrested early Thursday morning in Indian River County following an early-morning deputy chase. Deputies said a welfare check on 88-year-old Paul Eugene Baker, an Okeechobee County veteran, led to the discovery of his death and the arrest of Wadlington, the victim's grandson. Deputies are asking anyone who may have encountered Wadlington, observed him, or has information regarding his whereabouts between Sunday, Oct. 11, and his arrest in Indian River County on Thursday, Oct. 15 at approximately 3 a.m., to please come forward. Authorities said they are particularly interested in any sightings or interactions in Palm Beach, Martin and St. Lucie counties during this timeframe. WATCH: Suspect tracked down using license plate readers, deputies say Okeechobee homicide suspect tracked down using license plate readers, deputies say Photographs show Wadlington on the day he left Okeechobee and at the time of his arrest, deputies said, and they want the community to pay special attention to the noticeable change in his hairstyle and overall appearance. Deputies said even the smallest detail could help investigators establish a more complete timeline of his movements. Anyone who saw Wadlington, spoke with him, or have any information that may assist in their investigation, please contact Senior Detective Ashley Rojas with the Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office at 863-763-3117 Ext 5108.

entry.title: Palm Beach County launches new voter app ahead of 2026 General Election
entry.summary: Palm Beach County voters now have a new way to check their voter information, find voting locations and track vote-by-mail ballots ahead of the 2026 General Election. Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Wendy Sartory Link announced the launch of the free Vote Palm Beach mobile app ahead of Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3. SPECIAL SECTION: More election coverage, early voting locations The app is available through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store and is designed to give voters access to election information and services from their phones. 'Whether you're at home, at work, or on the go, we want to make it as easy as possible for every Palm Beach County voter to access accurate, reliable election information,' Link said in a Friday news release. According to the Supervisor of Elections Office, voters can use the app to: Check their voter information and registration Find voting locations View election dates and deadlines Track a vote-by-mail ballot Access information directly from the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Office 'With the 2026 General Election approaching, our new mobile app puts another trusted resource right in the palm of your hand,' Link said. 'It's all about meeting voters where they are and giving them the tools they need to vote with confidence.' The Elections Office said the launch follows a recent overhaul of its website and the introduction of the Palm Beach County Voter Dashboard, which also provides access to voter information and election services. The Vote Palm Beach app is available for free through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Voters can find additional information at VotePalmBeach.gov or call the Supervisor of Elections Office at 561-656-6200.

entry.article_text: A shooting in the Banner Lake area of Hobe Sound on Wednesday night left one person dead, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way and spent hours investigating. Authorities said one person was detained for questioning. Harriet Ford Greg, who said the victim was her grandson, shared that he lived with her. She recalled hearing three gunshots while she was in bed and immediately worrying about him, knowing he was out that night. When she stepped outside, she said she saw him on the ground as first responders tried to save him. " laying on the ground out there and the police officer was reviving him," Greg said. "I thought that he's not going to make it. Somebody shot him." Greg said she is trying to stay strong for her family but admitted she cannot bring herself to walk into the room where her grandson stayed, saying none of this feels real. The sheriff’s office is expected to release more information Thursday afternoon. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: American Heritage Delray senior Domenick Swanson commits to play football at Army while chasing a state title
entry.summary: The American Heritage Stallions are chasing a back-to-back 4A state football championship, and one of the players anchoring their offensive line has already secured his spot at the next level. Domenick Swanson, a senior at American Heritage in Delray, has committed to play college football at the United States Military Academy at West Point, New York. WATCH BELOW: American Heritage Delray offensive lineman commits to play football at Army American Heritage Delray offensive lineman commits to play football at Army 'I will be going to West Point to play football,' Swanson said. 'It is a great opportunity. I went up there, and I was talking to coaches, and everyone says it's an amazing campus. It's beautiful. I mean, it's such a great opportunity to join the military and serve my country and the ability to play college football. I'm very excited about it.' Swanson wears No. 66 and plays center a role he and his coach describe as the quarterback of the offensive line. 'You know, a big reason why our coach likes me at center is that it's like the leader of the offensive line. Being there for the guys and helping with all the plays, and it's a really important part,' Swanson said. Swanson also has family support behind him, his cousin Lily, saying Swanson is a football superstar. 'Lily's my biggest cheerleader.' Swanson said. As his high school career winds down, Swanson said what he will miss most is the bonds he has built with his teammates. 'Really just the relationships and bonds that I've made with my team. You know, I just, it's going to be sad to leave them all behind. Of course, you know, I'll always have my brothers, you know, we'll always be together, but playing football with them, it'll definitely be a big change.' Swanson said. At the college level, Swanson said he looks forward to performing on a bigger stage and playing in front of thousands of people. Before he gets there, he has one goal left for this season. 'I would love to see us just go win every other game. That's kind of an obvious answer. But then, you know, we got our state championship. Hopefully we can go back-to-back,' Swanson said. The Stallions are 7-1 heading into their Friday night game vs. Lakeland Christian.

entry.title: From heartbreak to hope: Jupiter mother turns personal loss into community support
entry.summary: After years of infertility, pregnancy loss and unanswered questions, one Jupiter mother is turning her personal journey into a source of hope for others. The inaugural Hope Rising 5K and Fun Walk will take place Oct. 17 at Carlin Park, bringing together families, wellness providers and community partners with a shared goal: ensuring that no one facing infertility or pregnancy loss feels alone. WATCH: Jupiter woman creates Hope Rising after infertility journey Jupiter mom turns pregnancy loss into hope for other families For founder Kimberly Malik, the event grew from her own experience navigating five miscarriages and four years of infertility. 'When you get told unexplained infertility, that's not really what you want to hear and that's not an answer I can accept,' Malik said. She spent years researching, advocating for herself and searching for answers before ultimately learning she had a blood-clotting condition that contributed to her losses. Despite the heartbreak, Malik said the experience eventually led her to a larger purpose. 'Welcomed our rainbow baby on Nov. 8 of 2024, my husband's birthday, and I just felt this calling of don't let others walk alone,' she said. That mission became the foundation of Hope Rising. Building a community of support Malik says one of the most difficult parts of infertility and pregnancy loss is the isolation many families experience. The Hope Rising event is designed to change that. Organizers are bringing together local businesses, wellness providers and community partners to create a Support Village where attendees can connect with resources and others who understand the journey firsthand. 'We can have those that unfortunately are on a fertility journey feel seen and supported,' Malik said. Among those helping organize the event is Jenny Frattaruolo, owner of Jupiter Fit Club, who became part of Malik's support system during her fertility journey. 'Just having resources and having someone along the journey with you is everything,' Malik said during an earlier interview. More than a race While the event centers around a 5K and fun walk, organizers say the focus extends far beyond race day. entry.title: Jupiter Fire Rescue answers first calls, unveils ladder truck honoring FDNY heroes
entry.summary: Jupiter Fire Rescue began its first day of municipal service Thursday by responding to four calls after midnight and unveiling Jupiter's first ladder truck, which carries a tribute to FDNY Ladder 10 and the six members who died in the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. Fire Chief Darrel Donatto said the department's first calls unfolded as its members had prepared. Jupiter Fire Rescue's Stash Game Is Strong 'They went perfectly, exactly as planned,' Donatto said. 'We've been planning for this moment for three years, and everything is perfect.' The launch marks a new chapter for public safety in Jupiter, with locally controlled fire rescue and emergency medical services operating from stations serving the town's eastern, central and western communities. Jupiter's first ladder truck expands local capabilities Jupiter's new ladder truck is based at Station 10, located at 500 N. U.S. Highway 1 near Burt Reynolds Park. It is the first ladder truck based in Jupiter, according to Donatto. Donatto said the equipment is important because of the town's oceanfront high-rises and multi-story residential developments. 'Jupiter has a lot of high-rise buildings all along the oceanfront here, plus a lot of three-story type townhomes all through the Abacoa community,' Donatto said. 'And so a ladder truck is vital to protecting those, those type of occupancies.' Palm Beach County Fire Rescue continues to serve nearby unincorporated areas, including county pockets near the Jupiter Inlet, DuBois Park and Jonathan's Landing, Donatto said. Ladder 10 honors firefighters lost on Sept. 11 Jupiter's first ladder truck features an American flag design and imagery of the Jupiter Lighthouse. The truck carries the number 10 as a tribute to FDNY Ladder 10, whose firehouse sits across from the World Trade Center site in New York City. Following the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, FDNY Ladder 10's replacement truck was wrapped in an American flag design honoring the firefighters who responded that day. entry.article_text: Jupiter Fire Rescue began its first day of municipal service Thursday by responding to four calls after midnight and unveiling Jupiter's first ladder truck, which carries a tribute to FDNY Ladder 10 and the six members who died in the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.Fire Chief Darrel Donatto said the department's first calls unfolded as its members had prepared."They went perfectly, exactly as planned," Donatto said. Highway 1 near Burt Reynolds Park. It is the first ladder truck based in Jupiter, according to Donatto.Donatto said the equipment is important because of the town's oceanfront high-rises and multi-story residential developments."Jupiter has a lot of high-rise buildings all along the oceanfront here, plus a lot of three-story type townhomes all through the Abacoa community," Donatto said. "And so a ladder truck is vital to protecting those, those type of occupancies."Palm Beach County Fire Rescue continues to serve nearby unincorporated areas, including county pockets near the Jupiter Inlet, DuBois Park and Jonathan's Landing, Donatto said.Jupiter's first ladder truck features an American flag design and imagery of the Jupiter Lighthouse. The truck carries the number 10 as a tribute to FDNY Ladder 10, whose firehouse sits across from the World Trade Center site in New York City.Following the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, FDNY Ladder 10's replacement truck was wrapped in an American flag design honoring the firefighters who responded that day. Before adopting the tribute, Town of Jupiter officials contacted FDNY Ladder 10 to seek their blessing.Rodman Leas, a firefighter with Jupiter Fire Rescue, explained the significance behind the tribute."Today marks a brand new chapter in Jupiter fire history as we roll out 10 Truck, our community is, like you said, our community's very first ladder truck ever," Leas said. "It carries the number 10 badge ... as we honor FDNY Truck 10, whose firehouse stands directly across from the Sept. 11th World Trade Center site." Leas said six members of FDNY Ladder 10 made the ultimate sacrifice on Sept. 11."I took an inspiration from their American flag design as well ... as a constant reminder of the bravery, courage, brotherhood that defined the fire service," Leas said.Battalion Chief Jason Bohan said Jupiter Fire Rescue worked with Palm Beach Gardens as crews prepared for the new department's launch."We've had an incredible partnership with Palm Beach Gardens," Bohan said. "We've been using their training facility, and because of that partnership over the last couple of months, they and us have been training, getting ready for today."That preparation includes learning to put on approximately 60 pounds of protective equipment quickly when an emergency call comes in.Bohan said the most exciting part of launch day was bringing the new department together around its public service mission."Getting us all together, knowing what we're called to do, which is to protect and save people," Bohan said. "So now that it finally came today, we're all really excited."For Lt. Christian Lainhart, joining Jupiter Fire Rescue also represents a personal homecoming. Lainhart previously worked for Martin County Fire Rescue and described himself as a sixth-generation Jupiter pioneer."I'm super excited, very blessed to be here," Lainhart said.Lainhart said his family's roots in the Jupiter area extend to the 1890s. He grew up and attended school in Jupiter and is now raising his family there."It's just truly remarkable," Lainhart said. "Growing up here, I'm a sixth-generation pioneer, so that really means something here. Grew up here, went to school here, currently raising my family, and now I'm here serving the community that I know and love."While Jupiter's new stations, apparatus and equipment are central to the launch, Donatto said the department's personnel are what make the milestone meaningful."The most exciting thing is the people in it," Donatto said. "We've just been so incredibly blessed to hire some of the best people in the world. They're excited to serve the town of Jupiter."By 5 a.m. Thursday, Jupiter Fire Rescue's firefighters and paramedics had already answered four calls while introducing the community to the people and equipment behind the new department.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Port St. Lucie residents could pay about $11 more a month for trash - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie residents could pay about $11 more a month for trash    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie residents are being asked in a straw poll whether they would support paying more for an additional weekly trash pickup, with the proposal adding at least $131 annually to the residential solid-waste assessment. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Right now, residents receive one garbage pickup per week. The proposed change would increase costs by about $11 per month, with service potentially starting in 2028 if the city moves forward. “This is something that is nonbinding, but it gives City Council an opportunity to get a sense of the will of the people and what they would prefer to see,” said Scott Samples, spokesperson for the city of Port St. The city emphasized that the poll is not a final decision. A "yes" vote would indicate support for the additional cost, while a "no" vote would signal opposition. However, the results will not automatically change the current trash pickup schedule. City Council controls the trash contract and service levels, meaning any changes would require council approval and an updated agreement with the current waste management provider, FCC Environmental Services. The city also noted that a second pickup would be an ongoing expense and could increase with inflation. “City Council would take this up. They would have to work with the vendor to understand what the logistics of that would be. And then, the City Council would then vote on whether or not to move forward with this,” Samples said. The poll aims to provide city leaders with insight into residents' preferences, but the final decision will rest with the City Council. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Fort Pierce police investigate after body found in Lincoln Park lake - cw34.com
entry.summary: Fort Pierce police investigate after body found in Lincoln Park lake    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A man in his 30s was found dead in a lake at Lincoln Park in Fort Pierce Wednesday morning, and police are investigating how he ended up in the water. An officer was flagged down by a citizen just after 9 a.m. who reported seeing a body floating in the lake near the 400 block of North 13th Street, Fort Pierce Police Major Michael Santiago said. Officers say they arrived and found a man face down in the water. Rescue crews pulled him out, but he was pronounced dead. Police identified the man but are waiting to notify his next of kin. Santiago described him as a Black man believed to be between 30 and 32 years old. Investigators are working to determine how the man entered the water and what he was doing before his death. See also: Man fatally shot by PBSO deputy after Boynton Beach pursuit identified There were no apparent signs of trauma to the man's body, Santiago said, but he noted the body appeared to have been in the water for some time. Police are canvassing the area, speaking with potential witnesses and looking for surveillance footage that could help investigators determine how the man ended up in the lake, per FPPD. Santiago said investigators are also looking into whether currents in the waterway could have played a role in where the body was found. It is too early to determine whether foul play or drugs were involved. Investigators are waiting for the medical examiner's findings, including autopsy and toxicology results, to help determine the cause of death. CBS12 News will provide updates as more information becomes available.
